sense_groups.english: Crop rotation is a recognized way
sense_groups.chinese: 作物轮作是一种公认的方式

sense_groups.english: to keep soil and the food ecosystem healthy.
sense_groups.chinese: 来保持土壤和食物生态系统的健康。

sense_groups.english: Now, scientists are saying
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，科学家们表示

sense_groups.english: that rotation could be a useful tool—in the sea.
sense_groups.chinese: 轮作在海洋中也可能是一种有用的工具。

sense_groups.english: Researchers tracked a shallow-water, near-shore species used for food: sea cucumbers.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员追踪了一种用于食物的浅水近岸物种：海参。

sense_groups.english: They're easy to harvest and are fairly valuable.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们容易捕捞且相当有价值。

sense_groups.english: But those same attributes mean they're easy to overharvest.
sense_groups.chinese: 但同样的特性意味着它们容易被过度捕捞。

sense_groups.english: The practice has put some sea cucumber species at high risk of extinction,
sense_groups.chinese: 这种做法使一些海参物种面临很高的灭绝风险，

sense_groups.english: even in a relatively well-managed area, the Great Barrier Marine Park in Australia.
sense_groups.chinese: 即使在管理相对较好的区域，澳大利亚的大堡礁海洋公园。

sense_groups.english: In 2004 authorities split the Great Barrier Reef into 154 zones,
sense_groups.chinese: 2004年，当局将大堡礁划分为154个区域，

sense_groups.english: where each zone was fished only once every three years.
sense_groups.chinese: 每个区域每三年只捕捞一次。

sense_groups.english: Fishers rotate through the region.
sense_groups.chinese: 渔民在该区域轮换捕捞。

sense_groups.english: In computer models, the researchers ran through dozens of simulations of each zone,
sense_groups.chinese: 在计算机模型中，研究人员对每个区域进行了数十次模拟，

sense_groups.english: both before and after the divisions took place.
sense_groups.chinese: 无论是在划分之前还是之后。

sense_groups.english: The trials revealed that even with an identical and low-catch allowance in all cases,
sense_groups.chinese: 试验表明，即使在所有情况下都有相同且低捕捞配额的情况下，

sense_groups.english: the sea cucumbers would recover more fully under the rotation strategy
sense_groups.chinese: 海参在轮作策略下恢复得更充分

sense_groups.english: than by harvesting simultaneously throughout the region.
sense_groups.chinese: 而不是在整个区域同时捕捞。

sense_groups.english: In fact, in trials that included rotations, the yield actually increased.
sense_groups.chinese: 事实上，在包含轮作的试验中，产量实际上增加了。

sense_groups.english: The research is in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。

sense_groups.english: The scientists say their results suggest
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们表示，他们的结果表明

sense_groups.english: that such rotation might be beneficial in these kinds of shallow marine regions around the world,
sense_groups.chinese: 这种轮作可能对世界各地这类浅海区域有益，

sense_groups.english: particularly for species that are in high demand.
sense_groups.chinese: 特别是对于需求量大的物种。

sense_groups.english: Because you should not eat your seed corn.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为你不应该吃掉你的种子玉米。

sense_groups.english: Or your seed sea cucumbers.
sense_groups.chinese: 或者你的种子海参。

questions.name: #46 Expelled
questions.en:
By now, you've probably heard of Expelled, the new Ben Stein anti-evolution crockumentary.
It officially opens today as I speak, that's April 18th.
Because of my job, I've had the ______ of sitting through this film twice now.
As least I was getting paid.
The film tries very hard to connect Darwin with the Holocaust.
Toward the end, Stein reads the following quote from the book Descent of Man: "With savages, the weak in body or mind are soon eliminated.
We ______ men, on the other hand, do our utmost to check the process of elimination.
We build asylums for the imbecile, the maimed and the sick.
Thus the weak members of civilized societies propagate their kind.
No one who has attended to the ______ of domestic animals will doubt that this must be highly injurious to the race of man.
Hardly anyone is so ignorant as to allow his worst animals to breed."
That's the end of the quote.
And when he finishes reading the quote, Ben Stein intones the guilty verdict by naming the source: Charles Darwin.
Oh my, it sounds like Darwin actually did provide a rationale to the horrific practices of the Nazis.
Well, I've been covering the anti-evolution crowd for over 20 years.
So I immediately suspected that the propaganda-makers had engaged in what's called quote-mining—you examine the writings of somebody you want to smear and then selectively quote those portions that appear to make your point.
I bet that whatever came immediately after the quoted portion would be something that Ben Stein wouldn't want you to hear.
My research took all of about three minutes.
I went to a full text of Descent of Man online and found the quoted passage.
And then found the sentences that come right after where Ben Stein stopped quoting.
So here's Charles Darwin again, from Descent of Man: "The aid which we feel impelled to give to the helpless is mainly an incidental result of the instinct of sympathy, which was originally acquired as part of the social instincts, but subsequently rendered, in the manner previously indicated, more tender and more widely diffused.
Nor could we check our sympathy, even at the urging of hard reason, without deterioration in the noblest part of our nature.
The surgeon may harden himself whilst ______ an operation, for he knows that he is acting for the good of his patient; but if we were intentionally to neglect the weak and helpless, it could only be for a contingent benefit, with an overwhelming present evil."
Leads to kind of the very opposite impression of Darwin that the filmmakers want you to take away.
Mind you, none of this has anything to do with whether or not Darwin's ______ findings were correct.
They were.
But Ben Stein and his cronies, in their selective use of passages written by a great man merely showed themselves to be so very small.
We have a package of coverage about ______ and its misinformation at our website, sciam.com.
Also check out a ______ page put together by the National Center for Science Education, www. expelledexposed.com.
questions.answer:
1. misfortune
2. civilized
3. breeding
4. performing
5. scientific
6. Expelled
7. resource

sense_groups.english: By now, you've probably heard of Expelled, the new Ben Stein anti-evolution crockumentary.
sense_groups.chinese: 到现在，你可能已经听说过《驱逐》了，就是本·斯坦那部反进化的烂片。

sense_groups.english: It officially opens today as I speak, that's April 18th.
sense_groups.chinese: 就在我说话的这会儿，它今天正式上映，也就是4月18日。

sense_groups.english: Because of my job, I've had the misfortune of sitting through this film twice now.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为工作原因，我不幸地已经硬着头皮看了两遍这部电影。

sense_groups.english: As least I was getting paid.
sense_groups.chinese: 至少我还能拿到报酬。

sense_groups.english: The film tries very hard to connect Darwin with the Holocaust.
sense_groups.chinese: 这部电影极力将达尔文与大屠杀联系起来。

sense_groups.english: Toward the end, Stein reads the following quote from the book Descent of Man: "With savages, the weak in body or mind are soon eliminated.
sense_groups.chinese: 接近结尾时，斯坦读了《人类的由来》中的一段话：“在野蛮人中，身体或心智虚弱的人很快就被淘汰。

sense_groups.english: We civilized men, on the other hand, do our utmost to check the process of elimination.
sense_groups.chinese: 而我们文明人，则竭尽全力阻止这种淘汰过程。

sense_groups.english: We build asylums for the imbecile, the maimed and the sick.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们为低能者、伤残者和病人建造收容所。

sense_groups.english: Thus the weak members of civilized societies propagate their kind.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，文明社会中的弱势成员得以繁衍后代。

sense_groups.english: No one who has attended to the breeding of domestic animals will doubt that this must be highly injurious to the race of man."
sense_groups.chinese: 任何关注过家畜育种的人都不会怀疑，这对人类种族必然极为有害。”

sense_groups.english: That's the end of the quote.
sense_groups.chinese: 引文到此结束。

sense_groups.english: And when he finishes reading the quote, Ben Stein intones the guilty verdict by naming the source: Charles Darwin.
sense_groups.chinese: 读完引文后，本·斯坦念出来源——查尔斯·达尔文，仿佛在宣判有罪。

sense_groups.english: Oh my, it sounds like Darwin actually did provide a rationale to the horrific practices of the Nazis.
sense_groups.chinese: 天哪，听起来达尔文似乎真的为纳粹的可怕行径提供了理由。

sense_groups.english: Well, I've been covering the anti-evolution crowd for over 20 years.
sense_groups.chinese: 嗯，我报道反进化论群体已经超过20年了。

sense_groups.english: So I immediately suspected that the propaganda-makers had engaged in what's called quote-mining—you examine the writings of somebody you want to smear and then selectively quote those portions that appear to make your point.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以我立刻怀疑这些宣传者使用了所谓的“断章取义”——你仔细研究你想抹黑的人的著作，然后选择性地引用那些似乎能支持你观点的部分。

sense_groups.english: I bet that whatever came immediately after the quoted portion would be something that Ben Stein wouldn't want you to hear.
sense_groups.chinese: 我敢打赌，引文后面紧接着的内容一定是本·斯坦不想让你听到的。

sense_groups.english: My research took all of about three minutes.
sense_groups.chinese: 我花了大约三分钟就查到了。

sense_groups.english: I went to a full text of Descent of Man online and found the quoted passage.
sense_groups.chinese: 我在网上找到了《人类的由来》全文，找到了那段引文。

sense_groups.english: And then found the sentences that come right after where Ben Stein stopped quoting.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后找到了本·斯坦停止引用后紧接着的句子。

sense_groups.english: So here's Charles Darwin again, from Descent of Man: "The aid which we feel impelled to give to the helpless is mainly an incidental result of the instinct of sympathy, which was originally acquired as part of the social instincts, but subsequently rendered, in the manner previously indicated, more tender and more widely diffused.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以，还是查尔斯·达尔文，《人类的由来》中写道：“我们感到被迫给予无助者的帮助，主要是同情本能的附带结果，这种本能最初是作为社会本能的一部分获得的，但随后按照先前指出的方式，变得更加温柔和广泛传播。

sense_groups.english: Nor could we check our sympathy, even at the urging of hard reason, without deterioration in the noblest part of our nature.
sense_groups.chinese: 即使受到冷酷理性的催促，我们也无法抑制同情心，否则我们天性中最崇高的部分就会退化。

sense_groups.english: The surgeon may harden himself whilst performing an operation, for he knows that he is acting for the good of his patient; but if we were intentionally to neglect the weak and helpless, it could only be for a contingent benefit, with an overwhelming present evil."
sense_groups.chinese: 外科医生在做手术时可能会硬起心肠，因为他知道这是为了病人的利益；但如果我们故意忽视弱者和无助者，那只能是为了一个不确定的好处，而带来巨大的现实罪恶。”

sense_groups.english: Leads to kind of the very opposite impression of Darwin that the filmmakers want you to take away.
sense_groups.chinese: 这给人的印象与电影制作者希望你得到的关于达尔文的印象截然相反。

sense_groups.english: Mind you, none of this has anything to do with whether or not Darwin's scientific findings were correct.
sense_groups.chinese: 注意，这些都与达尔文的科学发现是否正确无关。

sense_groups.english: They were.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们是正确的。

sense_groups.english: But Ben Stein and his cronies, in their selective use of passages written by a great man merely showed themselves to be so very small.
sense_groups.chinese: 但本·斯坦和他的同伙，通过选择性引用一位伟人的文章，恰恰暴露了他们自己的渺小。

sense_groups.english: We have a package of coverage about Expelled and its misinformation at our website, sciam.com.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们在网站sciam.com上有一组关于《驱逐》及其错误信息的报道。

sense_groups.english: Also check out a resource page put together by the National Center for Science Education, www. expelledexposed.com.
sense_groups.chinese: 另外，可以看看国家科学教育中心整理的资源页面：www.expelledexposed.com。

questions.name: #47 Texas Board of Education

The Texas Board of Education has long promoted the teaching of ______ in schools instead of actual science.

Somebody's gotta stand up to experts that are just…I think, I don't know why they're doing it, they're ______ people."

Its former chairman and current member Don McLeroy uttered this immortal line when confronted with numerous actual ______ urging that evolution be discussed accurately in the curriculum: "I disagree with these experts.

sense_groups.english: The Texas Board of Education has long promoted the teaching of creationism in schools instead of actual science.
sense_groups.chinese: 德克萨斯州教育委员会长期以来一直推动在学校教授神创论，而不是真正的科学。

sense_groups.english: Its former chairman and current member Don McLeroy uttered this immortal line when confronted with numerous actual scientists urging that evolution be discussed accurately in the curriculum:
sense_groups.chinese: 其前主席、现任成员唐·麦克勒罗伊在面对众多真正的科学家敦促在课程中准确讨论进化论时，说出了这句不朽的话：

sense_groups.english: "I disagree with these experts.

sense_groups.english: Somebody's gotta stand up to experts that are just…I think, I don't know why they're doing it, they're wonderful people."
sense_groups.chinese: 总得有人站出来反对那些只是……我认为，我不知道他们为什么这么做，他们是很好的人。”

sense_groups.english: This stuff is important nationwide.

sense_groups.english: Because Texas buys so many textbooks.

sense_groups.english: And it decreed that a list of people who were influential in fomenting revolutions would no longer include Thomas Jefferson.
sense_groups.chinese: 并且它规定，一份在煽动革命方面有影响力的人物名单将不再包括托马斯·杰斐逊。

sense_groups.english: The board's not crazy about Jefferson because of the whole separation of church and state thing.
sense_groups.chinese: 委员会对杰斐逊不感兴趣，因为政教分离的问题。

sense_groups.english: But if the guy who wrote the Declaration of Independence doesn't meet your standards, maybe it's really time to start listening to experts.

questions.name: #48 HIW
questions.en:
If you ever get an ______ of the cornea and you wear contact lenses, save the lenses!
They could help your doctor figure out what medication would be the best bet to cure what ails you.
Wearing ______ is associated with an increased risk of microbial keratitis, or corneal eye infection.
Such an infection can sometimes lead to complications that might threaten your sight.
Doctors will take a scraping from the cornea and then try to identify whatever organisms are present.
But in a study reported in the ______ issue of Archives of Ophthalmology, only 34 percent of corneal scrapings from contact lens-wearing keratitis patients allowed researchers to identify the microbes involved.
But 70 percent of contact lenses from the affected patients harbored microbes.
The study ______ 49 patients—with a total of 50 infected eyes—seen at a hospital in Melbourne, Australia.
Said one of the study's authors, "Contact lens culture may give a clue regarding the ______ of the causative ______ in ______ in which the corneal scraping is culture negative, and may help in choosing the appropriate antimicrobial agent."
questions.answer:
1. infection
2. contacts
3. September
4. included
5. identity
6. organism
7. situations
questions.full:
If you ever get an ______ of the cornea and you wear contact lenses, save the lenses!
They could help your doctor figure out what medication would be the best bet to cure what ails you.
Wearing ______ is associated with an increased risk of microbial keratitis, or corneal eye infection.
Such an infection can sometimes lead to complications that might threaten your sight.

The study ______ 49 patients—with a total of 50 infected eyes—seen at a hospital in Melbourne, Australia.

sense_groups.english: If you ever get an infection of the cornea and you wear contact lenses, save the lenses!
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你得了角膜感染并且佩戴隐形眼镜，请保存好镜片！

sense_groups.english: They could help your doctor figure out what medication would be the best bet to cure what ails you.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们可以帮助医生确定哪种药物最适合治疗你的病症。

sense_groups.english: Wearing contacts is associated with an increased risk of microbial keratitis, or corneal eye infection.
sense_groups.chinese: 佩戴隐形眼镜与微生物性角膜炎（即角膜感染）的风险增加有关。

sense_groups.english: Such an infection can sometimes lead to complications that might threaten your sight.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种感染有时会导致可能威胁视力的并发症。

sense_groups.english: Doctors will take a scraping from the cornea and then try to identify whatever organisms are present.
sense_groups.chinese: 医生会从角膜上刮取样本，然后尝试识别存在的任何微生物。

sense_groups.english: But in a study reported in the September issue of Archives of Ophthalmology, only 34 percent of corneal scrapings from contact lens-wearing keratitis patients allowed researchers to identify the microbes involved.
sense_groups.chinese: 但在一项发表在《眼科学档案》九月刊的研究中，只有34%的佩戴隐形眼镜的角膜炎患者的角膜刮片让研究人员识别出了相关微生物。

sense_groups.english: But 70 percent of contact lenses from the affected patients harbored microbes.
sense_groups.chinese: 但来自受影响患者的隐形眼镜中，有70%含有微生物。

sense_groups.english: The study included 49 patients—with a total of 50 infected eyes—seen at a hospital in Melbourne, Australia.
sense_groups.chinese: 该研究纳入了在澳大利亚墨尔本一家医院就诊的49名患者（共50只感染的眼睛）。

sense_groups.english: Said one of the study's authors, "Contact lens culture may give a clue regarding the identity of the causative organism in situations in which the corneal scraping is culture negative, and may help in choosing the appropriate antimicrobial agent."
sense_groups.chinese: 该研究的一位作者说：“在角膜刮片培养阴性的情况下，隐形眼镜培养可能提供关于致病微生物身份的线索，并有助于选择合适的抗菌药物。”

questions.name: #49 HIW
questions.en:
It takes a Y ______ to make a man.
But that doesn't mean its counterpart, the X chromosome, plays no part.
In fact, it has a big role in making sperm.
To study X evolution, researchers first sequenced the human chromosome more accurately than ever before.
Then they compared the code to that of a mammal whose ______ lineage split from ours about 80 million years ago: the mouse.
It turns out that humans and mice share 95 percent of their X genes.
This finding was no surprise.
In the 1960s, biologist Susumu Ohno suggested the X chromosome would evolve slowly, and thus remain similar in most ______ species.
But some things did change over evolutionary time.
Or rather, 144 things.
One-hundred-forty-four human X chromosome genes had no ______ in mice.
And these genes seemed to be constantly developing.
Many of the genes remained dormant in females, only ______ active in tissues involved in sperm production.
The study is in the journal Nature Genetics.
Clearly, the X chromosome Xceeds its feminine responsibilities.
Which is Xcellent news for male fertility.
questions.full:
It takes a Y ______ to make a man.
But that doesn't mean its counterpart, the X chromosome, plays no part.
In fact, it has a big role in making sperm.
To study X evolution, researchers first sequenced the human chromosome more accurately than ever before.
Then they compared the code to that of a mammal whose ______ lineage split from ours about 80 million years ago: the mouse.
It turns out that humans and mice share 95 percent of their X genes.
This finding was no surprise.
In the 1960s, biologist Susumu Ohno suggested the X chromosome would evolve slowly, and thus remain similar in most ______ species.
But some things did change over evolutionary time.
Or rather, 144 things.
One-hundred-forty-four human X chromosome genes had no ______ in mice.
And these genes seemed to be constantly developing.
Many of the genes remained dormant in females, only ______ active in tissues involved in sperm production.
The study is in the journal Nature Genetics.
Clearly, the X chromosome Xceeds its feminine responsibilities.
Which is Xcellent news for male fertility.

答案:
1. chromosome
2. evolutionary
3. mammalian
4. counterparts
5. becoming

sense_groups.english: It takes a Y chromosome to make a man.
sense_groups.chinese: 需要Y染色体才能造就一个男人。

sense_groups.english: But that doesn't mean its counterpart, the X chromosome, plays no part.
sense_groups.chinese: 但这并不意味着它的对应物X染色体不起作用。

sense_groups.english: In fact, it has a big role in making sperm.
sense_groups.chinese: 事实上，它在制造精子中扮演重要角色。

sense_groups.english: To study X evolution, researchers first sequenced the human chromosome more accurately than ever before.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了研究X染色体的进化，研究人员首先比以前更精确地测序了人类染色体。

sense_groups.english: Then they compared the code to that of a mammal whose evolutionary lineage split from ours about 80 million years ago: the mouse.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后他们将代码与一种哺乳动物的代码进行比较，这种哺乳动物的进化谱系大约在8000万年前与我们分道扬镳：老鼠。

sense_groups.english: It turns out that humans and mice share 95 percent of their X genes.
sense_groups.chinese: 结果发现，人类和老鼠共享了95%的X染色体基因。

sense_groups.english: This finding was no surprise.
sense_groups.chinese: 这一发现并不令人惊讶。

sense_groups.english: In the 1960s, biologist Susumu Ohno suggested the X chromosome would evolve slowly, and thus remain similar in most mammalian species.
sense_groups.chinese: 在20世纪60年代，生物学家大野进提出X染色体进化缓慢，因此在大多数哺乳动物物种中保持相似。

sense_groups.english: But some things did change over evolutionary time.
sense_groups.chinese: 但有些东西在进化过程中确实发生了变化。

sense_groups.english: Or rather, 144 things.
sense_groups.chinese: 或者更确切地说，是144个东西。

sense_groups.english: One-hundred-forty-four human X chromosome genes had no counterparts in mice.
sense_groups.chinese: 144个人类X染色体基因在老鼠中没有对应物。

sense_groups.english: And these genes seemed to be constantly developing.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些基因似乎在不断进化。

sense_groups.english: Many of the genes remained dormant in females, only becoming active in tissues involved in sperm production.
sense_groups.chinese: 许多基因在女性体内保持休眠状态，只在参与精子生成的组织中变得活跃。

sense_groups.english: The study is in the journal Nature Genetics.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《自然遗传学》杂志上。

sense_groups.english: Clearly, the X chromosome exceeds its feminine responsibilities.
sense_groups.chinese: 显然，X染色体超越了其雌性职责。

sense_groups.english: Which is excellent news for male fertility.
sense_groups.chinese: 这对男性生育能力来说是个极好的消息。

questions.name: #50 HIW
questions.en:
In the day of the dinosaur, insects had ______ of nearly two-and-a-half feet.
So why are today's bugs so puny?
  ______ to researchers at U.C. Santa Cruz, we may have birds and bats to thank.
Their conclusions appear in the Proceedings of the ______ Academy of Sciences.
If you ever sat through a high school biology course, you might remember hearing that insects are limited in size by their ability to utilize oxygen.
The bigger you get, the harder it is to get O2 to your tissues.
And bugs don't have lungs to help.
To test the oxygen connection, researchers turned to fossils.
They charted the wingspan of more than 10,000 fossilized insects and found that for the first 150 million years of bug evolution size tracked closely with atmospheric oxygen levels: the more O2, the bigger the bugs.
But then insects started shrinking, even though oxygen continued to rise.
This wave of reduction happens to ______ with the emergence of ______ features that made birds more agile ______ predators.
And insects got even smaller about 60 million years ago, when bats hit the scene.
Being little makes you harder to catch—which may have given bugs with teeny wings an evolutionary leg up.
questions.answer:
1. wingspans
2. According
3. National
4. coincide
5. anatomical
6. airborne
questions.full:
In the day of the dinosaur, insects had ______ of nearly two-and-a-half feet.
So why are today's bugs so puny?
  ______ to researchers at U.C. Santa Cruz, we may have birds and bats to thank.
Their conclusions appear in the Proceedings of the ______ Academy of Sciences.
If you ever sat through a high school biology course, you might remember hearing that insects are limited in size by their ability to utilize oxygen.
The bigger you get, the harder it is to get O2 to your tissues.
And bugs don't have lungs to help.
To test the oxygen connection, researchers turned to fossils.
They charted the wingspan of more than 10,000 fossilized insects and found that for the first 150 million years of bug evolution size tracked closely with atmospheric oxygen levels: the more O2, the bigger the bugs.
But then insects started shrinking, even though oxygen continued to rise.
This wave of reduction happens to ______ with the emergence of ______ features that made birds more agile ______ predators.
And insects got even smaller about 60 million years ago, when bats hit the scene.
Being little makes you harder to catch—which may have given bugs with teeny wings an evolutionary leg up.

答案:
1. wingspans
2. According
3. National
4. coincide
5. anatomical
6. airborne

sense_groups.english: In the day of the dinosaur, insects had wingspans of nearly two-and-a-half feet.
sense_groups.chinese: 在恐龙时代，昆虫的翼展接近两英尺半。

sense_groups.english: So why are today's bugs so puny?
sense_groups.chinese: 那么为什么今天的虫子这么小呢？

sense_groups.english: According to researchers at U.C. Santa Cruz, we may have birds and bats to thank.
sense_groups.chinese: 据加州大学圣克鲁兹分校的研究人员称，我们可能要感谢鸟类和蝙蝠。

sense_groups.english: Their conclusions appear in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们的结论发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。

sense_groups.english: If you ever sat through a high school biology course, you might remember hearing that insects are limited in size by their ability to utilize oxygen.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你上过高中生物课，你可能记得听说过昆虫的大小受其利用氧气能力的限制。

sense_groups.english: The bigger you get, the harder it is to get O2 to your tissues.
sense_groups.chinese: 体型越大，将氧气输送到组织就越困难。

sense_groups.english: And bugs don't have lungs to help.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且虫子没有肺来帮忙。

sense_groups.english: To test the oxygen connection, researchers turned to fossils.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了测试与氧气的关联，研究人员转向了化石。

sense_groups.english: They charted the wingspan of more than 10,000 fossilized insects and found that for the first 150 million years of bug evolution size tracked closely with atmospheric oxygen levels: the more O2, the bigger the bugs.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们绘制了超过一万只昆虫化石的翼展图，发现在昆虫进化的前1.5亿年里，体型与大气氧含量密切相关：氧气越多，虫子越大。

sense_groups.english: But then insects started shrinking, even though oxygen continued to rise.
sense_groups.chinese: 但随后昆虫开始变小，尽管氧气含量持续上升。

sense_groups.english: This wave of reduction happens to coincide with the emergence of anatomical features that made birds more agile airborne predators.
sense_groups.chinese: 这一波体型缩小恰逢鸟类解剖特征的出现，这些特征使它们成为更敏捷的空中捕食者。

sense_groups.english: And insects got even smaller about 60 million years ago, when bats hit the scene.
sense_groups.chinese: 大约6000万年前，当蝙蝠出现时，昆虫变得更小了。

sense_groups.english: Being little makes you harder to catch—which may have given bugs with teeny wings an evolutionary leg up.
sense_groups.chinese: 体型小让你更难被抓住——这可能给了翅膀极小的虫子进化上的优势。

questions.name: #51 Button Cell
questions.en:
They're called button cells, coin cells or watch batteries.
By any name, these tiny, round ______ pose a choking danger to small kids.
And if a child succeeds in swallowing a button cell, the battery may short-circuit in the moist ______ environment, burning the tissue.
A few thousand kids wind up in emergency rooms each year after swallowing a button battery.
But a team of Harvard and M.I.T. researchers that ______ prolific inventor Robert Langer thinks they have a partial solution: a protective coating.
The ______ covered batteries with a material—technically a ______ composite—in which microparticles of conductive metal are suspended in an insulating layer.
Under most circumstances, including inside of a child, the layer is nonconductive.
But when the material is subjected to high pressure, the microparticles are squeezed close enough together to carry a current.
One such pressurized environment is the typical battery compartment in a small device—you often have to force the battery into place.
So the same battery that remains inert when swallowed works just fine when it's jammed into its slot in a hearing aid.
The waterproof design would also protect batteries from corrosion in high humidity.
The research is in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
Tests with pigs found the coated batteries to be gentle on the porcine esophagus.
Next step: figure out a way to keep kids from putting the batteries in their mouths in the first place.
Can a quantum tunneling composite be made to taste terrible?
questions.full:
They're called button cells, coin cells or watch batteries.
By any name, these tiny, round ______ pose a choking danger to small kids.

The ______ covered batteries with a material—technically a ______ composite—in which microparticles of conductive metal are suspended in an insulating layer.
Under most circumstances, including inside of a child, the layer is nonconductive.
But when the material is subjected to high pressure, the microparticles are squeezed close enough together to carry a current.
One such pressurized environment is the typical battery compartment in a small device—you often have to force the battery into place.
So the same battery that remains inert when swallowed works just fine when it's jammed into its slot in a hearing aid.
The waterproof design would also protect batteries from corrosion in high humidity.
The research is in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
Tests with pigs found the coated batteries to be gentle on the porcine esophagus.
Next step: figure out a way to keep kids from putting the batteries in their mouths in the first place.
Can a quantum tunneling composite be made to taste terrible?

答案:

2. esophageal
3. includes
4. scientists

sense_groups.english: They're called button cells, coin cells or watch batteries.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们被称为纽扣电池、硬币电池或手表电池。

sense_groups.english: By any name, these tiny, round batteries pose a choking danger to small kids.
sense_groups.chinese: 无论叫什么名字，这些微小的圆形电池都会对小孩造成窒息危险。

sense_groups.english: And if a child succeeds in swallowing a button cell, the battery may short-circuit in the moist esophageal environment, burning the tissue.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果孩子成功吞下纽扣电池，电池可能会在潮湿的食道环境中短路，灼伤组织。

sense_groups.english: A few thousand kids wind up in emergency rooms each year after swallowing a button battery.
sense_groups.chinese: 每年有数千名儿童因吞下纽扣电池而被送往急诊室。

sense_groups.english: But a team of Harvard and M.I.T. researchers that includes prolific inventor Robert Langer thinks they have a partial solution: a protective coating.
sense_groups.chinese: 但一个包括多产发明家罗伯特·兰格在内的哈佛和麻省理工学院研究团队认为，他们有一个部分解决方案：一种保护涂层。

sense_groups.english: The scientists covered batteries with a material—technically a quantum-tunneling composite—in which microparticles of conductive metal are suspended in an insulating layer.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们用一种材料——严格来说是一种量子隧穿复合材料——覆盖电池，其中导电金属微粒悬浮在绝缘层中。

sense_groups.english: Under most circumstances, including inside of a child, the layer is nonconductive.
sense_groups.chinese: 在大多数情况下，包括在儿童体内，该层是不导电的。

sense_groups.english: But when the material is subjected to high pressure, the microparticles are squeezed close enough together to carry a current.
sense_groups.chinese: 但当材料受到高压时，微粒被挤压得足够近，从而能够传导电流。

sense_groups.english: One such pressurized environment is the typical battery compartment in a small device—you often have to force the battery into place.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种加压环境的一个例子是小型设备中的典型电池仓——你通常需要用力将电池推入到位。

sense_groups.english: So the same battery that remains inert when swallowed works just fine when it's jammed into its slot in a hearing aid.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，同一块电池在吞下时保持惰性，但当被塞入助听器的插槽时却能正常工作。

sense_groups.english: The waterproof design would also protect batteries from corrosion in high humidity.
sense_groups.chinese: 防水设计还能保护电池在高湿度环境中免受腐蚀。

sense_groups.english: The research is in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

questions.name: #53 Advertising
questions.en:
Companies spend ______ on advertising every year.
But they're not just pushing products—they're selling their brand's "personality," too.
Think: Red Bull.
What comes to mind?
Most people say things like speed...power...hyper...extreme.
Well, a pair of scientists wanted to see if the energy drink's alleged qualities would ______ people's performance in a racecar video game—without sipping Red Bull.
So they had 70 volunteers race cars with identical specs, but different paint jobs.
Four with the logo and colors of a drink—Guinness, Tropicana, Coca-Cola or Red Bull—and one car just plain green.
The drivers clocked similar times with most of the cars.
But behind the wheel of the Red Bull car, they ______ drove more aggressively, scoring either incredibly fast race times, or their slowest—by driving recklessly and crashing.
The study appears in the Journal of Consumer Psychology.
Polled after the game, the players didn't realize the Red Bull image apparently ______ their driving.
Which suggests marketing doesn't just influence a brand's personality.
It could be shaping our personalities, too, without our even knowing it.

questions.name: #55 Black Mamba
questions.en:
The black mamba is one of the world's most venomous snakes—its bite can kill a human in just half an hour.
But along with deadly neurotoxins, the black mamba's venom has a special ingredient: a painkiller as potent as morphine.
So says a study in the journal Nature.
Researchers ______ proteins from mamba venom called mambalgins, and injected them into mice.
Then they tested how long it took those mice to yank their paws out of water heated to a painful—but not damaging—115 degrees Fahrenheit.
Turns out mice treated with ______ could take the heat for just as long as mice dosed with morphine, indicating the two drugs had similar pain-relieving effects.
Morphine works by binding opioid receptors, but mambalgins target a completely different pain pathway.
Which is a good thing.
Because they don't slow down ______ like opiates.
And the body doesn't build up tolerance to mambalgins as fast as it does to morphine—meaning mambalgins could keep the pain away for longer.
The French company Theralpha is now developing a drug from the venom.
Just don't call it snake oil.

questions.name: #56 Beluga Whales
questions.en:
Beluga whales live in the world's cold northern seas, where they endure months of perpetual darkness.
"So they have to use sound, rather than sight, in order to find their way around." That's Aran Mooney, a marine ______ at Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, in Massachusetts.
He says belugas have really fast hearing, too: "Sound underwater travels five times faster than it does in air.
And so those guys have to basically perceive and utilize sound five times faster than we do."
He and his colleagues traveled to Bristol Bay, Alaska, to test belugas' hearing in the wild.
They captured seven belugas for routine physicals.
And played them a series of frequencies, while measuring the whales' brain activity with electrodes.
Turns out the whales' hearing was sharp, and similar to that of captive belugas.
Which means they could ______ sound ranging from about 4 kilohertz to 150—a frequency nearly eight times higher than the upper limit of our ears.
The results are in The Journal of Experimental Biology.
The older belugas tested in this survey still had decent hearing too.
But that might not be the case for belugas living in noisier Cook Inlet, near Anchorage.
"There's a lot of military activities, a lot of ______ activities in Cook Inlet, and those animals are known to be ______ at a rate of about two percent per year.
And we think noise is a major ______ to those animals."
And now that researchers know what wild belugas should be able to hear, they can test Cook Inlet belugas—to see whether that underwater noise is, literally, deafening.

sense_groups.chinese: 在野外测试白鲸的听力。

sense_groups.english: They captured seven belugas for routine physicals.

sense_groups.english: And played them a series of frequencies,
sense_groups.chinese: 并向它们播放一系列频率的声音，

sense_groups.chinese: 同时用电极测量鲸鱼的大脑活动。

sense_groups.english: Turns out the whales' hearing was sharp,

sense_groups.english: But that might not be the case for belugas living in noisier Cook Inlet, near Anchorage.

sense_groups.english: And we think noise is a major stressor to those animals."
sense_groups.chinese: 我们认为噪音是这些动物的主要压力源。"

sense_groups.english: And now that researchers know what wild belugas should be able to hear,
sense_groups.chinese: 现在研究人员知道了野生白鲸应该能听到什么，

sense_groups.chinese: 看看水下噪音是否真的震耳欲聋。

questions.name: #57 Yellow Banana
questions.en:
It's not easy being yellow: bananas now face two separate fungal epidemics, which threaten to pluck the fruit off of our tables.
Fortunately, ______ have now sequenced banana DNA, producing the genome of a banana variety that may hold the secret to defeating the diseases.
The report is in the journal Nature.
Today, half of all bananas, including the ones you probably buy, belong to the ______ variety, whose popularity stems in part from having no seeds.
But this trait also removes sexual reproduction from the equation.
The bananas are thus all genetically identical—and identically vulnerable to the two fungal epidemics, Panama disease and black leaf streak disease.
Researchers sequenced the genome of a banana variety called DH-Pahang, whose genes ______ to the Cavendish.
While the genome shows where this fruit fits in the history of plant evolution, it could also help researchers understand why DH-Pahang, unlike its descendant, is resistant to the ______ behind both Panama and black leaf streak disease.
Knowing the genes responsible for this resistance could help ______ create stronger, more resistant bananas.
Which has a lot of appeal.

questions.name: #58 Baby Smile
questions.en:
Ever try to get a baby to smile?
It can seem close to impossible—and then suddenly there it is: that elusive, ______ joyous grin.
Well it turns out those smiles aren't spontaneous—they're strategic.
Researchers have found that when babies smile, it's for a reason.
They want whoever they're interacting with—typically a parent—to smile back.
And they time it just so, a smile here and a smile there.
The researchers call it ______ timing.
The study is in the journal PLoS ONE.
The researchers enlisted real mothers and infants and quantified their interactions, which fell into four categories.
One: babies wanted to maximize the amount of time smiling at their mothers.
Two: they wanted to maximize the time the mothers smiled at them.
Three: they wanted to ______ ______ smiling, and four: no smiling at all.
By studying when smiles happened and what the ______ effect was, the investigators were able to figure out that for mothers the goal 70 percent of the time was to be smiling simultaneously—while for babies 80 percent of the time they just wanted their mother smiling at them.
So, mothers want the interaction, while babies just want to be smiled at.
So your baby may not be able to feed itself, talk or even turn over yet.

questions.name: #59 Baby Tone
questions.en:
How can you tell the difference between a French baby and a German baby?
No, it's not that one is wearing a saucy little beret while the other is tucked into tiny pair of lederhosen.
Well, maybe that's part of it.
But a new study in the journal Current Biology shows that the babies ______ sound different.
Because the melody of an infant's cry matches its mother tongue.
We all know that babies start ______ while they're still in the womb.
So when they come out, they know their mother's voice.
When they're older, they start to imitate the sounds they hear.
  ______ they babble, and then start to speak, and then you never hear the end of it.
But long before that first burble or coo, babies are ______ the elements of language.
A team of scientists recorded the cries of 60 newborns: 30 born into ______ families and 30 that heard German.
And they found that French infants wail on a rising note while the Germans favor a falling melody .
Those patterns match the rhythms of their native languages.
So next time you hear a baby cry, listen closely.
He could be telling you where he's from.
questions.full:
How can you tell the difference between a French baby and a German baby?
No, it's not that one is wearing a saucy little beret while the other is tucked into tiny pair of lederhosen.

Those patterns match the rhythms of their native languages.

1. actually
2. eavesdropping
3. Eventually
4. learning

sense_groups.english: How can you tell the difference between a French baby and a German baby?
sense_groups.chinese: 你怎么分辨法国宝宝和德国宝宝？

sense_groups.english: No, it's not that one is wearing a saucy little beret while the other is tucked into tiny pair of lederhosen.
sense_groups.chinese: 不，不是因为他们一个戴着俏皮的小贝雷帽，另一个穿着小皮裤。

sense_groups.english: Well, maybe that's part of it.
sense_groups.chinese: 嗯，也许这是部分原因。

sense_groups.english: But a new study in the journal Current Biology shows that the babies actually sound different.
sense_groups.chinese: 但《当代生物学》杂志上的一项新研究表明，这些婴儿的哭声实际上听起来不同。

sense_groups.english: Because the melody of an infant's cry matches its mother tongue.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为婴儿哭声的旋律与其母语相匹配。

sense_groups.english: We all know that babies start eavesdropping while they're still in the womb.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们都知道婴儿还在子宫里时就开始偷听了。

sense_groups.english: So when they come out, they know their mother's voice.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以当他们出生时，他们就知道母亲的声音。

sense_groups.english: When they're older, they start to imitate the sounds they hear.
sense_groups.chinese: 当他们长大一些，他们开始模仿听到的声音。

sense_groups.english: Eventually they babble, and then start to speak, and then you never hear the end of it.
sense_groups.chinese: 最终他们咿呀学语，然后开始说话，然后你就再也听不到尽头了。

sense_groups.english: But long before that first burble or coo, babies are learning the elements of language.
sense_groups.chinese: 但在第一次咕咕或咿呀之前很久，婴儿就在学习语言的要素了。

sense_groups.english: A team of scientists recorded the cries of 60 newborns: 30 born into French-speaking families and 30 that heard German.
sense_groups.chinese: 一组科学家记录了60名新生儿的哭声：30名出生在讲法语的家庭，30名听到德语。

sense_groups.english: And they found that French infants wail on a rising note while the Germans favor a falling melody.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现法国婴儿的哭声音调上升，而德国婴儿则偏好下降的旋律。

sense_groups.english: Those patterns match the rhythms of their native languages.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些模式与他们母语的节奏相匹配。

sense_groups.english: So next time you hear a baby cry, listen closely.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以下次你听到婴儿哭时，仔细听。

sense_groups.english: He could be telling you where he's from.
sense_groups.chinese: 他可能正在告诉你他来自哪里。

questions.name: #60 Auditory Sensitivity
questions.en:
Have you ever wanted to turn down the volume at a deafening concert or noisy bar?
Envy the whale: a new study finds that toothed whales can reduce their own ______ sensitivity when they expect a loud sound.
The work is presented at this week's Acoustics 2012 meeting.
Whales and dolphins rely on their responsive hearing to interpret returning ______ clicks.
Previous research suggested that these marine mammals could dull their hearing before uttering outgoing echolocation clicks, which are very loud.
Could they use the same coping ______ for external noises?
To find out, ______ trained a false killer whale that a loud noise would always follow a brief warning signal.
Then, they ______ ______ sensors to the outside of the whale's head and played the signal.
The sensors measured ______ that indicated the whale did reduce its hearing sensitivity in expectation of a clamor.
The researchers hope to test other species as well.
Loud noises from ships can disturb whales.
To accommodate marine life, perhaps vessels could emit signals before making a ruckus, warning whales to tune us out.
questions.answer:
1. auditory
2. echolocation
3. mechanism
4. researchers
5. attached
6. suction-cup
7. brainwaves

sense_groups.english: Have you ever wanted to turn down the volume at a deafening concert or noisy bar?

sense_groups.english: Envy the whale: a new study finds that toothed whales can reduce their own auditory sensitivity when they expect a loud sound.

sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究在本周的2012年声学会议上发表。

sense_groups.chinese: 鲸鱼和海豚依靠灵敏的听觉来解读返回的回声定位咔嗒声。

sense_groups.english: Previous research suggested that these marine mammals could dull their hearing before uttering outgoing echolocation clicks, which are very loud.
sense_groups.chinese: 先前的研究表明，这些海洋哺乳动物在发出非常响亮的回声定位咔嗒声之前，可以钝化自己的听觉。

sense_groups.english: The sensors measured brainwaves that indicated the whale did reduce its hearing sensitivity in expectation of a clamor.

questions.name: #61 HIW
questions.en:
Ants are known for working together, operating as a unit for the good of the colony.
But not so fast, say researchers from the Universities of Leeds and Copenhagen.
It turns out that ants can scheme like a stage mom.
Scientists say that some ants hide out to ensure that their offspring become child-bearing queens instead of barren workers.
The accepted ______ had been that random ants were fed certain foods that would allow them to develop into queens.

sense_groups.chinese: 我们不在乎他们的血压是高还是低

sense_groups.english: And our objective was to see whether or not lowering average or below average blood pressure in diabetics was beneficial
sense_groups.chinese: 我们的目标是观察降低糖尿病患者平均或低于平均水平的血压是否有益

sense_groups.english: and the result suggested that irrespective of whether your blood pressure was high or low, if you had diabetes you benefited
sense_groups.chinese: 结果提示，无论你的血压是高还是低，如果你患有糖尿病，你都会受益

questions.name: #71 Probability
questions.en:
Oh, it’s very spooky.
First of all, probability by itself is spooky.
Give me… let me show you how probability enters the system .
You walk past a store window and you see an image of yourself in the store window, you straighten the part, not so bad you know, for a man of my age.
The guy in the store window who’s fooling around with mannequins he sees you and you see yourself.
What does that mean?
A stream of photons from sunlight leaves your face, heads for the store window – let’s consider one of them.
It has a choice: it can go right through, so that the guy behind the window can see you, or it can be reflected from the store window.
Some ______ of them are reflected, and some of them go through.
What determines that?
What determines the future of that photon?
And countless such examples teach us that it’s random, that it’s a throw of the dice, and that’s where Einstein made his famous statement “God plays dice with the universe.” That every instant of that single object, that quantum object we have probability, we do not have certainty.

questions.name: #72 Loan Guarantee
questions.en:
Well there… there… there’s a positive obligation on the bank to ensure that the people who are signing a loan guarantee, ______ what they’re doing.
Loan guarantees are ... er ... kind of ______ in that … in that someone is giving security or a guarantee and placing themselves at risk for someone else, and they receive nothing ______ in return.
So you’ve got to ask yourself why is this person doing this, do they know what they’re doing?
They’re risking a lot, and not really getting anything back for it.
So the imperative is that the bank must ______ that these people know what they’re doing, and that they fully understand the ______ of what they’re doing, and they know that their ______ may be sold if another person doesn’t meet their obligations.
questions.answer:

2. unique
3. material
4. ensure
5. implications
6. properties

sense_groups.english: Well there… there… there’s a positive obligation on the bank
sense_groups.chinese: 银行有积极的义务

sense_groups.english: to ensure that the people who are signing a loan guarantee, know what they’re doing.
sense_groups.chinese: 确保签署贷款担保的人知道自己在做什么。

sense_groups.english: Loan guarantees are ... er ... kind of unique
sense_groups.chinese: 贷款担保有点特殊

sense_groups.chinese: 而且他们没有得到任何实质性的回报。

sense_groups.english: So you’ve got to ask yourself

sense_groups.english: do they know what they’re doing?
sense_groups.chinese: 他们知道自己在做什么吗？

sense_groups.english: They’re risking a lot,

sense_groups.chinese: 这些人知道自己在做什么，

sense_groups.english: and that they fully understand the implications of what they’re doing,
sense_groups.chinese: 并且他们完全理解自己行为的后果，

sense_groups.english: and they know that their properties may be sold
sense_groups.chinese: 并且他们知道自己的财产可能会被出售

sense_groups.english: if another person doesn’t meet their obligations.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果另一个人没有履行他们的义务。

questions.name: #73 Poverty Ending
questions.en:
For some people, this ______ may seem far fetched, but ending poverty is both ______ necessary and actually feasible.
All of us must play a role in making it happen.
All human beings want, and have a ______ to live in dignity, to determine our own destinies, and to be respected by other, by other people.
Despite the universality of ______ rights, our capacities to fulfill them vary enormously, and no ______ line is more profound in influencing the quality of our lives than the gulf between poverty and prosperity.
questions.full:
For some people, this ______ may seem far fetched, but ending poverty is both ______ necessary and actually feasible.
All of us must play a role in making it happen.
All human beings want, and have a ______ to live in dignity, to determine our own destinies, and to be respected by other, by other people.
Despite the universality of ______ rights, our capacities to fulfill them vary enormously, and no ______ line is more profound in influencing the quality of our lives than the gulf between poverty and prosperity.

答案:
1. proposition
2. morally
3. right
4. these
5. dividing

sense_groups.english: For some people, this proposition may seem far fetched,
sense_groups.chinese: 对一些人来说，这个提议可能显得不切实际，

sense_groups.english: but ending poverty is both morally necessary and actually feasible.
sense_groups.chinese: 但消除贫困在道德上是必要的，实际上也是可行的。

sense_groups.english: All of us must play a role in making it happen.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们所有人都必须为此发挥作用。

sense_groups.english: All human beings want, and have a right to live in dignity,
sense_groups.chinese: 所有人类都渴望并有权利有尊严地生活，

sense_groups.english: to determine our own destinies,
sense_groups.chinese: 决定我们自己的命运，

sense_groups.english: and to be respected by other people.
sense_groups.chinese: 并受到他人的尊重。

sense_groups.english: Despite the universality of these rights,
sense_groups.chinese: 尽管这些权利具有普遍性，

sense_groups.english: our capacities to fulfill them vary enormously,
sense_groups.chinese: 我们实现这些权利的能力却大相径庭，

sense_groups.english: and no dividing line is more profound in influencing the quality of our lives
sense_groups.chinese: 没有哪条分界线比贫困与繁荣之间的鸿沟更能深刻地影响我们的生活质量，

sense_groups.english: than the gulf between poverty and prosperity.
sense_groups.chinese: 比贫困与繁荣之间的鸿沟更深刻。

questions.name: #75 Vaccine
questions.en:
In the ______ vaccine wars, I'm siding with actress Amanda Peet.
And comedian Bill Maher, well, I like your show, but when it comes to vaccines you don't know a punchline from a clothesline.
Maher recently tweeted to his Twitter followers "if u get a swine flu shot ur an idiot." On his HBO program Real Time last week, Maher went head-to-head with former Senator Dr. Bill Frist, who patiently ______ why vaccines were in fact good.
But Maher wasn't buying it.
He advocates a healthy lifestyle over vaccines.
But polio and smallpox outmatched many robust immune systems.
Actress Amanda Peet, meanwhile, has used her celebrity to encourage vaccinations, specifically in response to the alleged vaccine-autism connection, for which there's no scientific evidence, but which has some parents afraid of ______ vaccinations.
In a letter to a parenting magazine, Peet wrote: "It's ______ to suggest that virtually the entire medical community, and the CDC, and the American Academy of Pediatrics are behind a massive cover-up about vaccine safety." See you in the line for the flu shot.

sense_groups.english: In the ______ vaccine wars, I'm siding with actress Amanda Peet.

sense_groups.chinese: 还有喜剧演员比尔·马赫，嗯，我喜欢你的节目，但说到疫苗，你分不清笑点和晾衣绳。

sense_groups.english: Maher recently tweeted to his Twitter followers "if u get a swine flu shot ur an idiot."
sense_groups.chinese: 马赫最近在推特上对他的粉丝说：“如果你打猪流感疫苗，你就是个白痴。”

sense_groups.english: On his HBO program Real Time last week, Maher went head-to-head with former Senator Dr. Bill Frist, who patiently ______ why vaccines were in fact good.
sense_groups.chinese: 上周在他的HBO节目《实时》中，马赫与前参议员比尔·弗里斯特博士正面交锋，弗里斯特耐心地______为什么疫苗实际上是有益的。

sense_groups.chinese: 在一封给育儿杂志的信中，皮特写道：“暗示几乎整个医学界、疾病控制中心和美国儿科学会都在大规模掩盖疫苗安全问题是______的。”

sense_groups.english: See you in the line for the flu shot.
sense_groups.chinese: 流感疫苗注射队伍见。

questions.name: #76 Chromosome
questions.en:
It takes a Y ______ to make a man.
But that doesn't mean its counterpart, the X chromosome, plays no part.
In fact, it has a big role in making sperm.
To study X evolution, researchers first sequenced the human chromosome more accurately than ever before.
Then they compared the code to that of a mammal whose ______ lineage split from ours about 80 million years ago: the mouse.
It turns out that humans and mice share 95 percent of their X genes.
This finding was no surprise.
In the 1960s, biologist Susumu Ohno suggested the X chromosome would evolve slowly, and thus remain similar in most ______ species.
But some things did change over evolutionary time.
Or rather, 144 things.
One-hundred-forty-four human X chromosome genes had no ______ in mice.
And these genes seemed to be constantly developing.
Many of the genes remained dormant in females, only ______ active in tissues involved in sperm production.
The study is in the journal Nature Genetics.
Clearly, the X chromosome Xceeds its feminine responsibilities.
Which is Xcellent news for male fertility.
questions.full:
It takes a Y ______ to make a man.
But that doesn't mean its counterpart, the X chromosome, plays no part.
In fact, it has a big role in making sperm.
To study X evolution, researchers first sequenced the human chromosome more accurately than ever before.
Then they compared the code to that of a mammal whose ______ lineage split from ours about 80 million years ago: the mouse.
It turns out that humans and mice share 95 percent of their X genes.
This finding was no surprise.
In the 1960s, biologist Susumu Ohno suggested the X chromosome would evolve slowly, and thus remain similar in most ______ species.
But some things did change over evolutionary time.
Or rather, 144 things.
One-hundred-forty-four human X chromosome genes had no ______ in mice.
And these genes seemed to be constantly developing.
Many of the genes remained dormant in females, only ______ active in tissues involved in sperm production.
The study is in the journal Nature Genetics.
Clearly, the X chromosome Xceeds its feminine responsibilities.
Which is Xcellent news for male fertility.

答案:
1. chromosome
2. evolutionary
3. mammalian
4. counterparts
5. becoming

sense_groups.english: It takes a Y chromosome to make a man.
sense_groups.chinese: 需要Y染色体才能造就一个男人。

sense_groups.english: But that doesn't mean its counterpart, the X chromosome, plays no part.
sense_groups.chinese: 但这并不意味着它的对应物X染色体不起作用。

sense_groups.english: In fact, it has a big role in making sperm.
sense_groups.chinese: 事实上，它在制造精子中扮演重要角色。

sense_groups.english: To study X evolution, researchers first sequenced the human chromosome more accurately than ever before.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了研究X染色体的进化，研究人员首先以比以往更精确的方式对人类染色体进行了测序。

sense_groups.english: Then they compared the code to that of a mammal whose evolutionary lineage split from ours about 80 million years ago: the mouse.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后他们将编码与一种哺乳动物的编码进行了比较，这种哺乳动物的进化谱系在大约8000万年前与人类分离：老鼠。

sense_groups.english: It turns out that humans and mice share 95 percent of their X genes.
sense_groups.chinese: 结果发现，人类和老鼠共享95%的X染色体基因。

sense_groups.english: This finding was no surprise.
sense_groups.chinese: 这一发现并不令人惊讶。

sense_groups.english: In the 1960s, biologist Susumu Ohno suggested the X chromosome would evolve slowly, and thus remain similar in most mammalian species.
sense_groups.chinese: 在20世纪60年代，生物学家Susumu Ohno提出X染色体进化缓慢，因此在大多数哺乳动物物种中保持相似。

sense_groups.english: But some things did change over evolutionary time.
sense_groups.chinese: 但有些东西在进化过程中确实发生了变化。

sense_groups.english: Or rather, 144 things.
sense_groups.chinese: 或者更确切地说，有144个变化。

sense_groups.english: One-hundred-forty-four human X chromosome genes had no counterparts in mice.
sense_groups.chinese: 144个人类X染色体基因在老鼠中没有对应物。

sense_groups.english: And these genes seemed to be constantly developing.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些基因似乎在不断进化。

sense_groups.english: Many of the genes remained dormant in females, only becoming active in tissues involved in sperm production.
sense_groups.chinese: 许多基因在女性体内保持休眠状态，只在涉及精子产生的组织中变得活跃。

sense_groups.english: The study is in the journal Nature Genetics.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《自然遗传学》杂志上。

sense_groups.english: Clearly, the X chromosome exceeds its feminine responsibilities.
sense_groups.chinese: 显然，X染色体超越了其雌性职责。

sense_groups.english: Which is excellent news for male fertility.
sense_groups.chinese: 这对男性生育能力来说是个好消息。

questions.name: #77 Nearby Star
questions.en:
There's an old-timer in the neighborhood, and it's got a story to tell.
A new study of a relatively nearby star shows that it's almost as ______ as the big bang itself.
The star HD 140283 lies about 190 light-years away in the constellation Libra.
Astronomers have long known that it's ancient, because it ______ mostly hydrogen and helium - which were present at the dawn of the universe - and few of the heavy elements that were ______ later in stellar furnaces.
With the Hubble Space Telescope, researchers have now pinned down the distance to HD 140283, which allowed them to determine how bright the star is.
Along with the chemical ______ of the star, the newly derived stellar properties allowed for a new age estimate.
The study of HD 140283, in the Astrophysical Journal Letters found that the star is 14.46 billion years old.
But the entire universe, as you may have noted heard, is only 13.77 billion years old.
The two age estimates aren't actually in conflict, because there's always some uncertainty.
The full age estimate is thus 14.46 billion years plus or minus 800 million years.
questions.full:
There's an old-timer in the neighborhood, and it's got a story to tell.
A new study of a relatively nearby star shows that it's almost as ______ as the big bang itself.
The star HD 140283 lies about 190 light-years away in the constellation Libra.
Astronomers have long known that it's ancient, because it ______ mostly hydrogen and helium - which were present at the dawn of the universe - and few of the heavy elements that were ______ later in stellar furnaces.
With the Hubble Space Telescope, researchers have now pinned down the distance to HD 140283, which allowed them to determine how bright the star is.
Along with the chemical ______ of the star, the newly derived stellar properties allowed for a new age estimate.
The study of HD 140283, in the Astrophysical Journal Letters found that the star is 14.46 billion years old.
But the entire universe, as you may have noted heard, is only 13.77 billion years old.
The two age estimates aren't actually in conflict, because there's always some uncertainty.
The full age estimate is thus 14.46 billion years plus or minus 800 million years.

答案:
1. old
2. contains
3. forged
4. ceremonials

sense_groups.english: There's an old-timer in the neighborhood, and it's got a story to tell.
sense_groups.chinese: 附近有一颗古老的恒星，它有一个故事要讲。

sense_groups.english: A new study of a relatively nearby star shows that it's almost as old as the big bang itself.
sense_groups.chinese: 一项对一颗相对较近的恒星的新研究表明，它几乎和大爆炸本身一样古老。

sense_groups.english: The star HD 140283 lies about 190 light-years away in the constellation Libra.
sense_groups.chinese: HD 140283 恒星位于天秤座，距离我们大约 190 光年。

sense_groups.english: Astronomers have long known that it's ancient, because it contains mostly hydrogen and helium - which were present at the dawn of the universe - and few of the heavy elements that were forged later in stellar furnaces.
sense_groups.chinese: 天文学家早就知道它很古老，因为它主要包含氢和氦——这些元素在宇宙诞生之初就存在——而很少含有后来在恒星熔炉中锻造的重元素。

sense_groups.english: With the Hubble Space Telescope, researchers have now pinned down the distance to HD 140283, which allowed them to determine how bright the star is.
sense_groups.chinese: 借助哈勃太空望远镜，研究人员现在确定了 HD 140283 的距离，从而能够确定这颗恒星的亮度。

sense_groups.english: Along with the chemical composition of the star, the newly derived stellar properties allowed for a new age estimate.
sense_groups.chinese: 结合恒星的化学成分，新得出的恒星特性使得新的年龄估算成为可能。

sense_groups.english: The study of HD 140283, in the Astrophysical Journal Letters found that the star is 14.46 billion years old.
sense_groups.chinese: 发表在《天体物理学杂志快报》上的对 HD 140283 的研究发现，这颗恒星有 144.6 亿年的历史。

sense_groups.english: But the entire universe, as you may have noted heard, is only 13.77 billion years old.
sense_groups.chinese: 但整个宇宙，正如你可能已经听说的，只有 137.7 亿年的历史。

sense_groups.english: The two age estimates aren't actually in conflict, because there's always some uncertainty.
sense_groups.chinese: 这两个年龄估算实际上并不矛盾，因为总存在一些不确定性。

questions.name: #81 Baby Learning
questions.en:
"Babies come ______ to learn any of the world's languages." Alison Bruderer, a cognitive scientist at the University of British Columbia.
"Which means that no matter where you're growing up in the world, the brains are prepared to pick up the language they're listening to around them."
And listen they do.
But another key factor to discerning a language's particular sounds may be for babies to move their tongues as they listen.
Bruderer and her colleagues tested that notion by sitting 24 sixth-month-olds in front of a video screen and displaying a checkerboard pattern, while they played one of two tracks: a single, repeated "D" sound in Hindi; or two slightly different, alternating "D" sounds.
The idea here is that babies have a short attention span, so novel things hold their gaze.
And indeed, the babies did stare at the screen longer while the alternating "D"s played than for the single "D"—indicating they could detect the novelty.
Until, that is, the researchers blocked the babies' tongue movements by having them suck on a teething device.
Then the effect disappeared, with the babies unable to differentiate ... from ...
And when the babies used a ______ teether that did not block tongue movement, they once again ______ to ______ the difference between the Ds.
The study is in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
So is it time to pull the pacifier?
"At this point I don't think that these data suggest parents should be taking away teething toys or soothers.
The majority of infants are chewing on something semi-regularly throughout the day, and probably not doing it all day and every day.
And most of these infants do go on to develop speech normally." So not to worry.
Bruderer says the ______ might instead offer insight into how ______ with oral motor impairments or cleft palate ______ speech ... now that we know the tongue really does matter, when first learning it.
questions.answer:
1. prepared
2. different
3. appeared
4. comprehend
5. research
6. children
7. perceive

questions.name: #82 Family Gathering
questions.en:
Pop-pop!
It's so good to see you.
How are you?
Man's voice: Good, good.
How are those knees holding up?
And the old ticker?
Man: Fine.
Can't complain.
What ______ are you taking now, Pop?
Have you ever been diagnosed with high-blood pressure?
Kidney disease?
What about asthma?
Any trouble breathing?
Now, can you read the letters on the third line?
Man: E, Uh, M. P?
Taking grandpa's medical history might not seem like the best way to spread warm holiday wishes.
But geneticists at the University of Alabama at ______ note that family gatherings are a great time to learn more about your family's health issues.
Lots of disorders—like diabetes, heart disease, and cancer—have strong roots in your genes.
So it's good to know whether grandma has glaucoma or your mom had a brother who died young of a massive coronary.
That way your docs can screen you for diseases to which you might be susceptible.
Or maybe the info will inspire you to start taking better care of yourself.
Either way, offer the relatives a cup of holiday cheer.
And feel free to note how much they drank.
For your records.

questions.name: #83 Oil Reuse
questions.en:
To keep your car purring, you have to change the oil.
Such maintenance ______ eight billion gallons of used motor oil annually.
Some waste oil does get re-refined to produce oil for lubrication or heating.
And some just gets dumped.
So it would be more environmentally friendly and provide fresh fuel if we could convert the old motor oil to something really valuable: new gasoline.
And that's what a ______ team thinks they've done.
They ______ their work at the annual meeting of the American Chemical Society.
Their approach involves pyrolysis, decomposing organic ______ with heat in the absence of oxygen.
Pyrolysis can break down waste oil into gases, liquids, a little bit of solids.
The gases and liquids can be converted into gas or diesel.
But ______ pyrolysis methods don't do a great job with motor oil.
The new technique mixes the oil with a material really good at absorbing microwave radiation.
Tests showed that heating this mixture with microwaves was about 90 percent efficient at creating precursors to fuel—which beats tossing the oil down the drain.

questions.name: #84 Robot Emotion
questions.en:
Can your heart bleed for a robot?
In two experiments, people reacted to videos where a human appeared to either torture or coddle one of three subjects: another human wearing green, a small green robot, or an ______ green box.
And viewers had a definite emotional ______ to the treatment of the robot.
The work will be presented at the International ______ Association's annual conference.
Forty volunteers watched clips of the robot, which reacted to abuse with upset crying and choking noises and to affection with happy purring and babbling sounds.
Viewers became physically agitated ______ the abusive video, and afterwards they reported a negative emotional response.
In the second experiment 14 people watched the videos while undergoing a functional MRI brain scan.
The scans revealed similar responses when either the robot or the human received affection.
But the human's apparent abuse caused more concern than the robot's.
Understanding our emotional response to robots may help inform the ______ of robotic assistants.
In the meantime, be nice to your Roomba.

questions.name: #85 Bed Bug
questions.en:
City dwellers across the U.S. might agree on one common enemy: bed bugs.
But hey, not to worry, right?
"Bed bugs are not known to spread diseases, but bites can be very itchy and irritating." Or so says the New York City Department of Health.
But that assertion may not be true.
Because a new study suggests bed bugs could be capable of spreading infection… specifically, by passing on the parasite that causes Chagas disease.
Chagas can cause anything from mild headaches to eventual heart failure.
The condition is usually spread by what's called the kissing bug—a relative of bedbugs, which also feeds on blood.
But it doesn't pass the parasite through its saliva, as happens with malaria, for example.
"You get it when the bug bites you and then ______ on you.
The parasite is in the feces of the bug." Michael Levy, a disease ecologist at the ______ of Pennsylvania.
Levy says scratching the bite then works the parasite into the skin, ______ the victim.
Levy and his colleagues wanted to see if the same thing could happen with bed bugs.
So they let em loose on mice that carried the Tripanosoma cruzi parasite.
The bugs caught it—and were then able to ______ the parasite back to mice.
With one caveat—some mice actually hunted and ate the bugs—a sure route for infection.
"People don't eat bed bugs, so we're not really at risk of being infected through the oral route by bed bugs." That said, one mouse actually did catch the disease not by snacking, but through a bedbug bite—more analogous to the way a human might.
The study is in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene.
Any advice for the bed bug-phobic?
"Don't panic.
It's important to remember that bed bugs may be able to carry the disease, but they don't cause it." Meaning, you'd need to live with someone with Chagas disease, who can pass the parasite to a bed bug, and then actually catch it from that bug.
Still, Levy says, bugs pave the way for pathogens to spread.
"It's very dangerous to let bugs that feed on human blood get out of control, like unfortunately has ______ in the United States and across the world with bed bugs." Maybe it's time to treat bed bugs like a public health issue, Levy says, rather than just a pest.

Levy and his colleagues wanted to see if the same thing could happen with bed bugs.
So they let em loose on mice that carried the Tripanosoma cruzi parasite.
The bugs caught it—and were then able to ______ the parasite back to mice.
With one caveat—some mice actually hunted and ate the bugs—a sure route for infection.
"People don't eat bed bugs, so we're not really at risk of being infected through the oral route by bed bugs." That said, one mouse actually did catch the disease not by snacking, but through a bedbug bite—more analogous to the way a human might.
The study is in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene.
Any advice for the bed bug-phobic?
"Don't panic.
It's important to remember that bed bugs may be able to carry the disease, but they don't cause it." Meaning, you'd need to live with someone with Chagas disease, who can pass the parasite to a bed bug, and then actually catch it from that bug.
Still, Levy says, bugs pave the way for pathogens to spread.
"It's very dangerous to let bugs that feed on human blood get out of control, like unfortunately has ______ in the United States and across the world with bed bugs." Maybe it's time to treat bed bugs like a public health issue, Levy says, rather than just a pest.

答案:
1. defecates
2. University
3. infecting
4. transmit
5. happened

sense_groups.english: City dwellers across the U.S. might agree on one common enemy: bed bugs.
sense_groups.chinese: 全美国的城市居民可能都同意一个共同的敌人：臭虫。

sense_groups.english: But hey, not to worry, right?
sense_groups.chinese: 但是，嘿，别担心，对吧？

sense_groups.english: "Bed bugs are not known to spread diseases, but bites can be very itchy and irritating."
sense_groups.chinese: “臭虫已知不会传播疾病，但叮咬会非常痒和刺激。”

sense_groups.english: Or so says the New York City Department of Health.
sense_groups.chinese: 纽约市卫生局是这么说的。

sense_groups.english: But that assertion may not be true.
sense_groups.chinese: 但这个说法可能不对。

sense_groups.english: Because a new study suggests bed bugs could be capable of spreading infection…
sense_groups.chinese: 因为一项新研究表明臭虫可能能够传播感染……

sense_groups.english: specifically, by passing on the parasite that causes Chagas disease.
sense_groups.chinese: 具体来说，是通过传播引起恰加斯病的寄生虫。

sense_groups.english: Chagas can cause anything from mild headaches to eventual heart failure.
sense_groups.chinese: 恰加斯病可以引起从轻微头痛到最终心力衰竭的各种症状。

sense_groups.english: The condition is usually spread by what's called the kissing bug—
sense_groups.chinese: 这种病通常由所谓的亲吻虫传播——

sense_groups.english: a relative of bedbugs, which also feeds on blood.
sense_groups.chinese: 它是臭虫的近亲，也以血液为食。

sense_groups.english: But it doesn't pass the parasite through its saliva, as happens with malaria, for example.
sense_groups.chinese: 但它不像疟疾那样通过唾液传播寄生虫。

sense_groups.english: "You get it when the bug bites you and then defecates on you.
sense_groups.chinese: “当虫子咬你然后在你身上排便时，你就会感染。

sense_groups.english: The parasite is in the feces of the bug."
sense_groups.chinese: 寄生虫在虫子的粪便里。”

sense_groups.english: Michael Levy, a disease ecologist at the University of Pennsylvania.
sense_groups.chinese: 宾夕法尼亚大学的疾病生态学家迈克尔·利维说。

sense_groups.english: Levy says scratching the bite then works the parasite into the skin, infecting the victim.
sense_groups.chinese: 利维说，抓挠叮咬处会把寄生虫弄进皮肤，感染受害者。

sense_groups.english: Levy and his colleagues wanted to see if the same thing could happen with bed bugs.
sense_groups.chinese: 利维和他的同事想看看臭虫是否也会发生同样的情况。

sense_groups.english: So they let em loose on mice that carried the Tripanosoma cruzi parasite.
sense_groups.chinese: 于是他们让臭虫去叮咬携带克氏锥虫寄生虫的老鼠。

sense_groups.english: The bugs caught it—and were then able to transmit the parasite back to mice.
sense_groups.chinese: 臭虫感染了寄生虫，然后能够将寄生虫传回给老鼠。

sense_groups.english: With one caveat—some mice actually hunted and ate the bugs—a sure route for infection.
sense_groups.chinese: 有一个警告——有些老鼠实际上捕食并吃掉了臭虫——这是一个确定的感染途径。

sense_groups.english: "People don't eat bed bugs, so we're not really at risk of being infected through the oral route by bed bugs."
sense_groups.chinese: “人们不吃臭虫，所以我们实际上没有通过口腔途径被臭虫感染的风险。”

sense_groups.english: That said, one mouse actually did catch the disease not by snacking, but through a bedbug bite—
sense_groups.chinese: 尽管如此，有一只老鼠实际上并不是通过吃臭虫，而是通过臭虫叮咬感染了这种病——

sense_groups.english: more analogous to the way a human might.
sense_groups.chinese: 这更类似于人类可能感染的方式。

sense_groups.english: The study is in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《美国热带医学与卫生杂志》上。

sense_groups.english: Any advice for the bed bug-phobic?
sense_groups.chinese: 对害怕臭虫的人有什么建议吗？

sense_groups.english: "Don't panic.
sense_groups.chinese: “别慌。

sense_groups.english: It's important to remember that bed bugs may be able to carry the disease, but they don't cause it."
sense_groups.chinese: 重要的是要记住，臭虫可能携带这种疾病，但它们不会引起这种疾病。”

sense_groups.english: Meaning, you'd need to live with someone with Chagas disease, who can pass the parasite to a bed bug, and then actually catch it from that bug.
sense_groups.chinese: 意思是，你需要和恰加斯病患者住在一起，他可以把寄生虫传给臭虫，然后你才能真正从那只臭虫那里感染。

sense_groups.english: Still, Levy says, bugs pave the way for pathogens to spread.
sense_groups.chinese: 不过，利维说，虫子为病原体的传播铺平了道路。

sense_groups.english: "It's very dangerous to let bugs that feed on human blood get out of control, like unfortunately has happened in the United States and across the world with bed bugs."
sense_groups.chinese: “让以人类血液为食的虫子失控是非常危险的，就像不幸在美国和世界各地发生的臭虫问题一样。”

sense_groups.english: Maybe it's time to treat bed bugs like a public health issue, Levy says, rather than just a pest.
sense_groups.chinese: 利维说，也许是时候把臭虫当作一个公共卫生问题，而不仅仅是一种害虫来对待了。

questions.name: #86 Climbing Stairs
questions.en:
Not taking the elevator is a good way to sneak in a little extra ______ every day.
And if you do get some of your exercise ______ elevators, here's a burning question: do you burn more ______ climbing stairs one at a time or bounding up them two at a time?
To find out, researchers had subjects climb stairs reaching 46 feet high.
Based on the subjects' heart rate measurements, the researchers ______ calories burned.
They found that ______ who took the stairs two at a time had a higher rate of energy expenditure over the 86 steps they climbed—but those who climbed one at a time burned more energy in total over the entire staircase.
The study is in the journal PLoS One.
It makes sense.
Although the bounders had a more intense workout, the one-steppers take longer to get to the top.
So even though they're burning fewer calories per minute than the bounders do, they work out enough longer to burn more total calories.
And one step or two, there's never a wait for the stairs.
questions.full:

And one step or two, there's never a wait for the stairs.

sense_groups.english: Not taking the elevator is a good way to sneak in a little extra exercise every day.
sense_groups.chinese: 不坐电梯是每天偷偷多锻炼一点的好方法。

sense_groups.english: And if you do get some of your exercise avoiding elevators, here's a burning question: do you burn more calories climbing stairs one at a time or bounding up them two at a time?
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你确实通过不坐电梯来锻炼，这里有个紧迫的问题：一次一阶地爬楼梯和一次两阶地跳着上，哪种方式消耗更多卡路里？

sense_groups.english: To find out, researchers had subjects climb stairs reaching 46 feet high.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了找出答案，研究人员让受试者爬46英尺高的楼梯。

sense_groups.english: Based on the subjects' heart rate measurements, the researchers estimated calories burned.
sense_groups.chinese: 根据受试者的心率测量结果，研究人员估计了消耗的卡路里。

sense_groups.english: They found that volunteers who took the stairs two at a time had a higher rate of energy expenditure over the 86 steps they climbed—but those who climbed one at a time burned more energy in total over the entire staircase.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现，一次两阶爬楼梯的志愿者在爬86级台阶时能量消耗率更高——但那些一次一阶爬的人在整段楼梯上消耗的总能量更多。

sense_groups.english: The study is in the journal PLoS One.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《公共科学图书馆·综合》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: It makes sense.
sense_groups.chinese: 这说得通。

sense_groups.english: Although the bounders had a more intense workout, the one-steppers take longer to get to the top.
sense_groups.chinese: 虽然跳着上的人锻炼强度更大，但一次一阶的人需要更长时间才能到达顶部。

sense_groups.english: So even though they're burning fewer calories per minute than the bounders do, they work out enough longer to burn more total calories.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以，尽管他们每分钟消耗的卡路里比跳着上的人少，但他们锻炼的时间足够长，从而消耗了更多的总卡路里。

sense_groups.english: And one step or two, there's never a wait for the stairs.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且，不管是一次一阶还是两阶，楼梯从来不需要排队等候。

questions.name: #87 Pythons
questions.en:
Here's another reason to stop global warming: to keep the Burmese pythons in Florida.
Burmese pythons have been turning up in south Florida in recent years.
Perhaps you've seen the famous photo of a python ripped apart by its efforts to ingest a large alligator.
Apparently people with pythons as pets have been getting rid of the snakes when they get too big by dumping them in the Everglades.
And in 2003, biologists confirmed the presence of a breeding population of the slithering serpents in Everglades National Park.
Which skeeves me out, because I spend a lot of time there.
I'm not afraid of timid alligators, but hungry Burmese pythons give me the willies.
Anyway, the US ______ Survey recently did an analysis of ______ temperatures around the country by the end of this century.
And then analyzed where Burmese pythons would be comfortable, based on their home territory, from ______ to Indonesia.
The result: pythons could colonize a third of the US.
Did I mention that they can be over 20 feet long and 250 pounds?
Might be the best motivation to do ______ about climate change.

sense_groups.english: Here's another reason to stop global warming:
sense_groups.chinese: 这是阻止全球变暖的另一个理由：

sense_groups.chinese: 把缅甸蟒留在佛罗里达。

sense_groups.english: Burmese pythons have been turning up in south Florida in recent years.
sense_groups.chinese: 近年来，缅甸蟒不断出现在南佛罗里达。

sense_groups.english: Perhaps you've seen the famous photo of a python ripped apart by its efforts to ingest a large alligator.
sense_groups.chinese: 也许你见过那张著名的照片：一条蟒蛇因试图吞下一只大鳄鱼而把自己撑裂。

sense_groups.english: Apparently people with pythons as pets have been getting rid of the snakes when they get too big by dumping them in the Everglades.
sense_groups.chinese: 显然，养蟒蛇当宠物的人会在它们长得太大时，把它们丢弃在大沼泽地。

sense_groups.english: And in 2003, biologists confirmed the presence of a breeding population of the slithering serpents in Everglades National Park.
sense_groups.chinese: 2003年，生物学家确认大沼泽地国家公园存在一个繁殖中的蛇群。

sense_groups.english: And then analyzed where Burmese pythons would be comfortable, based on their home territory, from Pakistan to Indonesia.

questions.name: #89 Vegetables and Fertility
questions.en:
Guys, here's another reason to eat your veggies: they might be good for your sperm.
Some studies show that male fertility and what's called seminal quality have ______ over the last few decades.
So ______ from two fertility clinics in Spain looked at the reproductive power of fruits and vegetables.
The scientists have spent the past four years analyzing diet and possible exposure to workplace contaminants in men with fertility problems.
One effort examined the effects that antioxidants might have on sperm.

sense_groups.english: Guys, here's another reason to eat your veggies:
sense_groups.chinese: 伙计们，吃蔬菜的另一个理由是：

sense_groups.english: they might be good for your sperm.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们可能对你的精子有好处。

sense_groups.english: Some studies show that male fertility and what's called seminal quality have declined over the last few decades.
sense_groups.chinese: 一些研究表明，男性生育能力和所谓的精液质量在过去几十年里有所下降。

sense_groups.english: So researchers from two fertility clinics in Spain looked at the reproductive power of fruits and vegetables.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，西班牙两家生育诊所的研究人员研究了水果和蔬菜的生殖能力。
