sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们花了四年时间分析有生育问题的男性的饮食和可能接触的工作场所污染物。

sense_groups.english: One effort examined the effects that antioxidants might have on sperm.
sense_groups.chinese: 一项研究考察了抗氧化剂可能对精子产生的影响。

sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员假设抗氧化剂可以降低可能损害精子的氧化应激。

sense_groups.chinese: 该研究招募了61名来自有生育问题夫妇的男性。

sense_groups.chinese: 其中30名男性被发现有精子问题。

Some 75,000 genes have been mapped.

sense_groups.english: Wheat helped create ______ in the Middle East.

sense_groups.english: Instead, an international consortium devised another strategy, involving physically mapping individual ______ and chromosome arms.

sense_groups.english: Here's one way bats might get their next meal:

sense_groups.chinese: 苍蝇通常在蝙蝠的领地里保持安静，

questions.name: #92 Energy Effeciency
questions.en:
Most of us know we should rein in our energy use.
But to be successful, it'd help if we knew the best way to do it.
So scientists asked more than 500 people, "What's the most ______ thing you can do to conserve energy?" The results were illuminating.
More than half the ______ focused on conservation by curtailment: ______ off the lights, changing thermostat ______ and driving less.
Only 12 percent went for efficiency: using compact fluorescent bulbs, insulating the house or driving a hybrid car.
But scientists say that it's actually these moves that yield the bigger energy savings.
The results appear in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
The study authors think that a big factor is that curtailment is easier to imagine doing—while efforts to improve ______ would involve, for example, doing research about new appliances or cars, and spending money up front to buy them.
But if people knew more about the actual energy requirements of their activities versus the savings available through efficiency, they might be spurred to act.
To quote physicist and energy expert Arthur Rosenfeld: "Energy efficiency is like a Saudi Arabia under our cities."
questions.full:
Most of us know we should rein in our energy use.
But to be successful, it'd help if we knew the best way to do it.
So scientists asked more than 500 people, "What's the most ______ thing you can do to conserve energy?" The results were illuminating.
More than half the ______ focused on conservation by curtailment: ______ off the lights, changing thermostat ______ and driving less.
Only 12 percent went for efficiency: using compact fluorescent bulbs, insulating the house or driving a hybrid car.
But scientists say that it's actually these moves that yield the bigger energy savings.
The results appear in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
The study authors think that a big factor is that curtailment is easier to imagine doing—while efforts to improve ______ would involve, for example, doing research about new appliances or cars, and spending money up front to buy them.
But if people knew more about the actual energy requirements of their activities versus the savings available through efficiency, they might be spurred to act.
To quote physicist and energy expert Arthur Rosenfeld: "Energy efficiency is like a Saudi Arabia under our cities."

答案:
1. effective
2. participants
3. switching
4. settings
5. efficiency

sense_groups.english: Most of us know we should rein in our energy use.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们大多数人都知道应该控制能源使用。

sense_groups.english: But to be successful, it'd help if we knew the best way to do it.
sense_groups.chinese: 但要成功，知道最佳方法会有所帮助。

sense_groups.english: So scientists asked more than 500 people, "What's the most effective thing you can do to conserve energy?"
sense_groups.chinese: 于是科学家询问了500多人：“你能做的最有效的节能措施是什么？”

sense_groups.english: The results were illuminating.
sense_groups.chinese: 结果令人深思。

sense_groups.english: More than half the participants focused on conservation by curtailment: switching off the lights, changing thermostat settings and driving less.
sense_groups.chinese: 超过一半的参与者关注通过缩减来节能：关灯、调节恒温器设置和减少开车。

sense_groups.english: Only 12 percent went for efficiency: using compact fluorescent bulbs, insulating the house or driving a hybrid car.
sense_groups.chinese: 只有12%的人选择效率：使用节能灯泡、给房屋隔热或开混合动力车。

sense_groups.english: But scientists say that it's actually these moves that yield the bigger energy savings.
sense_groups.chinese: 但科学家表示，实际上这些举措能带来更大的节能效果。

sense_groups.english: The results appear in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究结果发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。

sense_groups.english: The study authors think that a big factor is that curtailment is easier to imagine doing—while efforts to improve efficiency would involve, for example, doing research about new appliances or cars, and spending money up front to buy them.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究作者认为，一个重要因素是缩减更容易想象实施——而提高效率的努力则涉及，例如，研究新电器或汽车，并预先花钱购买它们。

sense_groups.english: But if people knew more about the actual energy requirements of their activities versus the savings available through efficiency, they might be spurred to act.
sense_groups.chinese: 但如果人们更了解自己活动的实际能源需求与通过效率可获得的节省，他们可能会受到激励而行动。

sense_groups.english: To quote physicist and energy expert Arthur Rosenfeld: "Energy efficiency is like a Saudi Arabia under our cities."
sense_groups.chinese: 引用物理学家和能源专家阿瑟·罗森菲尔德的话：“能源效率就像我们城市地下的沙特阿拉伯。”

questions.name: #93 Accelerating Expansion
questions.en:
The 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics goes to Saul Perlmutter at the Lawrence Berkeley ______ Lab, Brian Schmidt at the Australian National Lab and Adam Reiss at Johns Hopkins.

sense_groups.english: The 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics goes to Saul Perlmutter at the Lawrence Berkeley National Lab, Brian Schmidt at the Australian National Lab and Adam Reiss at Johns Hopkins.
sense_groups.chinese: 2011年诺贝尔物理学奖授予劳伦斯伯克利国家实验室的索尔·珀尔马特、澳大利亚国家实验室的布莱恩·施密特和约翰·霍普金斯大学的亚当·里斯。

sense_groups.english: The Royal Swedish Academy's Olga Botner:
sense_groups.chinese: 瑞典皇家科学院的奥尔加·博特纳说：

sense_groups.english: "In a universe which is dominated by matter, one would expect gravity eventually should make the expansion slow down.
sense_groups.chinese: “在一个由物质主导的宇宙中，人们会预期引力最终会使膨胀减速。

sense_groups.english: Imagine then the utter astonishment when two groups of scientists headed by this year's Nobel laureates in 1998 discovered that the expansion was not slowing down, it was actually accelerating.
sense_groups.chinese: 想象一下，当由今年诺贝尔奖得主领导的两个科学家团队在1998年发现膨胀并没有减速，反而在加速时，他们是多么震惊。

sense_groups.english: By comparing the brightness of distant, far-away supernovae with the brightness of nearby supernovae, the scientists discovered that the far-away supernovae were about 25 percent too faint.
sense_groups.chinese: 通过比较遥远超新星的亮度与附近超新星的亮度，科学家们发现遥远超新星大约暗了25%。

sense_groups.english: They were too far away.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们太远了。

sense_groups.english: The universe was accelerating.
sense_groups.chinese: 宇宙在加速。

sense_groups.english: And so this discovery is fundamental and a milestone for cosmology.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，这一发现是基础性的，也是宇宙学的里程碑。

sense_groups.english: And a challenge for generations of scientists to come."
sense_groups.chinese: 也是对未来几代科学家的挑战。”

questions.name: #94 Bacteria and Oxygen
questions.en:
Once upon a time, our ______ was a little thin on oxygen.
Like, there wasn't any.
Then, about three billion years ago, a handful of ______ figured out how to harvest the energy from ______ to make themselves some food.
In the process, they consumed carbon dioxide, and gave off oxygen.
So the air filled with oxygen, and all was right with the world.
If you've ever taken an intro biology course, you've no doubt heard the tale.
Photosynthetic bacteria are the heroes who brought oxygen to our planet.
But maybe there's more to the story than that.
Because in the online issue of Nature Geoscience, researchers from ______ say: the bacteria didn't act alone.
The ______ looked at ______ oxygen levels throughout Earth's history.
And they found that the amount of oxygen in the air spiked each time smaller land masses collided to form a supercontinent, like Pangea.
These massive pile-ups generated mountain chains, and as the mountains eroded, they released nutrients into the oceans, feeding the photosynthetic bacteria.
So the young Earth and its inhabitants worked ______ to produce a planet where you can really find inspiration.
questions.answer:
1. atmosphere
2. bacteria
3. sunlight
4. Australia
5. scientists
6. atmospheric
7. together

sense_groups.english: Once upon a time, our atmosphere was a little thin on oxygen.
sense_groups.chinese: 从前，我们的大气层氧气有点稀薄。

sense_groups.english: Like, there wasn't any.
sense_groups.chinese: 就像，根本没有氧气。

sense_groups.english: Then, about three billion years ago, a handful of bacteria figured out how to harvest the energy from sunlight to make themselves some food.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后，大约三十亿年前，一些细菌弄明白了如何从阳光中获取能量来为自己制造食物。

sense_groups.english: In the process, they consumed carbon dioxide, and gave off oxygen.
sense_groups.chinese: 在这个过程中，它们消耗二氧化碳，释放氧气。

sense_groups.english: So the air filled with oxygen, and all was right with the world.
sense_groups.chinese: 于是空气中充满了氧气，世界变得美好。

sense_groups.english: If you've ever taken an intro biology course, you've no doubt heard the tale.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你上过生物学入门课程，你肯定听过这个故事。

sense_groups.english: Photosynthetic bacteria are the heroes who brought oxygen to our planet.
sense_groups.chinese: 光合细菌是将氧气带到我们星球的英雄。

sense_groups.english: But maybe there's more to the story than that.
sense_groups.chinese: 但也许这个故事还有更多内容。

sense_groups.english: Because in the online issue of Nature Geoscience, researchers from Australia say: the bacteria didn't act alone.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为在《自然·地球科学》的网络版上，来自澳大利亚的研究人员说：这些细菌并非单独行动。

sense_groups.english: The scientists looked at atmospheric oxygen levels throughout Earth's history.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们研究了地球历史上大气氧气的水平。

sense_groups.english: And they found that the amount of oxygen in the air spiked each time smaller land masses collided to form a supercontinent, like Pangea.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现，每当较小的陆地碰撞形成超级大陆（如盘古大陆）时，空气中的氧气含量就会激增。

sense_groups.english: These massive pile-ups generated mountain chains, and as the mountains eroded, they released nutrients into the oceans, feeding the photosynthetic bacteria.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些巨大的碰撞产生了山脉，随着山脉的侵蚀，它们向海洋释放了营养物质，滋养了光合细菌。

sense_groups.english: So the young Earth and its inhabitants worked together to produce a planet where you can really find inspiration.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以，年轻的地球和它的居民共同努力，创造了一个真正能让你找到灵感的星球。

sense_groups.chinese: 为了弄清这一点，加拿大达尔豪西大学临床心理学专业的学生马克·佩特决定对几只狗狗撒个小谎。

sense_groups.english: In his experiment, dogs were shown two covered containers.
sense_groups.chinese: 在他的实验中，狗狗们看到两个盖着的容器。

sense_groups.english: One held a treat.
sense_groups.chinese: 一个里面放着零食。

sense_groups.english: The other: nothing but disappointment.
sense_groups.chinese: 另一个：只有失望。

sense_groups.english: In half the trials, a helpful trainer stood behind and pointed to the container holding the treat.
sense_groups.chinese: 在一半的试验中，一位友善的训练员站在后面，指向放着零食的容器。

sense_groups.english: In the other half, a deceptive trainer pointed to the empty container.
sense_groups.chinese: 在另一半试验中，一位欺骗性的训练员指向空容器。

sense_groups.english: The results?
sense_groups.chinese: 结果呢？

sense_groups.english: The dogs approached the honest trainer a little more often than they did the deceiver.
sense_groups.chinese: 狗狗们靠近诚实训练员的次数比靠近欺骗者稍多一些。

sense_groups.english: But not enough to conclude that the pups had figured out that one of the guys was pulling their leg.
sense_groups.chinese: 但不足以得出结论，认为狗狗们已经明白其中一个人在戏弄它们。

sense_groups.english: So dogs may be able to sniff out bombs.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以，狗狗或许能嗅出炸弹。

sense_groups.english: But they can't pick up the smell of mendacity.
sense_groups.chinese: 但它们闻不出谎言的味道。

questions.name: #101 Killer Bee
questions.en:
Unless you're talking about killer bees, it's hard to imagine a situation in which "killers" and "bees" would be related.
But it turns out that ______ are using the same mathematical model to ______ the behavior of both bumblebees and human serial killers.
The method, called geographic profiling, was developed by a detective who was trying to predict where serial killers might live based on where they commit their crimes.
Believe it or not, murderers operate fairly close to home.
But not too close.
They ______ a kind of kill-free "buffer zone" around their actual digs.
A similar pattern of activity seems to hold true for bumblebees—when they're ______ for food.
Bees tend to avoid stopping at flowers too close to home, perhaps to reduce the risk of drawing predators, parasites or nosy scientists to the nest.
And working with the former detective, scientists in the U.K. found that geographic profiling allowed them to ______ the entrance to a hive based on mapping which flowers the bees visit.
The results appear online in the Journal of the Royal Society Interface.
Repeating such experiments, with bees or other foraging critters, could help hone the model for catching criminals.

The results appear online in the Journal of the Royal Society Interface.
Repeating such experiments, with bees or other foraging critters, could help hone the model for catching criminals.

1. scientists
2. describe
3. maintain
4. foraging
5. locate

sense_groups.chinese: 但事实证明，科学家们正在用同样的数学模型来描述大黄蜂和人类连环杀手的行为。

sense_groups.english: The method, called geographic profiling, was developed by a detective who was trying to predict where serial killers might live based on where they commit their crimes.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种方法叫做地理画像，是由一位侦探开发的，他试图根据连环杀手作案的地点来预测他们可能住在哪里。

sense_groups.english: Believe it or not, murderers operate fairly close to home.
sense_groups.chinese: 信不信由你，凶手通常会在离家很近的地方作案。

sense_groups.english: But not too close.
sense_groups.chinese: 但也不会太近。

sense_groups.english: They maintain a kind of kill-free 'buffer zone' around their actual digs.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们会在自己的住所周围保留一个没有杀人的‘缓冲区’。

sense_groups.english: A similar pattern of activity seems to hold true for bumblebees—when they're foraging for food.
sense_groups.chinese: 大黄蜂似乎也有类似的活动模式——当它们觅食时。

sense_groups.english: Bees tend to avoid stopping at flowers too close to home, perhaps to reduce the risk of drawing predators, parasites or nosy scientists to the nest.
sense_groups.chinese: 蜜蜂往往会避免在离家太近的花朵上停留，可能是为了降低将捕食者、寄生虫或好事科学家引到蜂巢的风险。

sense_groups.chinese: 与这位前侦探合作，英国的科学家发现，地理画像使他们能够根据蜜蜂访问花朵的分布图来定位蜂巢入口。

sense_groups.chinese: 研究结果发表在《皇家学会界面杂志》的在线版上。

sense_groups.english: Repeating such experiments, with bees or other foraging critters, could help hone the model for catching criminals.
sense_groups.chinese: 用蜜蜂或其他觅食生物重复此类实验，可能有助于完善抓捕罪犯的模型。

In trials, the paper tests competed with conventional methods at ______ concentrations.
The ______ is now spinning off a company to develop the technology.

questions.name: #103 Budget Bill
questions.en:
In last week's pre-Christmas rush, the U.S. Congress slammed together the $1-trillion federal budget bill for 2015, just before funds ran out.
But the bill wasn't all about the money.
Congress took advantage of the fiscal scramble to change rules about the environment and energy, which do not belong in appropriation bills.
Normally such changes are encoded in what are called "laws," and are debated out in the open.
But the budget bill is a chance for Congress to slip in controversial rules—called riders—without much debate.
If members object, the bill stalls, and the government shuts down—and no one wants to be blamed for that fiasco.
So the riders gallop in.
The Environmental Protection Agency got its budget, for instance, but with strings attached: although agriculture is a major source of atmospheric methane, the EPA now is ______ from using its money to require farmers to report greenhouse gas emissions.
And the agency cannot regulate farm ponds and irrigation ditches under the Clean Water Act.
In another example, the Department of ______ must speed up permits for companies making genetically ______ organisms.
And the feds must loan money to firms to build coal-fired power plants overseas.
That requirement ______ a previous ban.
These rules and others last through September 2015, when this budget bill runs out.
And then, if history is any guide, the whole stealth legislation process will start all over again.
questions.full:
In last week's pre-Christmas rush, the U.S. Congress slammed together the $1-trillion federal budget bill for 2015, just before funds ran out.
But the bill wasn't all about the money.
Congress took advantage of the fiscal scramble to change rules about the environment and energy, which do not belong in appropriation bills.

sense_groups.english: In last week's pre-Christmas rush, the U.S. Congress slammed together the $1-trillion federal budget bill for 2015, just before funds ran out.
sense_groups.chinese: 在上周圣诞前的匆忙中，美国国会赶在资金耗尽前拼凑出了2015年1万亿美元的联邦预算案。

sense_groups.english: But the bill wasn't all about the money.
sense_groups.chinese: 但该法案并不全是关于钱。

sense_groups.english: Congress took advantage of the fiscal scramble to change rules about the environment and energy, which do not belong in appropriation bills.
sense_groups.chinese: 国会利用财政混乱来修改环境和能源规则，而这些规则本不属于拨款法案。

sense_groups.english: Normally such changes are encoded in what are called 'laws,' and are debated out in the open.
sense_groups.chinese: 通常，这类修改会被编入所谓的“法律”，并在公开场合进行辩论。

sense_groups.english: But the budget bill is a chance for Congress to slip in controversial rules—called riders—without much debate.
sense_groups.chinese: 但预算案是国会悄悄加入有争议规则（称为附加条款）的机会，无需太多辩论。

sense_groups.chinese: 这一要求______了之前的禁令。

sense_groups.english: And then, if history is any guide, the whole stealth legislation process will start all over again.

questions.name: #104 Origin of Species
questions.en:
November 24th marks the 150th anniversary of the publication of Darwin's Origin of Species.
On ______ 19th, a guy named Ray Comfort, who does not accept evolution, will celebrate the fact that when ______ expire and works enter the public domain you're free to do with them what you will.
Thus Comfort will be distributing his own edition of Darwin's masterwork, with a new introduction.
This is roughly the equivalent of me ______ on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel so as to improve the work.
According to the folks at the National Center for Science Education, the NCSE, who monitor efforts to interfere with evolution education in public schools, Comfort in his intro repeats numerous familiar ______ claims.
For example, that there's a lack of transitional fossils and that the second law of thermodynamics makes evolution impossible.
These assertions have been disproved more often than the chant "Yankees suck".

For example, that there's a lack of transitional fossils and that the second law of thermodynamics makes evolution impossible.
These assertions have been disproved more often than the chant "Yankees suck".

答案:
1. November
2. copyrights
3. fingerpainting
4. anti-evolution

sense_groups.english: November 24th marks the 150th anniversary of the publication of Darwin's Origin of Species.
sense_groups.chinese: 11月24日是达尔文《物种起源》出版150周年纪念日。

sense_groups.english: On November 19th, a guy named Ray Comfort, who does not accept evolution, will celebrate the fact that when copyrights expire and works enter the public domain you're free to do with them what you will.
sense_groups.chinese: 11月19日，一个名叫雷·康福特、不接受进化论的人，将庆祝版权到期、作品进入公有领域后你可以自由处理它们这一事实。

sense_groups.english: Thus Comfort will be distributing his own edition of Darwin's masterwork, with a new introduction.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，康福特将分发他自己版本的达尔文杰作，并附有一篇新的引言。

sense_groups.english: This is roughly the equivalent of me fingerpainting on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel so as to improve the work.
sense_groups.chinese: 这大致相当于我在西斯廷教堂的天花板上用手指画画，以改进那幅作品。

sense_groups.english: According to the folks at the National Center for Science Education, the NCSE, who monitor efforts to interfere with evolution education in public schools, Comfort in his intro repeats numerous familiar anti-evolution claims.
sense_groups.chinese: 据国家科学教育中心（NCSE）的人士说，该中心监控着干扰公立学校进化论教育的努力，康福特在他的引言中重复了许多熟悉的反对进化论的说法。

sense_groups.english: For example, that there's a lack of transitional fossils and that the second law of thermodynamics makes evolution impossible.
sense_groups.chinese: 例如，缺乏过渡化石，以及热力学第二定律使进化不可能。

sense_groups.english: These assertions have been disproved more often than the chant "Yankees suck".
sense_groups.chinese: 这些断言被驳斥的次数比“洋基队烂”的喊声还要多。

questions.name: #105 Operations Research
questions.en:
The ______ ______ problem is a ______ math conundrum: if a salesman has to visit a bunch of cities, how do you get him to all of them once via the ______ possible route.
But the traveling salesman's predicament pales in ______ to figuring out the best ways to get four-man crews of umpires to every major league baseball game.
A research team attacked the problem for the last few years.
Their solution appears in Interfaces.
It's a journal of operations research.
In addition to minimizing travel, here are some of the umpire constraints.
Crews should visit each MLB city at least once.
They should work each team at home and on the road.
They should not work more than 21 days in a row.
They should not ump any one team's games for more than four series all year.
There are plenty more.
The researchers first had to develop the question, dubbed the "traveling umpire problem." They used ______ computation and heuristics for their solutions.
The result was good enough for Major League Baseball to adopt the last three seasons.
Previously, a former umpire made the schedule.
That guy is out.
questions.answer:
1. traveling
2. salesman
3. favorite
4. shortest
5. comparison
6. brute-force

sense_groups.english: It's a journal of operations research.

sense_groups.english: Crews should visit each MLB city at least once.
sense_groups.chinese: 每个裁判组应至少访问每个MLB城市一次。

sense_groups.english: They should work each team at home and on the road.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们应在每支球队的主场和客场执裁。

sense_groups.english: They should not work more than 21 days in a row.

sense_groups.english: They should not ump any one team's games for more than four series all year.

sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员首先必须定义这个问题，称为“旅行裁判问题”。

sense_groups.english: The result was good enough for Major League Baseball to adopt the last three seasons.
sense_groups.chinese: 结果足够好，美国职业棒球大联盟在过去三个赛季中采用了它。

questions.name: #107 Garbage Patches
questions.en:
There are now at least five major garbage patches in the world's oceans, and much of that trash is plastic.
But last month ______ said they can only account for one percent of the plastic they'd expect to find in the oceans.
So, where'd the rest of it go?
Well, animals eat some of it.
Plastic has been found in turtles, seabirds, fish, plankton, shellfish, even ______ invertebrates.
But there's another way sea creatures might be accumulating plastic: by sucking up tiny plastic ______ with their siphons and gills.
  ______ added common shore crabs—Carcinus maenas—to tanks of seawater containing millions of tiny plastic particles, just 10 microns in diameter.
After 16 hours, all the crabs had plastic lodged in their gills.
And the particles stuck around for up to three weeks, too.
The results are in the journal Environmental Science and Technology.
The longer plastic sits in an animal, researchers say, the better the chances it will travel up the food chain.
Meaning all our plastic waste could come back to bite us—or rather be bitten by us.
"Of course we eat mussels whole, without the shells.
But we're ______ eating plastic, if they're from a site where there's plastic present." Lead researcher Andrew Watts, of the University of Exeter.
"We don't know how much plastic we have in our stomachs… chances are we do have some."

questions.name: #108 Baby Meaning
questions.en:
Babies sometimes laugh and sometimes cry.
It doesn't take a genius to decode the meaning of these sounds.
But it isn't quite as straightforward to ______ the meaning, if any, of an infant's babbles.
And humans a little older can make the same sounds regardless of how you actually feel—you're able to say "I'm hungry" whether you're ravenous or just gorged yourself.
Scientists think that the ability to make the same sounds across a range of emotional states is critical to language development.
They also believe it to be uniquely human, because in previous studies of animal communication, researchers only observed fixed vocalizations.
For example, bonobo chimpanzee pant-laughs and threat barks are tied to a specific emotion or behavior.
But the new study finds ______ that bonobos in the wild are also capable of flexible vocalizations.
Bonobos have a specific call type, a "peep" that they use independent of emotional context.
They peep while eating, traveling, grooming, resting, engaging in sexual activity, and even during shows of aggression.
Because peeps, like a baby's babbles, don't convey meaningful information on their own, bonobos need to combine them with other calls and environmental context to supply meaning.
Previously, researchers thought this type of complex, language-like comprehension was unique to humans.
The study is in the journal PeerJ.
Bonobos are our closest evolutionary relatives, so it's ______ that the functional flexibility of human speech appeared in a common ancestor.
This discovery adds to the growing pile of evidence that we're not quite as special as we've long believed—and that our furry cousins may be even closer to us than we thought.

questions.name: #109 Sharks
questions.en:
They're called ______ sharks.
But perhaps thrasher is more accurate.
Because a population of these fearsome predators was spotted engaging in an unusual hunting strategy.
Forget jaws—try the other end.
  ______ observed them slapping their long, scythe-like tails at high speeds through the water.
These whaps stunned or killed several smaller fish with each strike.
The observations were made off the coast of the Philippines.
Killer whales and dolphins also may use a similar tail-slapping strategy.
But this is the first time the behavior has been seen in sharks.
Although the formidable, three-meter-long pelagic thresher shark seems able to catch food face-first, the ability to immobilize more than one fish at a time makes the method highly efficient.
The ______ are in the journal PLoS ONE.
These sharks used both ______ and horizontal tail slaps to capture prey, which were stunned or killed either by direct impact or by a shockwave from the smack.
More than a third of the vertical slaps resulted in a meal for the shark—better stats than when sharks chased prey head on.
And that's no tall tale.

questions.name: #110 Sexual Reproduction
questions.en:
Sex might seem like one of those little gifts from evolution.
But it's pretty inefficient from an ______ perspective.
It'd be much easier to reproduce if you could do away with finding the right member of the opposite sex to help you create the next generation.
So why did ______ come up with sex?
Biologists have hypothesized that one driving force might have been parasites.
Now scientists have had a chance to test that theory.
A sexual reproduction leads to clones.
Being genetically identical, clones are also weak in the same ways, and thus more likely to all succumb to a parasite.
But sex keeps shuffling the genetic deck.
Well, there's a snail common in New Zealand lakes that does both—some ______ have sex and some reproduce asexually.
So researchers spent 10 years monitoring the two populations, and the number of parasites living off both groups.
As expected, cloned snails that were plentiful at the beginning of the study suffered big losses as they became infected with parasites.
But the sexual snail populations remained stable, results published in the journal American Naturalist.
So, next time you're feeling sexy, thank a parasite.

sense_groups.english: Sex might seem like one of those little gifts from evolution.

sense_groups.chinese: 现在科学家有机会验证这个理论。

sense_groups.chinese: 所以，下次你感到性感时，感谢寄生虫吧。

questions.name: #111 Horror
questions.en:
You've landed a small role in a low-budget horror movie.
To get ready, you need to ______ your reaction shot—you know, that look you'll get when your boss peels off his face to reveal the slime-oozing alien he really is.
So, look in the mirror and give us some terror.
If you're doing it right, your eyes are wide open and your eyebrows are raised.
But why is that?
I mean, how come people, when they're scared, all make a similar face?
Darwin thought there was a reason, that our ______ evolved because they offer some benefit.
And scientists from Ontario think Darwin was right.
They asked volunteers to try to look ______ and then they ______ the physiological effects.
They found that making a fraidy face allows people to see farther, locate targets faster and take in more air when they breathe.
The findings appear in the current online issue of Nature Neuroscience.
Those reactions make sense, because if you see something ______ or out of the ordinary, you can use your ______ vision to assess the situation and, if need be, take a deep, fear-boosted breath—and run!

sense_groups.chinese: 你知道，就是当你老板剥下他的脸，露出他实际上是个流着粘液的外星人时，你会露出的表情。

sense_groups.chinese: 但这是为什么呢？

sense_groups.chinese: 我的意思是，为什么人们害怕时都会做出相似的表情？

sense_groups.english: And scientists from Ontario think Darwin was right.
sense_groups.chinese: 安大略省的科学家认为达尔文是对的。

sense_groups.chinese: 他们让志愿者试着做出害怕的表情，然后测量了生理效应。

sense_groups.chinese: 这些反应是有道理的，因为如果你看到令人吃惊或不寻常的东西，你可以利用增强的恐惧视觉来评估情况，如果需要的话，深吸一口因恐惧而增强的气息——然后逃跑！

questions.name: #112 Elephant Enclaves
questions.en:
It's a ______ story.
When immigrants arrive in a new place, they tend to stick together, forming segregated enclaves that feel like a home away from home.
Then, over time, they become assimilated, and integrate into the local community.
It was true of the German and Irish immigrants who came to the U.S. in the 1800s.
And it's also true of elephants when they find themselves in ______ territory.
In ______ wild ______ populations, rangers will often transport the animals from one place to another, removing them from a familiar habitat and placing them in one that's new.
So scientists in California got to wondering how elephants, which are highly social creatures, handle making themselves at home when they get to a new neighborhood.
It turns out they start by forming enclaves that are the elephant equivalent of a ghetto, where the new pachyderms in the park associate with one another and with other immigrant elephants.
Then, once the transplants have been around for a year, they get ______ with the locals, findings that were published by the Royal Society on ______ 10th.
The cautious approach seems to be a good one: not knowing whether the natives are friendly, it's probably best not to step on any toes.
  ______ if you're an elephant.

questions.name: #114 Women vs Men
questions.en:
Women are so much better than men at so many things.
But according to a report published by the Royal Society, chess is not one of them.
The topic of sex differences when it comes to matters of the mind is, needless to say, a divisive one.
Those who wish to argue that women are just not as smart as men often point to chess as their proof.
Although girls can obviously play, no woman's ever been world champion.
But before looking for ______ or ______ explanations for the disparity, ______ say you need to do the math.
Serious chess players are assigned ratings based on their ______ against other players.
So the scientists compared the ratings of the top hundred male and top hundred female players from Germany.
And they found that the men indeed outperformed the women.
However that difference can be almost entirely explained by statistics.
Because the larger the population, the wider the range of measured scores—the bell curve has a longer tail.
And because many more men play than women, the best male players are extreme ______ on that bell curve.
As more women play, a few should also reach those extremes, right out there with the men.
To which one might be tempted to say: Checkmate.

But according to a report published by the Royal Society, chess is not one of them.

2. biological

sense_groups.chinese: 严肃的国际象棋棋手会根据他们与其他棋手的比赛表现获得评分。

sense_groups.english: So the scientists compared the ratings of the top hundred male and top hundred female players from Germany.
sense_groups.chinese: 于是科学家比较了德国前一百名男棋手和前一百名女棋手的评分。

sense_groups.english: And they found that the men indeed outperformed the women.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现男性确实比女性表现更好。

sense_groups.english: However that difference can be almost entirely explained by statistics.
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，这种差异几乎完全可以由统计学解释。

sense_groups.english: Because the larger the population, the wider the range of measured scores—the bell curve has a longer tail.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为人口越多，测量分数的范围就越广——钟形曲线的尾巴更长。

sense_groups.english: And because many more men play than women, the best male players are extreme outliers on that bell curve.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且由于男性棋手远多于女性，最优秀的男棋手是那条钟形曲线上的极端异常值。

sense_groups.english: As more women play, a few should also reach those extremes, right out there with the men.
sense_groups.chinese: 随着更多女性参与，少数女性也应该能达到那些极端水平，与男性并驾齐驱。

sense_groups.english: To which one might be tempted to say: Checkmate.
sense_groups.chinese: 对此，人们可能会忍不住说：将军。

questions.name: #115 To Chase Flies
questions.en:
You've probably chased a fly or two around the house this summer.
And, chances are, it took a few swings before you brought down the buzzing nuisance.
Now a study in the August 28th issue of the journal Current Biology has uncovered just what makes a fly so hard to swat.
Michael ______ from the California ______ of Technology used ______ digital video to record the evasive maneuvers of fruit flies.
In the slow-mo instant replay, the flies' bodies react to a swatter well before their wings carry them to safety.
Blessed with nearly 360 degree vision, the fly first gauges the position of the swatter, then ______ an escape within 200 milliseconds.
When approached from the front, for example, a fly shifts its middle legs forward and leans back.
If you sneak in from the side, the fly leans in the opposite direction.
This ______ then lets the fly spring into a flight pattern that takes it out of the danger zone.
So, if you want to get a fly on the first try, Dickinson says to aim at where you think it's going, not where it is.
Or you could always call in a SWAT team.
questions.full:
You've probably chased a fly or two around the house this summer.
And, chances are, it took a few swings before you brought down the buzzing nuisance.
Now a study in the August 28th issue of the journal Current Biology has uncovered just what makes a fly so hard to swat.
Michael ______ from the California ______ of Technology used ______ digital video to record the evasive maneuvers of fruit flies.
In the slow-mo instant replay, the flies' bodies react to a swatter well before their wings carry them to safety.
Blessed with nearly 360 degree vision, the fly first gauges the position of the swatter, then ______ an escape within 200 milliseconds.
When approached from the front, for example, a fly shifts its middle legs forward and leans back.
If you sneak in from the side, the fly leans in the opposite direction.
This ______ then lets the fly spring into a flight pattern that takes it out of the danger zone.
So, if you want to get a fly on the first try, Dickinson says to aim at where you think it's going, not where it is.
Or you could always call in a SWAT team.

答案:
1. Dickinson
2. Institute
3. high-speed
4. prepares
5. positioning

sense_groups.english: You've probably chased a fly or two around the house this summer.
sense_groups.chinese: 今年夏天你可能在屋里追过一两只苍蝇。

sense_groups.english: And, chances are, it took a few swings before you brought down the buzzing nuisance.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且，很可能你挥了好几下才打中这个嗡嗡作响的讨厌鬼。

sense_groups.english: Now a study in the August 28th issue of the journal Current Biology has uncovered just what makes a fly so hard to swat.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，《当代生物学》杂志8月28日刊的一项研究揭示了苍蝇为什么这么难打。

sense_groups.english: Michael Dickinson from the California Institute of Technology used high-speed digital video to record the evasive maneuvers of fruit flies.
sense_groups.chinese: 加州理工学院的迈克尔·迪金森使用高速数字视频记录了果蝇的逃避动作。

sense_groups.english: In the slow-mo instant replay, the flies' bodies react to a swatter well before their wings carry them to safety.
sense_groups.chinese: 在慢动作回放中，苍蝇的身体在翅膀带它们飞向安全地带之前就对蝇拍做出了反应。

sense_groups.english: Blessed with nearly 360 degree vision, the fly first gauges the position of the swatter, then prepares an escape within 200 milliseconds.
sense_groups.chinese: 苍蝇拥有近乎360度的视野，它首先判断蝇拍的位置，然后在200毫秒内准备逃跑。

sense_groups.english: When approached from the front, for example, a fly shifts its middle legs forward and leans back.
sense_groups.chinese: 例如，当从前方靠近时，苍蝇会把中腿前移并向后倾斜。

sense_groups.english: If you sneak in from the side, the fly leans in the opposite direction.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你从侧面偷袭，苍蝇会向相反方向倾斜。

sense_groups.english: This positioning then lets the fly spring into a flight pattern that takes it out of the danger zone.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种定位使苍蝇能够跃入飞行模式，从而脱离危险区域。

sense_groups.english: So, if you want to get a fly on the first try, Dickinson says to aim at where you think it's going, not where it is.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以，如果你想一次就打中苍蝇，迪金森说，要瞄准你认为它会去的地方，而不是它所在的位置。

sense_groups.english: Or you could always call in a SWAT team.
sense_groups.chinese: 或者你总是可以叫一个特警队来。

questions.name: #116 Romantic Music

Maybe you should check what music is playing.

questions.name: #117 Longevity Diets
questions.en:
Sometimes it's not what you eat, but when you eat it.
At least when it comes to longevity diets.
For some time, ______ have known that animals kept on a strict diet live longer than their well-fed peers.
But this Methuselah meal plan is no ordinary ______ of pie kind of diet.
To reap the ______ benefits, some of these animals cut their calorie consumption in half.
Such a diet might be do-able for captive mice and monkeys, but it would be a tough sell for people.
Then, five years ago, studies in mice suggested that ______ fasting would work just as well.
These mice abstained from eating every other day, and lived longer then their gluttonous comrades—without really skimping on the total ______ they consumed.
Now, scientists at Kyoto University have found the same thing in worms that fasted every third day.
And they found a gene that regulates the effect, results reported in the journal Nature.
Like the mice, these fasting worms did not cut their total calorie intake.
But they boosted their lifespan by 50 percent, and showed fewer signs of ______ decline than their peers.
So go ahead, enjoy that extra slice of pie.
Because tomorrow's another day.
To not eat.
questions.answer:
1. scientists
2. just-say-no-to-that-second-slice
3. life-extending
4. intermittent
5. calories
6. physical
questions.full:
Sometimes it's not what you eat, but when you eat it.
At least when it comes to longevity diets.
For some time, ______ have known that animals kept on a strict diet live longer than their well-fed peers.
But this Methuselah meal plan is no ordinary ______ of pie kind of diet.

Now, scientists at Kyoto University have found the same thing in worms that fasted every third day.
And they found a gene that regulates the effect, results reported in the journal Nature.
Like the mice, these fasting worms did not cut their total calorie intake.
But they boosted their lifespan by 50 percent, and showed fewer signs of ______ decline than their peers.

2. just-say-no-to-that-second-slice

sense_groups.english: Sometimes it's not what you eat, but when you eat it.
sense_groups.chinese: 有时候重要的不是你吃什么，而是你什么时候吃。

sense_groups.english: At least when it comes to longevity diets.
sense_groups.chinese: 至少在长寿饮食方面是这样。

sense_groups.english: For some time, scientists have known that animals kept on a strict diet live longer than their well-fed peers.
sense_groups.chinese: 一段时间以来，科学家们已经知道，严格节食的动物比吃得饱的同伴活得更久。

sense_groups.english: But this Methuselah meal plan is no ordinary just-say-no-to-that-second-slice of pie kind of diet.
sense_groups.chinese: 但这种玛土撒拉饮食计划并非普通的“拒绝第二块馅饼”式节食。

sense_groups.english: To reap the life-extending benefits, some of these animals cut their calorie consumption in half.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了获得延长寿命的好处，其中一些动物将热量摄入减半。

sense_groups.english: Such a diet might be do-able for captive mice and monkeys, but it would be a tough sell for people.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种饮食对圈养的老鼠和猴子可能可行，但对人类来说很难推广。

sense_groups.english: Then, five years ago, studies in mice suggested that intermittent fasting would work just as well.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后，五年前，对老鼠的研究表明，间歇性禁食同样有效。

sense_groups.english: These mice abstained from eating every other day, and lived longer then their gluttonous comrades—without really skimping on the total calories they consumed.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些老鼠每隔一天禁食，比它们贪吃的同伴活得更久——而且并没有真正减少总热量摄入。

sense_groups.english: Now, scientists at Kyoto University have found the same thing in worms that fasted every third day.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，京都大学的科学家在每三天禁食一次的蠕虫中发现了同样的现象。

sense_groups.english: And they found a gene that regulates the effect, results reported in the journal Nature.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现了一个调节这种效果的基因，研究结果发表在《自然》杂志上。

sense_groups.english: Like the mice, these fasting worms did not cut their total calorie intake.
sense_groups.chinese: 和老鼠一样，这些禁食的蠕虫并没有减少总热量摄入。

sense_groups.english: But they boosted their lifespan by 50 percent, and showed fewer signs of physical decline than their peers.
sense_groups.chinese: 但它们的寿命延长了50%，并且比同龄蠕虫表现出更少的身体衰退迹象。

sense_groups.english: So go ahead, enjoy that extra slice of pie.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以，去吧，享受那额外的一块馅饼。

sense_groups.english: Because tomorrow's another day.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为明天又是新的一天。

sense_groups.english: To not eat.
sense_groups.chinese: 不吃东西。

questions.name: #118 Good Workout
questions.en:
We've all heard exercise is good for your physical and mental well-being.
But a good workout can actually influence the mental well-being of others, too.
Because bosses who hit the gym tend to be less abusive to their employees.
That's according to a study in the Journal of ______ and Psychology.
  ______ asked 98 MBA ______ who were also employed full-time to rate how their supervisors treated them, by ______ to statements like "my boss puts me down in front of others." The researchers also had supervisors fill out a ______ survey, about their stress levels and weekly exercise.
And, as the authors expected, the more stressed-out supervisors were, the more their employees felt belittled by them.
But the employees felt better about bosses who exercised, whether it was yoga, cardio or weight lifting.
And just one or two days a week did the trick.
Exercise didn't simply melt away the stress—bosses who worked out reported feeling just as much ______ as their sedentary counterparts.
Active bosses just spared subordinates the verbal attacks.
So next time you feel like telling your boss to take a hike, it might actually be sound advice!
questions.answer:
1. Business
2. Researchers
3. students
4. responding
5. different
6. pressure
questions.full:
We've all heard exercise is good for your physical and mental well-being.
But a good workout can actually influence the mental well-being of others, too.
Because bosses who hit the gym tend to be less abusive to their employees.
That's according to a study in the Journal of ______ and Psychology.
  ______ asked 98 MBA ______ who were also employed full-time to rate how their supervisors treated them, by ______ to statements like "my boss puts me down in front of others." The researchers also had supervisors fill out a ______ survey, about their stress levels and weekly exercise.
And, as the authors expected, the more stressed-out supervisors were, the more their employees felt belittled by them.
But the employees felt better about bosses who exercised, whether it was yoga, cardio or weight lifting.
And just one or two days a week did the trick.
Exercise didn't simply melt away the stress—bosses who worked out reported feeling just as much ______ as their sedentary counterparts.
Active bosses just spared subordinates the verbal attacks.
So next time you feel like telling your boss to take a hike, it might actually be sound advice!

答案:

2. Researchers
3. students
4. responding
5. different

sense_groups.english: We've all heard exercise is good for your physical and mental well-being.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们都听说过锻炼对身心健康有益。

sense_groups.english: But a good workout can actually influence the mental well-being of others, too.
sense_groups.chinese: 但一次好的锻炼实际上也能影响他人的心理健康。

sense_groups.english: Because bosses who hit the gym tend to be less abusive to their employees.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为去健身房的老板往往对员工不那么苛刻。

sense_groups.english: That's according to a study in the Journal of Business and Psychology.
sense_groups.chinese: 这是根据《商业与心理学杂志》的一项研究得出的。

sense_groups.english: Researchers asked 98 MBA students who were also employed full-time to rate how their supervisors treated them,
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员让98名同时全职工作的MBA学生评价他们的主管如何对待他们，

sense_groups.english: by responding to statements like "my boss puts me down in front of others."
sense_groups.chinese: 通过回应诸如“我的老板在别人面前贬低我”这样的陈述。

sense_groups.english: The researchers also had supervisors fill out a different survey, about their stress levels and weekly exercise.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员还让主管填写另一份关于他们压力水平和每周锻炼情况的调查问卷。

sense_groups.english: And, as the authors expected, the more stressed-out supervisors were, the more their employees felt belittled by them.
sense_groups.chinese: 并且，正如作者所料，主管压力越大，员工就越感到被他们轻视。

sense_groups.english: But the employees felt better about bosses who exercised, whether it was yoga, cardio or weight lifting.
sense_groups.chinese: 但员工对那些锻炼的老板感觉更好，无论是瑜伽、有氧运动还是举重。

sense_groups.english: And just one or two days a week did the trick.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且每周只需一两天就能奏效。

sense_groups.english: Exercise didn't simply melt away the stress—bosses who worked out reported feeling just as much pressure as their sedentary counterparts.
sense_groups.chinese: 锻炼并没有简单地消除压力——锻炼的老板报告说，他们感受到的压力与久坐的老板一样大。

sense_groups.english: Active bosses just spared subordinates the verbal attacks.
sense_groups.chinese: 活跃的老板只是让下属免于遭受言语攻击。

sense_groups.english: So next time you feel like telling your boss to take a hike, it might actually be sound advice!
sense_groups.chinese: 所以下次你想让老板去远足时，这实际上可能是个好建议！

questions.name: #119 Cats
questions.en:
Lions roaming the savannah are a staple of nature documentaries.
But the millions of little lions that live in our homes and ______ also lead fascinating lives.
We know more about those lives now, because a two-year-long study used ______ to track cats at the ______ edge of the cities of Champaign and Urbana in Illinois.
It would have taken a dozen field researchers to collect the same data.
The study is in the Journal of Wildlife Management.
The entire kittie cohort included both housecats and feral cats, and ranged over almost 6,300 acres.
One feral cat's range topped out at 1,351 acres.
New York's Central Park covers 843 acres.
Owned cats with homes roamed way less than their feral counterparts.
But they still ______ a range of just under five acres.
The pets were highly active just 3 percent of the time, compared with 14 percent for the cats that need to find their own food.
The work should shed light on protecting species that the cats hunt, and inform the efforts to stop the spread of feline ______ diseases.
questions.full:
Lions roaming the savannah are a staple of nature documentaries.
But the millions of little lions that live in our homes and ______ also lead fascinating lives.
We know more about those lives now, because a two-year-long study used ______ to track cats at the ______ edge of the cities of Champaign and Urbana in Illinois.
It would have taken a dozen field researchers to collect the same data.
The study is in the Journal of Wildlife Management.
The entire kittie cohort included both housecats and feral cats, and ranged over almost 6,300 acres.
One feral cat's range topped out at 1,351 acres.
New York's Central Park covers 843 acres.
Owned cats with homes roamed way less than their feral counterparts.
But they still ______ a range of just under five acres.
The pets were highly active just 3 percent of the time, compared with 14 percent for the cats that need to find their own food.
The work should shed light on protecting species that the cats hunt, and inform the efforts to stop the spread of feline ______ diseases.

答案:
1. neighborhoods
2. radio-transmitters
3. southern
4. averaged
5. contagious

sense_groups.english: Lions roaming the savannah are a staple of nature documentaries.
sense_groups.chinese: 在稀树草原上漫步的狮子是自然纪录片的常见内容。

sense_groups.english: But the millions of little lions that live in our homes and neighborhoods also lead fascinating lives.
sense_groups.chinese: 但生活在我们的家和社区里的数百万只小狮子也过着迷人的生活。

sense_groups.english: We know more about those lives now, because a two-year-long study used radio-transmitters to track cats at the southern edge of the cities of Champaign and Urbana in Illinois.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们现在对这些生活有了更多了解，因为一项为期两年的研究使用无线电发射器追踪了伊利诺伊州尚佩恩和厄巴纳两市南缘的猫。

sense_groups.english: It would have taken a dozen field researchers to collect the same data.
sense_groups.chinese: 收集同样的数据需要十几名实地研究人员。

sense_groups.english: The study is in the Journal of Wildlife Management.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《野生动物管理杂志》上。

sense_groups.english: The entire kittie cohort included both housecats and feral cats, and ranged over almost 6,300 acres.
sense_groups.chinese: 整个猫咪群体包括家猫和野猫，活动范围覆盖近6300英亩。

sense_groups.english: One feral cat's range topped out at 1,351 acres.
sense_groups.chinese: 一只野猫的活动范围最大达到1351英亩。

sense_groups.english: New York's Central Park covers 843 acres.
sense_groups.chinese: 纽约中央公园占地843英亩。

sense_groups.english: Owned cats with homes roamed way less than their feral counterparts.
sense_groups.chinese: 有家的家猫活动范围远小于野猫。

questions.name: #120 Early Farming
questions.en:
Early farming began in the Near East about 10,500 years ago.
Farming first reached the Balkans in Europe some 8 to 9,000 years ago, and then crept westward.
Locals in Britain, ______ from the ______ by the relatively newly formed English Channel, did not start farming until about 6,000 years ago.
But an ______ of sediment from a submerged British archaeological site called ______ Cliff found something unexpected.
"Amongst our Bouldner Cliff samples we found ancient DNA evidence of wheat at the site, which was not seen in mainland Britain for another 2,000 years." Robin Allaby of the ______ of Warwick.
"However, wheat was already being grown in southern Europe.
This is incredibly ______ because it means Bouldner's inhabitants were not as isolated as ______ thought.
In fact, they were in touch, one way or another, with more advanced Neolithic farming communities in southern Europe." The work by Allaby and colleagues is in the journal Science.
The researchers showed that the wheat remains are genetically more similar to Near Eastern domesticated wheat than to local distant cousins.
And they found no evidence of pollen—meaning that the wheat was almost certainly imported.
In an accompanying Perspectives piece in the journal, archaeologist Greger Larsen of Durham University writes that the findings show that DNA analysis can help scientists tease out details about the historical movement of plant and animal species.
questions.answer:
1. separated
2. mainland
3. analysis
4. Bouldner
5. University
6. exciting
7. previously

sense_groups.english: Early farming began in the Near East about 10,500 years ago.

questions.name: #121 Sex of Lizard
questions.en:
When it comes to lizard sex, size does matter.
But not in the way you might think.
Because in the June 4th online issue of the journal Current Biology, ______ say that for at least one type of lizard, larger eggs are more likely to make girls while smaller eggs yield boys.
For many animals, the sex of an individual is dictated solely by its chromosomes.
But for small alpine lizards, gender isn't so cut-and-dried.
The scientists had earlier found that nest temperature can ______ the sex of lizard hatchlings.
Cooler nests turn out more boys—no matter what their ______ say.
At the same time, the researchers noticed that larger eggs seemed to make more daughters.
But they wanted to put their observation to the test.
So they took big eggs and removed some yolk—and, voila, they made males.
Adding yolk to a little egg was a recipe for a female.
This egg size ______ might allow moms to balance their babies' sexes when a chilly nest would ______ produce mostly sons.
Because when it comes to alpine lizards, sex ______ all comes down to a practical yolk.
questions.answer:
1. scientists
2. influence
3. chromosomes
4. manipulation
5. otherwise
6. determination
questions.full:
When it comes to lizard sex, size does matter.
But not in the way you might think.
Because in the June 4th online issue of the journal Current Biology, ______ say that for at least one type of lizard, larger eggs are more likely to make girls while smaller eggs yield boys.
For many animals, the sex of an individual is dictated solely by its chromosomes.
But for small alpine lizards, gender isn't so cut-and-dried.
The scientists had earlier found that nest temperature can ______ the sex of lizard hatchlings.
Cooler nests turn out more boys—no matter what their ______ say.
At the same time, the researchers noticed that larger eggs seemed to make more daughters.
But they wanted to put their observation to the test.
So they took big eggs and removed some yolk—and, voila, they made males.
Adding yolk to a little egg was a recipe for a female.

答案:

2. influence
3. chromosomes
4. manipulation
5. otherwise
6. determination

sense_groups.english: When it comes to lizard sex, size does matter.
sense_groups.chinese: 说到蜥蜴的性别，大小确实很重要。

sense_groups.english: But not in the way you might think.
sense_groups.chinese: 但并非你想的那样。

sense_groups.english: Because in the June 4th online issue of the journal Current Biology, scientists say that for at least one type of lizard, larger eggs are more likely to make girls while smaller eggs yield boys.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为在《当代生物学》期刊6月4日的网络版中，科学家们说，至少对于一种蜥蜴来说，较大的卵更可能孵出雌性，而较小的卵则孵出雄性。

sense_groups.english: For many animals, the sex of an individual is dictated solely by its chromosomes.
sense_groups.chinese: 对许多动物来说，个体的性别完全由染色体决定。

sense_groups.english: But for small alpine lizards, gender isn't so cut-and-dried.
sense_groups.chinese: 但对于小型高山蜥蜴来说，性别并非如此简单明了。

sense_groups.english: The scientists had earlier found that nest temperature can influence the sex of lizard hatchlings.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们早些时候发现，巢穴温度可以影响蜥蜴幼体的性别。

sense_groups.english: Cooler nests turn out more boys—no matter what their chromosomes say.
sense_groups.chinese: 较冷的巢穴会孵出更多雄性——无论它们的染色体如何。

sense_groups.english: At the same time, the researchers noticed that larger eggs seemed to make more daughters.
sense_groups.chinese: 同时，研究人员注意到较大的卵似乎孵出更多雌性。

sense_groups.english: But they wanted to put their observation to the test.
sense_groups.chinese: 但他们想验证这一观察结果。

sense_groups.english: So they took big eggs and removed some yolk—and, voila, they made males.
sense_groups.chinese: 于是他们取了大卵，移除了一些蛋黄——瞧，它们变成了雄性。

sense_groups.english: Adding yolk to a little egg was a recipe for a female.
sense_groups.chinese: 给小卵添加蛋黄则能孵出雌性。

sense_groups.english: This egg size manipulation might allow moms to balance their babies' sexes when a chilly nest would otherwise produce mostly sons.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种卵大小的操控可能让母亲在巢穴寒冷时平衡后代的性别，否则巢穴会主要孵出雄性。

sense_groups.english: Because when it comes to alpine lizards, sex determination all comes down to a practical yolk.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为对于高山蜥蜴来说，性别决定完全归结于实用的蛋黄。

questions.name: #122 Tree Frog
questions.en:
The eastern grey tree frog (sound) looks exactly like the closely related Cope's grey tree frog (sound).
The big difference between the two species is beneath the surface—the eastern has twice the number of ______ as does the Cope's.
Having more sets of chromosomes makes the cells of the eastern frog larger than the cells found in the Cope's. And those bigger cells makes the eastern's song just a little deeper.
Now University of Missouri ______ Carl Gerhardt and his student Mitch Tucker have determined that the slight difference in the calls—here's the eastern again and here's the Cope's (sound)—is how the females know which species' males to buddy up with: the ones with the same ______ number that they have.
The work is in the ______ of the Royal Society B-Biological Sciences.
  ______ is often caused by a geographic barrier that keeps populations from mating.
But the tree frog situation may be a rare case in which chromosome duplication, and its ______ effects, presented a ______ barrier.
As in humans, it comes down to whether he calls.
questions.answer:
1. chromosomes
2. researcher
3. chromosome
4. Proceedings
5. Speciation
6. subsequent
7. reproductive

The big difference between the two species is beneath the surface—the eastern has twice the number of ______ as does the Cope's.

The work is in the ______ of the Royal Society B-Biological Sciences.
  ______ is often caused by a geographic barrier that keeps populations from mating.
But the tree frog situation may be a rare case in which chromosome duplication, and its ______ effects, presented a ______ barrier.
As in humans, it comes down to whether he calls.

答案:
1. chromosomes
2. researcher
3. chromosome
4. Proceedings
5. Speciation
6. subsequent
7. reproductive

sense_groups.english: The eastern grey tree frog (sound) looks exactly like the closely related Cope's grey tree frog (sound).
sense_groups.chinese: 东部灰树蛙（声音）看起来与近亲科佩斯灰树蛙（声音）一模一样。

sense_groups.english: The big difference between the two species is beneath the surface—the eastern has twice the number of chromosomes as does the Cope's.
sense_groups.chinese: 这两个物种之间的主要区别在于表面之下——东部灰树蛙的染色体数量是科佩斯灰树蛙的两倍。

sense_groups.english: Having more sets of chromosomes makes the cells of the eastern frog larger than the cells found in the Cope's.
sense_groups.chinese: 拥有更多套染色体使得东部灰树蛙的细胞比科佩斯灰树蛙的细胞更大。

sense_groups.english: And those bigger cells makes the eastern's song just a little deeper.
sense_groups.chinese: 而这些更大的细胞使得东部灰树蛙的叫声稍微低沉一些。

sense_groups.english: Now University of Missouri researcher Carl Gerhardt and his student Mitch Tucker have determined that the slight difference in the calls—here's the eastern again and here's the Cope's (sound)—is how the females know which species' males to buddy up with: the ones with the same chromosome number that they have.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，密苏里大学的研究员卡尔·格哈特和他的学生米奇·塔克已经确定，叫声的细微差别——这是东部灰树蛙的叫声，这是科佩斯灰树蛙的叫声（声音）——是雌性如何知道该与哪个物种的雄性配对：那些与它们拥有相同染色体数量的雄性。

sense_groups.english: The work is in the Proceedings of the Royal Society B-Biological Sciences.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《皇家学会学报B-生物科学》上。

sense_groups.english: Speciation is often caused by a geographic barrier that keeps populations from mating.
sense_groups.chinese: 物种形成通常是由地理屏障引起的，这种屏障阻止种群交配。

sense_groups.english: But the tree frog situation may be a rare case in which chromosome duplication, and its subsequent effects, presented a reproductive barrier.
sense_groups.chinese: 但树蛙的情况可能是一个罕见的例子，其中染色体复制及其后续效应构成了生殖屏障。

sense_groups.english: As in humans, it comes down to whether he calls.
sense_groups.chinese: 就像人类一样，归根结底在于他是否发出呼唤。

questions.name: #123 Migration
questions.en:
Want to know the route humans took when they first migrated from Africa into Europe?
Seems that they might have marked the path.
Not like Hansel and Gretel, who ______ left bread crumbs.
Ancient humans ate as they trekked.
And they appear to have chucked aside the packaging for some of their slimy sustenance: snails.
Conventional wisdom has been that humans initially ______ from Africa to the Near East, then up around the Mediterranean through Lebanon before heading into Europe some 40 to 50,000 years ago.
But recently, some ______ have theorized that humans made it to Europe first and then headed east.
Now there's more support for the old view that humans traveled through the Levant on the way to Europe-in the form of the shells of edible marine snails.
The study is in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
Researchers evaluated shells from an ______ site dated to the Upper ______ in Lebanon.
The shells were mostly intact, except the tapered pointy tip had been removed—most likely for easier access to the meat inside.
The scientists calculated the age of the shells via a variety of methods.
And they found that the snails dated back almost 46,000 years.
The earliest ______ of modern human remains in Europe seem to be no more than 45,000 years old.
The snail evidence thus adds weight to the hypothesis that ancient people passed through the Levant on their way to Europe.
And not at a snail's pace, either.
questions.answer:
1. consciously
2. traveled
3. scientists
4. archaeological
5. Paleolithic
6. evidence

sense_groups.english: Want to know the route humans took when they first migrated from Africa into Europe?
sense_groups.chinese: 想知道人类首次从非洲迁徙到欧洲时走的路线吗？

sense_groups.english: Seems that they might have marked the path.
sense_groups.chinese: 看来他们可能标记了路径。

sense_groups.english: Not like Hansel and Gretel, who consciously left bread crumbs.
sense_groups.chinese: 不像汉塞尔和格蕾特那样有意识地留下面包屑。

sense_groups.english: Ancient humans ate as they trekked.
sense_groups.chinese: 古代人类边走边吃。

sense_groups.english: And they appear to have chucked aside the packaging for some of their slimy sustenance: snails.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且他们似乎扔掉了部分黏糊糊的食物包装：蜗牛。

sense_groups.english: Conventional wisdom has been that humans initially traveled from Africa to the Near East, then up around the Mediterranean through Lebanon before heading into Europe some 40 to 50,000 years ago.
sense_groups.chinese: 传统观点认为，人类最初从非洲迁徙到近东，然后绕过地中海经黎巴嫩，大约在4万到5万年前进入欧洲。

sense_groups.english: But recently, some scientists have theorized that humans made it to Europe first and then headed east.
sense_groups.chinese: 但最近，一些科学家提出理论，认为人类先到达欧洲，然后向东迁徙。

sense_groups.english: Now there's more support for the old view that humans traveled through the Levant on the way to Europe-in the form of the shells of edible marine snails.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在有更多证据支持旧观点，即人类在前往欧洲途中经过黎凡特地区——证据来自可食用海螺的壳。

sense_groups.english: The study is in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。

sense_groups.english: Researchers evaluated shells from an archaeological site dated to the Upper Paleolithic in Lebanon.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员评估了黎巴嫩一处旧石器时代晚期考古遗址的贝壳。

sense_groups.english: The shells were mostly intact, except the tapered pointy tip had been removed—most likely for easier access to the meat inside.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些贝壳大多完好无损，只是锥形尖端被移除——很可能是为了更容易吃到里面的肉。

sense_groups.english: The scientists calculated the age of the shells via a variety of methods.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们通过多种方法计算了这些贝壳的年代。

sense_groups.english: And they found that the snails dated back almost 46,000 years.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现这些蜗牛可以追溯到近4.6万年前。

sense_groups.english: The earliest evidence of modern human remains in Europe seem to be no more than 45,000 years old.
sense_groups.chinese: 欧洲最早的现代人类遗骸似乎不超过4.5万年。

sense_groups.english: The snail evidence thus adds weight to the hypothesis that ancient people passed through the Levant on their way to Europe.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，蜗牛证据为古代人类在前往欧洲途中经过黎凡特地区的假说增添了分量。

sense_groups.english: And not at a snail's pace, either.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且也不是以蜗牛般的速度。

questions.name: #124 G.M.
questions.en:

Now, for the first time in the U.S., researchers report a large population of GM crops beyond the farm.
Transgenic canola plants in North Dakota had ______ genes making them resistant to herbicides, such as the weed killer Roundup.
Researchers collected and tested 406 canola plants along thousands of miles of state roads.
They found 347 carrying at least one resistance gene.

sense_groups.english: Researchers collected and tested 406 canola plants along thousands of miles of state roads.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员沿着数千英里的州际公路收集并测试了406株油菜。

sense_groups.english: They found 347 carrying at least one resistance gene.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现347株携带至少一种抗性基因。

sense_groups.english: There were also indications that the inserted genes were being passed on to new generations, producing some plants in the wild with multiple transgenes.
sense_groups.chinese: 也有迹象表明，插入的基因正在传递给后代，在野外产生了一些具有多个转基因的植株。

sense_groups.english: The findings were presented on August 6th at the annual meeting of the Ecological Society of America in Pittsburgh.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些发现于8月6日在匹兹堡举行的美国生态学会年会上公布。

sense_groups.english: The transgenic canola plants are not about to take over the world.
sense_groups.chinese: 转基因油菜植株并不会接管世界。

sense_groups.english: But researchers are obviously curious about how these particular plants managed to make it in places like the edges of parking lots rather than pampered fields.
sense_groups.chinese: 但研究人员显然很好奇，这些特殊的植物是如何在停车场边缘等地方生存下来，而不是在精心照料的田地里。

sense_groups.english: Any answers they find will likely affect future biotechnology regulation.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们找到的任何答案都可能影响未来的生物技术监管。

questions.name: #125 Early Ocean
questions.en:
The early Earth's oceans were home to a lot of interesting chemistry.
Now scientists have found that amino acids thought to be present way back when could have been cooked into other compounds vital for life—an idea you should take with a grain of salt.
Four billion years ago, the planet was probably covered by a salty ocean, dotted with volcanic islands and short lived continents.
German researchers recently mimicked some of the chemistry taking place along the coasts of the volcanic islands.
They created an approximation of primordial seawater.
Then they evaporated it, to simulate what went on at those volcanic coasts.
They baked the residue, ______ salt crusts.
At those high temperatures, amino acids interacted with metal ions in the salt crusts and were converted into other ______ ______ molecules, such as pyrroles—which are part of the structures of chlorophyll in plants and hemoglobin in animals.
The scientists ______ their findings September 17th at the European Planetary Science Conference in Potsdam.
Over ______ of ______ of years, these novel compounds could have built up along the volcanic coasts, creating materials for the first living cells.
Which were really worth their salt.
questions.answer:
1. creating
2. important
3. biological
4. presented
5. hundreds
6. thousands

Now scientists have found that amino acids thought to be present way back when could have been cooked into other compounds vital for life—an idea you should take with a grain of salt.

Then they evaporated it, to simulate what went on at those volcanic coasts.

The scientists ______ their findings September 17th at the European Planetary Science Conference in Potsdam.
Over ______ of ______ of years, these novel compounds could have built up along the volcanic coasts, creating materials for the first living cells.
Which were really worth their salt.

答案:
1. creating
2. important
3. biological
4. presented
5. hundreds
6. thousands

sense_groups.english: The early Earth's oceans were home to a lot of interesting chemistry.
sense_groups.chinese: 早期地球的海洋中发生了许多有趣的化学反应。

sense_groups.english: Now scientists have found that amino acids thought to be present way back when could have been cooked into other compounds vital for life—an idea you should take with a grain of salt.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在科学家发现，被认为存在于远古时期的氨基酸可能被转化成了其他对生命至关重要的化合物——不过对这个观点你应持保留态度。

sense_groups.english: Four billion years ago, the planet was probably covered by a salty ocean, dotted with volcanic islands and short lived continents.
sense_groups.chinese: 40亿年前，地球可能被咸水海洋覆盖，散布着火山岛和短暂存在的大陆。

sense_groups.english: German researchers recently mimicked some of the chemistry taking place along the coasts of the volcanic islands.
sense_groups.chinese: 德国研究人员最近模拟了火山岛沿岸发生的一些化学反应。

sense_groups.english: They created an approximation of primordial seawater.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们制造了近似原始海水的溶液。

sense_groups.english: Then they evaporated it, to simulate what went on at those volcanic coasts.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后将其蒸发，模拟火山海岸发生的过程。

sense_groups.english: They baked the residue, creating salt crusts.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们烘烤残留物，形成了盐壳。

sense_groups.english: At those high temperatures, amino acids interacted with metal ions in the salt crusts and were converted into other important biological molecules, such as pyrroles—which are part of the structures of chlorophyll in plants and hemoglobin in animals.
sense_groups.chinese: 在高温下，氨基酸与盐壳中的金属离子相互作用，转化为其他重要的生物分子，例如吡咯——它是植物叶绿素和动物血红蛋白结构的一部分。

sense_groups.english: The scientists presented their findings September 17th at the European Planetary Science Conference in Potsdam.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家于9月17日在波茨坦举行的欧洲行星科学会议上展示了他们的发现。

sense_groups.english: Over hundreds of thousands of years, these novel compounds could have built up along the volcanic coasts, creating materials for the first living cells.
sense_groups.chinese: 经过数十万年，这些新型化合物可能在火山海岸积累，为第一批活细胞创造了物质基础。

sense_groups.english: Which were really worth their salt.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些细胞确实名副其实（值得其盐分）。

questions.name: #126 Gun Control
questions.en:
Here's an impassioned plea for gun control.
Of nail guns, that is.
Because accidents involving nail guns have gone through the renovated roof.
In 2005, almost 15,000 people were treated in US emergency rooms for nail gun injuries.
That's twice the number in 2001 and three times the ______ back in 1991, according to data released in the April 13th issue of Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, put out by the CDC.
The rising ______ of do it yourselfing seems to be behind the unfortunate trend.
Most injuries are puncture wounds to the hands, followed by hits to the forearms, legs and feet.
Six percent of the wounded wind up being hospitalized.
Although better safety instruction would no doubt help, the report's authors suggest a systems ______ to the problem—they'd like nail guns to be ______ to fire until the nose was depressed, which would ______ happen only when the gun was flush up against whatever needed nailing.
By the way, 96 percent of the injured were males, which could mean that they're doing most of the work, or that women read the instructions.

In 2005, almost 15,000 people were treated in US emergency rooms for nail gun injuries.

答案:
1. injuries

sense_groups.english: Here's an impassioned plea for gun control.

sense_groups.english: impossible

sense_groups.english: presumably

questions.name: #127 Antibiotics
questions.en:
The pain-relieving effects of drugs like ibuprofen are well known.
But ibuprofen and its relatives, known as nonsteroidal ______ drugs, may someday have another use—as antibiotics.
Researchers tested three anti-inflammatory drugs: bromfenac, used in eye drops, and carprofen and vedaprofen, both for treating ______ like arthritis in dogs.
The investigators found that all three drugs bind to something called the "DNA clamp" in bacteria.
That clamp is ______ to repairing and replicating DNA.
By jamming it, the painkillers can ______ kill live E. coli—in a test tube, at least.
The findings appear in the journal ______ Biology.
Study author Aaron Oakley, of Australia's University of Wollongong, says we still need ______ trials to tell if this trick holds true in humans.
But this study is a first step.
"I guess it alerts a lot of clinicians to the fact that some of the nonsteroidal anti-inflammatories that they're using may have this off-target effect." And it gives drug developers—like Oakley and his colleagues—a whole new way to attack antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
questions.answer:
1. anti-inflammatory
2. conditions
3. essential
4. actually
5. Chemistry
6. clinical

But ibuprofen and its relatives, known as nonsteroidal ______ drugs, may someday have another use—as antibiotics.

The investigators found that all three drugs bind to something called the "DNA clamp" in bacteria.
That clamp is ______ to repairing and replicating DNA.
By jamming it, the painkillers can ______ kill live E. coli—in a test tube, at least.
The findings appear in the journal ______ Biology.
Study author Aaron Oakley, of Australia's University of Wollongong, says we still need ______ trials to tell if this trick holds true in humans.
But this study is a first step.
"I guess it alerts a lot of clinicians to the fact that some of the nonsteroidal anti-inflammatories that they're using may have this off-target effect." And it gives drug developers—like Oakley and his colleagues—a whole new way to attack antibiotic-resistant bacteria.

答案:

2. conditions
3. essential
4. actually

sense_groups.english: The pain-relieving effects of drugs like ibuprofen are well known.
sense_groups.chinese: 像布洛芬这类药物的镇痛效果是众所周知的。

sense_groups.english: But ibuprofen and its relatives, known as nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs,
sense_groups.chinese: 但布洛芬及其同类药物，即非甾体抗炎药，

sense_groups.english: may someday have another use—as antibiotics.
sense_groups.chinese: 或许有一天会有另一种用途——作为抗生素。

sense_groups.english: Researchers tested three anti-inflammatory drugs: bromfenac, used in eye drops,
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员测试了三种抗炎药：用于眼药水的溴芬酸，

sense_groups.english: and carprofen and vedaprofen, both for treating conditions like arthritis in dogs.
sense_groups.chinese: 以及卡洛芬和维达洛芬，两者都用于治疗犬类关节炎等疾病。

sense_groups.english: The investigators found that all three drugs bind to something called the "DNA clamp" in bacteria.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员发现，这三种药物都能与细菌中所谓的“DNA夹钳”结合。

sense_groups.english: That clamp is essential to repairing and replicating DNA.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种夹钳对DNA的修复和复制至关重要。

sense_groups.english: By jamming it, the painkillers can actually kill live E. coli—in a test tube, at least.
sense_groups.chinese: 通过阻塞它，这些止痛药实际上可以杀死活的大肠杆菌——至少在试管中是这样。

sense_groups.english: The findings appear in the journal Chemistry Biology.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究结果发表在《化学生物学》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: Study author Aaron Oakley, of Australia's University of Wollongong, says we still need clinical trials to tell if this trick holds true in humans.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究作者、澳大利亚伍伦贡大学的亚伦·奥克利表示，我们仍需要临床试验来验证这一方法在人体中是否有效。

sense_groups.english: But this study is a first step.
sense_groups.chinese: 但这项研究是第一步。

sense_groups.english: "I guess it alerts a lot of clinicians to the fact that some of the nonsteroidal anti-inflammatories that they're using may have this off-target effect."
sense_groups.chinese: “我想这会让许多临床医生意识到，他们正在使用的一些非甾体抗炎药可能具有这种脱靶效应。”

sense_groups.english: And it gives drug developers—like Oakley and his colleagues—a whole new way to attack antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
sense_groups.chinese: 这为药物开发者——比如奥克利和他的同事们——提供了一种全新的方法来对抗耐药菌。

questions.name: #128 Superstition
questions.en:
Breaking a mirror means seven years bad luck.
So does spilling salt or meeting a black cat.
We've all heard such silly-sounding superstitions.
Of course why anybody would believe that stepping on a crack could break your mother's back is a mystery.
But according to an article in the Royal Society journal Biological Sciences, ______ behaviors are a natural product of evolution.
Imagine an animal living in an environment where, over the course of a day, he might hear some rustling in the leaves or maybe in the grass.
Now, movements in the grass could signal a ______ attack, whereas the breeze in the trees is ______ just the wind.
Still, the animal has a choice: he can ignore all this rustling and go about his business, or he can run and hide.
The most logical response would be to hide only when he hears the grass move.
But what if it's hard to tell whether the noise came from the grass or the trees?
"I could've sworn that was the trees" could be his final thought.
So the animal learns to bolt at the sound of the breeze, because it could foretell certain doom.
That better-safe-than-sorry attitude is essentially a superstition.
One that that cautious critter will likely pass on to his young.
Knock on wood.

Still, the animal has a choice: he can ignore all this rustling and go about his business, or he can run and hide.

But what if it's hard to tell whether the noise came from the grass or the trees?

That better-safe-than-sorry attitude is essentially a superstition.

1. superstitious
2. predator

sense_groups.english: Breaking a mirror means seven years bad luck.
sense_groups.chinese: 打碎镜子意味着七年厄运。

sense_groups.english: So does spilling salt or meeting a black cat.
sense_groups.chinese: 打翻盐或遇到黑猫也是如此。

sense_groups.english: We've all heard such silly-sounding superstitions.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们都听过这些听起来很傻的迷信说法。

sense_groups.english: Of course why anybody would believe that stepping on a crack could break your mother's back is a mystery.
sense_groups.chinese: 当然，为什么有人会相信踩到裂缝会折断母亲的背，这真是个谜。

sense_groups.english: But according to an article in the Royal Society journal Biological Sciences,
sense_groups.chinese: 但根据皇家学会期刊《生物科学》上的一篇文章，

sense_groups.english: superstitious behaviors are a natural product of evolution.
sense_groups.chinese: 迷信行为是进化的自然产物。

sense_groups.english: Imagine an animal living in an environment where, over the course of a day,
sense_groups.chinese: 想象一只动物生活在这样的环境中：一天当中，

sense_groups.english: he might hear some rustling in the leaves or maybe in the grass.
sense_groups.chinese: 它可能会听到树叶或草丛中的沙沙声。

sense_groups.english: Now, movements in the grass could signal a predator attack,
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，草丛中的动静可能预示着捕食者的攻击，

sense_groups.english: whereas the breeze in the trees is probably just the wind.
sense_groups.chinese: 而树上的微风可能只是风而已。

sense_groups.english: Still, the animal has a choice: he can ignore all this rustling and go about his business,
sense_groups.chinese: 尽管如此，动物有一个选择：它可以忽略所有这些沙沙声，继续做自己的事，

sense_groups.english: or he can run and hide.
sense_groups.chinese: 或者它可以逃跑躲藏。

sense_groups.english: The most logical response would be to hide only when he hears the grass move.
sense_groups.chinese: 最合理的反应是只在听到草丛动静时才躲藏。

sense_groups.english: But what if it's hard to tell whether the noise came from the grass or the trees?
sense_groups.chinese: 但如果很难判断声音来自草丛还是树木呢？

sense_groups.english: "I could've sworn that was the trees" could be his final thought.
sense_groups.chinese: “我发誓那是树的声音”可能是它最后的念头。

sense_groups.english: So the animal learns to bolt at the sound of the breeze,
sense_groups.chinese: 所以动物学会了一听到风声就逃跑，

sense_groups.english: because it could foretell certain doom.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为那可能预示着厄运。

sense_groups.english: That better-safe-than-sorry attitude is essentially a superstition.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种宁可谨慎也不后悔的态度本质上是一种迷信。

sense_groups.english: One that that cautious critter will likely pass on to his young.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种态度，那个谨慎的小动物很可能会传给它的后代。

sense_groups.english: Knock on wood.
sense_groups.chinese: 敲敲木头（但愿好运）。

questions.name: #129 BioBonanza
questions.en:
BioBonanza is a one-day-open-house festival.
All of the researchers in the Department of Biology are going to be showcasing their research so ______ can come and see research, interact with the researchers.
And we want people to be able to interact and have fun of this event.
As soon as you walk in the doors, you'll see all sorts of activities, ______ of how a human heart works.
We'll have ______ of spinal cord and brain.
You'll get to be able to see ______ and all sorts of insects.

sense_groups.english: All of the researchers in the Department of Biology are going to be showcasing their research
