答案:
1. substances
2. clustered
3. compounds
4. expected
5. represents

sense_groups.english: Take a deep breath.
sense_groups.chinese: 深呼吸一下。

sense_groups.english: Taste anything?
sense_groups.chinese: 尝到什么味道了吗？

sense_groups.english: Actually, your lungs may.
sense_groups.chinese: 实际上，你的肺可能尝到了。

sense_groups.english: Because scientists have discovered
sense_groups.chinese: 因为科学家发现，

sense_groups.english: that the same receptors that exist on the tongue to taste bitter substances
sense_groups.chinese: 舌头上用于品尝苦味物质的相同受体，

sense_groups.english: are also found on the smooth muscle of the lungs.
sense_groups.chinese: 也存在于肺的平滑肌上。

sense_groups.english: Researchers were studying the receptors on smooth lung muscles
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员正在研究肺平滑肌上的受体，

sense_groups.english: that regulate contraction and relaxation of the airways.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些受体调节气道的收缩和放松。

sense_groups.english: That's when they made the discovery—
sense_groups.chinese: 就在那时他们有了这个发现——

sense_groups.english: which was so unexpected
sense_groups.chinese: 这个发现如此出乎意料，

sense_groups.english: that the researchers themselves were skeptical.
sense_groups.chinese: 以至于研究人员自己都持怀疑态度。

sense_groups.english: Finally, they became convinced
sense_groups.chinese: 最终，他们确信

sense_groups.english: that the receptors were really there,
sense_groups.chinese: 这些受体确实存在，

sense_groups.english: though not clustered in taste buds as they are on the tongue.
sense_groups.chinese: 尽管不像在舌头上那样聚集在味蕾中。

sense_groups.english: The scientists then exposed human and mouse airways
sense_groups.chinese: 随后，科学家将人类和小鼠的气道

sense_groups.english: to various bitter compounds
sense_groups.chinese: 暴露于各种苦味化合物中，

sense_groups.english: to gauge the effects.
sense_groups.chinese: 以评估其效果。

sense_groups.english: Many toxic compounds are bitter,
sense_groups.chinese: 许多有毒化合物是苦的，

sense_groups.english: so the researchers expected the lung muscle to tense up and contract—
sense_groups.chinese: 所以研究人员预期肺肌肉会紧张收缩——

sense_groups.english: to compel the breather to move away
sense_groups.chinese: 迫使呼吸者远离

sense_groups.english: from whatever was bitter and perhaps toxic.
sense_groups.chinese: 任何苦的、可能有毒的东西。

sense_groups.english: But, in a second surprise,
sense_groups.chinese: 但，第二个意外是，

sense_groups.english: bitter compounds relaxed and opened airways
sense_groups.chinese: 苦味化合物放松并打开了气道，

sense_groups.english: better than any existing asthma drug.
sense_groups.chinese: 效果比任何现有的哮喘药物都好。

sense_groups.english: The study is in the journal Nature Medicine.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《自然医学》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: Researchers will continue to search
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员将继续探索

sense_groups.english: for the role of the receptors.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些受体的作用。

sense_groups.english: Meanwhile, the work represents
sense_groups.chinese: 同时，这项工作代表着

sense_groups.english: a surprising new lead
sense_groups.chinese: 一个令人惊讶的新线索，

sense_groups.english: in the search for drugs to treat asthma, emphysema or chronic bronchitis.
sense_groups.chinese: 在寻找治疗哮喘、肺气肿或慢性支气管炎的药物方面。

questions.name: #164 Trust and Lie
questions.en:
When you think of someone who's trusting, you may assume that they're gullible.
But that's not necessarily true—a fact that your Pollyanna pal might be in a good ______ to point out.
Because people who have faith in their fellow human beings are actually good at ______ lies.
The finding is described in the journal Social Psychological and ______ Science.
Researchers videotaped a cadre of second-year MBA ______ as they pretended to interview for a job.
Half the interviewees were entirely truthful, and half told at least three whoppers, lies they thought would make them more attractive candidates for the fake job.
The scientists then showed these videos to a second set of subjects and asked them to rate the honesty of the interviewees and say which ones they'd hire.
The results: subjects who said they think that most people are basically honest, good-natured, and kind were better at spotting the liars than the self-described cynics.
  ______ who were more suspicious were, ironically, more likely to hire the liars and less likely to detect their fabrications.
So trust may lend itself to better interpersonal intuition.
And if you don't believe that, well, maybe you're just not being honest with yourself.

sense_groups.english: When you think of someone who's trusting,

questions.name: #165 Bloody Mary
questions.en:
2011 is the ______ Year of Chemistry.
So scientists at the national meeting of the American Chemical Society in Anaheim raised a glass.
Or a beaker.
And they celebrated as only chemists can—by ______ analyzing its contents.
The drink they ______ was the Bloody Mary, perhaps the world's most ______ complex cocktail.
A mix of tomato juice and vodka, along with lemon or lime, horseradish, Tabasco and Worcestershire sauces, black pepper and celery salt, the Bloody Mary packs a punch.
And it lights up nearly our entire range of taste receptors, giving us sweet, salty, sour and savory.
To find out the Bloody Mary's secret, researchers shared one with a chromatograph, which identified the various compounds that ______ to the drink's flavor and bouquet.
The scientists turned up plenty of antioxidants, as well as a few bartending tips.
First, make it fresh.
The acids in tomato juice can degrade the drink's other ingredients.
Also, make it cold—ice slows the degradation.
Use the best tomato juice—the major source of flavor.
But feel free to cheap out on the vodka.
Its taste gets lost in the mix.
In other words, chemists say to save the Grey Goose for other experiments.

5. contribute

sense_groups.english: 2011 is the International Year of Chemistry.
sense_groups.chinese: 2011年是国际化学年。

sense_groups.english: So scientists at the national meeting of the American Chemical Society in Anaheim raised a glass.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，在阿纳海姆举行的美国化学学会全国会议上，科学家们举起了酒杯。

sense_groups.english: Or a beaker.
sense_groups.chinese: 或者一个烧杯。

sense_groups.english: And they celebrated as only chemists can—by carefully analyzing its contents.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们以只有化学家才能做到的方式庆祝——仔细分析其内容。

sense_groups.english: The drink they dissected was the Bloody Mary, perhaps the world's most chemically complex cocktail.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们剖析的饮品是血腥玛丽，也许是世界上化学成分最复杂的鸡尾酒。

sense_groups.english: A mix of tomato juice and vodka, along with lemon or lime, horseradish, Tabasco and Worcestershire sauces, black pepper and celery salt, the Bloody Mary packs a punch.
sense_groups.chinese: 由番茄汁和伏特加混合，加上柠檬或酸橙、辣根、塔巴斯科辣酱和伍斯特酱、黑胡椒和芹菜盐，血腥玛丽口感强烈。

sense_groups.english: And it lights up nearly our entire range of taste receptors, giving us sweet, salty, sour and savory.
sense_groups.chinese: 它几乎激活了我们所有的味觉感受器，带来甜、咸、酸和鲜味。

sense_groups.english: To find out the Bloody Mary's secret, researchers shared one with a chromatograph, which identified the various compounds that contribute to the drink's flavor and bouquet.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了找出血腥玛丽的秘密，研究人员用色谱仪分析了一杯，识别出各种对饮品风味和香气有贡献的化合物。

sense_groups.english: The scientists turned up plenty of antioxidants, as well as a few bartending tips.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们发现了大量的抗氧化剂，以及一些调酒技巧。

sense_groups.english: First, make it fresh.
sense_groups.chinese: 首先，要新鲜调制。

sense_groups.english: The acids in tomato juice can degrade the drink's other ingredients.
sense_groups.chinese: 番茄汁中的酸会降解饮品的其他成分。

sense_groups.english: Also, make it cold—ice slows the degradation.
sense_groups.chinese: 另外，要冰镇——冰块能减缓降解。

questions.name: #168 HIW
questions.en:
Saturn's largest moon, Titan, has a thick atmosphere.
Clouds.
Complex organic molecules.
NASA has called it "one of the most Earth-like worlds we have found to date." With one glaring exception.
"It's awfully cold down there.
It's about 94 degrees Kelvin.
Which means that water would be a rock."
Paulette Clancy, a chemical engineer at Cornell University.
At temperatures that cold—minus 290 degrees Fahrenheit—one of the most basic biological structures, the cell membrane, can't exist.
Because to form, the oily membranes depend on the presence of liquid water.
That said, Titan does have plenty of liquid to go around—but it's liquid methane.
So Clancy and her colleagues used ______ models to determine whether any ______ on Titan might mimic the membrane-forming compounds here on Earth.
Based on a catalogue of ______ observed by NASA's Cassini mission, they found a candidate: acrylonitrile.
Its internal ______ charge distribution would allow it to self-assemble into membranes, just like phospholipids do here on Earth.
It's similarly flexible and stable.
And there's a lot of it on Titan.
The findings are in the journal Science Advances.
Of course just because a cell membrane could form, does not mean it will.
And actual life is a good deal more complicated than just a membrane.
Still, Clancy says we might do well to expand the search for life beyond just places with liquid water.
"I think we tend to look for things that we know and understand.
If we were more broad-minded we might find ______ kinds of life elsewhere.
And maybe that would be ______ too."
questions.answer:

2. molecules
3. organics
4. electrical
5. different

Saturn's largest moon, Titan, has a thick atmosphere.
Clouds.

"It's awfully cold down there.
It's about 94 degrees Kelvin.
Which means that water would be a rock."

Because to form, the oily membranes depend on the presence of liquid water.

sense_groups.english: Saturn's largest moon, Titan, has a thick atmosphere.
sense_groups.chinese: 土星最大的卫星土卫六有厚厚的大气层。

sense_groups.english: Clouds.
sense_groups.chinese: 云层。

sense_groups.english: Complex organic molecules.
sense_groups.chinese: 复杂的有机分子。

sense_groups.english: NASA has called it "one of the most Earth-like worlds we have found to date."
sense_groups.chinese: 美国宇航局称它是“迄今为止我们发现的最像地球的世界之一”。

sense_groups.english: With one glaring exception.
sense_groups.chinese: 但有一个明显的例外。

sense_groups.english: "It's awfully cold down there.
sense_groups.chinese: “那里非常寒冷。

sense_groups.english: It's about 94 degrees Kelvin.
sense_groups.chinese: 温度大约为94开尔文。

sense_groups.english: Which means that water would be a rock."
sense_groups.chinese: 这意味着水会像岩石一样。”

sense_groups.english: Paulette Clancy, a chemical engineer at Cornell University.
sense_groups.chinese: 康奈尔大学的化学工程师波莱特·克兰西说。

sense_groups.english: At temperatures that cold—minus 290 degrees Fahrenheit—one of the most basic biological structures, the cell membrane, can't exist.
sense_groups.chinese: 在如此低温（零下290华氏度）下，最基本的生物结构之一——细胞膜——无法存在。

sense_groups.english: Because to form, the oily membranes depend on the presence of liquid water.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为油性膜的形成依赖于液态水的存在。

sense_groups.english: That said, Titan does have plenty of liquid to go around—but it's liquid methane.
sense_groups.chinese: 尽管如此，土卫六确实有大量液体存在——但那是液态甲烷。

sense_groups.english: So Clancy and her colleagues used computer models to determine whether any molecules on Titan might mimic the membrane-forming compounds here on Earth.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，克兰西和她的同事使用计算机模型来确定土卫六上是否有任何分子可以模仿地球上形成膜的化合物。

sense_groups.english: Based on a catalogue of organics observed by NASA's Cassini mission, they found a candidate: acrylonitrile.
sense_groups.chinese: 根据美国宇航局卡西尼号任务观测到的有机物目录，他们找到了一个候选者：丙烯腈。

sense_groups.english: Its internal electrical charge distribution would allow it to self-assemble into membranes, just like phospholipids do here on Earth.
sense_groups.chinese: 其内部电荷分布使其能够自组装成膜，就像地球上的磷脂一样。

sense_groups.english: It's similarly flexible and stable.
sense_groups.chinese: 它同样灵活且稳定。

sense_groups.english: And there's a lot of it on Titan.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且土卫六上有很多这种物质。

sense_groups.english: The findings are in the journal Science Advances.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《科学进展》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: Of course just because a cell membrane could form, does not mean it will.
sense_groups.chinese: 当然，细胞膜能够形成并不意味着它一定会形成。

sense_groups.english: And actual life is a good deal more complicated than just a membrane.
sense_groups.chinese: 而真正的生命远比一层膜复杂得多。

sense_groups.english: Still, Clancy says we might do well to expand the search for life beyond just places with liquid water.
sense_groups.chinese: 尽管如此，克兰西说，我们或许应该将寻找生命的范围扩大到液态水之外的地方。

sense_groups.english: "I think we tend to look for things that we know and understand.
sense_groups.chinese: “我认为我们倾向于寻找我们已知和理解的东西。

sense_groups.english: If we were more broad-minded we might find different kinds of life elsewhere.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果我们思想更开阔，也许会在其他地方发现不同种类的生命。

sense_groups.english: And maybe that would be fascinating too."
sense_groups.chinese: 而且那可能也会很迷人。”

questions.name: #169 Sodium in Bread
questions.en:
Plan on breaking bread with friends and family this holiday season, but worried about the salt?
Well, chemists may have come up with an ______ solution.
They've discovered that bread that's more airy tastes saltier.
The finding is in the Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry.
There's sodium ______ in everything we eat.
It enhances flavor and improves the shelf life of foods.
But too much salt can contribute to hypertension, and baked goods top the list of offenders.
So can we cut back on sodium without saying no to dinner rolls?
To find out, ______ hit the kitchen and they whipped up some loaves with the same amount of salt but with ______ textures.
By adjusting how long they allowed the dough to rise, they made breads that were either fine-grained and dense or more porous and light.
And they found that ______ rated the fluffier bread as tasting more briny.
By collecting samples of their subjects' spit, the researchers determined that bread with larger pores releases its sodium faster when it's chewed.
It's that rush of sodium that makes salt a mouthwatering saline sensation—even if there's less of it.
questions.full:
Plan on breaking bread with friends and family this holiday season, but worried about the salt?
Well, chemists may have come up with an ______ solution.
They've discovered that bread that's more airy tastes saltier.
The finding is in the Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry.
There's sodium ______ in everything we eat.
It enhances flavor and improves the shelf life of foods.
But too much salt can contribute to hypertension, and baked goods top the list of offenders.
So can we cut back on sodium without saying no to dinner rolls?
To find out, ______ hit the kitchen and they whipped up some loaves with the same amount of salt but with ______ textures.
By adjusting how long they allowed the dough to rise, they made breads that were either fine-grained and dense or more porous and light.
And they found that ______ rated the fluffier bread as tasting more briny.
By collecting samples of their subjects' spit, the researchers determined that bread with larger pores releases its sodium faster when it's chewed.
It's that rush of sodium that makes salt a mouthwatering saline sensation—even if there's less of it.

答案:
1. enlightening
2. chloride
3. researchers
4. different
5. volunteers

sense_groups.english: Plan on breaking bread with friends and family this holiday season, but worried about the salt?
sense_groups.chinese: 打算在这个假期与朋友和家人一起吃饭，但担心盐分吗？

sense_groups.english: Well, chemists may have come up with an enlightening solution.
sense_groups.chinese: 嗯，化学家们可能想出了一个有启发性的解决方案。

sense_groups.english: They've discovered that bread that's more airy tastes saltier.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现，更蓬松的面包尝起来更咸。

sense_groups.english: The finding is in the Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry.
sense_groups.chinese: 这一发现发表在《农业与食品化学杂志》上。

sense_groups.english: There's sodium chloride in everything we eat.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们吃的所有东西里都含有氯化钠。

sense_groups.english: It enhances flavor and improves the shelf life of foods.
sense_groups.chinese: 它能增强风味并延长食品的保质期。

sense_groups.english: But too much salt can contribute to hypertension, and baked goods top the list of offenders.
sense_groups.chinese: 但过多的盐会导致高血压，而烘焙食品是罪魁祸首之首。

sense_groups.english: So can we cut back on sodium without saying no to dinner rolls?
sense_groups.chinese: 那么，我们能否在不拒绝晚餐面包卷的情况下减少钠的摄入呢？

sense_groups.english: To find out, researchers hit the kitchen and they whipped up some loaves with the same amount of salt but with different textures.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了找到答案，研究人员进入厨房，制作了一些盐量相同但质地不同的面包。

sense_groups.english: By adjusting how long they allowed the dough to rise, they made breads that were either fine-grained and dense or more porous and light.
sense_groups.chinese: 通过调整面团发酵的时间，他们制作了要么细密紧实、要么多孔轻盈的面包。

sense_groups.english: And they found that volunteers rated the fluffier bread as tasting more briny.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现，志愿者认为更蓬松的面包尝起来更咸。

sense_groups.english: By collecting samples of their subjects' spit, the researchers determined that bread with larger pores releases its sodium faster when it's chewed.
sense_groups.chinese: 通过收集受试者的唾液样本，研究人员确定，孔隙较大的面包在咀嚼时释放钠的速度更快。

sense_groups.english: It's that rush of sodium that makes salt a mouthwatering saline sensation—even if there's less of it.
sense_groups.chinese: 正是这种钠的快速释放，让盐产生令人垂涎的咸味——即使含量更少。

questions.name: #170 Drinking and Pregnancy
questions.en:
Pregnant women shouldn't drink.
It's become gospel, because of the danger of fetal alcohol spectrum disorder.
Alcohol can disturb the normal development of a fetus, leading to a lifetime of learning ______ and social problems.
But the ______ of children born with the ______ has remained constant, despite the warnings.
And not all fetuses of drinking mothers suffer.
Now research with rats has shown why some fetuses are naturally protected.
Which could lead to ways to protect the vulnerable ones.
The work is in the FASEB Journal.
The key is a gene called Dio3, which governs the levels of thyroid hormone in the brain.
If mom passes on a normal Dio3, no problem.
And a male fetus that inherits a problem Dio3 ______ from mom but a normal Dio3 from dad should be okay.
But alcohol can stop dad's normal Dio3 gene from working.
Now mom's bad Dio3 allows the brain to be flooded with thyroid hormone, ______ the hippocampus.
The hope is that gene screening could ID women whose fetuses would be at-risk, and that dietary supplements or drugs could block alcohol's effect.
And keep a child from suffering from a parent's addiction.
questions.full:
Pregnant women shouldn't drink.
It's become gospel, because of the danger of fetal alcohol spectrum disorder.
Alcohol can disturb the normal development of a fetus, leading to a lifetime of learning ______ and social problems.
But the ______ of children born with the ______ has remained constant, despite the warnings.

If mom passes on a normal Dio3, no problem.
And a male fetus that inherits a problem Dio3 ______ from mom but a normal Dio3 from dad should be okay.
But alcohol can stop dad's normal Dio3 gene from working.
Now mom's bad Dio3 allows the brain to be flooded with thyroid hormone, ______ the hippocampus.
The hope is that gene screening could ID women whose fetuses would be at-risk, and that dietary supplements or drugs could block alcohol's effect.
And keep a child from suffering from a parent's addiction.

答案:
1. disabilities
2. percentage
3. disorder
4. variation
5. damaging

sense_groups.english: Pregnant women shouldn't drink.
sense_groups.chinese: 孕妇不应该喝酒。

sense_groups.english: It's become gospel, because of the danger of fetal alcohol spectrum disorder.
sense_groups.chinese: 这已成为金科玉律，因为存在胎儿酒精谱系障碍的风险。

sense_groups.english: Alcohol can disturb the normal development of a fetus, leading to a lifetime of learning disabilities and social problems.
sense_groups.chinese: 酒精会干扰胎儿的正常发育，导致终身的学习障碍和社交问题。

sense_groups.english: But the percentage of children born with the disorder has remained constant, despite the warnings.
sense_groups.chinese: 但尽管有这些警告，患有该障碍的儿童出生比例却保持不变。

sense_groups.english: And not all fetuses of drinking mothers suffer.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且并非所有饮酒母亲所怀的胎儿都会受到影响。

sense_groups.english: Now research with rats has shown why some fetuses are naturally protected.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，对大鼠的研究揭示了为什么有些胎儿天生受到保护。

sense_groups.english: Which could lead to ways to protect the vulnerable ones.
sense_groups.chinese: 这可能会带来保护脆弱胎儿的方法。

sense_groups.english: The work is in the FASEB Journal.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《FASEB期刊》上。

sense_groups.english: The key is a gene called Dio3, which governs the levels of thyroid hormone in the brain.
sense_groups.chinese: 关键是一种名为Dio3的基因，它控制着大脑中甲状腺激素的水平。

sense_groups.english: If mom passes on a normal Dio3, no problem.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果母亲遗传了正常的Dio3，就没有问题。

sense_groups.english: And a male fetus that inherits a problem Dio3 variation from mom but a normal Dio3 from dad should be okay.
sense_groups.chinese: 而一个从母亲那里遗传了有问题的Dio3变异、但从父亲那里遗传了正常Dio3的男性胎儿应该也没事。

sense_groups.english: But alcohol can stop dad's normal Dio3 gene from working.
sense_groups.chinese: 但酒精会阻止父亲正常的Dio3基因发挥作用。

sense_groups.english: Now mom's bad Dio3 allows the brain to be flooded with thyroid hormone, damaging the hippocampus.
sense_groups.chinese: 这时母亲有缺陷的Dio3会让大脑充满甲状腺激素，损害海马体。

sense_groups.english: The hope is that gene screening could ID women whose fetuses would be at-risk, and that dietary supplements or drugs could block alcohol's effect.
sense_groups.chinese: 希望在于基因筛查可以识别出胎儿有风险的女性，并且膳食补充剂或药物可以阻断酒精的影响。

sense_groups.english: And keep a child from suffering from a parent's addiction.
sense_groups.chinese: 从而防止孩子因父母的成瘾而受苦。

questions.name: #171 Yeast
questions.en:
Yeast.
They already participate in producing some of the most popular pain-killing substances around: beer and wine.
Now, ______ have engineered yeast that can also make one of the most powerful analgesics: morphine.
Their work is in the journal Nature Chemical Biology.
Opiates like ______ and codeine are essential for treating severe pain.
But making these meds isn't easy.
All are derived from opium poppies, and tens to hundreds of thousands of tons are needed to meet global needs.
The crops can also be affected by climate, disease and even political turmoil in the countries where the plants are grown, which further limits commercial production.
To get around these ______ challenges, researchers have turned to yeast, an organism that can be grown easily on ______ scales.
The scientists inserted into yeast cells a handful of genes isolated from the opium poppy.
These genes encode the enzymes the plants use to produce opiates.
After tweaking the system to adjust the ______ amounts of the enzymes, the researchers could feed their yeast a precursor chemical called thebaine, and get pure morphine in return.
The yeast can't yet make opiates from scratch.
But with a bit more effort and a few more enzymes, yeast may produce ______ that are prescription strength.
questions.answer:
1. scientists
2. morphine
3. potential
4. industrial
5. relative
6. painkillers
questions.full:
Yeast.
They already participate in producing some of the most popular pain-killing substances around: beer and wine.
Now, ______ have engineered yeast that can also make one of the most powerful analgesics: morphine.

But with a bit more effort and a few more enzymes, yeast may produce ______ that are prescription strength.

答案:
1. scientists
2. morphine
3. potential
4. industrial
5. relative
6. painkillers

sense_groups.english: Yeast.
sense_groups.chinese: 酵母。

sense_groups.english: They already participate in producing some of the most popular pain-killing substances around: beer and wine.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们已经参与生产一些最流行的止痛物质：啤酒和葡萄酒。

sense_groups.english: Now, scientists have engineered yeast that can also make one of the most powerful analgesics: morphine.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，科学家们已经改造了酵母，使其也能制造最强大的镇痛剂之一：吗啡。

sense_groups.english: Their work is in the journal Nature Chemical Biology.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们的研究成果发表在《自然化学生物学》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: Opiates like morphine and codeine are essential for treating severe pain.
sense_groups.chinese: 像吗啡和可待因这样的阿片类药物对于治疗剧烈疼痛至关重要。

sense_groups.english: But making these meds isn't easy.
sense_groups.chinese: 但制造这些药物并不容易。

sense_groups.english: All are derived from opium poppies, and tens to hundreds of thousands of tons are needed to meet global needs.
sense_groups.chinese: 所有药物都来自罂粟，需要数十万到数百万吨才能满足全球需求。

sense_groups.english: The crops can also be affected by climate, disease and even political turmoil in the countries where the plants are grown, which further limits commercial production.
sense_groups.chinese: 作物还可能受到气候、疾病甚至种植国政治动荡的影响，这进一步限制了商业生产。

sense_groups.english: To get around these potential challenges, researchers have turned to yeast, an organism that can be grown easily on industrial scales.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了绕过这些潜在的挑战，研究人员转向了酵母，这种生物可以很容易地大规模工业化培养。

sense_groups.english: The scientists inserted into yeast cells a handful of genes isolated from the opium poppy.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们将一些从罂粟中分离出来的基因插入酵母细胞中。

sense_groups.english: These genes encode the enzymes the plants use to produce opiates.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些基因编码了植物用于生产阿片类药物的酶。

sense_groups.english: After tweaking the system to adjust the relative amounts of the enzymes, the researchers could feed their yeast a precursor chemical called thebaine, and get pure morphine in return.
sense_groups.chinese: 在调整系统以调节酶的相对含量后，研究人员可以给他们的酵母喂食一种名为蒂巴因的前体化学物质，然后得到纯吗啡。

sense_groups.english: The yeast can't yet make opiates from scratch.
sense_groups.chinese: 酵母还不能从零开始制造阿片类药物。

sense_groups.english: But with a bit more effort and a few more enzymes, yeast may produce painkillers that are prescription strength.
sense_groups.chinese: 但再努力一点，加入更多的酶，酵母可能会生产出处方强度的止痛药。

questions.name: #172 Birth Control Pill
questions.en:
Some people like to think there's something fated about who we fall in love with.
It's that perfect mix of attraction, compatibility, and of course timing.
But in some cases, fate may be taking its cues from birth control pills.
First, let's go over a woman's cycle and how that affects attraction.
When women are ovulating, their ______ change in ways that men unconsciously pick up.
So men are particularly ______ to women when they're fertile.
And it works the other way, too.
When a woman is fertile, she's more attracted to men with more traditionally masculine features and who are ______ dissimilar to her, or more compatible in terms of procreating.
Of course oral contraception changes a woman's ______ cycles.
Her body thinks it's pregnant and doesn't go through ovulation-induced changes.
And in a study published this month in the journal Trends in Ecology and Evolution, researchers say that women on the pill do not show the ovulation-induced ______ to genetically dissimilar partners.
So they might be choosing men who are more genetically similar—which could lead to some of the problems with conception that have become ______ common.
Because attraction isn't fate.
It's chemistry.
questions.answer:
1. features
2. attracted
3. genetically
4. hormonal
5. attraction
6. increasingly

sense_groups.english: Some people like to think there's something fated about who we fall in love with.
sense_groups.chinese: 有些人喜欢认为，我们爱上谁是有某种宿命的。

sense_groups.english: It's that perfect mix of attraction, compatibility, and of course timing.
sense_groups.chinese: 那是吸引力、兼容性，当然还有时机的完美结合。

sense_groups.english: But in some cases, fate may be taking its cues from birth control pills.
sense_groups.chinese: 但在某些情况下，命运可能是在听从避孕药的指示。

sense_groups.english: First, let's go over a woman's cycle and how that affects attraction.
sense_groups.chinese: 首先，我们来回顾一下女性的周期以及它如何影响吸引力。

sense_groups.english: When women are ovulating, their features change in ways that men unconsciously pick up.
sense_groups.chinese: 当女性排卵时，她们的特征会以男性无意识察觉的方式发生变化。

sense_groups.english: So men are particularly attracted to women when they're fertile.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以男性在女性生育期时特别被她们吸引。

sense_groups.english: And it works the other way, too.
sense_groups.chinese: 反过来也是如此。

sense_groups.english: When a woman is fertile, she's more attracted to men with more traditionally masculine features and who are genetically dissimilar to her, or more compatible in terms of procreating.
sense_groups.chinese: 当女性处于生育期时，她更容易被具有更传统男性特征、基因上与自己不同、或者说在生育方面更兼容的男性所吸引。

sense_groups.english: Of course oral contraception changes a woman's hormonal cycles.
sense_groups.chinese: 当然，口服避孕药会改变女性的激素周期。

sense_groups.english: Her body thinks it's pregnant and doesn't go through ovulation-induced changes.
sense_groups.chinese: 她的身体认为自己怀孕了，因此不会经历排卵引起的变化。

sense_groups.english: And in a study published this month in the journal Trends in Ecology and Evolution, researchers say that women on the pill do not show the ovulation-induced attraction to genetically dissimilar partners.
sense_groups.chinese: 在本月发表在《生态学与进化趋势》期刊上的一项研究中，研究人员表示，服用避孕药的女性不会表现出排卵引起的对基因不同伴侣的吸引力。

sense_groups.english: So they might be choosing men who are more genetically similar—which could lead to some of the problems with conception that have become increasingly common.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，她们可能会选择基因更相似的男性——这可能导致一些日益常见的受孕问题。

sense_groups.english: Because attraction isn't fate.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为吸引力不是命运。

sense_groups.english: It's chemistry.
sense_groups.chinese: 它是化学反应。

questions.name: #173 HIW
questions.en:
When the first shots were fired at JFK's motorcade, police couldn't ______ locate the gunman based on sound alone.
Today, the technology exists for them to it with their smartphones, less than a second after the first shot.
Here's how.
Most bullets travel at supersonic speeds, ______ a shock wave along their path.
To track that path, researchers built a small bluetooth sensor for smartphones.
The sensor uses four mics to measure the shock wave's angle, and its time of arrival.
Then each phone ______ with nearby phones to triangulate the sniper's location, mapping it on the smartphone screen within a second of the gun blast.
Researchers tested the system with an AK-47, and were able to calculate the shooter's bearings with less than seven degrees of error, and get a decent ______ of his range.
They ______ the method at the Conference on Information Processing in Sensor ______ in Philadelphia.
Since the system ______ at least two phones to work, researchers say it would be ideal for a security force fanned out around a likely target—allowing them to respond to threats almost as fast as a speeding bullet.
questions.answer:
1. immediately
2. generating
3. networks
4. estimate
5. presented
6. Networks
7. requires
questions.full:
When the first shots were fired at JFK's motorcade, police couldn't ______ locate the gunman based on sound alone.
Today, the technology exists for them to it with their smartphones, less than a second after the first shot.
Here's how.

To track that path, researchers built a small bluetooth sensor for smartphones.
The sensor uses four mics to measure the shock wave's angle, and its time of arrival.
Then each phone ______ with nearby phones to triangulate the sniper's location, mapping it on the smartphone screen within a second of the gun blast.
Researchers tested the system with an AK-47, and were able to calculate the shooter's bearings with less than seven degrees of error, and get a decent ______ of his range.
They ______ the method at the Conference on Information Processing in Sensor ______ in Philadelphia.
Since the system ______ at least two phones to work, researchers say it would be ideal for a security force fanned out around a likely target—allowing them to respond to threats almost as fast as a speeding bullet.

答案:
1. immediately
2. generating
3. networks
4. estimate
5. presented
6. Networks
7. requires

sense_groups.english: When the first shots were fired at JFK's motorcade,
sense_groups.chinese: 当第一声枪响在肯尼迪总统车队响起时，

sense_groups.english: police couldn't immediately locate the gunman based on sound alone.
sense_groups.chinese: 警方无法仅凭声音立即定位枪手。

sense_groups.english: Today, the technology exists for them to do it with their smartphones,
sense_groups.chinese: 如今，技术已经存在，他们可以用智能手机做到这一点，

sense_groups.english: less than a second after the first shot.
sense_groups.chinese: 在第一声枪响后不到一秒钟。

sense_groups.english: Here's how.
sense_groups.chinese: 方法如下。

sense_groups.english: Most bullets travel at supersonic speeds,
sense_groups.chinese: 大多数子弹以超音速飞行，

sense_groups.english: generating a shock wave along their path.
sense_groups.chinese: 沿路径产生冲击波。

sense_groups.english: To track that path, researchers built a small bluetooth sensor for smartphones.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了追踪这条路径，研究人员为智能手机制造了一个小型蓝牙传感器。

sense_groups.english: The sensor uses four mics to measure the shock wave's angle, and its time of arrival.
sense_groups.chinese: 该传感器使用四个麦克风测量冲击波的角度和到达时间。

sense_groups.english: Then each phone communicates with nearby phones
sense_groups.chinese: 然后每部手机与附近的手机通信，

sense_groups.english: to triangulate the sniper's location,
sense_groups.chinese: 以三角测量狙击手的位置，

sense_groups.english: mapping it on the smartphone screen within a second of the gun blast.
sense_groups.chinese: 在枪响后一秒钟内将其映射到智能手机屏幕上。

sense_groups.english: Researchers tested the system with an AK-47,
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员用AK-47测试了该系统，

sense_groups.english: and were able to calculate the shooter's bearings
sense_groups.chinese: 并能够计算出射手的方位，

sense_groups.english: with less than seven degrees of error,
sense_groups.chinese: 误差小于七度，

sense_groups.english: and get a decent estimate of his range.
sense_groups.chinese: 并获得对其距离的合理估计。

sense_groups.english: They presented the method
sense_groups.chinese: 他们展示了该方法

sense_groups.english: at the Conference on Information Processing in Sensor Networks
sense_groups.chinese: 在传感器网络信息处理会议上

sense_groups.english: in Philadelphia.
sense_groups.chinese: 在费城。

sense_groups.english: Since the system requires at least two phones to work,
sense_groups.chinese: 由于该系统需要至少两部手机才能工作，

sense_groups.english: researchers say it would be ideal for a security force
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员表示，它对于一支安全部队来说非常理想，

sense_groups.english: fanned out around a likely target—
sense_groups.chinese: 分散在可能的目标周围——

sense_groups.english: allowing them to respond to threats
sense_groups.chinese: 使他们能够应对威胁，

sense_groups.english: almost as fast as a speeding bullet.
sense_groups.chinese: 几乎和飞驰的子弹一样快。

questions.name: #174 Epidemic
questions.en:
The epidemic swept the world.
Fortunately, it was only the World of Warcraft, a popular online role-playing game.
But that got the attention of real disease experts at Tufts and Rutgers Universities.
That's because the ______ outbreak that attacked the virtual ______ offered a unique opportunity to study how social groups can help spread a disease.
In late 2005 the epidemic hit the World of Warcraft, played by millions.
It all started with an error.
One creature was supposed to infect only a few virtual players with so-called corrupted blood.
But some of the nastiest virtual ______ exploited a flaw and spread the disease to unsuspecting masses.
The virtual quarantines game ______ tried to impose didn't work, in part because the virtual people didn't follow them, and so entire virtual cities were virtually destroyed.
The experts were fascinated because they've have never had a way to realistically simulate how large groups of people will react to an epidemic.
But the cure for a real epidemic still won't be as easy as the virtual one was—they just reprogrammed the computers.
questions.full:
The epidemic swept the world.
Fortunately, it was only the World of Warcraft, a popular online role-playing game.
But that got the attention of real disease experts at Tufts and Rutgers Universities.
That's because the ______ outbreak that attacked the virtual ______ offered a unique opportunity to study how social groups can help spread a disease.
In late 2005 the epidemic hit the World of Warcraft, played by millions.

One creature was supposed to infect only a few virtual players with so-called corrupted blood.
But some of the nastiest virtual ______ exploited a flaw and spread the disease to unsuspecting masses.
The virtual quarantines game ______ tried to impose didn't work, in part because the virtual people didn't follow them, and so entire virtual cities were virtually destroyed.
The experts were fascinated because they've have never had a way to realistically simulate how large groups of people will react to an epidemic.
But the cure for a real epidemic still won't be as easy as the virtual one was—they just reprogrammed the computers.

答案:
1. accidental
2. characters
3. inhabitants
4. designers

sense_groups.english: The epidemic swept the world.
sense_groups.chinese: 这场流行病席卷了世界。

sense_groups.english: Fortunately, it was only the World of Warcraft, a popular online role-playing game.
sense_groups.chinese: 幸运的是，它只是《魔兽世界》，一款流行的在线角色扮演游戏。

sense_groups.english: But that got the attention of real disease experts at Tufts and Rutgers Universities.
sense_groups.chinese: 但这引起了塔夫茨大学和罗格斯大学真实疾病专家的注意。

sense_groups.english: That's because the accidental outbreak that attacked the virtual inhabitants offered a unique opportunity to study how social groups can help spread a disease.
sense_groups.chinese: 这是因为这场意外爆发袭击了虚拟居民，为研究社会群体如何帮助传播疾病提供了独特的机会。

sense_groups.english: In late 2005 the epidemic hit the World of Warcraft, played by millions.
sense_groups.chinese: 2005年底，这场流行病袭击了有数百万人玩的《魔兽世界》。

sense_groups.english: It all started with an error.
sense_groups.chinese: 一切都始于一个错误。

sense_groups.english: One creature was supposed to infect only a few virtual players with so-called corrupted blood.
sense_groups.chinese: 一种生物本应只感染少数虚拟玩家，传播所谓的堕落之血。

sense_groups.english: But some of the nastiest virtual characters exploited a flaw and spread the disease to unsuspecting masses.
sense_groups.chinese: 但一些最恶劣的虚拟角色利用了一个漏洞，将疾病传播给了毫无戒心的大众。

sense_groups.english: The virtual quarantines game designers tried to impose didn't work, in part because the virtual people didn't follow them, and so entire virtual cities were virtually destroyed.
sense_groups.chinese: 游戏设计师试图强制实施的虚拟隔离没有奏效，部分原因是虚拟人物不遵守，因此整个虚拟城市几乎被摧毁。

sense_groups.english: The experts were fascinated because they've have never had a way to realistically simulate how large groups of people will react to an epidemic.
sense_groups.chinese: 专家们对此着迷，因为他们从未有过一种方法来真实模拟大量人群对流行病的反应。

sense_groups.english: But the cure for a real epidemic still won't be as easy as the virtual one was—they just reprogrammed the computers.
sense_groups.chinese: 但真实流行病的治疗仍然不会像虚拟的那样容易——他们只是重新编程了计算机。

questions.name: #175 Smoker's Teeth
questions.en:
It's no secret cigarettes can yellow your teeth.
But tobacco smoke has another, unseen effect.
It can wipe out the healthy ______ in your mouth, leaving the field open for pathogenic bugs—like the kind that cause gum disease.
So says a study in the journal Infection and Immunity.
Researchers gave a complete dental cleaning to 30 volunteers, half of whom were regular smokers.
Then, as bacteria moved back in, they took plaque samples and sequenced the DNA in those scrapings.
And they found that ______ tended to have stable bacterial communities, ______ by a few benign species.
That's good, because a healthy biofilm educates your immune system—preventing unnecessary attacks and inflammation—and it keeps bad bacteria at bay.
Smokers, on the other hand, had wildly transient populations, with species moving in and out—which opened up real estate for the bad bugs.
Smokers also had higher levels of inflammation, which can destroy ______ bacteria, too.
The ______ aren't sure yet why smoking has this effect.
But if you're looking for a new reason to quit, how about avoiding your dentist?
questions.full:
It's no secret cigarettes can yellow your teeth.
But tobacco smoke has another, unseen effect.
It can wipe out the healthy ______ in your mouth, leaving the field open for pathogenic bugs—like the kind that cause gum disease.
So says a study in the journal Infection and Immunity.
Researchers gave a complete dental cleaning to 30 volunteers, half of whom were regular smokers.
Then, as bacteria moved back in, they took plaque samples and sequenced the DNA in those scrapings.
And they found that ______ tended to have stable bacterial communities, ______ by a few benign species.
That's good, because a healthy biofilm educates your immune system—preventing unnecessary attacks and inflammation—and it keeps bad bacteria at bay.
Smokers, on the other hand, had wildly transient populations, with species moving in and out—which opened up real estate for the bad bugs.
Smokers also had higher levels of inflammation, which can destroy ______ bacteria, too.
The ______ aren't sure yet why smoking has this effect.
But if you're looking for a new reason to quit, how about avoiding your dentist?

答案:
1. bacteria
2. non-smokers
3. dominated
4. friendly
5. researchers

sense_groups.english: It's no secret cigarettes can yellow your teeth.
sense_groups.chinese: 众所周知，香烟会让牙齿变黄。

sense_groups.english: But tobacco smoke has another, unseen effect.
sense_groups.chinese: 但烟草烟雾还有另一种看不见的影响。

sense_groups.english: It can wipe out the healthy bacteria in your mouth,
sense_groups.chinese: 它会消灭口腔中的健康细菌，

sense_groups.english: leaving the field open for pathogenic bugs—like the kind that cause gum disease.
sense_groups.chinese: 为致病菌——比如导致牙龈疾病的细菌——敞开大门。

sense_groups.english: So says a study in the journal Infection and Immunity.
sense_groups.chinese: 《感染与免疫》期刊上的一项研究如是说。

sense_groups.english: Researchers gave a complete dental cleaning to 30 volunteers,
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员为30名志愿者进行了彻底的口腔清洁，

sense_groups.english: half of whom were regular smokers.
sense_groups.chinese: 其中一半是经常吸烟的人。

sense_groups.english: Then, as bacteria moved back in,
sense_groups.chinese: 然后，当细菌重新定植时，

sense_groups.english: they took plaque samples and sequenced the DNA in those scrapings.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们采集了牙菌斑样本，并对这些刮取物中的DNA进行了测序。

sense_groups.english: And they found that non-smokers tended to have stable bacterial communities,
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现，不吸烟者的细菌群落往往很稳定，

sense_groups.english: dominated by a few benign species.
sense_groups.chinese: 由少数良性物种主导。

sense_groups.english: That's good, because a healthy biofilm educates your immune system—
sense_groups.chinese: 这很好，因为健康的生物膜能训练你的免疫系统——

sense_groups.english: preventing unnecessary attacks and inflammation—
sense_groups.chinese: 防止不必要的攻击和炎症——

sense_groups.english: and it keeps bad bacteria at bay.
sense_groups.chinese: 并抑制有害细菌。

sense_groups.english: Smokers, on the other hand, had wildly transient populations,

questions.name: #176 Rumors and Internet
questions.en:
During the 2008 presidential election, the ______ became a giant rumor mill.
For example, there were the viral e-mails claiming that Barack Obama's birth ______ was a fake.
Or ones spreading the phony Sarah Palin quote, "God made dinosaurs 4,000 years ago".
Some political scholars worry the Web could undermine democracy, by ______ and polarizing voters.
But Web sites and blogs don't serve up the most ______ rumors.
Our in-boxes do.
So says a study of e-mail in the journal Human Communication Research.
Just after the election, researcher R. Kelly Garrett randomly surveyed 600 ______ about their online habits, and whether they'd heard—and believed—a number of ______ rumors.
He found that the Web does expose us to more rumors.
But the Web also delivers more rebuttals, which can even the field.
E-mail's more insidious.
Because you're more likely to believe that rumor forwarded by cousin Rob.
And the more you believe something, Garrett says, the more you want to share it with your social network—spawning a nasty cascade of misperception.
So before you hit SEND to forward e-mail, ask yourself: Do I know the item I'm sharing is true, or do I just want it to be?
questions.answer:
1. Internet
2. certificate
3. misinforming
4. influential
5. Americans
6. widespread
questions.full:
During the 2008 presidential election, the ______ became a giant rumor mill.

sense_groups.english: During the 2008 presidential election, the Internet became a giant rumor mill.

sense_groups.english: For example, there were the viral e-mails claiming that Barack Obama's birth certificate was a fake.

sense_groups.english: Or ones spreading the phony Sarah Palin quote, "God made dinosaurs 4,000 years ago".
sense_groups.chinese: 或者有些邮件传播了萨拉·佩林的虚假引语：“上帝在4000年前创造了恐龙”。

sense_groups.english: Some political scholars worry the Web could undermine democracy, by misinforming and polarizing voters.

sense_groups.english: But Web sites and blogs don't serve up the most influential rumors.

sense_groups.chinese: 因为你更可能相信表兄罗布转发的那条谣言。

sense_groups.english: And the more you believe something, Garrett says, the more you want to share it with your social network—spawning a nasty cascade of misperception.

sense_groups.chinese: 所以在你点击发送转发邮件之前，问问自己：我知道我分享的内容是真的吗，还是我只是希望它是真的？

questions.name: #177 Mosquito Formation
questions.en:
Aha—got 'im!
Yes, the ______ are swarming this time of year.
Alaskans joke that the ______ is their state bird.

This collective, yet disordered, flight ______ ______ in Rome.

Flocks and schools move in formation only once the group reaches a critical density.

questions.name: #179 Bone and Weight
questions.en:
Some dinosaurs were really huge.
And now we may have a better way to ______ just how heavy these giants were.
Researchers have developed a method to weigh dinosaurs, based on laser scans of their skeletons.
The study is in the journal Biology Letters.
Looking at a bare human skeleton, how would you guess whether its owner was chubby or svelte?
If you calculated how much space the fully-fleshed body occupied, you could ______ that volume by tissue density to find the weight.
Researchers laser-scanned 14 modern mammal skeletons to create digital models of each body.
These 3-D models were unrealistically scrawny, with skin ______ tight over the bones.
But their undersized volumes were consistent, measuring in as 21 percent less than the actual animals.
Based on this information, the researchers scanned Giraffatitan bones, added 21 percent to the digital model's volume, and then calculated the dinosaur's weight: about 51,000 pounds.
The technique could become the ______ way to estimate mass based on skeletons, improving our understanding of how extinct species lived and moved.
And helping paleontologists make earth-shaking discoveries.
questions.full:

And now we may have a better way to ______ just how heavy these giants were.

The technique could become the ______ way to estimate mass based on skeletons, improving our understanding of how extinct species lived and moved.
And helping paleontologists make earth-shaking discoveries.

1. estimate
2. multiply
3. stretched
4. preferred

sense_groups.english: Some dinosaurs were really huge.
sense_groups.chinese: 有些恐龙真的非常巨大。

sense_groups.english: And now we may have a better way to estimate just how heavy these giants were.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，我们可能有更好的方法来估算这些庞然大物到底有多重。

sense_groups.english: Researchers have developed a method to weigh dinosaurs, based on laser scans of their skeletons.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员开发了一种基于激光扫描恐龙骨骼来称重的方法。

sense_groups.english: The study is in the journal Biology Letters.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《生物学快报》上。

sense_groups.english: Looking at a bare human skeleton, how would you guess whether its owner was chubby or svelte?
sense_groups.chinese: 看着一副裸露的人类骨骼，你会如何猜测它的主人是胖还是瘦？

sense_groups.english: If you calculated how much space the fully-fleshed body occupied, you could multiply that volume by tissue density to find the weight.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你计算出完整身体所占的空间，你可以将该体积乘以组织密度来得出重量。

sense_groups.english: Researchers laser-scanned 14 modern mammal skeletons to create digital models of each body.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员激光扫描了14具现代哺乳动物的骨骼，为每具身体创建了数字模型。

sense_groups.english: These 3-D models were unrealistically scrawny, with skin stretched tight over the bones.

sense_groups.english: But their undersized volumes were consistent, measuring in as 21 percent less than the actual animals.
sense_groups.chinese: 但它们偏小的体积是一致的，测量结果比实际动物少21%。

sense_groups.english: The technique could become the preferred way to estimate mass based on skeletons, improving our understanding of how extinct species lived and moved.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项技术可能成为基于骨骼估算质量的首选方法，增进我们对灭绝物种如何生活和移动的理解。

sense_groups.english: And helping paleontologists make earth-shaking discoveries.
sense_groups.chinese: 并帮助古生物学家做出惊天动地的发现。

sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究涉及海蜗牛，但可能适用于所有蜗牛，它们可能会消耗三分之一的总能量来产生黏液。

sense_groups.english: So an obvious benefit is that individual snails can save energy that would otherwise go into cutting fresh trails.

sense_groups.english: Snail experts had thought this was the case, but the new study proves it.
sense_groups.chinese: 蜗牛专家们之前就认为情况如此，但这项新研究证实了这一点。

sense_groups.english: And it wasn't easy—the researchers actually measured the thickness of snail trails.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且这并不容易——研究人员实际上测量了蜗牛痕迹的厚度。

sense_groups.english: But weathered trails got thicker, as snails added a bit of mucus where necessary.
sense_groups.chinese: 但风化后的痕迹变厚了，因为蜗牛在必要的地方添加了一点黏液。

sense_groups.english: Here's a strange tale of two previously unrelated food products.
sense_groups.chinese: 这里有个关于两种原本毫不相干食品的奇怪故事。

sense_groups.english: First: chitlins, that delicacy of fried pig large intestines.
sense_groups.chinese: 首先是炸猪大肠这道美味——chitlins。

sense_groups.english: They're well-loved throughout the South, especially during the upcoming holiday season.
sense_groups.chinese: 在美国南部很受欢迎，尤其是在即将到来的假日季节。

sense_groups.english: But the smell of them cooking inspires significantly less affection.
sense_groups.chinese: 但烹饪时的气味可就没那么讨人喜欢了。

sense_groups.english: Because the cooking process sometimes smells like, well, feces.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为烹饪过程有时闻起来就像……嗯，粪便。

sense_groups.english: Researchers in Japan thought that cilantro could help.
sense_groups.chinese: 日本的研究人员认为香菜或许能帮上忙。

sense_groups.english: Because cilantro is used in a variety of cuisines around the world to mask smells, as well as to add distinctive flavors.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为香菜在世界各地的多种菜系中被用来掩盖气味，同时增添独特风味。

sense_groups.english: And in a previous study, the research team had shown that cilantro can mask the cooking-chitlin stench.
sense_groups.chinese: 在之前的一项研究中，该研究团队已经证明香菜可以掩盖烹饪chitlins时的恶臭。

sense_groups.english: In the new research, in the Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry, they isolated cilantro's volatile compounds and tested each one for its odor-fighting power.
sense_groups.chinese: 在新研究中，发表在《农业与食品化学杂志》上，他们分离了香菜的挥发性化合物，并测试了每种化合物的除臭能力。

sense_groups.english: Many seemed to lessen the stink, but one in particular, according to human sniffers, entirely cancels out the odor.
sense_groups.chinese: 许多化合物似乎能减轻臭味，但据人类嗅探员称，有一种化合物能完全消除气味。

sense_groups.english: It's called (E,E)-2,4-Undecadienal.
sense_groups.chinese: 它叫做(E,E)-2,4-十一碳二烯醛。

sense_groups.english: It works at a very low concentration—10 parts per billion—so you can't smell the compound.
sense_groups.chinese: 它在极低浓度下就能起作用——十亿分之十——所以你闻不到这种化合物本身。

sense_groups.english: It's not masking the chitlin odor, it's actually neutralizing it.
sense_groups.chinese: 它并不是在掩盖chitlin的气味，而是在真正地中和它。

sense_groups.english: So it's not just better living through chemistry.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以这不仅仅是化学让生活更美好。

sense_groups.english: It's better chitlins too.
sense_groups.chinese: 也是更好的chitlins。

questions.name: #182 Good Bacteria
questions.en:
Sometimes a bit of ______ can be just what the doctor ordered.
If you prize yogurt for its "active cultures," you know what I'm talking about.
Now a new study, ______ in the September 21st online issue of Nature, suggests that good bugs might even hold ______ at bay.
Type I diabetes is caused by an immune system malfunction.
Basically, the immune cells that usually chase after bacteria instead attack the pancreas, wiping out the cells that produce insulin.
So researchers decided to see what would happen if they reigned in the immune response in mice that are prone to diabetes.
As expected, they found that the animals were less likely to develop the disease.
But the effect depended entirely on the critters having a normal complement of friendly bacteria in their intestine.
Mice that were raised in a totally sterile, germ-free environment were rampant diabetics.
But simply ______ those mice with a cocktail of bugs found in most mammals' bellies cured the disease.
How bacteria in the intestine can stave off diabetes is not yet clear.
But the finding could lead to some interesting new treatments.
In the meantime, ______ that we can't live without the stuff that lives in us.

But the finding could lead to some interesting new treatments.

答案:
1. bacteria
2. published
3. diabetes
4. treating
5. remember

sense_groups.english: Sometimes a bit of bacteria can be just what the doctor ordered.
sense_groups.chinese: 有时候，一点细菌可能正是医生所建议的。

sense_groups.english: If you prize yogurt for its "active cultures," you know what I'm talking about.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你因为酸奶的“活性菌”而珍视它，你就明白我在说什么。

sense_groups.english: Now a new study, published in the September 21st online issue of Nature, suggests that good bugs might even hold diabetes at bay.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，一项发表在《自然》杂志9月21日网络版上的新研究表明，好细菌甚至可能控制糖尿病。

sense_groups.english: Type I diabetes is caused by an immune system malfunction.
sense_groups.chinese: I型糖尿病是由免疫系统故障引起的。

sense_groups.english: Basically, the immune cells that usually chase after bacteria instead attack the pancreas, wiping out the cells that produce insulin.
sense_groups.chinese: 基本上，通常追捕细菌的免疫细胞反而攻击胰腺，摧毁产生胰岛素的细胞。

sense_groups.english: So researchers decided to see what would happen if they reigned in the immune response in mice that are prone to diabetes.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以研究人员决定看看，如果他们在易患糖尿病的小鼠中抑制免疫反应会发生什么。

sense_groups.english: As expected, they found that the animals were less likely to develop the disease.
sense_groups.chinese: 正如预期的那样，他们发现这些动物不太可能患上这种疾病。

sense_groups.english: But the effect depended entirely on the critters having a normal complement of friendly bacteria in their intestine.
sense_groups.chinese: 但这种效果完全取决于这些动物肠道中拥有正常数量的友好细菌。

sense_groups.english: Mice that were raised in a totally sterile, germ-free environment were rampant diabetics.
sense_groups.chinese: 在完全无菌、无微生物环境中饲养的小鼠则普遍患有糖尿病。

sense_groups.english: But simply treating those mice with a cocktail of bugs found in most mammals' bellies cured the disease.
sense_groups.chinese: 但只需用大多数哺乳动物肠道中常见的一组细菌混合物治疗这些小鼠，就能治愈这种疾病。

sense_groups.english: How bacteria in the intestine can stave off diabetes is not yet clear.
sense_groups.chinese: 肠道细菌如何预防糖尿病尚不清楚。

sense_groups.english: But the finding could lead to some interesting new treatments.
sense_groups.chinese: 但这一发现可能会带来一些有趣的新疗法。

sense_groups.english: In the meantime, remember that we can't live without the stuff that lives in us.
sense_groups.chinese: 与此同时，请记住，我们离不开生活在我们体内的这些微生物。

questions.name: #183 Pop Music
questions.en:
Flip through Rolling Stone, and you'll read about a lot of "revolutions" in popular music: Rock'n'roll and punk, disco and new wave.
But for Matthias Mauch—an engineer at Queen Mary University of London—the qualitative analysis of musical evolution—the music critic's take—left him wondering: "Is there some way in which we can take this kind of pub conversation, and make it more quantifiable?"
So he and his colleagues analyzed fragments from more than 17,000 songs on the Billboard Hot 100, from 1960 to 2010.
They ______ the audio to extract information about timbral and harmonic qualities—tagging the files for attributes like "orchestra/harmonic" or "calm/quiet/mellow." Then they used those tags—which they compare to a musical "fossil record"—to tease out trends about musical evolution over time.
Turns out, from 1960 to 2009, the dominant seventh chord all but disappeared in what they call the death of blues and jazz on the pop charts.
But as dominant sevenths faded, the minor seventh came into its own… ... more than doubling in frequency between 1967 and '77.
"We can really see the influx of funk, which is then turning into disco."
But next—as you know—came the '80s.
  ______ by a rise in musical tags like "percussive" and "guitar/aggressive" [Bon Jovi—"Bad Medicine"], the '80s were a low point for musical diversity.
In fact 1986 stands out as the year that chart-topping songs sounded most alike.
"Then ______ the charts got saved in terms of diversity, by this new kid on the block, the rap and hip-hop coming in.
And then suddenly, boom: the diversity's back up and ______ higher than before." The study appears in the journal Royal Society Open Science.
Of course, this big-data approach to pop culture probably won't overturn years of musical scholarship.
But the analysis does show that in the evolution of popular music, there really have been long periods of stasis, punctuated by periods of rapid change—musical revolutions—particularly in 1964, 1983 and 1991.
And the more you study it, Matthias says, the more musical evolution starts to resemble plain old species evolution.
"You take ______ that exists.
And that in biology would be genes.
But it's not genes here.
You just take some styles.
You recombine them, like genes are recombined, and you change them as well—a bit like mutation."
Who knows—maybe that might have been a better argument against copyright infringement for Robin Thicke and Pharrell Williams.

questions.name: #184 Acoustic Cloak
questions.en:
When Harry Potter slips underneath his ______ cloak, he can wander freely, undetected.
But what about a cloak of silence, one that completely deadens sound?
That's just what scientists from Spain's University of Valencia have designed, on a tiny scale.
They wrote about their research in the New Journal of Physics.
A paper published last year showed how such a cloak could be made in theory—researchers ______ using materials made up of what are called sonic crystals.
These are solid cylinders that can scatter sound waves.
The Spanish scientists wanted to figure out the specs to make a real acoustic cloak that could totally reroute sound around a given object.
According to their models, it would take about 200 layers of the sound-silencing materials to make it completely ______ to sound waves.
They also think that they'll eventually be able to get the same effect with a thinner cover.
Among the first ______ could be a silent coating for naval ships, so that they're rendered invisible to sonar.
But even more important could be wall ______ that would finally protect your ears from those annoyingly noisy neighbors.

questions.name: #185 Whales
questions.en:
The world's oceans were once home to 10 times as many whales… before the Captain Ahabs of the world came round.
Hunting hit big species the hardest, wiping out 99 percent of the Southern ______ blue whales, for example.
And as the gentle giants disappeared… so did another lesser known element of the oceans: their poop.
"I've described it as, sort of like oversteeped green tea.
Like well steeped green tea.
So it's very diffuse, in a big plume." Joe Roman, a conservation biologist at the University of Vermont.
"My ______ friends say I'm a whale poop scientist." And he says, he studies all kinds.
"When whales are feeding on krill, they're really high lipids, lots of fat, so it can be sort of clumps together and floats at the surface.
So there's a great variety of fecal plumes out there in the oceans."
Whale poop is important because it transports nutrients from the deep ocean, up to the surface.
"Sperm whales feed on giant squid and other deep sea creatures.
So they'll dive more than a kilometer down." Then they come to the surface to breathe, and digest, "and as it turns out they poop and they also pee.
So they're releasing all these nutrients." Nutrients like phosphorous, which are slurped up by phytoplankton and algae.
"Which is in turn is consumed by zooplankton, copepods or krill.
And those are either eaten by fish or they can be eaten by seabirds."
Some fish swim up rivers and die; birds sprinkle the land with their guano; and those ______ nutrients slowly work their way into ecosystems on land with the help of bald eagles and bears and the like.
Roman and his ______ modeled how that conveyer belt of nutrients has slowed due to the huge ______ in whale, seabird and fish populations.
And they reckon that only a quarter as much phosphorus makes it to surface waters today compared with the past.
And the flow of phosphorus to land has nearly stopped--at just 4 percent of historic levels.
The results are in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
Roman says this slowing of the nutrient conveyer belt is reversible, though.
"The most important part for me is trying to restore these species as ecological engineers on the planet, and really try and share the planet with them.
Let's not just keep them in zoos or even in small island pockets of protected areas.
Let's let them move around the planet more freely." And when they do, he says… those key nutrients, too, will once again roam the Earth.

questions.name: #186 Contraception
questions.en:
It sounds obvious—pregnancies could be avoided by using contraception.
But 15 million unwanted ______ could be avoided annually in 35 low- and ______ countries if women did in fact use modern contraception.
That's according to a study in the journal Human Reproduction.
Unwanted pregnancy has a wide range of serious consequences.
Women may have to stop their education or employment.
They might pursue unsafe abortions.
And they can face disability, disease and death as a result of the pregnancy.
To determine barriers to the use of contraception, researchers ______ surveys and ______ of nearly 13,000 women who became pregnant unintentionally.
They compared the data to that from more than a hundred thousand women who were sexually active and did not want to be pregnant.
For women who were sexually active, did not want to be pregnant, but did not use contraception, 37 percent feared health side effects from contraception.
Twenty-two percent said they or their partner objected.
These issues outweighed cost or availability.
Women also underestimated the risks of getting pregnant from unprotected sex.
The World Health Organization's Howard Sobel is one of the authors of the study.
In a press release he says the research shows that health workers need to play a bigger role in educating and reassuring women, along with helping individuals determine the best contraceptive for them.
He advises that effective, affordable ______ should be coupled with education about the myths of contraception—and information about the real risks of unintended pregnancies.
questions.full:
It sounds obvious—pregnancies could be avoided by using contraception.
But 15 million unwanted ______ could be avoided annually in 35 low- and ______ countries if women did in fact use modern contraception.
That's according to a study in the journal Human Reproduction.
Unwanted pregnancy has a wide range of serious consequences.
Women may have to stop their education or employment.
They might pursue unsafe abortions.
And they can face disability, disease and death as a result of the pregnancy.
To determine barriers to the use of contraception, researchers ______ surveys and ______ of nearly 13,000 women who became pregnant unintentionally.

He advises that effective, affordable ______ should be coupled with education about the myths of contraception—and information about the real risks of unintended pregnancies.

答案:
1. pregnancies
2. middle-income
3. compared
4. interviews
5. contraception

sense_groups.english: It sounds obvious—pregnancies could be avoided by using contraception.
sense_groups.chinese: 这听起来很明显——怀孕可以通过使用避孕措施来避免。

sense_groups.english: But 15 million unwanted pregnancies could be avoided annually in 35 low- and middle-income countries if women did in fact use modern contraception.
sense_groups.chinese: 但如果在35个低收入和中等收入国家，女性确实使用了现代避孕措施，每年可以避免1500万次意外怀孕。

sense_groups.english: That's according to a study in the journal Human Reproduction.
sense_groups.chinese: 这是根据《人类生殖》期刊上的一项研究得出的。

sense_groups.english: Unwanted pregnancy has a wide range of serious consequences.
sense_groups.chinese: 意外怀孕会带来一系列严重的后果。

sense_groups.english: Women may have to stop their education or employment.
sense_groups.chinese: 女性可能不得不中断学业或工作。

sense_groups.english: They might pursue unsafe abortions.
sense_groups.chinese: 她们可能会寻求不安全的堕胎。

sense_groups.english: And they can face disability, disease and death as a result of the pregnancy.
sense_groups.chinese: 并且她们可能因怀孕而面临残疾、疾病和死亡。

sense_groups.english: To determine barriers to the use of contraception, researchers compared surveys and interviews of nearly 13,000 women who became pregnant unintentionally.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了确定使用避孕措施的障碍，研究人员比较了对近13000名意外怀孕女性的调查和访谈。

sense_groups.english: They compared the data to that from more than a hundred thousand women who were sexually active and did not want to be pregnant.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们将数据与超过10万名有性生活但不想怀孕的女性数据进行了比较。

sense_groups.english: For women who were sexually active, did not want to be pregnant, but did not use contraception, 37 percent feared health side effects from contraception.
sense_groups.chinese: 对于有性生活、不想怀孕但未使用避孕措施的女性，37%的人担心避孕措施的健康副作用。

sense_groups.english: Twenty-two percent said they or their partner objected.
sense_groups.chinese: 22%的人表示她们或她们的伴侣反对。

sense_groups.english: These issues outweighed cost or availability.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些问题比成本或可获得性更重要。

sense_groups.english: Women also underestimated the risks of getting pregnant from unprotected sex.
sense_groups.chinese: 女性也低估了无保护性行为导致怀孕的风险。

sense_groups.english: The World Health Organization's Howard Sobel is one of the authors of the study.
sense_groups.chinese: 世界卫生组织的霍华德·索贝尔是该研究的作者之一。

sense_groups.english: In a press release he says the research shows that health workers need to play a bigger role in educating and reassuring women, along with helping individuals determine the best contraceptive for them.
sense_groups.chinese: 在一份新闻稿中，他表示研究表明卫生工作者需要在教育和安抚女性方面发挥更大作用，同时帮助个人确定最适合她们的避孕方法。

sense_groups.english: He advises that effective, affordable contraception should be coupled with education about the myths of contraception—and information about the real risks of unintended pregnancies.
sense_groups.chinese: 他建议，有效且负担得起的避孕措施应与关于避孕误区的教育以及意外怀孕真实风险的信息相结合。

questions.name: #187 Sniff
questions.en:
Imagine if you could focus your nose, the way you focus your eyes.
  ______ now believe that animals with a highly developed sense of smell, like rats and dogs, do just that.
Similar to the way we taste sweet, salty, sour and bitter on different parts of the tongue, animals detect various smells in different parts of the nose.
Researchers at the University of Chicago ______ that rats, by changing the way air flows across the insides of the nostrils, could direct the scent to the nasal region where it could be best detected.
Turns out they were right.
When presented with different odors, rats actually changed the way they sniffed.
For example, long slow sniffs for hard-to-detect scents, or short fast ones for easy ones.
Rats even sniffed ______ while learning a new scent than when the smell was familiar.
The study is in the Journal of Neuroscience.
The researchers say the finding shows that there's more to a good sense of smell than ______ thought.
A ______ nose is important, but so is how you use it.
questions.full:
Imagine if you could focus your nose, the way you focus your eyes.
  ______ now believe that animals with a highly developed sense of smell, like rats and dogs, do just that.
Similar to the way we taste sweet, salty, sour and bitter on different parts of the tongue, animals detect various smells in different parts of the nose.
Researchers at the University of Chicago ______ that rats, by changing the way air flows across the insides of the nostrils, could direct the scent to the nasal region where it could be best detected.
Turns out they were right.
When presented with different odors, rats actually changed the way they sniffed.
For example, long slow sniffs for hard-to-detect scents, or short fast ones for easy ones.
Rats even sniffed ______ while learning a new scent than when the smell was familiar.
The study is in the Journal of Neuroscience.
The researchers say the finding shows that there's more to a good sense of smell than ______ thought.
A ______ nose is important, but so is how you use it.

答案:
1. Scientists
2. hypothesized
3. differently
4. originally
5. sensitive

sense_groups.english: Imagine if you could focus your nose, the way you focus your eyes.
sense_groups.chinese: 想象一下，如果你能像聚焦眼睛那样聚焦鼻子。

sense_groups.english: Scientists now believe that animals with a highly developed sense of smell, like rats and dogs, do just that.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们现在相信，嗅觉高度发达的动物，比如老鼠和狗，正是这样做的。

sense_groups.english: Similar to the way we taste sweet, salty, sour and bitter on different parts of the tongue, animals detect various smells in different parts of the nose.
sense_groups.chinese: 类似于我们在舌头的不同部位品尝甜、咸、酸、苦，动物在鼻子的不同部位检测不同的气味。

sense_groups.english: Researchers at the University of Chicago hypothesized that rats, by changing the way air flows across the insides of the nostrils, could direct the scent to the nasal region where it could be best detected.
sense_groups.chinese: 芝加哥大学的研究人员假设，老鼠通过改变空气在鼻孔内部流动的方式，可以将气味引导到最能被检测到的鼻腔区域。

sense_groups.english: Turns out they were right.
sense_groups.chinese: 结果证明他们是对的。

sense_groups.english: When presented with different odors, rats actually changed the way they sniffed.
sense_groups.chinese: 当面对不同的气味时，老鼠实际上改变了它们嗅闻的方式。

sense_groups.english: For example, long slow sniffs for hard-to-detect scents, or short fast ones for easy ones.
sense_groups.chinese: 例如，对于难以检测的气味，它们会缓慢地长嗅；对于容易检测的气味，则快速短嗅。

sense_groups.english: Rats even sniffed differently while learning a new scent than when the smell was familiar.
sense_groups.chinese: 老鼠在学习新气味时，嗅闻方式甚至与熟悉气味时不同。

sense_groups.english: The study is in the Journal of Neuroscience.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《神经科学杂志》上。

sense_groups.english: The researchers say the finding shows that there's more to a good sense of smell than originally thought.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员表示，这一发现表明，良好的嗅觉比最初认为的要复杂得多。

sense_groups.english: A sensitive nose is important, but so is how you use it.
sense_groups.chinese: 一个敏感的鼻子很重要，但如何使用它也同样重要。

questions.name: #188 Ventilation
questions.en:
Contrary to popular wisdom, a new study finds that if you want to avoid getting sick you should open a window.
At least if you don't want to catch TB in a hospital in Lima, Peru.
  ______ from the Imperial College London were looking for ways to limit the spread of tuberculosis in the Peruvian situation.
One major site of transmission is apparently the hospital waiting room, where infected ______ come to be treated.
In close quarters, one person with TB can infect many others, by sneezing, coughing, even speaking.
To curb the contagion, the ______ prescribed ventilation.
And the best ventilation, they find, is the simplest—opening the doors and windows.
Such natural ______ really keeps things moving, allowing the air in the room to be replaced by fresh air an average of 28 times an hour.
Even ______ systems designed specifically to exchange the air in isolation wards only achieve 12 air changes an hour, and that's when they're working at maximum capacity, which is not often the case.
The study is good news for ______ that can't afford sophisticated mechanical ventilation systems.
And it's a real shot in the arm for people who've always said that a little fresh air is good for you.

2. individuals
3. researchers
4. ventilation
5. mechanical
6. hospitals

Such natural ______ really keeps things moving, allowing the air in the room to be replaced by fresh air an average of 28 times an hour.
Even ______ systems designed specifically to exchange the air in isolation wards only achieve 12 air changes an hour, and that's when they're working at maximum capacity, which is not often the case.
The study is good news for ______ that can't afford sophisticated mechanical ventilation systems.
And it's a real shot in the arm for people who've always said that a little fresh air is good for you.

答案:
1. Researchers
2. individuals
3. researchers
4. ventilation
5. mechanical
6. hospitals

sense_groups.english: Contrary to popular wisdom, a new study finds that if you want to avoid getting sick you should open a window.
sense_groups.chinese: 与普遍看法相反，一项新研究发现，如果你想避免生病，应该打开窗户。

sense_groups.english: At least if you don't want to catch TB in a hospital in Lima, Peru.
sense_groups.chinese: 至少，如果你不想在秘鲁利马的一家医院里感染肺结核的话。

sense_groups.english: Researchers from the Imperial College London were looking for ways to limit the spread of tuberculosis in the Peruvian situation.
sense_groups.chinese: 伦敦帝国理工学院的研究人员正在寻找在秘鲁情况下限制结核病传播的方法。

sense_groups.english: One major site of transmission is apparently the hospital waiting room, where infected individuals come to be treated.
sense_groups.chinese: 一个主要的传播地点显然是医院候诊室，受感染的个体来这里接受治疗。

sense_groups.english: In close quarters, one person with TB can infect many others, by sneezing, coughing, even speaking.
sense_groups.chinese: 在密闭空间里，一个肺结核患者可以通过打喷嚏、咳嗽甚至说话感染许多人。

sense_groups.english: To curb the contagion, the researchers prescribed ventilation.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了遏制传染，研究人员建议通风。

sense_groups.english: And the best ventilation, they find, is the simplest—opening the doors and windows.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现，最好的通风方式是最简单的——打开门窗。

sense_groups.english: Such natural ventilation really keeps things moving, allowing the air in the room to be replaced by fresh air an average of 28 times an hour.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种自然通风确实能让空气流动，使房间内的空气平均每小时被新鲜空气替换28次。

sense_groups.english: Even mechanical systems designed specifically to exchange the air in isolation wards only achieve 12 air changes an hour, and that's when they're working at maximum capacity, which is not often the case.
sense_groups.chinese: 即使是专门设计用于隔离病房换气的机械系统，每小时也只能实现12次换气，而且这是在它们以最大容量运行时的情况，但这种情况并不常见。

sense_groups.english: The study is good news for hospitals that can't afford sophisticated mechanical ventilation systems.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究对那些负担不起复杂机械通风系统的医院来说是个好消息。

sense_groups.english: And it's a real shot in the arm for people who've always said that a little fresh air is good for you.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且，对于那些一直说一点新鲜空气对你有好处的人来说，这真是一剂强心针。

questions.name: #189 Limb Evolution
questions.en:
What had the legs of a 'gator and the jaws of a fish?
Why, the earliest land animals.
Because a new study shows that animals evolved weight-bearing limbs long before they had the chompers to really take ______ of a terrestrial diet.

What had the legs of a 'gator and the jaws of a fish?
Why, the earliest land animals.
Because a new study shows that animals evolved weight-bearing limbs long before they had the chompers to really take ______ of a terrestrial diet.

sense_groups.english: What had the legs of a 'gator and the jaws of a fish?
sense_groups.chinese: 什么动物有鳄鱼的腿和鱼的颚？

sense_groups.english: Why, the earliest land animals.
sense_groups.chinese: 哦，是最早的陆地动物。

sense_groups.english: Because a new study shows that animals evolved weight-bearing limbs long before they had the chompers to really take advantage of a terrestrial diet.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为一项新研究表明，动物进化出承重四肢的时间远早于它们拥有真正享用陆地食物的牙齿。

sense_groups.english: The research is in the journal Integrative and Comparative Biology.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《整合与比较生物学》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: Scientists had suspected that the first four-legged creatures to haul their carcasses out of the ocean didn't belly up to the salad bar straight away.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们曾怀疑，第一批将身体拖出海洋的四足动物并没有立刻冲向沙拉吧。

sense_groups.english: But they lacked definitive proof.
sense_groups.chinese: 但他们缺乏确凿证据。

sense_groups.english: Now, researchers have carefully examined the fossilized faces of 89 beasties that lived on land and sea some 300 to 400 million years ago.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，研究人员仔细检查了生活在3亿到4亿年前陆地和海洋中的89种小动物的化石面部。

sense_groups.english: They probed the jaws for a range of biomechanical features, such as how much force they could give to their bite.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们探测了这些颚的一系列生物力学特征，比如它们咬合时能产生多大的力量。

sense_groups.english: The result: seems it took tens of millions of years after setting foot on land to come up with a mouth that could munch on the greenery.
sense_groups.chinese: 结果：似乎在踏上陆地数千万年后，才进化出能够咀嚼绿色植物的嘴巴。

sense_groups.english: Why the lag?
sense_groups.chinese: 为什么会有延迟？

sense_groups.english: Could be the critters had to stop being such mouth breathers and shift from using gills to using lungs, which freed their jaws to develop in new ways.
sense_groups.chinese: 可能是因为这些生物必须停止用嘴呼吸，从用鳃呼吸转向用肺呼吸，这解放了它们的颚，使其以新的方式发育。

sense_groups.english: And which left no more excuses to not eat their veggies.
sense_groups.chinese: 这也让它们再也没有借口不吃蔬菜了。

questions.name: #190 Freedom
questions.en:
What's the best way for ______ to really learn basic science?
New research just ______ at the annual meeting of the American ______ for the Advancement of Science ______ an answer: freedom.
After years of watching nonscience majors struggle with biology courses, Steve Rissing of Ohio State University decided to see how the boring old cookbook method of ______ stacked up against something new.

Eighty-three percent of the free students gave the right answer to the simple question, "Where do enzymes occur in nature?" Just 23 percent of the cookbook group ______ correctly.
