sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员认为，其他将摄像头与减少事故和伤害联系起来的研究是有缺陷的——这些研究与公路安全保险协会（一个行业组织）有关联。

sense_groups.english: But insurers may profit from red light cameras, because revenues go up with increased citations and accidents.
sense_groups.chinese: 但保险公司可能从红灯摄像头中获利，因为随着罚单和事故的增加，收入也会上升。

sense_groups.english: The new report notes that North Carolina, Virginia and Ontario all had increased crash rates and injuries associated with red light cameras.
sense_groups.chinese: 新报告指出，北卡罗来纳州、弗吉尼亚州和安大略省与红灯摄像头相关的事故率和伤害都有所增加。

sense_groups.english: In Florida, injuries related to red light running are down anyway.
sense_groups.chinese: 在佛罗里达州，与闯红灯相关的伤害无论如何都在下降。

sense_groups.english: So drivers needing to make a quick decision at a yellow light may be better off not seeing red.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，在黄灯时需要快速做出决定的司机，最好别看到红灯。

questions.name: #221 Ant
questions.en:
When is an ant like a piece of fruit?
When it's infected by a parasite.

They found some colony members with bright red swollen abdomens.
The scientists took specimens back to the lab and discovered they were full of hundreds of ______ eggs.
The bright red bellies look suspiciously like the brilliant red and pink berries that proliferate in the rainforest.
Researchers think that the nematode makes the ant look like fruit to get birds to eat the ants.
Birds usually keep the ants off their menu because of armor and a bad chemical taste.
The birds then spread ______ eggs in their droppings.
Ants forage through bird ______ for seeds.
They feed the infected droppings to ant larvae, beginning the infection process all over again.
The red-bellied ant is the first known case of a parasite causing fruit mimicry.

But evolution works no matter how dumb ______ are.
questions.answer:
1. nematode
2. parasite
3. droppings
4. manipulate
5. sophisticated
6. organisms

sense_groups.english: When is an ant like a piece of fruit?
sense_groups.chinese: 蚂蚁什么时候像水果？

sense_groups.english: When it's infected by a parasite.
sense_groups.chinese: 当它被寄生虫感染时。

sense_groups.english: Researchers affiliated with the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute discovered this bizarre occurrence in Central America
sense_groups.chinese: 史密森尼热带研究所的研究人员在中美洲发现了这一奇怪现象。

sense_groups.english: as they were studying the gliding ability of a certain species of ant.
sense_groups.chinese: 当时他们正在研究某种蚂蚁的滑翔能力。

sense_groups.english: They found some colony members with bright red swollen abdomens.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现一些蚁群成员有鲜红色肿胀的腹部。

sense_groups.english: The scientists took specimens back to the lab
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们将标本带回实验室，

sense_groups.english: and discovered they were full of hundreds of nematode eggs.
sense_groups.chinese: 发现它们体内充满了数百个线虫卵。

sense_groups.english: The bright red bellies look suspiciously like the brilliant red and pink berries that proliferate in the rainforest.
sense_groups.chinese: 鲜红色的腹部看起来很像雨林中大量生长的亮红色和粉色浆果。

sense_groups.english: Researchers think that the nematode makes the ant look like fruit
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员认为线虫让蚂蚁看起来像水果，

sense_groups.english: to get birds to eat the ants.
sense_groups.chinese: 以诱使鸟类吃掉蚂蚁。

sense_groups.english: Birds usually keep the ants off their menu
sense_groups.chinese: 鸟类通常将蚂蚁排除在菜单之外，

sense_groups.english: because of armor and a bad chemical taste.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为它们有盔甲和难闻的化学味道。

sense_groups.english: The birds then spread parasite eggs in their droppings.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后鸟类通过粪便传播寄生虫卵。

sense_groups.english: Ants forage through bird droppings for seeds.
sense_groups.chinese: 蚂蚁在鸟粪中寻找种子。

sense_groups.english: They feed the infected droppings to ant larvae,
sense_groups.chinese: 它们将受感染的粪便喂给蚂蚁幼虫，

sense_groups.english: beginning the infection process all over again.
sense_groups.chinese: 重新开始感染过程。

sense_groups.english: The red-bellied ant is the first known case of a parasite causing fruit mimicry.
sense_groups.chinese: 红腹蚂蚁是已知的第一个寄生虫导致果实拟态的案例。

sense_groups.english: One of the researchers was surprised that something "dumb as a nematode" can manipulate its host in such a sophisticated way.
sense_groups.chinese: 其中一位研究人员惊讶于像线虫这样“愚蠢”的东西能以如此复杂的方式操纵宿主。

sense_groups.english: But evolution works no matter how dumb organisms are.
sense_groups.chinese: 但无论生物多么愚蠢，进化都在起作用。

questions.name: #222 Bird Song
questions.en:
That, of course, is the sound of the Himalayan forest thrush.
And that sound was a clue to field ______ that they might have a new species of bird on their hands.
Even though it was in the bush.
You know what I mean.
You see, the Himalayan forest thrush looks a great deal like another well-known bird called the alpine thrush.
They're both found in ______ India and nearby parts of China.
But the alpine thrush has a raspy song ______ with the more mellifluous Himalayan forest thrush.
One of the researchers, ______ Dalvi of India's National Centre for Biological ______ and the Wildlife Conservation Society, likened the two different birds to Rod Stewart versus Adele.
Further analyses, including of the birds' DNA, confirmed that the song differences were indicative of these birds indeed belonging to two separate species.
The finding is in the journal Avian Research.
The discovery of a new bird species is relatively rare.
Since the year 2000, ornithologists have found five new species annually on average, mostly in South America.
So this newly characterized thrush—only the fourth new species found in India since it became independent in 1947—should send ______ from all over the world flocking.
I mean, it's a sound discovery.
questions.answer:
1. researchers
2. northeastern
3. compared
4. Shashank
5. Sciences
6. birdwatchers
questions.full:
That, of course, is the sound of the Himalayan forest thrush.
And that sound was a clue to field ______ that they might have a new species of bird on their hands.
Even though it was in the bush.
You know what I mean.

sense_groups.english: That, of course, is the sound of the Himalayan forest thrush.
sense_groups.chinese: 那当然是喜马拉雅森林鸫的叫声。

sense_groups.english: And that sound was a clue to field researchers that they might have a new species of bird on their hands.
sense_groups.chinese: 那个声音给野外研究人员一个线索，他们可能发现了一种新的鸟类。

sense_groups.english: Even though it was in the bush.
sense_groups.chinese: 尽管它藏在灌木丛中。

sense_groups.english: You know what I mean.
sense_groups.chinese: 你明白我的意思。

sense_groups.english: You see, the Himalayan forest thrush looks a great deal like another well-known bird called the alpine thrush.
sense_groups.chinese: 你看，喜马拉雅森林鸫和另一种著名的鸟——高山鸫——长得非常像。

sense_groups.english: They're both found in northeastern India and nearby parts of China.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们都分布在印度东北部和中国邻近地区。

sense_groups.english: But the alpine thrush has a raspy song compared with the more mellifluous Himalayan forest thrush.
sense_groups.chinese: 但高山鸫的叫声沙哑，而喜马拉雅森林鸫的叫声更悦耳动听。

sense_groups.english: One of the researchers, Shashank Dalvi of India's National Centre for Biological Sciences and the Wildlife Conservation Society, likened the two different birds to Rod Stewart versus Adele.
sense_groups.chinese: 其中一位研究人员，印度国家生物科学中心与野生动物保护协会的Shashank Dalvi，将这两种不同的鸟比作Rod Stewart和Adele。

sense_groups.english: Further analyses, including of the birds' DNA, confirmed that the song differences were indicative of these birds indeed belonging to two separate species.
sense_groups.chinese: 进一步的分析，包括鸟类的DNA，证实了叫声差异表明这两种鸟确实属于不同的物种。

sense_groups.english: The finding is in the journal Avian Research.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项发现发表在《鸟类研究》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: The discovery of a new bird species is relatively rare.
sense_groups.chinese: 发现新鸟种相对罕见。

sense_groups.english: Since the year 2000, ornithologists have found five new species annually on average, mostly in South America.
sense_groups.chinese: 自2000年以来，鸟类学家平均每年发现五种新物种，主要在南美洲。

sense_groups.english: So this newly characterized thrush—only the fourth new species found in India since it became independent in 1947—should send birdwatchers from all over the world flocking.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，这种新描述的鸫——自印度1947年独立以来发现的第四种新物种——应该会吸引世界各地的观鸟者蜂拥而至。

sense_groups.english: I mean, it's a sound discovery.
sense_groups.chinese: 我的意思是，这是一个声音上的发现。

questions.name: #223 Salty Skin
questions.en:
It's both painful and insulting to rub salt in a wound.
But a new study shows that salty skin can ______ ward off infections, at least in mice fed a high-sodium diet.
That's according to a study in the journal Cell Metabolism.
We tend to think of dietary salt as a health threat.
And it is.
Too much sodium has been linked to high blood ______ and an ______ risk for heart attack and stroke.
But we also crave salty snacks and store the accumulated sodium in our bodies, ______ in the skin.
A clue to explaining this paradox came when ______ noticed that mice that were attacked by a cage mate wound up with an unusually large amount of sodium at the site of the bite.
They then found high sodium levels in people at the locations of ______ skin infections.
So the researchers fed mice a high-sodium diet.
And found that the dietary salt boosted the ______ of immune cells in the animals' skin, which gave them a leg up when it came to healing their wounds.
The findings could lead to treatments that would help us assault infections without having to resort to pretzels, potato chips or pickles.
questions.answer:
1. actually
2. pressure
3. increased
4. particularly
5. researchers
6. bacterial
7. activity
questions.full:
It's both painful and insulting to rub salt in a wound.
But a new study shows that salty skin can ______ ward off infections, at least in mice fed a high-sodium diet.
That's according to a study in the journal Cell Metabolism.

The findings could lead to treatments that would help us assault infections without having to resort to pretzels, potato chips or pickles.

答案:
1. actually
2. pressure
3. increased
4. particularly
5. researchers
6. bacterial
7. activity

sense_groups.english: It's both painful and insulting to rub salt in a wound.
sense_groups.chinese: 在伤口上撒盐既痛苦又侮辱人。

sense_groups.english: But a new study shows that salty skin can actually ward off infections,
sense_groups.chinese: 但一项新研究表明，咸的皮肤实际上可以抵御感染，

sense_groups.english: at least in mice fed a high-sodium diet.
sense_groups.chinese: 至少在喂食高钠饮食的老鼠身上是这样。

sense_groups.english: That's according to a study in the journal Cell Metabolism.
sense_groups.chinese: 这是根据《细胞代谢》杂志上的一项研究得出的。

sense_groups.english: We tend to think of dietary salt as a health threat.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们倾向于认为食盐对健康构成威胁。

sense_groups.english: And it is.
sense_groups.chinese: 确实如此。

sense_groups.english: Too much sodium has been linked to high blood pressure and an increased risk for heart attack and stroke.
sense_groups.chinese: 过多的钠与高血压以及心脏病发作和中风风险增加有关。

sense_groups.english: But we also crave salty snacks and store the accumulated sodium in our bodies, particularly in the skin.
sense_groups.chinese: 但我们也渴望咸味零食，并将积累的钠储存在体内，尤其是皮肤中。

sense_groups.english: A clue to explaining this paradox came when researchers noticed that mice that were attacked by a cage mate wound up with an unusually large amount of sodium at the site of the bite.
sense_groups.chinese: 解释这一悖论的线索来自研究人员注意到，被笼中同伴攻击的老鼠在咬伤处有异常大量的钠。

sense_groups.english: They then found high sodium levels in people at the locations of bacterial skin infections.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们随后在人类细菌性皮肤感染部位发现了高钠水平。

sense_groups.english: So the researchers fed mice a high-sodium diet.
sense_groups.chinese: 于是研究人员给老鼠喂食高钠饮食。

sense_groups.english: And found that the dietary salt boosted the activity of immune cells in the animals' skin,
sense_groups.chinese: 并发现饮食中的盐增强了动物皮肤中免疫细胞的活性，

sense_groups.english: which gave them a leg up when it came to healing their wounds.
sense_groups.chinese: 这在伤口愈合方面给了它们优势。

sense_groups.english: The findings could lead to treatments that would help us assault infections without having to resort to pretzels, potato chips or pickles.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些发现可能会带来治疗方法，帮助我们对抗感染，而不必依赖椒盐卷饼、薯片或泡菜。

questions.name: #224 Brain Size
questions.en:
Comparisons of different animals have shown that larger brains provide greater intelligence, but they also guzzle more energy and have other consequences.
Now scientists have ______ the effects of varying brain size within a single species: guppies.
The work is in Current Biology.
Swedish researchers bred two different lines of guppies, selecting one for larger brains and one for smaller.
The fish quickly modified until brains were nine percent larger in the ______ line than in the other.
Not surprisingly, when 48 guppies were given learning tests, ______ female fish outperformed small-brained females.
However, males from both lines scored about the same, ______ because the female guppies' visual system was more suited to the type of ______ test used.
But big brains also had a downside—the brainier fish had smaller guts, by 20 percent for males and 8 percent for females.
Plus, the large-brained guppies produced 19 percent fewer offspring.
In order to provide energy to their bigger brains, the egghead fish made sacrifices that may be evolutionary disadvantages.
It may indeed be possible to be too smart for your own good.
questions.full:
Comparisons of different animals have shown that larger brains provide greater intelligence, but they also guzzle more energy and have other consequences.
Now scientists have ______ the effects of varying brain size within a single species: guppies.
The work is in Current Biology.
Swedish researchers bred two different lines of guppies, selecting one for larger brains and one for smaller.
The fish quickly modified until brains were nine percent larger in the ______ line than in the other.
Not surprisingly, when 48 guppies were given learning tests, ______ female fish outperformed small-brained females.
However, males from both lines scored about the same, ______ because the female guppies' visual system was more suited to the type of ______ test used.
But big brains also had a downside—the brainier fish had smaller guts, by 20 percent for males and 8 percent for females.
Plus, the large-brained guppies produced 19 percent fewer offspring.
In order to provide energy to their bigger brains, the egghead fish made sacrifices that may be evolutionary disadvantages.
It may indeed be possible to be too smart for your own good.

答案:
1. observed
2. big-brained
3. large-brained
4. possibly
5. intelligence

sense_groups.english: Comparisons of different animals have shown that larger brains provide greater intelligence,
sense_groups.chinese: 对不同动物的比较表明，更大的大脑提供更高的智力，

sense_groups.english: but they also guzzle more energy and have other consequences.
sense_groups.chinese: 但它们也消耗更多能量并带来其他后果。

sense_groups.english: Now scientists have observed the effects of varying brain size within a single species: guppies.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在科学家们观察了单一物种——孔雀鱼——中大脑大小变化的影响。

sense_groups.english: The work is in Current Biology.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《当代生物学》上。

sense_groups.english: Swedish researchers bred two different lines of guppies,
sense_groups.chinese: 瑞典研究人员培育了两个不同的孔雀鱼品系，

sense_groups.english: selecting one for larger brains and one for smaller.
sense_groups.chinese: 选择其中一个品系的大脑更大，另一个更小。

sense_groups.english: The fish quickly modified until brains were nine percent larger in the large-brained line than in the other.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些鱼迅速改变，直到大脑大的品系的大脑比另一个大9%。

sense_groups.english: Not surprisingly, when 48 guppies were given learning tests,
sense_groups.chinese: 毫不奇怪，当48条孔雀鱼接受学习测试时，

sense_groups.english: big-brained female fish outperformed small-brained females.
sense_groups.chinese: 大脑大的雌鱼表现优于大脑小的雌鱼。

sense_groups.english: However, males from both lines scored about the same,
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，两个品系的雄鱼得分大致相同，

sense_groups.english: possibly because the female guppies' visual system was more suited to the type of intelligence test used.
sense_groups.chinese: 可能是因为雌孔雀鱼的视觉系统更适应所使用的智力测试类型。

sense_groups.english: But big brains also had a downside—
sense_groups.chinese: 但大脑大也有缺点——

sense_groups.english: the brainier fish had smaller guts, by 20 percent for males and 8 percent for females.
sense_groups.chinese: 更聪明的鱼肠道更小，雄鱼小20%，雌鱼小8%。

sense_groups.english: Plus, the large-brained guppies produced 19 percent fewer offspring.
sense_groups.chinese: 此外，大脑大的孔雀鱼产下的后代少19%。

sense_groups.english: In order to provide energy to their bigger brains,
sense_groups.chinese: 为了给它们更大的大脑提供能量，

sense_groups.english: the egghead fish made sacrifices that may be evolutionary disadvantages.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些聪明的鱼做出了牺牲，这可能是进化上的劣势。

sense_groups.english: It may indeed be possible to be too smart for your own good.
sense_groups.chinese: 确实可能聪明反被聪明误。

questions.name: #225 Memory
questions.en:
A book a day may keep dementia away.
Even if you read it as a kid.
Because a study finds that exercising the brain, at any age, may preserve memory.
The work appears online in the journal Neurology.
  ______ studies have shown that ______ in brain-building activities is ______ with a delay in late-life cognitive decline.
But why?
Does flexing the old gray matter somehow buffer against ______ intellectual impairment?
Or is cognitive loss simply a consequence of the aging brain's ______ decline?
To find out, researchers questioned nearly 300 elderly individuals about their lifelong participation in intellectual pursuits—like reading books, writing letters and looking things up in the library.
Then, every year, for an average of six years until they died, the subjects took tests to measure their memory and thinking.
What the researchers found is that folks who worked their mental muscles, both early and late in life, remained more intellectually limber than those who didn't—even when a post-mortem look at their brains ______ the ______ signs of physical decline.
So if you're headed to the beach, don't forget a hat and a book, both to protect your head.

1. Previous
2. engaging
3. associated
4. age-related
5. physical
6. revealed
7. telltale

questions.name: #230 Peanut Butter
questions.en:
Peanut butter: It's a staple of childhood sandwiches—and a nightmare for parents whose kids have nut allergies. Now it might also be a cure for hunger in sub-Saharan Africa. Or so say scientists at the Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis. These researchers have used a nutrient-rich paste made from peanuts, powdered milk, oil and sugar—spiked with added libelous and minerals—to combat starvation in boundless of mechanism in Malawi. Nearly underachievers of the kids there are malnourished, and more than 10 percent die from it before the age of 5.
The scientists enlisted village health aides to identify those who needed help. Of the 2,000 wherry malnourished children who were given the peanut paste, 89% recovered. That's far better than the 50% recovery rate seen in starving kids who are treated with a frosted made of corn or milk. Probably because peanut butter is packed with protein and calories. A hungry child would have to eat 25 spoonfuls of porridge to equal the subtleties in just one glop of peanut paste. Best of all, the peanut butter is produced locally, does not require cooking and can be administered by doctor mom.

questions.name: #231 Floating Trash
questions.en:
The Great Pacific Garbage Patch may be the most infamous of the world's floating trash dumps.
But it's far from the only one.
There's plastic trash littering "the Bay of Bengal, the Mediterranean Sea, the coast of Indonesia, all five subtropical gyres; coastal regions, enclosed bays, seas and gulfs." Marcus Eriksen, director of ______ at the Five Gyres Institute.
Eriksen surveyed those areas, along with his seafaring colleagues.
Collectively, they spent some 900 hours logging every large piece of plastic they could spot from their boats.
And they trawled for plastic nearly 700 times along the way, picking through their nets and cataloguing the debris.
"I find the necks of bottles, I find fragments of ______ and combs.
Action figure parts.
Army men.
I find a lot of army men."
The ______ plugged that trash census data into ocean models, which simulate the circulation of the world's waters.
Based on the densities of trash the researchers found, the models predicted some 5.25 ______ particles of plastic may be floating out there…adding up to about 269,000 tons.
And more than 90 percent of those pieces may be smaller than a grain of rice.
The study appears in the journal PLOS ONE.
So, what happens to all that plastic?
"The ocean's going to take it, blast it to smithereens, it's going to cycle it through marine organisms, and sink it to the sea floor.
That's the ultimate life cycle, I believe, for plastics.
We're like constantly, you know, ______ fish food on the entire ocean surface." The solution, Marcus says, isn't some fleet of seafaring garbage trucks.
It's keeping our trash to ourselves—which would be a real sea change in behavior.

sense_groups.english: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch may be the most infamous of the world's floating trash dumps.
sense_groups.chinese: 大太平洋垃圾带可能是世界上最臭名昭著的漂浮垃圾堆。

sense_groups.english: But it's far from the only one.

sense_groups.english: There's plastic trash littering "the Bay of Bengal, the Mediterranean Sea, the coast of Indonesia, all five subtropical gyres; coastal regions, enclosed bays, seas and gulfs."
sense_groups.chinese: 塑料垃圾遍布“孟加拉湾、地中海、印度尼西亚海岸、所有五个亚热带环流；沿海地区、封闭海湾、海洋和海湾。”

sense_groups.english: Marcus Eriksen, director of research at the Five Gyres Institute.
sense_groups.chinese: 五环流研究所的研究主任马库斯·埃里克森。

sense_groups.english: Eriksen surveyed those areas, along with his seafaring colleagues.
sense_groups.chinese: 埃里克森和他的航海同事们调查了这些区域。

sense_groups.english: Collectively, they spent some 900 hours logging every large piece of plastic they could spot from their boats.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们总共花了大约900个小时，记录从船上能看到的每一块大塑料。

sense_groups.english: And they trawled for plastic nearly 700 times along the way, picking through their nets and cataloguing the debris.
sense_groups.chinese: 沿途他们拖网捕捞塑料近700次，翻检渔网并分类记录碎片。

sense_groups.english: "I find the necks of bottles, I find fragments of toothbrushes and combs.
sense_groups.chinese: “我发现瓶口，发现牙刷和梳子的碎片。

sense_groups.english: Action figure parts.

sense_groups.english: Army men.
sense_groups.chinese: 玩具士兵。

sense_groups.english: I find a lot of army men."
sense_groups.chinese: 我找到很多玩具士兵。”

sense_groups.english: The researchers plugged that trash census data into ocean models, which simulate the circulation of the world's waters.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员将这些垃圾普查数据输入海洋模型，这些模型模拟全球水体的环流。

sense_groups.english: Based on the densities of trash the researchers found, the models predicted some 5.25 trillion particles of plastic may be floating out there…adding up to about 269,000 tons.
sense_groups.chinese: 根据研究人员发现的垃圾密度，模型预测大约有5.25万亿个塑料颗粒漂浮在那里……总计约26.9万吨。

sense_groups.english: And more than 90 percent of those pieces may be smaller than a grain of rice.
sense_groups.chinese: 其中超过90%的碎片可能比米粒还小。

sense_groups.english: The study appears in the journal PLOS ONE.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《公共科学图书馆·综合》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: So, what happens to all that plastic?
sense_groups.chinese: 那么，所有这些塑料会怎样呢？

sense_groups.english: "The ocean's going to take it, blast it to smithereens, it's going to cycle it through marine organisms, and sink it to the sea floor.
sense_groups.chinese: “海洋会接收它，把它炸成碎片，让它通过海洋生物循环，然后沉入海底。

sense_groups.english: That's the ultimate life cycle, I believe, for plastics.
sense_groups.chinese: 我相信，这就是塑料的最终生命周期。

sense_groups.english: We're like constantly, you know, sprinkling fish food on the entire ocean surface."
sense_groups.chinese: 我们就像在不断地往整个海洋表面撒鱼食。”

sense_groups.english: The solution, Marcus says, isn't some fleet of seafaring garbage trucks.
sense_groups.chinese: 马库斯说，解决方案不是一支海上垃圾车舰队。

sense_groups.english: It's keeping our trash to ourselves—which would be a real sea change in behavior.
sense_groups.chinese: 而是把垃圾留给自己——这将是行为上的真正巨变。

questions.en:

Build a giant radio telescope on the far side of the moon.

The MIT team will use ______ vehicles to arrange hundreds of antennas across two square ______ of the moon's quiet side.
From this perch, they hope to hear the waves produced from the birth of the universe and get in tune with how it all came to be.

sense_groups.english: Earlier this month, NASA announced that an MIT physics professor will lead a team of scientists on a new mission.
sense_groups.chinese: 本月早些时候，美国宇航局宣布，一位麻省理工学院的物理学教授将带领一组科学家执行一项新任务。

sense_groups.english: The objective?
sense_groups.chinese: 目标是什么？

sense_groups.english: Build a giant radio telescope on the far side of the moon.
sense_groups.chinese: 在月球背面建造一个巨大的射电望远镜。

sense_groups.english: You see, long, long ago—before there even was a galaxy far, far away—the universe settled into a cosmic Dark Age.
sense_groups.chinese: 你看，很久很久以前——甚至在一个遥远的星系存在之前——宇宙进入了一个宇宙黑暗时代。

sense_groups.english: It was a billion year period following the Big Bang and it produced the structure of space as we know it.
sense_groups.chinese: 这是大爆炸之后的一个十亿年时期，它产生了我们所知的空间结构。

sense_groups.english: Astronomers have long hoped to detect the faint, low-frequency radio emissions generated from this time so they could learn more.
sense_groups.chinese: 天文学家长期以来一直希望探测到这一时期产生的微弱低频射电辐射，以便了解更多。

sense_groups.english: But thanks to interference from the ionosphere, not to mention tons of radio and TV signals, Earth is a lousy place to hear.
sense_groups.chinese: 但由于电离层的干扰，更不用说大量的无线电和电视信号，地球是一个糟糕的收听地点。

sense_groups.english: Luckily, the moon rotates so that one side always faces out into space, making it free and clear of noise pollution.
sense_groups.chinese: 幸运的是，月球自转使得一侧始终面向太空，使其免受噪音污染。

sense_groups.english: The MIT team will use automated vehicles to arrange hundreds of antennas across two square kilometers of the moon's quiet side.
sense_groups.chinese: 麻省理工学院的团队将使用自动车辆在月球安静的一侧两平方公里范围内布置数百根天线。

sense_groups.english: From this perch, they hope to hear the waves produced from the birth of the universe and get in tune with how it all came to be.
sense_groups.chinese: 从这个位置，他们希望听到宇宙诞生时产生的波，并了解这一切是如何形成的。

questions.name: #233 Artificial Tastes
questions.en:
Back in ancient times, philosophers like Aristotle were already speculating about the origins of taste, and how the tongue sensed elemental tastes like sweet, bitter, salty and sour.
"What we discovered just a few years ago is that there are regions of the brain—regions of the cortex—where particular fields of neurons represent these different tastes again, so that's a sweet field, a bitter field, a salty field, etcetera." Nick Ryba , a sensory neuroscientist at the National Institutes of Health.
Ryba and his ______ found that you can actually taste without a tongue at all, simply by stimulating the "taste" part of the brain—the insular cortex.
They ran the experiment in mice with a special sort of brain implant—a ______ cable that turns neurons on with a pulse of laser light.
And by switching on the "bitter" sensing part of the brain, they were able to make mice pucker up, as if they were tasting something bitter—even though absolutely nothing bitter was touching the tongues of the mice.
In another experiment, the researchers fed the mice a bitter flavoring on their tongues—but then made it more palatable by switching on the "sweet" zone in the brain.
"What we were doing here was adding the sweetness, but only adding it in the brain, not in what we were giving to the mouse." Think adding sugar to your coffee—but doing it only in your mind.
The results appear in the journal Nature.
Ryba says the study suggests that a lot of our basic judgments about taste—sweet means good, bitter means bad—are actually hard-wired at the level of the brain.
As for that virtual-sugar-in-your-coffee idea?
"I think it's basically science fiction to think that this would be something that would be applied to humans." But today's science fiction might be tomorrow's ______ sweetener.

sense_groups.english: In another experiment, the researchers fed the mice a bitter flavoring on their tongues—but then made it more palatable by switching on the "sweet" zone in the brain.

sense_groups.chinese: 瑞巴说，这项研究表明，我们关于味觉的许多基本判断——甜意味着好，苦意味着坏——实际上是在大脑层面硬连接的。

sense_groups.chinese: 至于那个在咖啡里加虚拟糖的想法？

questions.name: #234 Science in Baseball
questions.en:
Hall of Famer Ted Williams once famously commented that hitting a baseball is the hardest thing to do in sports.
Although Williams—a 0.344 career hitter—made it look easy, he had a point.
Hitting a round ball with a round bat squarely is difficult.
It's also an excellent example of some very ______ applied physics.
No surprise then that professional baseball players are turning to science to improve their multimillion-dollar strokes.
Some approaches focus on the neuroscience of hitting—the deep internal brain ______ behind seeing the pitch and reacting to it.
But for more info about the swing itself, a sports tech company called Zepp Labs makes a sensor that can help break down those mechanics.
The sensor sits in the knob of the company's so-called "Smart Bat" and uses two ______ and a three-axis ______ to measure bat speed, hand speed, attack angle and other factors.
The sensor, which weighs only about eight grams, sends this info to a ______ app via Bluetooth.
The app can then use this data to have an onscreen avatar reenact the swing, in the hope that the batter can pick up some details and make the necessary adjustments.
Zepp's sensors can also be fitted to golf clubs and tennis rackets.
Never one to mince words, Ted Williams also once said that pitchers were quote unquote "the stupidest people alive." Hmm, maybe somebody could come up with a smart baseball to help them.
Against any Ted ______ out there, anyway.

1. entertaining
2. mechanisms
3. accelerometers
4. gyroscope
5. smartphone
6. Williamses

questions.name: #235 Salt

questions.full:
Even if you have a light hand with the salt shaker, you probably get lots of sodium in processed or restaurant meals.
But sodium can contribute to high blood pressure, and ______ the risk for heart disease and failure, stroke, and kidney disease.
So how many of us are limiting our sodium intake to recommended levels—which scientists say could reduce new cases of ______ heart disease by 60-to-120 thousand per year.
Researchers at the Centers for Disease Control analyzed data from the ______ Health and Nutrition ______ Survey from 2005/2006, the most recent years available.

The study appears in the journal Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report.

2. coronary

sense_groups.english: Even if you have a light hand with the salt shaker,
sense_groups.chinese: 即使你撒盐时手很轻，

sense_groups.english: you probably get lots of sodium in processed or restaurant meals.
sense_groups.chinese: 你很可能从加工食品或餐馆餐食中摄入大量钠。

sense_groups.english: But sodium can contribute to high blood pressure,
sense_groups.chinese: 但钠可能导致高血压，

sense_groups.english: and increases the risk for heart disease and failure, stroke, and kidney disease.
sense_groups.chinese: 并增加心脏病、心力衰竭、中风和肾病的风险。

sense_groups.chinese: 那么我们中有多少人将钠摄入量控制在推荐水平呢？

sense_groups.chinese: 科学家称，这每年可减少6万至12万例新的冠心病病例。

sense_groups.english: Researchers at the Centers for Disease Control analyzed data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey from 2005/2006,

sense_groups.chinese: 并回答了一份关于过去24小时饮食的调查问卷。

sense_groups.chinese: 根据数据，

sense_groups.chinese: 只有不到10%的成年人将钠摄入量控制在推荐水平。

sense_groups.chinese: 该研究发表在《发病率和死亡率周报》上。

questions.name: #236 Perfect Pitch
questions.en:
We might think perfect pitch is an innate talent.
Well, a study in the American Journal of Human Genetics is ______ some ______ for that.
Perfect pitch, aka absolute pitch, is the rare ability to name or ______ musical notes like A or middle C without using any comparable reference.
Researchers at the University of California, San Francisco, studied the results from an online test taken by over ten thousand people.
Not surprisingly, individuals tended to either have perfect pitch or not.
But in a closer study of 73 families researchers found a region of genes on ______ eight in those with perfect pitch and also they happened to be from European ancestry.
More study is needed to actually zero in on just which gene or ______ genes might be responsible.
And for comparison they intend to study individuals without perfect pitch but with equivalent musical training.
There is some evidence that babies have the ability for absolute pitch, so researchers for this study theorize that maybe most lose this ability with age, but that what a so-called pitch gene does is extend this talent through a crucial period in childhood.

1. providing
2. evidence
3. recreate
4. chromosome
5. multiple

sense_groups.english: We might think perfect pitch is an innate talent.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们可能认为完美音高是一种天赋。

sense_groups.english: Well, a study in the American Journal of Human Genetics is providing some evidence for that.
sense_groups.chinese: 《美国人类遗传学杂志》的一项研究为此提供了一些证据。

sense_groups.english: Perfect pitch, aka absolute pitch, is the rare ability to name or recreate musical notes like A or middle C without using any comparable reference.
sense_groups.chinese: 完美音高，又称绝对音感，是一种罕见的能力，能够在不使用任何参考的情况下说出或再现像A或中央C这样的音符。

sense_groups.english: Researchers at the University of California, San Francisco, studied the results from an online test taken by over ten thousand people.
sense_groups.chinese: 加州大学旧金山分校的研究人员研究了超过一万人参加的在线测试结果。

sense_groups.english: Not surprisingly, individuals tended to either have perfect pitch or not.
sense_groups.chinese: 毫不奇怪，人们要么有完美音高，要么没有。

sense_groups.english: But in a closer study of 73 families researchers found a region of genes on chromosome eight in those with perfect pitch and also they happened to be from European ancestry.
sense_groups.chinese: 但在对73个家庭的更深入研究中，研究人员发现那些有完美音高的人（恰好是欧洲血统）的8号染色体上有一个基因区域。

sense_groups.english: More study is needed to actually zero in on just which gene or multiple genes might be responsible.
sense_groups.chinese: 需要更多的研究来真正确定是哪个基因或多个基因可能负责。

sense_groups.english: And for comparison they intend to study individuals without perfect pitch but with equivalent musical training.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了比较，他们打算研究没有完美音高但接受过同等音乐训练的人。

sense_groups.english: There is some evidence that babies have the ability for absolute pitch, so researchers for this study theorize that maybe most lose this ability with age, but that what a so-called pitch gene does is extend this talent through a crucial period in childhood.
sense_groups.chinese: 有证据表明婴儿具有绝对音感的能力，因此这项研究的研究人员推测，大多数人可能随着年龄增长失去这种能力，而所谓的音高基因的作用是在童年关键期延长这种天赋。

questions.name: #237 New Treatment
questions.en:
Open a ______ any day of the week and you're likely to read about a "promising new treatment" for one disease or another.
But according to a study published in the September 5th issue of Science, it can take decades for those cures to make it to the clinic.
  ______ from the U.S. and Greece combed through the ______ literature to see how long it actually takes for compounds that look good in the laboratory to get through clinical trials and get used on patients.
The scientists focused their attention on a handful of interventions that were widely hailed as being clinically effective.
And they found that, for the average drug, the time that elapsed between its initial ______ and the first paper to show its clinical effectiveness was about 24 years.
Some drugs moved much faster.
One of the protease inhibitors used to treat HIV made it from patenting through clinical trials in only four years.
Maybe that's because the team studying that drug included experts in both basic and clinical sciences.
The researchers say that such multidisciplinary efforts could help future treatments get to the clinic sooner.
In the meantime, they note, scientists should avoid making promises about quick cures.

questions.name: #238 Junk Food
questions.en:
The new Yankee Stadium has opened in the Bronx.
I went to a game Saturday, and it's a much friendlier place for anyone trying to eat ______ and ______ some environmental awareness.
When I entered the park I stopped at the produce stand—the produce stand!
—and bought a couple of fresh pears.
Later I went to the Noodle Bowl stand, where for $8.50 I got a bowl of noodles, veggies and tofu.
Tofu at the ballpark.
The snack was listed on the menu board at 240 calories.
All the food choices have calorie counts posted now, so you can avoid, or still indulge in, the almost 1,100 calorie Moe's Homewrecker Burrito at La Esquina Latina.
I also had a caramel apple.
Which as junk food goes is still pretty good.
Every few yards you find a trio of disposal cans.
For regular trash, plastic and compost.

And which may eventually foster a garden in which more fresh vegetables take root, root, root for the home team.

questions.name: #239 Obesity in US
questions.en:
As you've probably heard, the US is in the midst of an obesity epidemic.
  ______ just keep getting fatter and fatter.
But the bad news doesn't end there.
Because in today's issue of the New England Journal of Medicine, ______ from Harvard and the University of California in San Diego report that obesity is ______ contagious.
And it seems you catch it from your friends.

And that people with more mass tend to gravitate toward one another, too.
But it's not that folks seek friends with a similar physique.
Or that people who pack on the pounds all frequent the same fast-food franchises or avoid the same gyms.

And their friends as well.

So order the salad and skip dessert.

sense_groups.chinese: 而且体重较重的人也倾向于相互吸引。

sense_groups.english: But it's not that folks seek friends with a similar physique.
sense_groups.chinese: 但这并不是说人们会寻找体型相似的朋友。

sense_groups.english: Or that people who pack on the pounds all frequent the same fast-food franchises or avoid the same gyms.
sense_groups.chinese: 也不是说发胖的人都经常光顾同样的快餐连锁店或避开同样的健身房。

sense_groups.english: What the scientists think is happening is that as those around you start plumping out,
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家认为，实际情况是，当你周围的人开始变胖时，

sense_groups.english: you come to think that being a bit hefty isn't such a bad thing.
sense_groups.chinese: 你会开始觉得稍微胖一点也不是什么坏事。

sense_groups.english: Then as you become larger, so do your friends.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后当你变胖时，你的朋友也会变胖。

sense_groups.english: And your friends' friends.
sense_groups.chinese: 你朋友的朋友也会。

sense_groups.english: And their friends as well.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们的朋友也一样。

sense_groups.english: The good news is that losing weight should also make your friends lighter.
sense_groups.chinese: 好消息是，减肥也会让你的朋友变轻。

sense_groups.english: So order the salad and skip dessert.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以点沙拉，别吃甜点。

sense_groups.english: Believe me, your friends will be glad you did.
sense_groups.chinese: 相信我，你的朋友会很高兴你这么做。

questions.name: #240 Kettle Whistle
questions.en:
British physicist Lord ______ is best known for his ______ of argon and for explaining, in 1871, why the sky is blue.
But he also puzzled over this: .
Rayleigh knew that a kettle makes that sound when steam jets through the hole in a thick lid that has a gap in the middle.
He speculated that the jet becomes unstable inside that gap, setting up an acoustic feedback loop within the gap.
But he couldn't prove it.
Now two engineers at Cambridge University claim to have solved the puzzle—and proved Rayleigh wrong.
The work is in the journal Physics of Fluids.
The engineers found that a kettle ______ ______ in two distinct ways.
It starts off with air ______ in the gap between the layers of the lid, like when you do this and this [sound of whistling].
But as the pressure builds, vortices of steam peel off from the jet exiting the lid.
Each vortex creates sound waves at a ______ that depends on the length of the spout and the pressure inside it.
Rising temperature means rising pressure, which ______ a rising whistle.
Which means it's time for tea.
questions.answer:
1. Rayleigh
2. discovery
3. actually
4. whistles
5. vibrating
6. frequency
7. produces
questions.full:
British physicist Lord ______ is best known for his ______ of argon and for explaining, in 1871, why the sky is blue.
But he also puzzled over this: .
Rayleigh knew that a kettle makes that sound when steam jets through the hole in a thick lid that has a gap in the middle.
He speculated that the jet becomes unstable inside that gap, setting up an acoustic feedback loop within the gap.
But he couldn't prove it.
Now two engineers at Cambridge University claim to have solved the puzzle—and proved Rayleigh wrong.
The work is in the journal Physics of Fluids.
The engineers found that a kettle ______ ______ in two distinct ways.
It starts off with air ______ in the gap between the layers of the lid, like when you do this and this [sound of whistling].
But as the pressure builds, vortices of steam peel off from the jet exiting the lid.
Each vortex creates sound waves at a ______ that depends on the length of the spout and the pressure inside it.
Rising temperature means rising pressure, which ______ a rising whistle.
Which means it's time for tea.

答案:
1. Rayleigh
2. discovery
3. actually
4. whistles
5. vibrating
6. frequency
7. produces

sense_groups.english: British physicist Lord Rayleigh is best known for his discovery of argon
sense_groups.chinese: 英国物理学家瑞利勋爵因发现氩气而闻名

sense_groups.english: and for explaining, in 1871, why the sky is blue.
sense_groups.chinese: 并在1871年解释了天空为什么是蓝色的。

sense_groups.english: But he also puzzled over this: .
sense_groups.chinese: 但他也对这个问题感到困惑：

sense_groups.english: Rayleigh knew that a kettle makes that sound when steam jets through the hole in a thick lid that has a gap in the middle.
sense_groups.chinese: 瑞利知道，当蒸汽从中间有缝隙的厚盖子上的孔喷出时，水壶会发出那种声音。

sense_groups.english: He speculated that the jet becomes unstable inside that gap,
sense_groups.chinese: 他推测，蒸汽流在缝隙内变得不稳定，

sense_groups.english: setting up an acoustic feedback loop within the gap.
sense_groups.chinese: 在缝隙内形成声学反馈回路。

sense_groups.english: But he couldn't prove it.
sense_groups.chinese: 但他无法证明这一点。

sense_groups.english: Now two engineers at Cambridge University claim to have solved the puzzle—and proved Rayleigh wrong.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，剑桥大学的两位工程师声称解开了这个谜团，并证明瑞利是错误的。

sense_groups.english: The work is in the journal Physics of Fluids.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《流体物理学》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: The engineers found that a kettle actually whistles in two distinct ways.
sense_groups.chinese: 工程师们发现，水壶实际上以两种不同的方式发出哨声。

sense_groups.english: It starts off with air vibrating in the gap between the layers of the lid,
sense_groups.chinese: 一开始，空气在盖子各层之间的缝隙中振动，

sense_groups.english: like when you do this and this [sound of whistling].
sense_groups.chinese: 就像你这样做时发出的声音一样[哨声]。

sense_groups.english: But as the pressure builds, vortices of steam peel off from the jet exiting the lid.
sense_groups.chinese: 但随着压力增大，蒸汽涡旋从盖子喷出的气流中脱离。

sense_groups.english: Each vortex creates sound waves at a frequency that depends on the length of the spout and the pressure inside it.
sense_groups.chinese: 每个涡旋产生的声波频率取决于壶嘴的长度和内部压力。

sense_groups.english: Rising temperature means rising pressure, which produces a rising whistle.
sense_groups.chinese: 温度升高意味着压力增大，从而产生越来越高的哨声。

sense_groups.english: Which means it's time for tea.
sense_groups.chinese: 这意味着该喝茶了。

questions.name: #241 Particle Beams
questions.en:
Physicists at the Brookhaven National Laboratory have been able to send information ahead of particle beams ______ at nearly the speed of light.
And the message to the beams is: Get in line.
This technique has been developed at other labs but never used before with particle beams traveling in discrete bunches.
These bunches are important in recreating that ______ moment, the Big Bang.
In these experiments, there are two different sets of ions, electrically charged particles, zooming towards each other around a 2.4 mile track.
They collide into one another to ______ conditions that provide info about the Big Bang.
But the ions spread out as they move.
And this means that there are fewer collisions.
In a technique called stochastic cooling, scientists first measure fluctuations in the beams of ions.
Then they send signals even faster than these ______ to devices up ahead that can kick those particles back into shape.
Researchers say this technique allows them to create these collisions much more ______ and cheaply than other methods.
And so they can get more and better data about what our universe might have been like just after it came into existence.
questions.full:
Physicists at the Brookhaven National Laboratory have been able to send information ahead of particle beams ______ at nearly the speed of light.
And the message to the beams is: Get in line.
This technique has been developed at other labs but never used before with particle beams traveling in discrete bunches.
These bunches are important in recreating that ______ moment, the Big Bang.
In these experiments, there are two different sets of ions, electrically charged particles, zooming towards each other around a 2.4 mile track.
They collide into one another to ______ conditions that provide info about the Big Bang.
But the ions spread out as they move.
And this means that there are fewer collisions.
In a technique called stochastic cooling, scientists first measure fluctuations in the beams of ions.
Then they send signals even faster than these ______ to devices up ahead that can kick those particles back into shape.
Researchers say this technique allows them to create these collisions much more ______ and cheaply than other methods.
And so they can get more and better data about what our universe might have been like just after it came into existence.

答案:
1. racing
2. singular
3. recreate
4. particles
5. frequently

sense_groups.english: Physicists at the Brookhaven National Laboratory have been able to send information ahead of particle beams racing at nearly the speed of light.
sense_groups.chinese: 布鲁克海文国家实验室的物理学家们已经能够将信息发送到以接近光速飞驰的粒子束前方。

sense_groups.english: And the message to the beams is: Get in line.
sense_groups.chinese: 而传递给这些粒子束的信息是：排好队。

sense_groups.english: This technique has been developed at other labs but never used before with particle beams traveling in discrete bunches.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项技术已在其他实验室开发出来，但此前从未用于以离散束团形式运动的粒子束。

sense_groups.english: These bunches are important in recreating that singular moment, the Big Bang.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些束团对于重现那个独一无二的时刻——宇宙大爆炸——至关重要。

sense_groups.english: In these experiments, there are two different sets of ions, electrically charged particles, zooming towards each other around a 2.4 mile track.
sense_groups.chinese: 在这些实验中，有两组不同的离子（带电粒子）沿着一条2.4英里长的轨道相互飞驰靠近。

sense_groups.english: They collide into one another to recreate conditions that provide info about the Big Bang.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们相互碰撞，以重现能够提供宇宙大爆炸信息的条件。

sense_groups.english: But the ions spread out as they move.
sense_groups.chinese: 但离子在运动时会扩散开来。

sense_groups.english: And this means that there are fewer collisions.
sense_groups.chinese: 这意味着碰撞次数会减少。

sense_groups.english: In a technique called stochastic cooling, scientists first measure fluctuations in the beams of ions.
sense_groups.chinese: 在一种名为随机冷却的技术中，科学家首先测量离子束的波动。

sense_groups.english: Then they send signals even faster than these particles to devices up ahead that can kick those particles back into shape.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后，他们以比这些粒子更快的速度将信号发送到前方的装置，这些装置可以将那些粒子踢回原状。

sense_groups.english: Researchers say this technique allows them to create these collisions much more frequently and cheaply than other methods.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员表示，这项技术使他们能够比其他方法更频繁、更廉价地制造这些碰撞。

sense_groups.english: And so they can get more and better data about what our universe might have been like just after it came into existence.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，他们可以获得更多、更好的数据，了解宇宙诞生之初可能的样子。

questions.en:

Although Johnston and his team cloned the gene from a bacterium that thrives in the sea, they also found it in some unexpected places, including microbes that live in the roots of plants.
Because these species are so different, he ______ that the bugs got the gene through a process akin to mating.

sense_groups.english: And now for another episode of ______ Science.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在是《______科学》的另一集。

sense_groups.english: On Monday we talked about cooler sports uniforms, one of George Costanza's crusades.
sense_groups.chinese: 周一我们讨论了更酷的运动服，这是乔治·科斯坦萨的倡导之一。

sense_groups.english: Well, now it's Kramer's idea for a cologne that would make you smell like the beach.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，克莱默想出一种古龙水，让你闻起来像海滩。

sense_groups.english: ______ from the University of East Anglia have just cloned the gene ______ for that briny, fishy scent we associate with the seaside.
sense_groups.chinese: 东安格利亚大学的______刚刚克隆了______基因，这种基因负责我们联想到海边的咸腥气味。

sense_groups.english: Andrew Johnston and his ______ ______ some bacteria from a coastal salt marsh.
sense_groups.chinese: 安德鲁·约翰斯顿和他的______从沿海盐沼中______了一些细菌。

sense_groups.english: And they isolated a gene that makes dimethyl sulfide, a gas whose essence is pure eu d' ocean.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们分离出一种产生二甲硫醚的基因，这种气体的本质是纯正的海水味。

sense_groups.english: In its natural environment, dimethyl sulfide helps sea birds sniff out a meal—in this case the plankton that produce it.

sense_groups.chinese: 这种化合物大量产生，甚至在海洋上空形成云层，有助于冷却地球气候。

sense_groups.english: Although Johnston and his team cloned the gene from a bacterium that thrives in the sea, they also found it in some unexpected places, including microbes that live in the roots of plants.

sense_groups.english: Because these species are so different, he ______ that the bugs got the gene through a process akin to mating.

questions.name: #243 Art Studio
questions.en:
A new ______ find may signify one of the great leaps in human cultural and cognitive history.
Because researchers have discovered a 100,000-year-old art studio.
It was known that ochre—rock with red or yellow pigments—was used for paint even that far back in history.
But there was scant evidence for how it was prepared and handled.
Then, in 2008, researchers uncovered an ochre mixing kit in a South African cave.
They found two abalone shells, most likely used for paint mixing and storage.
They also found ochre, bone, charcoal, grindstones and hammerstones.
The researchers say the ochre was ______ rubbed on quartzite slabs to create a fine powder.
It was then mixed and heated with other crushed substances, including other stones or mammal-bone.
  ______ striations on the inner abalone surface are likely scrape marks left during paint mixing.
The research was published in the journal Science.
The paint may have been used for body adornment or for long-gone artwork.
And the ______ of this paint-production laboratory indicates that the early humans knew basic chemistry and could plan for the future.
One small paint-kit for a few humans, one major leap for humankind.

2. probably

sense_groups.english: A new ______ find may signify one of the great leaps in human cultural and cognitive history.
sense_groups.chinese: 一项新的______发现可能标志着人类文化和认知历史上的重大飞跃之一。

sense_groups.english: Because researchers have discovered a 100,000-year-old art studio.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为研究人员发现了一个10万年前的艺术工作室。

sense_groups.english: It was known that ochre—rock with red or yellow pigments—was used for paint even that far back in history.
sense_groups.chinese: 人们知道，赭石——带有红色或黄色颜料的岩石——早在那个历史时期就被用于绘画。

sense_groups.english: But there was scant evidence for how it was prepared and handled.
sense_groups.chinese: 但关于它是如何准备和处理的证据很少。

sense_groups.english: Then, in 2008, researchers uncovered an ochre mixing kit in a South African cave.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后，在2008年，研究人员在南非的一个洞穴中发现了一个赭石混合工具包。

sense_groups.english: They found two abalone shells, most likely used for paint mixing and storage.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现了两个鲍鱼壳，很可能用于颜料混合和储存。

sense_groups.english: They also found ochre, bone, charcoal, grindstones and hammerstones.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们还发现了赭石、骨头、木炭、磨石和锤石。

sense_groups.english: The researchers say the ochre was ______ rubbed on quartzite slabs to create a fine powder.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员说，赭石被______在石英岩板上摩擦以产生细粉。

sense_groups.english: It was then mixed and heated with other crushed substances, including other stones or mammal-bone.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后与其他粉碎的物质混合并加热，包括其他石头或哺乳动物骨头。

sense_groups.english: ______ striations on the inner abalone surface are likely scrape marks left during paint mixing.
sense_groups.chinese: 鲍鱼壳内表面的______条纹很可能是颜料混合过程中留下的刮痕。

sense_groups.english: The research was published in the journal Science.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《科学》杂志上。

sense_groups.english: The paint may have been used for body adornment or for long-gone artwork.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种颜料可能用于身体装饰或早已消失的艺术品。

sense_groups.english: And the ______ of this paint-production laboratory indicates that the early humans knew basic chemistry and could plan for the future.
sense_groups.chinese: 而这个颜料生产实验室的______表明早期人类了解基础化学并能规划未来。

sense_groups.english: One small paint-kit for a few humans, one major leap for humankind.
sense_groups.chinese: 对少数人类来说是一个小小的颜料工具包，对人类来说是一次重大飞跃。

questions.name: #244 Mars Winter
questions.en:
As many of us broil in August heat, the Mars rover Spirit is hunkered down to survive a far more brutal season—a Martian winter.
Spirit's been on Mars since January 2004 and already ______ previous winters, which run from May through November.
With ______ ______ Spirit at a weak angle, the rover hibernates and uses the scant solar power to recharge batteries and heat itself to -40 degrees .
At least, that's what's ______ in previous winters.
This winter, the game little unit just doesn't have enough juice to keep its heaters on, so temperatures inside the rover will plunge to a frigid -67 degrees Fahrenheit.
When NASA scientists began signaling Spirit on July 26, they hoped to receive a ______ beep back—but so far there's only silence.
The researchers say that in about two months sunlight will start to increase again through March 2011.
If we haven't heard from Spirit by that point, then the likelihood is that we never will.
The rover was ______ to work on Mars for three months, but was mobile for more than five years.
Now mission scientists wait through the Martian winter to see if this ET will phone home.

4. happened
5. communications

questions.name: #245 Jet Lag
questions.en:
Jet lag.
Jumping a few time zones causes problems with sleep and even digestion.
But new research means we could be a step closer to preventing this voyager's vexation.
The study centers on the hormone vasopressin, thought to have a role in maintaining our internal clock.
Researchers genetically ______ mice that do not respond to vasopressin.
Both engineered and normal rodents lived in a set cycle of light and dark for 2 weeks.
Then the researchers changed the light cycle by eight hours.
And the vasopressin-insensitive mice recovered from their induced jet lag much more quickly than did their ______ peers.
The work is in the journal Science.
Jet lag may seem like a minor annoyance.
But for those who travel frequently or work unusual hours, it's a chronic problem that can increase the risk of hypertension and obesity.
You cannot simply knock out ______ signaling permanently—that would have negative effects on behavior and brain activity.
But a drug that ______ suppresses vasopressin to reduce jet lag may be a frequent flier's dream.

2. hormone-sensitive

sense_groups.chinese: 但新研究意味着我们可能离预防这种旅行者的烦恼更近了一步。

sense_groups.english: The study centers on the hormone vasopressin, thought to have a role in maintaining our internal clock.
sense_groups.chinese: 该研究聚焦于激素加压素，它被认为在维持我们的生物钟方面起作用。

sense_groups.english: Researchers genetically engineered mice that do not respond to vasopressin.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员通过基因改造培育出对加压素无反应的小鼠。

sense_groups.english: Both engineered and normal rodents lived in a set cycle of light and dark for 2 weeks.
sense_groups.chinese: 改造过的小鼠和正常小鼠都在固定的光暗周期中生活了两周。

sense_groups.english: Then the researchers changed the light cycle by eight hours.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后研究人员将光周期改变了八小时。

questions.name: #247 Great Lies
questions.en:
When I was pregnant, a friend gave me a book called Great Lies to Tell Small Kids.
In it are gems like "wine makes mommy charming" and "men don't go bald naturally, they like getting their hair cut that way." Now, if you're filled with horror at the notion of pulling a toddler's leg like that, a new study in the Journal of Moral Education shows that parents regularly use deception to ______ their kids.
We can all recall lies our parents told us to get us to do something, or to stop doing something.
"If you cross your eyes they could stay that way" comes to mind.
But in the current study, ______ found that these parental fibs are hardly few and far between.
And that even parents who preach to their kids about the importance of being honest admit to lying to them as well.
The researchers plan to extend their studies to see whether all this lying ______ children's trust.
Until then, well, keep telling junior that if he spins around really fast, then stops, his face will skid around to the back of his head.
It could keep him busy while mommy becomes even more charming.

sense_groups.english: Now, if you're filled with horror at the notion of pulling a toddler's leg like that,
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，如果你对这种捉弄小孩的想法感到恐惧，

sense_groups.chinese: 我们都能回忆起父母为了让我们做某事或停止做某事而说的谎话。

questions.name: #248 Cereal Boxes
questions.en:
When you walk down the cereal aisle, do you ever get the feeling that Cap'n Crunch is looking at you?
Well, that's just silly.
He's ______ looking at your kids.
That's according to a study by Brian Wansink and colleagues at Cornell University's Food and Brand Lab.
The researchers wondered whether the ______ on cereal boxes actually make eye contact.
And whether that could influence a shopper's choice of breakfast fare.
So they hit the cereal aisle.
And they found that kids' cereals tend to be placed on lower shelves than grownup offerings.
What's more, Tony the Tiger and his kid-friendly pals tend to gaze downward, while the Quaker Oats guy stares straight ahead.
In a second study, adult volunteers were handed a box of Trix.
On some boxes, the rabbit looked straight ahead, on others, he gazed away.
When asked what they thought of Trix, it seems that folks felt more ______ to the brand, and said they preferred that cereal over others, when the rabbit looked them in the eye.
The results, which appear in the Journal of ______ and Behavior, suggest that certain tricks are not just for kids…but maybe for marketers, too.

sense_groups.chinese: 嗯，那只是傻想法。

sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员想知道麦片盒上的角色是否真的会进行眼神交流。

sense_groups.english: And whether that could influence a shopper's choice of breakfast fare.

questions.name: #249 Microbial Cloud
questions.en:
You might blame your pets for shedding all over the house.
But we humans do it too—and our stuff is alive.
"We're ______ emitting ______ around us.
And this is coming from shedding of our skin, from exhaling, our hair, we're just full of these guys." Adam Altrichter, a microbial ecologist at the ______ of Oregon.
"We've never been sterile organisms.
We are definitely masses of microbes both in and on us."
If you're picturing the Peanuts character Pig Pen, you may not be far off.
Because biologists ______ we shed a million particles an hour—including, of course, a lot of bacteria.
Altrichter and his ______ wanted to measure that cloud of particles—the "Pig Pen" effect, if you will—so they asked 11 volunteers not to shower, dressed them in shorts and tank tops, and put them in a sterile chamber for hours at a time, while collecting microbial samples on surfaces and in the air.
What they found in those samples was a menagerie of bacteria from the volunteers' skin, guts, genital tracts, lungs, noses and mouths.
And for eight of the 11 study subjects, the microbial cloud was unique enough to identify the individual who'd left it—suggesting that this bacterial 'fingerprint' could someday be used in forensics.
The study is in the journal PeerJ.
Given that we spend 90 percent of our lives indoors, our microbial clouds also colonize the places we live and work—and, yes, the people around us.
"And so it's just kind of interesting to think about how the people that we interact with at work, or in classrooms, or in other environments, how we could be sharing some of these microbial ______ between us, not even knowing anything about it." And now that you do know about it—hopefully your view of your coworkers won't become…clouded.
questions.answer:
1. constantly
2. microbes
3. University
4. estimate
5. colleagues
6. passengers

sense_groups.chinese: “所以，想想我们在工作中、教室里或其他环境中互动的人，我们如何在不知不觉中分享这些微生物乘客，这还挺有趣的。”

sense_groups.english: And now that you do know about it—hopefully your view of your coworkers won't become…clouded.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在你知道了——希望你对同事的看法不会变得……模糊不清。

questions.name: #251 Self-healed Scratches
questions.en:
If you get a scratch, your skin can heal itself.
But if your car gets scratched, it stays scratched.
Scientists at the ______ of Southern ______ think they may have solved that problem.
They've developed a new ______ that can self-heal ______ when exposed to sunlight.
They published this ______ in the March 13th issue of the journal Science.
The new technology first takes polyurethane—the coating on many cars.
Then researchers added chitosan—that's a key polymer in crab and shrimp shells.
The final bit thrown into the mix are minute amounts of oxetane rings, with three atoms of carbon and one of oxygen.
The researchers are trying to mimic natural processes.
Here's how it works.
When there's a scratch, ______ the molecule, the oxetane ring opens.
It has two reactive ends.
In sunlight, chitosan breaks into two chains and generates free radicals.
Then those chitosan chains link up with the reactive ends of the oxetane, filling in the scratch.
Researchers say this technique is much simpler and more cost-efficient than other attempts at self-healing.
So maybe in the future, when your car gets scraped, it'll be all healed up before you have to spend any of your hard earned scratch.
questions.answer:
1. University
2. Mississippi
3. material
4. scratches
5. research
6. damaging
questions.full:
If you get a scratch, your skin can heal itself.
But if your car gets scratched, it stays scratched.
Scientists at the ______ of Southern ______ think they may have solved that problem.

Researchers say this technique is much simpler and more cost-efficient than other attempts at self-healing.

答案:
1. University

sense_groups.english: If you get a scratch, your skin can heal itself.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你划伤了，你的皮肤可以自我愈合。

sense_groups.english: But if your car gets scratched, it stays scratched.
sense_groups.chinese: 但如果你的车被划伤，它会一直有划痕。

sense_groups.english: Scientists at the University of Southern Mississippi think they may have solved that problem.
sense_groups.chinese: 南密西西比大学的科学家们认为他们可能已经解决了这个问题。

sense_groups.english: They've developed a new material that can self-heal scratches when exposed to sunlight.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们开发了一种新材料，在阳光下可以自我修复划痕。

sense_groups.english: They published this research in the March 13th issue of the journal Science.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们在3月13日的《科学》杂志上发表了这项研究。

sense_groups.english: The new technology first takes polyurethane—the coating on many cars.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项新技术首先采用聚氨酯——许多汽车上的涂层。

sense_groups.english: Then researchers added chitosan—that's a key polymer in crab and shrimp shells.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后研究人员添加了壳聚糖——这是蟹和虾壳中的一种关键聚合物。

sense_groups.english: The final bit thrown into the mix are minute amounts of oxetane rings, with three atoms of carbon and one of oxygen.
sense_groups.chinese: 最后加入混合物的是微量的氧杂环丁烷环，含有三个碳原子和一个氧原子。

sense_groups.english: The researchers are trying to mimic natural processes.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员试图模仿自然过程。

sense_groups.english: Here's how it works.
sense_groups.chinese: 它的工作原理如下。

sense_groups.english: When there's a scratch, damaging the molecule, the oxetane ring opens.
sense_groups.chinese: 当有划痕损坏分子时，氧杂环丁烷环会打开。

sense_groups.english: It has two reactive ends.
sense_groups.chinese: 它有两个反应端。

sense_groups.english: In sunlight, chitosan breaks into two chains and generates free radicals.
sense_groups.chinese: 在阳光下，壳聚糖断裂成两条链并产生自由基。

sense_groups.english: Then those chitosan chains link up with the reactive ends of the oxetane, filling in the scratch.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后这些壳聚糖链与氧杂环丁烷的反应端连接，填补划痕。

sense_groups.english: Researchers say this technique is much simpler and more cost-efficient than other attempts at self-healing.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员表示，这项技术比其他自我修复尝试更简单、更经济。

sense_groups.english: So maybe in the future, when your car gets scraped, it'll be all healed up before you have to spend any of your hard earned scratch.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以也许在未来，当你的车被刮伤时，在你花掉辛苦赚来的钱之前，它就已经完全愈合了。

questions.name: #252 Steroids
questions.en:
Veteran sportswriter and ______ professor Justice B. Hill on August 1st at the annual meeting of the National Association of Black Journalists in Orlando.
But that resolution won't be easy.
"The science will always stay ahead of the detection.

"The ______ of the technology is going to make this detection game even more dicier in the years to come.

And I think baseball, the union, all of them are tired of the discussion of steroids.

2. recently

sense_groups.english: Veteran sportswriter and journalism professor Justice B. Hill
sense_groups.chinese: 资深体育记者兼新闻学教授贾斯蒂斯·B·希尔

sense_groups.english: on August 1st at the annual meeting of the National Association of Black Journalists in Orlando.
sense_groups.chinese: 8月1日在奥兰多举行的全国黑人记者协会年会上。

sense_groups.english: But that resolution won't be easy.
sense_groups.chinese: 但解决这个问题并不容易。

sense_groups.english: "The science will always stay ahead of the detection.
sense_groups.chinese: "科学总是领先于检测手段。

sense_groups.english: I did an interview recently with a bioethicist from Case Western Reserve University.
sense_groups.chinese: 我最近采访了凯斯西储大学的一位生物伦理学家。

sense_groups.english: And one of the things he advocates is, let players use whatever they want to under a doctor's supervision.
sense_groups.chinese: 他主张的一点是，让球员在医生监督下使用任何他们想用的东西。

sense_groups.english: Because he understands — I did a piece years ago where I was talking to one of the foremost authorities on PEDs,

sense_groups.english: and one of the things he said was we're going to get into gene cloning.
sense_groups.chinese: 他说的一件事是，我们将进入基因克隆领域。

sense_groups.english: "The sophistication of the technology is going to make this detection game even more dicier in the years to come.
sense_groups.chinese: "技术的复杂性将使未来的检测游戏更加棘手。

sense_groups.english: And I think baseball, the union, all of them are tired of the discussion of steroids.
sense_groups.chinese: 我认为棒球界、工会，所有人都厌倦了关于类固醇的讨论。

sense_groups.english: They want to get back to the playing of the game.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们想回到比赛本身。

sense_groups.english: And that's a huge issue for those of us who love baseball."
sense_groups.chinese: 这对我们这些热爱棒球的人来说是个大问题。"

questions.name: #253 Recognition of Voice
questions.en:
It's tough to pick a familiar face out of a crowd—but focusing on a known voice in a noisy room is easy.
And a new study scanned volunteers' brains to look at how we solve the so-called cocktail party problem.
The work is in the journal Nature.
Researchers ______ the activity of the subject's cerebral cortexes while playing them ______ spoken by ______ voices.
First, the subjects listened to ______ sentences and reported key ______ of each one.
Then, they heard two different sentences played at the same time, but had to listen to and recall details from only one voice.
Each voice drew a ______ response from the ______ cortex.
And even with an extra sentence playing simultaneously, researchers saw that the cortex responded specifically to the voice that the subject was focusing on.
This finding indicates that our brains process sound based not only on the audio input they receive, but also on our listening goals.
And it could lead to speech tracking systems that are accurate in crowds — even at a cocktail party.
questions.answer:

2. sentences
3. different
4. individual
5. features
6. particular
7. auditory

And a new study scanned volunteers' brains to look at how we solve the so-called cocktail party problem.

And it could lead to speech tracking systems that are accurate in crowds — even at a cocktail party.

2. sentences

sense_groups.english: It's tough to pick a familiar face out of a crowd—
sense_groups.chinese: 从人群中认出熟悉的面孔很难——

sense_groups.english: but focusing on a known voice in a noisy room is easy.
sense_groups.chinese: 但在嘈杂的房间里专注于一个熟悉的声音却很容易。

sense_groups.english: And a new study scanned volunteers' brains
sense_groups.chinese: 一项新研究扫描了志愿者的大脑

sense_groups.english: to look at how we solve the so-called cocktail party problem.
sense_groups.chinese: 以探究我们如何解决所谓的鸡尾酒会问题。

sense_groups.english: The work is in the journal Nature.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《自然》杂志上。

sense_groups.english: Researchers recorded the activity of the subject's cerebral cortexes
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员记录了受试者大脑皮层的活动

sense_groups.english: while playing them sentences spoken by different voices.
sense_groups.chinese: 同时播放由不同声音说出的句子。

sense_groups.english: First, the subjects listened to individual sentences
sense_groups.chinese: 首先，受试者听单独的句子

sense_groups.chinese: 并报告每个句子的关键特征。

sense_groups.english: Then, they heard two different sentences played at the same time,
sense_groups.chinese: 然后，他们同时听到两个不同的句子，

sense_groups.english: but had to listen to and recall details from only one voice.
sense_groups.chinese: 但必须只听并回忆其中一个声音的细节。

sense_groups.english: Each voice drew a particular response from the auditory cortex.
sense_groups.chinese: 每个声音都从听觉皮层引发了特定的反应。

sense_groups.english: And even with an extra sentence playing simultaneously,
sense_groups.chinese: 即使同时播放额外的句子，

sense_groups.english: researchers saw that the cortex responded specifically to the voice
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员发现，皮层会专门对

sense_groups.english: that the subject was focusing on.
sense_groups.chinese: 受试者正在关注的声音做出反应。

sense_groups.english: This finding indicates that our brains process sound

sense_groups.english: based not only on the audio input they receive,
sense_groups.chinese: 不仅基于接收到的音频输入，

sense_groups.chinese: 还基于我们的聆听目标。

questions.name: #254 Net Loss
questions.en:
Some things are hard to remember.
Others are hard to forget—especially things that are traumatic.
But kids, it turns out, are better than adults at ______ the bad stuff.
Now scientists think they know why.
According to an animal study in the September 4th issue of the journal Science, the brains of adults erect ______ barriers that keep painful ______ intact.
As adults, events that emotionally disturb us tend to get seared into our brains.
And those memories can resurface, causing anxiety, fear and even post-traumatic stress disorder.
But young brains are much more resilient—and can even erase unpleasant memories.
To get a better handle on this youthful forgetting, scientists studied the brains of young and old rats.
They found that in adult brains, a physical net forms around certain cells in the amygdala, a structure associated with ______ memories.
Adults that had been trained to associate a mild foot shock with a specific sound would flinch when they just heard the sound.
But using a drug to dissolve this barrier restored the older rats' ability to ______ fearful memories.
So rats that got the net-busting treatment stayed calm when they heard the sound.
It's one of the few instances where a net loss is a real gain.

sense_groups.english: Some things are hard to remember.
sense_groups.chinese: 有些事情很难记住。

sense_groups.english: Others are hard to forget—especially things that are traumatic.
sense_groups.chinese: 其他事情却很难忘记——尤其是那些创伤性的事情。

sense_groups.english: But kids, it turns out, are better than adults at forgetting the bad stuff.
sense_groups.chinese: 但事实证明，孩子们比成年人更擅长忘记不好的事情。

sense_groups.english: Now scientists think they know why.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在科学家们认为他们知道原因了。

sense_groups.english: According to an animal study in the September 4th issue of the journal Science,
sense_groups.chinese: 根据9月4日《科学》杂志上的一项动物研究，

sense_groups.english: the brains of adults erect physical barriers that keep painful memories intact.
sense_groups.chinese: 成年人的大脑会建立物理屏障，使痛苦的记忆保持完整。

sense_groups.english: As adults, events that emotionally disturb us tend to get seared into our brains.
sense_groups.chinese: 作为成年人，那些让我们情绪不安的事件往往会烙印在我们的大脑中。

sense_groups.english: And those memories can resurface, causing anxiety, fear and even post-traumatic stress disorder.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些记忆可能会重新浮现，导致焦虑、恐惧甚至创伤后应激障碍。

sense_groups.english: But young brains are much more resilient—and can even erase unpleasant memories.
sense_groups.chinese: 但年轻的大脑更具弹性——甚至能够抹去不愉快的记忆。

sense_groups.english: To get a better handle on this youthful forgetting,
sense_groups.chinese: 为了更好地理解这种年轻时的遗忘现象，

sense_groups.english: scientists studied the brains of young and old rats.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们研究了年轻和年老老鼠的大脑。

sense_groups.english: They found that in adult brains,
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现，在成年大脑中，

sense_groups.english: a physical net forms around certain cells in the amygdala,
sense_groups.chinese: 杏仁核中某些细胞周围会形成一个物理网，

sense_groups.english: a structure associated with emotional memories.
sense_groups.chinese: 杏仁核是与情感记忆相关的结构。

sense_groups.english: Adults that had been trained to associate a mild foot shock with a specific sound
sense_groups.chinese: 那些被训练将轻微足部电击与特定声音联系起来的成年老鼠，

sense_groups.chinese: 一听到那个声音就会退缩。

sense_groups.english: But using a drug to dissolve this barrier
sense_groups.chinese: 但使用一种药物溶解这个屏障后，

sense_groups.english: So rats that got the net-busting treatment stayed calm when they heard the sound.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，接受破网治疗的老鼠在听到声音时保持冷静。

sense_groups.english: It's one of the few instances where a net loss is a real gain.

questions.name: #255 Spicy Food
questions.en:
Chinese cuisine has a lot of ______ spicy dishes, like mapo tofu and hot pot.
And, of course, there's the ever-present chili oil.
"I like spicy food myself." Lu Qi, an epidemiologist at the Harvard School of Public Health.
"Almost every day, I eat spicy food." That spicy tradition served as ______ inspiration for Qi: he and colleagues performed a study which found that a daily dose of chilies might actually be a boon to your health.
The researchers enrolled nearly half a million Chinese volunteers, aged 30 to 79.
They quizzed them on their affinity for fiery foods, and followed each study subject for an average of seven years.
During that time, more than 20,000 of the ______ died.
But after controlling for factors like smoking history and income, the scientists found that the risk of death was 10 percent lower in those who ate spicy food a couple times a week, compared with those who abstained.
And daily chili eaters, like Lu, had a 14 percent lower risk of dying.
That figure held true for both men and women.
And yes, while it is a ______ modest effect, Lu says to keep in mind: we're just talking about chilies here.
"It's not medicine." The findings appear in the British Medical Journal.
Previous studies have shown that capsaicin, the active ingredient in chillies, has anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial effects, among others.
But before you grab the Tabasco, this study does not prove causation.
For example, could be that people with weaker constitutions avoid spicy foods—making chili lovers appear more hardy in comparison.
And the authors do not recommend starting a chili habit if you already have a sensitive stomach.
But at least one thing's clear: indulging in spicy food probably won't hurt.
Other than, well, your tongue.

questions.name: #256 Ringing Ears
questions.en:
If you're ever worried that you've had one too many drinks after a night of bar-hopping, you might want to ask yourself: Are my ears ringing?
Because it turns out that when the music gets loud, we tend to drain our mug of brew faster.
That's according to a study to be published in the journal Alcoholism: Clinical and Experimental Research.
Researchers staked out two bars in the west of France and ______ ______ habits of 40 patrons.
With permission from bartenders, the scientists pumped up the volume of a Top 40 station from 72 to 88 pounding decibels.
In this ______ din of pop-music, patrons drank more in less time.
While it's been known that music played in the mall can influence consumer behavior, this study is the first to take that theory to the bar scene.
The researchers ______ that loud music may energize and excite bar-hoppers, making them more likely to binge.
Or, they say, perhaps it was just too loud to talk, so people focused instead on their pint-sized companions.
Either way, if you're trying to cut back on your beer, might I suggest an earplug chaser?

questions.name: #257 Helmet Law
questions.en:
Jerry Seinfeld once said, "The stupidest thing is a helmet law, the point of which is to protect a brain that is functioning so poorly it's not even trying to prevent the ______ of the skull it's in." But helmet laws for kids, who may not have considered their skulls as deeply as Jerry did, aren't so dumb.
That's ______ to a new study in a publication from the Chocrane Collaboration, which is an international organization that ______ health care research.
The review looked at five studies of kids bike-helmet laws.
One big 10 year study in California found that bike-related ______ brain injury in kids dropped more than 18 percent after the state's bike helmet law was enacted.
A Canadian study looked at almost 10,000 bike related ______ admissions and found a 45 percent drop in childhood head injuries in provinces that passed helmet laws.
Provinces without helmet laws also saw a drop in the same period, but only half as much.
And three other studies found that helmet laws do indeed persuade kids to wear their helmets, with ______ in compliance ranging from 45 to 84 percent.
questions.answer:

2. according
3. evaluates
4. traumatic
5. hospital
6. increases

sense_groups.english: Jerry Seinfeld once said, "The stupidest thing is a helmet law, the point of which is to protect a brain that is functioning so poorly it's not even trying to prevent the cracking of the skull it's in."
sense_groups.chinese: 杰瑞·宋飞曾说过：‘最愚蠢的事情就是头盔法，其目的是保护一个功能如此差的大脑，它甚至都不试图防止其所在头骨的开裂。’

sense_groups.english: But helmet laws for kids, who may not have considered their skulls as deeply as Jerry did, aren't so dumb.
sense_groups.chinese: 但对于孩子们来说，头盔法并不那么愚蠢，他们可能没有像杰瑞那样深入考虑过自己的头骨。

sense_groups.english: That's according to a new study in a publication from the Chocrane Collaboration, which is an international organization that evaluates health care research.
