sense_groups.english: The review looked at five studies of kids bike-helmet laws.
sense_groups.chinese: 该综述考察了五项关于儿童自行车头盔法的研究。

sense_groups.english: One big 10 year study in California found that bike-related traumatic brain injury in kids dropped more than 18 percent after the state's bike helmet law was enacted.
sense_groups.chinese: 加州一项为期10年的大型研究发现，在该州自行车头盔法实施后，儿童中与自行车相关的创伤性脑损伤下降了超过18%。

sense_groups.english: A Canadian study looked at almost 10,000 bike related hospital admissions and found a 45 percent drop in childhood head injuries in provinces that passed helmet laws.
sense_groups.chinese: 一项加拿大研究调查了近1万例与自行车相关的住院病例，发现在通过头盔法的省份，儿童头部受伤下降了45%。

sense_groups.english: Provinces without helmet laws also saw a drop in the same period, but only half as much.
sense_groups.chinese: 没有头盔法的省份在同一时期也出现了下降，但只有一半的幅度。

sense_groups.english: And three other studies found that helmet laws do indeed persuade kids to wear their helmets, with increases in compliance ranging from 45 to 84 percent.
sense_groups.chinese: 另外三项研究发现，头盔法确实能说服孩子们佩戴头盔，合规率提高了45%到84%。

questions.name: #258 Foraging to Farming
questions.en:
A team of ______ working in Jordan has made a discovery that represents a new chapter in the story of our ______ move from foraging to farming.
The ______ ______ an ancient granary.
The round, mud hut dates back more than 11,000 years.
A raised floor was key for keeping grain dry and out of reach of hungry rats.
But what makes the find so special is that the granary was built a ______ years before people ate domesticated crops.
The report appears in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
The researchers found caches of wild barley and oats inside the structure.
Such evidence of a dedicated food-storage edifice has never been recorded from the pre-pottery Neolithic age.
The ______ say this selective cultivation and management of wild plants shows behaviors that led to agriculture.
What's more, the granaries were built in-between houses and buildings used for food processing, which led to the establishment of more permanent settlements.
By stockpiling a food surplus, our predecessors produced a new societal structure and curbed their wandering ways.
Which then led to today's foraging for junk food in supermarket aisles.
questions.answer:
1. archeologists
2. ancestors'
3. researchers
4. unearthed
5. thousand
6. investigators
questions.full:
A team of ______ working in Jordan has made a discovery that represents a new chapter in the story of our ______ move from foraging to farming.

The round, mud hut dates back more than 11,000 years.
A raised floor was key for keeping grain dry and out of reach of hungry rats.
But what makes the find so special is that the granary was built a ______ years before people ate domesticated crops.

The researchers found caches of wild barley and oats inside the structure.
Such evidence of a dedicated food-storage edifice has never been recorded from the pre-pottery Neolithic age.

By stockpiling a food surplus, our predecessors produced a new societal structure and curbed their wandering ways.

2. ancestors'
3. researchers
4. unearthed
5. thousand

sense_groups.english: A team of archeologists working in Jordan has made a discovery
sense_groups.chinese: 在约旦工作的一队考古学家有了一个发现

sense_groups.english: that represents a new chapter in the story of our ancestors' move from foraging to farming.
sense_groups.chinese: 这代表了我们的祖先从采集到农耕的故事的新篇章。

sense_groups.english: The researchers unearthed an ancient granary.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员发掘出了一个古老的粮仓。

sense_groups.english: The round, mud hut dates back more than 11,000 years.
sense_groups.chinese: 这个圆形的泥屋可追溯到11000多年前。

sense_groups.english: A raised floor was key for keeping grain dry and out of reach of hungry rats.
sense_groups.chinese: 抬高的地板对于保持谷物干燥和防止饥饿的老鼠接触至关重要。

sense_groups.english: But what makes the find so special is that the granary was built a thousand years before people ate domesticated crops.
sense_groups.chinese: 但这一发现之所以特别，是因为这个粮仓是在人们食用驯化作物前一千年建造的。

sense_groups.english: The report appears in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
sense_groups.chinese: 该报告发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。

sense_groups.english: The researchers found caches of wild barley and oats inside the structure.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员在该结构内发现了野生大麦和燕麦的储藏。

sense_groups.english: Such evidence of a dedicated food-storage edifice has never been recorded from the pre-pottery Neolithic age.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种专门用于储存食物的建筑证据在前陶新石器时代从未被记录过。

sense_groups.english: The investigators say this selective cultivation and management of wild plants shows behaviors that led to agriculture.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究者们说，这种对野生植物的选择性种植和管理显示了导致农业的行为。

sense_groups.english: What's more, the granaries were built in-between houses and buildings used for food processing, which led to the establishment of more permanent settlements.

sense_groups.chinese: 这进而导致了今天在超市过道里搜寻垃圾食品的行为。

questions.name: #259 Space Hazard
questions.en:
There are many occupational hazards in space travel.
But Russian researchers have discovered a new one: meaner bacteria.
Scientists ______ ______ of bacilli and E. coli into space and found they undergo significant changes.
And not good ones either.
The bacteria became much more aggressive and started to eat space ship components.
That's because they began to produce unusual enzymes, probably because of exposure to cosmic radiation and the lack of gravitation.
The study on board the Mir and Photon 2 ______ found that the changes occur even during short flights of 10 to 14 days.
The bacteria change size and shape and their DNA changes too.
Some genes that are dormant on earth switch on, ______ the enzymes.
The researchers think that it's also likely that the mutant bacteria could pose greater threats to astronauts, who already suffer from immune system ______ in space.
But there's one piece of good news: when the bacteria return to earth the aggressive traits vanish.

2. colonies
3. spaceships
4. producing
5. problems

sense_groups.chinese: 但俄罗斯研究人员发现了一个新的：更凶猛的细菌。

sense_groups.chinese: 细菌的大小和形状发生变化，它们的DNA也发生变化。

sense_groups.english: Some genes that are dormant on earth switch on, producing the enzymes.
sense_groups.chinese: 地球上休眠的一些基因被激活，产生这些酶。

sense_groups.english: The researchers think that it's also likely that the mutant bacteria could pose greater threats to astronauts, who already suffer from immune system problems in space.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员认为，变异细菌也可能对宇航员构成更大威胁，而宇航员在太空中已经面临免疫系统问题。

sense_groups.english: But there's one piece of good news: when the bacteria return to earth the aggressive traits vanish.
sense_groups.chinese: 但有一个好消息：当细菌返回地球时，攻击性特征消失。

questions.name: #260 Urban Birds
questions.en:
Animals that live in the city are usually less wary of humans than their rural counterparts.
Most people think the boldness comes from experience: since the ______ of humans are rather harmless, the critters learn to go about their business without fear.
But the truth turns out to be far more interesting, at least for Australian swans.
Turns out the city birds are genetically ______ from their country counterparts.
Australian ______ looked at two groups of swans.
One population lived on a pond in the center of Melbourne.
The second hung out just 30 kilometers away in a more bucolic setting, surrounded by far fewer humans.
The researchers measured what they call each bird's "flight initiation distance": basically, how close could a human get before the swan would fly away?
"We found that the flight initiation distance for the swans at the urban ______ was only 13 meters, and on average at the non-urban environment it was 96 meters.
So that's like an 83 meter difference, a really big ______ in how wary these swans are at the two habitats." Victoria University ecologist Wouter van Dongen.
The researchers also took blood samples from some of the swans to analyze their DNA.
And almost 90 percent of urban swans had the same variant of a gene for dopamine transport, while just 60 percent of rural birds had that version.
And those swans were less wary of humans than were the swans with the rarer genotypes.
Dopamine influences a lot of brain function, so the gene ______ could be behind the difference in swan attitudes.
The study is in the journal BMC Evolutionary Biology.
Since swans can easily fly wherever they want, the researchers think that the bolder birds don't mind setting up shop in the city, while the more timid swans prefer the quieter country life.
And that's something that wildlife managers should keep in mind.
"With release programs, often you breed up a small population of whatever animal and then you release them into the wild…and so one potential application of our research is to select individuals that are better able to cope with human disturbance, those that are less wary of humans, and release them into those areas that are more likely to experience human disturbance."

1. majority
2. different
3. researchers
4. environment
5. difference
6. variation

sense_groups.english: Animals that live in the city are usually less wary of humans than their rural counterparts.

sense_groups.english: Most people think the boldness comes from experience: since the majority of humans are rather harmless, the critters learn to go about their business without fear.
sense_groups.chinese: 大多数人认为这种大胆源于经验：由于大多数人类相当无害，这些小动物学会了无所畏惧地做自己的事。

sense_groups.english: But the truth turns out to be far more interesting, at least for Australian swans.
sense_groups.chinese: 但事实证明真相要有趣得多，至少对澳大利亚天鹅来说是这样。

sense_groups.english: Turns out the city birds are genetically different from their country counterparts.
sense_groups.chinese: 原来城市鸟类在基因上与其乡村同类不同。

sense_groups.english: Australian researchers looked at two groups of swans.
sense_groups.chinese: 澳大利亚研究人员观察了两组天鹅。

sense_groups.english: One population lived on a pond in the center of Melbourne.
sense_groups.chinese: 一群生活在墨尔本市中心的一个池塘上。

sense_groups.english: The second hung out just 30 kilometers away in a more bucolic setting, surrounded by far fewer humans.
sense_groups.chinese: 第二群就在30公里外一个更田园的环境中，周围人类少得多。

sense_groups.english: The researchers measured what they call each bird's "flight initiation distance": basically, how close could a human get before the swan would fly away?
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员测量了他们所谓的每只鸟的“飞行启动距离”：基本上，人类能靠近到多远天鹅才会飞走？

sense_groups.english: "We found that the flight initiation distance for the swans at the urban environment was only 13 meters, and on average at the non-urban environment it was 96 meters.
sense_groups.chinese: “我们发现城市环境中的天鹅的飞行启动距离只有13米，而非城市环境中平均为96米。”

sense_groups.english: So that's like an 83 meter difference, a really big difference in how wary these swans are at the two habitats." Victoria University ecologist Wouter van Dongen.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以这就像83米的差异，这些天鹅在两个栖息地的警惕性差异非常大。”维多利亚大学生态学家沃特·范·东根说。

sense_groups.english: The researchers also took blood samples from some of the swans to analyze their DNA.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员还从一些天鹅身上采集了血样来分析它们的DNA。

sense_groups.english: And almost 90 percent of urban swans had the same variant of a gene for dopamine transport, while just 60 percent of rural birds had that version.
sense_groups.chinese: 几乎90%的城市天鹅拥有相同的多巴胺转运基因变体，而只有60%的乡村天鹅拥有该版本。

sense_groups.english: And those swans were less wary of humans than were the swans with the rarer genotypes.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些天鹅比拥有更稀有基因型的天鹅对人类更不警惕。

sense_groups.english: Dopamine influences a lot of brain function, so the gene variation could be behind the difference in swan attitudes.
sense_groups.chinese: 多巴胺影响许多大脑功能，因此基因变异可能是天鹅态度差异的背后原因。

sense_groups.english: The study is in the journal BMC Evolutionary Biology.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《BMC进化生物学》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: Since swans can easily fly wherever they want, the researchers think that the bolder birds don't mind setting up shop in the city, while the more timid swans prefer the quieter country life.
sense_groups.chinese: 由于天鹅可以轻松飞到任何地方，研究人员认为更大胆的鸟不介意在城市安家，而更胆小的天鹅更喜欢安静的乡村生活。

sense_groups.english: And that's something that wildlife managers should keep in mind.
sense_groups.chinese: 这是野生动物管理者应该牢记的一点。

sense_groups.english: "With release programs, often you breed up a small population of whatever animal and then you release them into the wild…and so one potential application of our research is to select individuals that are better able to cope with human disturbance, those that are less wary of humans, and release them into those areas that are more likely to experience human disturbance."
sense_groups.chinese: “在放归项目中，通常你会繁殖一小群某种动物，然后将它们放归野外……因此我们研究的一个潜在应用是选择那些更能应对人类干扰的个体，即那些对人类不太警惕的个体，并将它们放归到更可能经历人类干扰的区域。”

questions.name: #261 Election
questions.en:
On election day, where do you vote?
If it's in a church, you might be inclined to vote more ______ than if you cast your ballot at a school or ______ building.
That's ______ to research published in the International Journal for the Psychology of Religion.
And the effect seems to hold, whether you're Christian, Muslim or agnostic, progressive, independent or conservative.
The study found that when random people were surveyed in front of a church, they gave more ______ and politically conservative responses than people surveyed while standing in front of a government building.
The shift in people's attitudes, the researchers suggest, was likely a result of visual priming—meaning that people who could see the religious ______ were, consciously or not, getting cues that influenced their response.
The surveys were conducted in Europe, so it's possible American voters might react differently.
But the survey included subjects from more than 30 ______ to try to minimize a particular national bias.
So before you cast your vote this election year, think about whether your view is influencing your views.
questions.answer:
1. conservatively
2. government
3. according
4. socially
5. building
6. countries

sense_groups.chinese: 如果是在教堂，你可能比在学校或政府大楼投票时更倾向于保守投票。

questions.name: #262 Dog Coat
questions.en:
You can't judge a book by its cover.
But you can judge a dog by its coat.
You can even read right through to its genes.
Because a study in the August 27th online issue of Science shows that just three key genes govern the length and texture of dog fur.
Domestic dogs come in a stunning variety of shapes and sizes, and ______ breeds wear different coats.
They can have short hair or long hair, or fur that's straight, wavy, curly, wiry or smooth.
To find the genes ______ for this furry rainbow, scientists scanned the DNA of a ______ individual dogs from 80 different breeds.
And they found that every coat's appearance boils down to three simple traits: length, curl and texture.
And that each of these traits is controlled by just one gene.
So, a long-haired Golden retriever has one variant of a gene called FGF5, whereas a short-haired lab has another.
By mixing and ______ variants of these three genes, you get ______ from a curly-haired poodle to a wire-haired Scottie with bushy eyebrows and a droopy mustache.
Which is probably more than you'll ever need to know about the hair of the dog that bit you.
questions.full:

2. responsible
3. thousand
4. matching
5. everything

sense_groups.english: You can't judge a book by its cover.
sense_groups.chinese: 你不能以貌取人。

sense_groups.english: But you can judge a dog by its coat.
sense_groups.chinese: 但你可以通过狗的皮毛来判断它。

sense_groups.english: You can even read right through to its genes.
sense_groups.chinese: 你甚至可以直接读到它的基因。

sense_groups.english: Because a study in the August 27th online issue of Science shows that just three key genes govern the length and texture of dog fur.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为8月27日《科学》杂志网络版的一项研究表明，仅三个关键基因就决定了狗毛的长度和质地。

sense_groups.english: Domestic dogs come in a stunning variety of shapes and sizes, and different breeds wear different coats.
sense_groups.chinese: 家犬的体型和大小千差万别，不同品种的狗有着不同的皮毛。

sense_groups.english: They can have short hair or long hair, or fur that's straight, wavy, curly, wiry or smooth.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们可以是短毛或长毛，或者直毛、波浪毛、卷毛、刚毛或顺滑的毛。

sense_groups.english: To find the genes responsible for this furry rainbow, scientists scanned the DNA of a thousand individual dogs from 80 different breeds.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了找到造成这种毛色多样性的基因，科学家扫描了来自80个不同品种的一千只狗的DNA。

sense_groups.english: And they found that every coat's appearance boils down to three simple traits: length, curl and texture.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现每种皮毛的外观都可归结为三个简单的特征：长度、卷曲度和质地。

sense_groups.english: And that each of these traits is controlled by just one gene.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且每个特征仅由一个基因控制。

sense_groups.english: So, a long-haired Golden retriever has one variant of a gene called FGF5, whereas a short-haired lab has another.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以，长毛的金毛寻回犬有一种名为FGF5的基因变体，而短毛的拉布拉多则有另一种。

sense_groups.english: By mixing and matching variants of these three genes, you get everything from a curly-haired poodle to a wire-haired Scottie with bushy eyebrows and a droopy mustache.
sense_groups.chinese: 通过混合和匹配这三个基因的变体，你可以得到从卷毛贵宾犬到刚毛苏格兰梗（有着浓密眉毛和下垂胡须）的一切品种。

sense_groups.english: Which is probably more than you'll ever need to know about the hair of the dog that bit you.
sense_groups.chinese: 这大概比你被狗咬后需要了解的关于狗毛的知识还要多。

questions.name: #263 Climate and Insect

questions.name: #264 Psychological Sex
questions.en:
Do psychological ______ vary by sex?
More boys are ______ with autism, and more girls with depression.
Scientists at the University of Rochester Medical Center want to understand any such sex differences.
So the ______ studied smell and gender in nearly ______ roundworms.
What can we learn about our brains from tiny worms?
Well, these creatures have a relatively simple and well-mapped nervous system.
Some are male, and some are hermaphroditic.
Scientists presented the worms with two scents.
One smelled like buttery popcorn, another like green vegetables.
Hermaphrodites mostly crawled towards buttery popcorn, while males preferred vegetables.
Then scientists manipulated some of the hermaphroditic neurons to behave like they were male.
And the newly male worms now crawled towards the green peppery smell.
What does this tell us about male and female human brains?
Well, not much yet.
But what surprised researchers is that brain neurons present in both sexes—like those that register smell preference—have different characteristics depending on the sex of the worm.
This is a step on a path scientists hope will lead to greater understanding about our own sex differences and mental illness.

sense_groups.chinese: 罗切斯特大学医学中心的科学家们想要了解这些性别差异。

sense_groups.english: So the researchers studied smell and gender in nearly microscopic roundworms.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，研究人员研究了近显微镜下的线虫的嗅觉和性别。

sense_groups.english: What can we learn about our brains from tiny worms?
sense_groups.chinese: 我们能从这些小虫子身上学到关于大脑的什么？

sense_groups.english: Well, these creatures have a relatively simple and well-mapped nervous system.
sense_groups.chinese: 嗯，这些生物拥有相对简单且绘制完善的神经系统。

sense_groups.english: Some are male, and some are hermaphroditic.
sense_groups.chinese: 有些是雄性，有些是雌雄同体。

sense_groups.english: Scientists presented the worms with two scents.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们给线虫提供了两种气味。

sense_groups.english: One smelled like buttery popcorn, another like green vegetables.
sense_groups.chinese: 一种闻起来像黄油爆米花，另一种像绿色蔬菜。

sense_groups.english: Hermaphrodites mostly crawled towards buttery popcorn, while males preferred vegetables.
sense_groups.chinese: 雌雄同体大多爬向黄油爆米花，而雄性更喜欢蔬菜。

sense_groups.english: Then scientists manipulated some of the hermaphroditic neurons to behave like they were male.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后科学家们操纵了一些雌雄同体的神经元，使其表现得像雄性。

sense_groups.english: And the newly male worms now crawled towards the green peppery smell.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，这些新变成雄性的线虫爬向了绿色胡椒味。

sense_groups.english: What does this tell us about male and female human brains?
sense_groups.chinese: 这告诉我们关于男性和女性人类大脑的什么？

sense_groups.english: Well, not much yet.
sense_groups.chinese: 嗯，目前还不多。

sense_groups.english: But what surprised researchers is that brain neurons present in both sexes—like those that register smell preference—have different characteristics depending on the sex of the worm.
sense_groups.chinese: 但令研究人员惊讶的是，两性中都存在的大脑神经元——比如那些记录气味偏好的神经元——根据线虫的性别具有不同的特征。

sense_groups.english: This is a step on a path scientists hope will lead to greater understanding about our own sex differences and mental illness.
sense_groups.chinese: 这是科学家希望最终能让我们更了解自身性别差异和精神疾病的一步。

questions.name: #265 Ethanol
questions.en:
For those interested in preserving the environment, this week brings sobering news about ethanol.
This fuel, distilled from plants like corn and switchgrass, has been widely touted as an eco-friendly, clean-burning ______ to gasoline.
But a study published this week in the journal Environmental Science and ______ suggests that replacing our current gas-guzzlers with vehicles that burn ethanol would ______ increase pollution and damage human health.
Stanford ______ Mark Jacobson used a computer model to predict air quality in the year 2020, when ethanol-powered cars are expected to be widely available in the US.
His simulation showed, among other things, that cars that burn a blend of 85 percent ethanol will significantly increase ozone, a prime ingredient in smog.
So in a world where the cars run on switchgrass juice, more people will get asthma, more people will be hospitalized with respiratory distress, and more people will die from ______ in ozone than if we'd kept on driving our ______ clunkers.
At least according to Jacobons.
So if you want to celebrate Earth Day this weekend, raise a glass of bubbly to our beautiful planet.
Just don't share any with your gas tank.
questions.answer:
1. alternative
2. Technology
3. actually
4. scientist
5. breathing
6. gas-powered

sense_groups.english: For those interested in preserving the environment,

sense_groups.english: this week brings sobering news about ethanol.

sense_groups.english: This fuel, distilled from plants like corn and switchgrass,
sense_groups.chinese: 这种从玉米和柳枝稷等植物中蒸馏出来的燃料，

sense_groups.english: But a study published this week in the journal Environmental Science and Technology

sense_groups.chinese: 比我们继续开汽油驱动的破车的情况更糟。

sense_groups.chinese: 为我们美丽的星球举杯庆祝。

questions.name: #266 Meteor Showers
questions.en:
If you woke up this morning and the newspaper headline ______ Meteor Headed for Earth, you'd think: That's not good.
And you'd ______ be right.
But ______ a little cosmic bombardment can be just what the doctor ordered.
In a study published online in the journal Nature Geoscience, researchers in Sweden say that 470 million years ago, meteor showers might have boosted our biodiversity.
The scientists were studying rocks from China and Scandinavia.
And they were looking for two things.
First, they were counting the number of different clam-like species they could find.
Second, they were searching for ______ that were carried here by meteorites—extraterrestrial chromite, stuff like that.
They found that a huge burst of diversification coincides exactly with a time when meteors a mile wide were raining down on the planet.
But wait.
Didn't an asteroid wipe out the dinosaurs?
Well, yes, but without all those earlier impacts promoting diversity, maybe there wouldn't have been any ______ in the first place.
And if a meteor hadn't then slammed the dinos, mammals like us might never have made the scene.
So when it comes to space rocks, one man's ceiling is another man's flora…and fauna.
questions.full:
If you woke up this morning and the newspaper headline ______ Meteor Headed for Earth, you'd think: That's not good.
And you'd ______ be right.
But ______ a little cosmic bombardment can be just what the doctor ordered.
In a study published online in the journal Nature Geoscience, researchers in Sweden say that 470 million years ago, meteor showers might have boosted our biodiversity.
The scientists were studying rocks from China and Scandinavia.
And they were looking for two things.
First, they were counting the number of different clam-like species they could find.
Second, they were searching for ______ that were carried here by meteorites—extraterrestrial chromite, stuff like that.
They found that a huge burst of diversification coincides exactly with a time when meteors a mile wide were raining down on the planet.
But wait.
Didn't an asteroid wipe out the dinosaurs?
Well, yes, but without all those earlier impacts promoting diversity, maybe there wouldn't have been any ______ in the first place.
And if a meteor hadn't then slammed the dinos, mammals like us might never have made the scene.
So when it comes to space rocks, one man's ceiling is another man's flora…and fauna.

答案:
1. screamed
2. probably
3. sometimes
4. chemicals
5. dinosaurs

sense_groups.english: If you woke up this morning and the newspaper headline screamed Meteor Headed for Earth,
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你今天早上醒来，报纸头条写着‘流星冲向地球’

sense_groups.english: you'd think: That's not good.
sense_groups.chinese: 你会想：这可不好。

sense_groups.english: And you'd probably be right.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且你很可能是对的。

sense_groups.english: But sometimes a little cosmic bombardment can be just what the doctor ordered.
sense_groups.chinese: 但有时候，一点宇宙轰炸正是医生所吩咐的。

sense_groups.english: In a study published online in the journal Nature Geoscience,
sense_groups.chinese: 在《自然·地球科学》杂志在线发表的一项研究中，

sense_groups.english: researchers in Sweden say that 470 million years ago,
sense_groups.chinese: 瑞典的研究人员说，4.7亿年前，

sense_groups.english: meteor showers might have boosted our biodiversity.
sense_groups.chinese: 流星雨可能促进了我们的生物多样性。

sense_groups.english: The scientists were studying rocks from China and Scandinavia.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们正在研究来自中国和斯堪的纳维亚的岩石。

sense_groups.english: And they were looking for two things.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们在寻找两样东西。

sense_groups.english: First, they were counting the number of different clam-like species they could find.
sense_groups.chinese: 首先，他们在统计能找到的不同蛤类物种的数量。

sense_groups.english: Second, they were searching for chemicals that were carried here by meteorites—
sense_groups.chinese: 其次，他们在寻找由陨石带来的化学物质——

sense_groups.english: extraterrestrial chromite, stuff like that.
sense_groups.chinese: 地外铬铁矿之类的东西。

sense_groups.english: They found that a huge burst of diversification coincides exactly with a time
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现，一次巨大的多样性爆发恰好与一个时期吻合，

sense_groups.english: when meteors a mile wide were raining down on the planet.
sense_groups.chinese: 当时一英里宽的流星正像雨点般落在地球上。

sense_groups.english: But wait.
sense_groups.chinese: 但等等。

sense_groups.english: Didn't an asteroid wipe out the dinosaurs?
sense_groups.chinese: 不是小行星灭绝了恐龙吗？

sense_groups.english: Well, yes, but without all those earlier impacts promoting diversity,
sense_groups.chinese: 嗯，是的，但如果没有那些早期撞击促进多样性，

sense_groups.english: maybe there wouldn't have been any dinosaurs in the first place.
sense_groups.chinese: 也许一开始就不会有恐龙。

sense_groups.english: And if a meteor hadn't then slammed the dinos,
sense_groups.chinese: 而如果后来没有流星撞击恐龙，

sense_groups.english: mammals like us might never have made the scene.
sense_groups.chinese: 像我们这样的哺乳动物可能永远不会出现。

sense_groups.english: So when it comes to space rocks,
sense_groups.chinese: 所以说到太空岩石，

sense_groups.english: one man's ceiling is another man's flora…and fauna.
sense_groups.chinese: 一个人的天花板是另一个人的植物群和动物群。

questions.name: #267 Nightmare
questions.en:
How ______ are ______ for toddlers, and what causes them?
Those are questions researchers at the University of Montreal hoped to answer.
They asked parents of about a ______ children to estimate the occurrence of their child's nightmares from age two and a half through age six.
The parents were also ______ about their child's disposition.
First, it turns out that nightmares aren't so frequent.
About a third of the parents reported no nightmares at all.
And then there's the second result.
Kids who were called "difficult" as early as 5 months were more likely to suffer from nightmares as toddlers.
And the ones who at a year and a half were more anxious, more likely to cry, and more difficult to calm down were also more likely to have bad dreams.
The study authors say this means children may be, well, like little adults.
It's already well established that adults tend to express ______ stress and emotional problems as nightmares.
The researchers suggest that focusing on the kids' day-time issues, and on parenting techniques, may help banish ______ demons.
questions.answer:
1. frequent
2. nightmares
3. thousand
4. questioned
5. real-live
6. night-time

sense_groups.english: How frequent are nightmares for toddlers, and what causes them?
sense_groups.chinese: 幼儿做噩梦的频率有多高，是什么原因导致的？

sense_groups.english: Those are questions researchers at the University of Montreal hoped to answer.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些是蒙特利尔大学的研究人员希望回答的问题。

sense_groups.english: They asked parents of about a thousand children to estimate the occurrence of their child's nightmares from age two and a half through age six.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们让大约一千名孩子的父母估算孩子从两岁半到六岁期间做噩梦的频率。

sense_groups.english: The parents were also questioned about their child's disposition.
sense_groups.chinese: 父母还被询问了孩子的性情。

sense_groups.english: First, it turns out that nightmares aren't so frequent.
sense_groups.chinese: 首先，结果发现噩梦并不那么频繁。

sense_groups.english: About a third of the parents reported no nightmares at all.
sense_groups.chinese: 大约三分之一的父母报告说孩子完全没有做过噩梦。

sense_groups.english: And then there's the second result.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后是第二个结果。

sense_groups.english: Kids who were called "difficult" as early as 5 months were more likely to suffer from nightmares as toddlers.
sense_groups.chinese: 早在5个月大时就被认为“难带”的孩子，在幼儿时期更容易做噩梦。

sense_groups.english: And the ones who at a year and a half were more anxious, more likely to cry, and more difficult to calm down were also more likely to have bad dreams.
sense_groups.chinese: 而那些在一岁半时更焦虑、更容易哭闹、更难安抚的孩子，也更可能做噩梦。

sense_groups.english: The study authors say this means children may be, well, like little adults.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究作者说，这意味着孩子可能就像小大人一样。

sense_groups.english: It's already well established that adults tend to express real-live stress and emotional problems as nightmares.
sense_groups.chinese: 已有充分证据表明，成年人倾向于将现实生活中的压力和情绪问题表现为噩梦。

sense_groups.english: The researchers suggest that focusing on the kids' day-time issues, and on parenting techniques, may help banish night-time demons.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员建议，关注孩子白天的问题以及育儿技巧，可能有助于驱散夜间的噩梦。

questions.name: #268 Face to Face
questions.en:
Any ______ business person can tell you about the ______ of "face time"—actually sitting down with clients, coworkers, maybe even competitors.
But there may be even more to this whole ______ business than meets the eye — or exactly as much as meets the eye.
Because a new study from Tufts University suggests that the success of a corporation rests squarely on the face of its CEO.
The researchers took photos of 50 CEOs from the highest and lowest ranked Fortune 1000 companies.
And they showed these pictures to a group of undergrads.
They asked the students to rate each face on whether its owner looked competent, dominant, likeable, mature or trustworthy.
What they found is that the students' impressions tracked with company profits.
The more ______ and leaderlike the CEO appeared, the more successful the corporation — even though the CEOs were all pretty much ______ white guys in ties.
The study, which will appear in the February issue of ______ Science, does not say whether profitable companies tend to promote people who look like leaders or whether successful CEOs grow to look the part.
Either way, looks like a company's financial about-face can actually be about face.
questions.answer:
1. successful
2. importance
3. face-to-face
4. powerful
5. middle-aged
6. Psychological

sense_groups.english: What they found is that the students' impressions tracked with company profits.

sense_groups.english: The study, which will appear in the February issue of ______ Science, does not say whether profitable companies tend to promote people who look like leaders or whether successful CEOs grow to look the part.

questions.name: #269 New Way to Slenderize
questions.en:
If you're like me, somewhere in your closet, or maybe in a drawer, you ______ have a pair of pants you hope to someday fit into.
Again.
But staying on a diet and finding time to exercise—it's no walk in the park.
But wait!
Before you swear off the spaghetti, scientists at the State ______ of New York in Stony Brook have stumbled onto a new way to slenderize.

Their results appear in the current online edition of the ______ of the ______ Academy of Sciences.
All the animals in the ______ were allowed to eat their fill.

But compared to the mice who hung out on a stationary platform, they had about 30 percent less fat around their middles.
The SUNY scientists think that the jiggling kept fat cells from forming.
Whether it would do the same for people, you never know.
And here you thought New Yorkers were lean and mean because they're always in a hurry rushing here and there.
Maybe it's because they spend so much time standing on vibrating subway platforms, waiting for the uptown express.

4. Proceedings
5. National

4. Proceedings
5. National

sense_groups.english: If you're like me, somewhere in your closet, or maybe in a drawer, you probably have a pair of pants you hope to someday fit into.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你像我一样，在衣柜的某个地方，或者抽屉里，你很可能有一条希望有一天能穿上的裤子。

sense_groups.english: Again.
sense_groups.chinese: 再次穿上。

sense_groups.english: But staying on a diet and finding time to exercise—it's no walk in the park.
sense_groups.chinese: 但坚持节食和找时间锻炼——这可不是件容易的事。

sense_groups.english: But wait!
sense_groups.chinese: 但等等！

sense_groups.english: Before you swear off the spaghetti, scientists at the State University of New York in Stony Brook have stumbled onto a new way to slenderize.
sense_groups.chinese: 在你发誓不吃意大利面之前，纽约州立大学石溪分校的科学家偶然发现了一种新的减肥方法。

sense_groups.english: They found that mice that spend 15 minutes a day standing on a vibrating platform are leaner than mice who just stand still.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现，每天在振动平台上站立15分钟的老鼠比那些静止站立的老鼠更瘦。

sense_groups.english: Their results appear in the current online edition of the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们的研究结果发表在最新一期的《美国国家科学院院刊》网络版上。

sense_groups.english: All the animals in the experiment were allowed to eat their fill.
sense_groups.chinese: 实验中所有动物都可以尽情进食。

sense_groups.english: After 15 weeks, the shaken mice didn't actually weigh any less.
sense_groups.chinese: 15周后，被振动的小鼠体重实际上并没有减轻。

sense_groups.english: But compared to the mice who hung out on a stationary platform, they had about 30 percent less fat around their middles.
sense_groups.chinese: 但与在静止平台上待着的小鼠相比，它们腰部的脂肪减少了约30%。

sense_groups.english: The SUNY scientists think that the jiggling kept fat cells from forming.
sense_groups.chinese: 石溪分校的科学家认为，这种振动阻止了脂肪细胞的形成。

sense_groups.english: Whether it would do the same for people, you never know.
sense_groups.chinese: 至于这对人类是否同样有效，谁也说不准。

sense_groups.english: And here you thought New Yorkers were lean and mean because they're always in a hurry rushing here and there.
sense_groups.chinese: 而你原本以为纽约人又瘦又刻薄是因为他们总是匆匆忙忙地跑来跑去。

sense_groups.english: Maybe it's because they spend so much time standing on vibrating subway platforms, waiting for the uptown express.
sense_groups.chinese: 也许是因为他们花太多时间站在振动的地铁站台上，等待开往住宅区的快车。

questions.name: #270 Tattoo
questions.en:
Thinking about getting a new tattoo?
Maybe a nice 3-D double helix or an I-heart-Higgs Bosons.
Well, you might wind up getting some mycobacteria with your body art.
The Centers for Disease Control and ______ has turned up about two dozen cases of this ______ from contaminated tattoo ink.
Last January, public health officials in western New York state ______ an investigation after a tattoo ______ reported a persistent rash--itchy red bumps all over his new tat.
A skin sample tested positive for Mycobacterium chelonae, a microbe common in tap water.
A list of the tattoo artist's clients turned up another 19 cases of the rash, including 14 ______ infections with the same bug.
The tattoo parlor itself was clean, no bacteria in the water supply.
But a bottle of premixed gray ink turned up positive.
This gray wash, which is used to give tats a shaded, 3-D quality, was most likely contaminated during its manufacture and has since been recalled.
But not before a handful of additional cases cropped up in elsewhere around the country.
So if you're really itching to express yourself, a tattoo might indeed be just what the doctor ordered.

sense_groups.english: Thinking about getting a new tattoo?
sense_groups.chinese: 想纹个新纹身吗？

sense_groups.english: Maybe a nice 3-D double helix or an I-heart-Higgs Bosons.
sense_groups.chinese: 也许是个漂亮的3D双螺旋，或者一个‘我爱希格斯玻色子’的图案。

sense_groups.english: Well, you might wind up getting some mycobacteria with your body art.
sense_groups.chinese: 嗯，你可能会在纹身时顺便得到一些分枝杆菌。

sense_groups.english: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has turned up about two dozen cases of this infection from contaminated tattoo ink.
sense_groups.chinese: 美国疾病控制与预防中心已经发现了大约二十多例因受污染纹身墨水引起的感染病例。

sense_groups.english: Last January, public health officials in western New York state launched an investigation after a tattoo recipient reported a persistent rash--itchy red bumps all over his new tat.
sense_groups.chinese: 去年一月，纽约州西部的公共卫生官员在一位纹身者报告出现持续皮疹——新纹身上布满发痒的红色肿块后，展开了调查。

sense_groups.english: A skin sample tested positive for Mycobacterium chelonae, a microbe common in tap water.
sense_groups.chinese: 皮肤样本检测出龟分枝杆菌阳性，这是一种自来水中常见的微生物。

sense_groups.english: A list of the tattoo artist's clients turned up another 19 cases of the rash, including 14 confirmed infections with the same bug.
sense_groups.chinese: 纹身师的客户名单中又发现了19例皮疹，其中14例确诊感染了同一种细菌。

sense_groups.english: The tattoo parlor itself was clean, no bacteria in the water supply.
sense_groups.chinese: 纹身店本身很干净，供水系统中没有细菌。

sense_groups.english: But a bottle of premixed gray ink turned up positive.
sense_groups.chinese: 但一瓶预混合的灰色墨水检测呈阳性。

sense_groups.english: This gray wash, which is used to give tats a shaded, 3-D quality, was most likely contaminated during its manufacture and has since been recalled.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种灰色墨水用于给纹身带来阴影和3D效果，很可能在生产过程中被污染，并已被召回。

sense_groups.english: But not before a handful of additional cases cropped up in elsewhere around the country.
sense_groups.chinese: 但在此之前，全国其他地方又出现了少量病例。

sense_groups.english: So if you're really itching to express yourself, a tattoo might indeed be just what the doctor ordered.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以，如果你真的渴望表达自己，纹身可能正是医生所嘱咐的。

questions.name: #271 Garlic
questions.en:
Various studies have suggested that eating garlic can be good for you.
It's been credited with ______ blood pressure, protecting against heart disease, preventing blood clots, even fighting off colds.
Now researchers from the University of Alabama at Birmingham think they have a better idea how garlic might work its medicinal magic.
The Alabama team exposed red blood cells to the juices pressed from a standard, supermarket-issue clove of garlic.
And they found that the ______ cells started giving off ______ sulfide, which is the gas that gives rotten eggs their delightful bouquet.
Ok, I know you're probably ______ that smelling like sewage seems even more odious than reeking of garlic.
But on a molecular level, a pinch of hydrogen sulfide can be just what the doctor ordered.
Because hydrogen sulfide serves as a chemical messenger that helps relax blood vessels and increase blood flow.
Which could explain some of garlic's cardiovascular benefits.
Of course more studies are needed to show whether a clove a day really does keep the doctor away.
In the meantime, enjoy your garlic bread.
And don't worry about the garlic breath.
Just think what the insides of your arteries must smell like.
questions.full:
Various studies have suggested that eating garlic can be good for you.
It's been credited with ______ blood pressure, protecting against heart disease, preventing blood clots, even fighting off colds.
Now researchers from the University of Alabama at Birmingham think they have a better idea how garlic might work its medicinal magic.
The Alabama team exposed red blood cells to the juices pressed from a standard, supermarket-issue clove of garlic.
And they found that the ______ cells started giving off ______ sulfide, which is the gas that gives rotten eggs their delightful bouquet.
Ok, I know you're probably ______ that smelling like sewage seems even more odious than reeking of garlic.
But on a molecular level, a pinch of hydrogen sulfide can be just what the doctor ordered.
Because hydrogen sulfide serves as a chemical messenger that helps relax blood vessels and increase blood flow.
Which could explain some of garlic's cardiovascular benefits.
Of course more studies are needed to show whether a clove a day really does keep the doctor away.
In the meantime, enjoy your garlic bread.
And don't worry about the garlic breath.
Just think what the insides of your arteries must smell like.

答案:
1. lowering
2. garlic-soaked
3. hydrogen
4. thinking

sense_groups.english: Various studies have suggested that eating garlic can be good for you.
sense_groups.chinese: 多项研究表明，吃大蒜对你有好处。

sense_groups.english: It's been credited with lowering blood pressure, protecting against heart disease, preventing blood clots, even fighting off colds.
sense_groups.chinese: 它被认为能降低血压、预防心脏病、防止血栓，甚至对抗感冒。

sense_groups.english: Now researchers from the University of Alabama at Birmingham think they have a better idea how garlic might work its medicinal magic.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，阿拉巴马大学伯明翰分校的研究人员认为，他们更清楚大蒜是如何发挥其药用魔力的。

sense_groups.english: The Alabama team exposed red blood cells to the juices pressed from a standard, supermarket-issue clove of garlic.
sense_groups.chinese: 阿拉巴马团队将红细胞暴露在从超市买来的普通大蒜瓣中挤出的汁液中。

sense_groups.english: And they found that the garlic-soaked cells started giving off hydrogen sulfide, which is the gas that gives rotten eggs their delightful bouquet.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现，浸泡过大蒜的细胞开始释放硫化氢，这种气体赋予了臭鸡蛋那种令人愉悦的气味。

sense_groups.english: Ok, I know you're probably thinking that smelling like sewage seems even more odious than reeking of garlic.
sense_groups.chinese: 好吧，我知道你可能在想，闻起来像污水比满身大蒜味更令人讨厌。

sense_groups.english: But on a molecular level, a pinch of hydrogen sulfide can be just what the doctor ordered.
sense_groups.chinese: 但在分子层面上，一点硫化氢正是医生所要求的。

sense_groups.english: Because hydrogen sulfide serves as a chemical messenger that helps relax blood vessels and increase blood flow.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为硫化氢作为一种化学信使，有助于放松血管、增加血流量。

sense_groups.english: Which could explain some of garlic's cardiovascular benefits.
sense_groups.chinese: 这可以解释大蒜对心血管的一些益处。

sense_groups.english: Of course more studies are needed to show whether a clove a day really does keep the doctor away.
sense_groups.chinese: 当然，还需要更多研究来证明每天一瓣大蒜是否真的能让医生远离。

sense_groups.english: In the meantime, enjoy your garlic bread.
sense_groups.chinese: 与此同时，享受你的蒜香面包吧。

sense_groups.english: And don't worry about the garlic breath.
sense_groups.chinese: 别担心大蒜味的口臭。

sense_groups.english: Just think what the insides of your arteries must smell like.
sense_groups.chinese: 想想你的动脉内部闻起来是什么味道吧。

questions.name: #272 HIW
questions.en:
Sometimes it pays to look like a pile of poop.
At least if you're a tasty ______ trying to avoid getting eaten by hungry birds.
Because a study in the journal Science shows that even young chicks tend to overlook ______ disguised as dung.
Animals have come up with some pretty clever tricks for keeping ______ off a predator's dinner plate.
Some use camouflage, ______ colors and patterns that help them blend into the environment.
Others masquerade as something inedible, like bird ______ or twigs.
But scientists got to wondering whether the two approaches are really so different.
Maybe critters dressed as twigs also "blend in" so that predators just don't see them.
To find out, scientists presented some twiggy-looking caterpillars to two sets of hand-reared chicks.
They found that baby birds that had never seen sticks before gobbled those bad boys right up.
But chicks who were shown real twigs first took much longer to peck at the mimics, and did so more ______ than their naïve friends.
That means the birds could see the caterpillars, but were fooled by the costume, at least temporarily.
Which, for a caterpillar on a leaf in the wild, could mean the difference between eating and being eaten.
questions.answer:
1. caterpillar
2. caterpillars
3. themselves
4. adopting
5. droppings
6. gingerly
questions.full:
Sometimes it pays to look like a pile of poop.
At least if you're a tasty ______ trying to avoid getting eaten by hungry birds.
Because a study in the journal Science shows that even young chicks tend to overlook ______ disguised as dung.
Animals have come up with some pretty clever tricks for keeping ______ off a predator's dinner plate.
Some use camouflage, ______ colors and patterns that help them blend into the environment.
Others masquerade as something inedible, like bird ______ or twigs.
But scientists got to wondering whether the two approaches are really so different.
Maybe critters dressed as twigs also "blend in" so that predators just don't see them.
To find out, scientists presented some twiggy-looking caterpillars to two sets of hand-reared chicks.
They found that baby birds that had never seen sticks before gobbled those bad boys right up.
But chicks who were shown real twigs first took much longer to peck at the mimics, and did so more ______ than their naïve friends.
That means the birds could see the caterpillars, but were fooled by the costume, at least temporarily.
Which, for a caterpillar on a leaf in the wild, could mean the difference between eating and being eaten.

答案:
1. caterpillar
2. caterpillars
3. themselves
4. adopting
5. droppings
6. gingerly

sense_groups.english: Sometimes it pays to look like a pile of poop.
sense_groups.chinese: 有时候，看起来像一堆粪便是有好处的。

sense_groups.english: At least if you're a tasty caterpillar trying to avoid getting eaten by hungry birds.
sense_groups.chinese: 至少，如果你是一条美味的毛毛虫，试图避免被饥饿的鸟吃掉的话。

sense_groups.english: Because a study in the journal Science shows that even young chicks tend to overlook caterpillars disguised as dung.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为《科学》杂志上的一项研究表明，即使是小鸡也倾向于忽视伪装成粪便的毛毛虫。

sense_groups.english: Animals have come up with some pretty clever tricks for keeping themselves off a predator's dinner plate.
sense_groups.chinese: 动物们想出了一些相当聪明的技巧，让自己远离捕食者的餐盘。

sense_groups.english: Some use camouflage, adopting colors and patterns that help them blend into the environment.
sense_groups.chinese: 有些使用伪装，采用帮助它们融入环境的颜色和图案。

sense_groups.english: Others masquerade as something inedible, like bird droppings or twigs.
sense_groups.chinese: 其他的则伪装成不可食用的东西，比如鸟粪或树枝。

sense_groups.english: But scientists got to wondering whether the two approaches are really so different.
sense_groups.chinese: 但科学家们开始怀疑这两种方法是否真的如此不同。

sense_groups.english: Maybe critters dressed as twigs also "blend in" so that predators just don't see them.
sense_groups.chinese: 也许伪装成树枝的小动物也“融入”了环境，这样捕食者就看不到它们了。

sense_groups.english: To find out, scientists presented some twiggy-looking caterpillars to two sets of hand-reared chicks.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了找出答案，科学家们向两组人工饲养的小鸡展示了一些看起来像树枝的毛毛虫。

sense_groups.english: They found that baby birds that had never seen sticks before gobbled those bad boys right up.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现，从未见过树枝的小鸟会立刻把这些“坏家伙”吞下去。

sense_groups.english: But chicks who were shown real twigs first took much longer to peck at the mimics, and did so more gingerly than their naïve friends.
sense_groups.chinese: 但先看过真正树枝的小鸡啄食这些模仿者所需的时间要长得多，而且比它们天真的同伴更小心翼翼。

sense_groups.english: That means the birds could see the caterpillars, but were fooled by the costume, at least temporarily.
sense_groups.chinese: 这意味着鸟儿能看到毛毛虫，但至少暂时被它们的伪装骗过了。

sense_groups.english: Which, for a caterpillar on a leaf in the wild, could mean the difference between eating and being eaten.
sense_groups.chinese: 对于野外叶子上的毛毛虫来说，这可能意味着吃与被吃的区别。

questions.name: #273 Location
questions.en:
Location, location, location.
We all know it's true of real estate.
But it may also apply to the ballot box.
Because a team of American ______ has found that where people vote affects how they vote.
The scientists looked at results from the 2000 general election.
In Arizona that year, the ballot included an initiative to raise state taxes to support education.
What they found is that people who ______ to be voting in a school ______ were more likely to vote for the ______ than people who voted at a firehouse or a church.
Their results appear in the June 23rd issue of the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
And same thing happened in the lab.
Subjects were shown a series of images, some of which pertained to schools.
Later on, in what they were told was an unrelated experiment, they were asked to vote on funding for education.
Folks who'd looked at lockers were more likely to vote yes.
Whether voting in a church might affect where people stand on gay ______ or stem cell research remains to be seen.
But it's ______ a good thing that more people don't cast ballots in diners—might make it impossible to get rid of all that political pork.
questions.answer:
1. researchers
2. happened
3. building
4. proposal
5. marriage
6. probably

sense_groups.english: Location, location, location.

sense_groups.english: But it may also apply to the ballot box.

sense_groups.chinese: 因为一组美国研究人员发现，人们在哪儿投票会影响他们如何投票。

sense_groups.english: The scientists looked at results from the 2000 general election.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们研究了2000年大选的结果。

sense_groups.english: In Arizona that year, the ballot included an initiative to raise state taxes to support education.
sense_groups.chinese: 那年亚利桑那州的选票上有一项提高州税以支持教育的倡议。

sense_groups.english: What they found is that people who happened to be voting in a school building were more likely to vote for the proposal than people who voted at a firehouse or a church.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现，碰巧在学校大楼投票的人比在消防站或教堂投票的人更可能支持该提案。

sense_groups.english: But it's probably a good thing that more people don't cast ballots in diners—might make it impossible to get rid of all that political pork.

questions.name: #275 HIW
questions.en:
New parents can act pretty strangely—for example, they often have an obsessive interest in what comes out of their baby's bottoms.
Now ______ at Stanford University join them in their diaper diving to explore when and how ______ colonize the human gut.
Adults harbor complex ______ ______ within their GI tracts.
These bacteria help digest food and contribute to a healthy immune system.
But when a baby is born, its intestine is devoid of bacterial inhabitants.
Within days, however, a ______ of microbes set up shop, establishing a vibrant intestinal community whose residents soon outnumber the baby's own cells.
The researchers found that the early months were chaotic…with established species disappearing and new ones taking their place.
But by the time the babies were 12 months old, each harbored a dynamic but unique ______ of intestinal fauna.
A set of fraternal twins had the most similar bugs, which suggests that genetics may have ______ to do with which bacteria stick around.
Next they'll look at how formula versus breast milk affects a baby's intestinal ecosystem.
With so many questions left to explore, the researchers will no doubt be mining diapers for some time to come.
questions.answer:
1. researchers
2. bacteria
3. microbial
4. ecosystems
5. cavalcade
6. collection
7. something
questions.full:
New parents can act pretty strangely—for example, they often have an obsessive interest in what comes out of their baby's bottoms.
Now ______ at Stanford University join them in their diaper diving to explore when and how ______ colonize the human gut.

Within days, however, a ______ of microbes set up shop, establishing a vibrant intestinal community whose residents soon outnumber the baby's own cells.

Next they'll look at how formula versus breast milk affects a baby's intestinal ecosystem.
With so many questions left to explore, the researchers will no doubt be mining diapers for some time to come.

答案:
1. researchers
2. bacteria
3. microbial
4. ecosystems
5. cavalcade
6. collection
7. something

sense_groups.english: New parents can act pretty strangely—for example, they often have an obsessive interest in what comes out of their baby's bottoms.
sense_groups.chinese: 新父母可能会表现得很奇怪——例如，他们常常对宝宝屁股里出来的东西有执着的兴趣。

sense_groups.english: Now researchers at Stanford University join them in their diaper diving to explore when and how bacteria colonize the human gut.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，斯坦福大学的研究人员也加入了他们的尿布探索，以探究细菌何时以及如何定植在人类肠道中。

sense_groups.english: Adults harbor complex microbial ecosystems within their GI tracts.
sense_groups.chinese: 成年人的胃肠道内栖息着复杂的微生物生态系统。

sense_groups.english: These bacteria help digest food and contribute to a healthy immune system.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些细菌帮助消化食物，并有助于健康的免疫系统。

sense_groups.english: But when a baby is born, its intestine is devoid of bacterial inhabitants.
sense_groups.chinese: 但婴儿出生时，其肠道内没有细菌居民。

sense_groups.english: Within days, however, a cavalcade of microbes set up shop, establishing a vibrant intestinal community whose residents soon outnumber the baby's own cells.
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，几天之内，一大群微生物就安营扎寨，建立了一个充满活力的肠道社区，其居民很快超过了婴儿自身的细胞。

sense_groups.english: The researchers found that the early months were chaotic…with established species disappearing and new ones taking their place.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员发现，最初几个月是混乱的……已有的物种消失，新物种取而代之。

sense_groups.english: But by the time the babies were 12 months old, each harbored a dynamic but unique collection of intestinal fauna.
sense_groups.chinese: 但当婴儿长到12个月大时，每个婴儿都拥有一个动态但独特的肠道菌群集合。

sense_groups.english: A set of fraternal twins had the most similar bugs, which suggests that genetics may have something to do with which bacteria stick around.
sense_groups.chinese: 一对异卵双胞胎拥有最相似的细菌，这表明基因可能与哪些细菌留存下来有关。

sense_groups.english: Next they'll look at how formula versus breast milk affects a baby's intestinal ecosystem.
sense_groups.chinese: 接下来，他们将研究配方奶与母乳如何影响婴儿的肠道生态系统。

sense_groups.english: With so many questions left to explore, the researchers will no doubt be mining diapers for some time to come.
sense_groups.chinese: 由于还有这么多问题有待探索，研究人员无疑将在未来一段时间内继续挖掘尿布。

questions.name: #277 HIW
questions.en:
A hungry fish can kill prey with a quick bite.
That is, of course, if its prey hasn't already died of fright.
Take tasty dragonflies.
The mere ______ of predators—even caged ones—is enough to scare ______ to death, ______ to a study in the journal Ecology.

The larvae could see and smell their hunters—but were kept safe by underwater cages.
After two months, the researchers took a head count—and found that dragonfly larvae sharing quarters with their killers were two to four times as likely to die off, ______ to ______ living in predator-free waters.
And they had slimmer chances of surviving metamorphosis, too.
The authors suggest a couple reasons why.
First, prey tend to make fewer forays for snacks when ______ are lurking around, so they may not be as nutritionally fit.
And previous studies have shown that the presence of predators ups stress levels in prey, weakening their immune systems and making them more vulnerable to disease—and death.
As if being eaten wasn't enough to worry about, looks can kill too.
questions.answer:
1. presence
2. dragonflies
3. according
4. compared
5. counterparts
6. predators
questions.full:
A hungry fish can kill prey with a quick bite.
That is, of course, if its prey hasn't already died of fright.

sense_groups.english: A hungry fish can kill prey with a quick bite.
sense_groups.chinese: 一条饥饿的鱼可以迅速咬死猎物。

sense_groups.english: That is, of course, if its prey hasn't already died of fright.
sense_groups.chinese: 当然，前提是它的猎物没有被吓死。

sense_groups.english: Take tasty dragonflies.
sense_groups.chinese: 以美味的蜻蜓为例。

sense_groups.english: The mere presence of predators—even caged ones—is enough to scare dragonflies to death, according to a study in the journal Ecology.
sense_groups.chinese: 仅仅捕食者的存在——即使是关在笼子里的——就足以把蜻蜓吓死，根据《生态学》杂志的一项研究。

sense_groups.english: Researchers collected wild dragonfly larvae, and placed them in tanks with fish or insect predators.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员收集了野生蜻蜓幼虫，并将它们与鱼类或昆虫捕食者放在同一个水箱中。

sense_groups.english: The larvae could see and smell their hunters—but were kept safe by underwater cages.
sense_groups.chinese: 幼虫能看到并闻到捕食者，但被水下笼子保护着。

sense_groups.english: After two months, the researchers took a head count—and found that dragonfly larvae sharing quarters with their killers were two to four times as likely to die off, compared to counterparts living in predator-free waters.
sense_groups.chinese: 两个月后，研究人员清点了数量，发现与捕食者共处的蜻蜓幼虫死亡率是生活在无捕食者水域中的同类的2到4倍。

sense_groups.english: And they had slimmer chances of surviving metamorphosis, too.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且它们成功完成变态的几率也更低。

sense_groups.english: The authors suggest a couple reasons why.
sense_groups.chinese: 作者提出了几个可能的原因。

sense_groups.english: First, prey tend to make fewer forays for snacks when predators are lurking around, so they may not be as nutritionally fit.
sense_groups.chinese: 首先，当捕食者潜伏在附近时，猎物往往更少外出觅食，因此它们的营养状况可能不佳。

sense_groups.english: And previous studies have shown that the presence of predators ups stress levels in prey, weakening their immune systems and making them more vulnerable to disease—and death.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且先前的研究表明，捕食者的存在会增加猎物的压力水平，削弱它们的免疫系统，使它们更容易生病和死亡。

sense_groups.english: As if being eaten wasn't enough to worry about, looks can kill too.
sense_groups.chinese: 好像被吃掉还不够担心似的，眼神也能杀死人。

questions.en:
Back on January 15th, US Airways Flight 1549 made that amazing water landing in the Hudson after both engines were taken out by Canada geese, which can weigh eight pounds each.
Now scientists have used forensic ______ to clear local geese—the perpetrators were out-of-towners.

Crash ______ sent feather samples from the plane's engines to the Smithsonian, which has a dedicated Feather Identification Lab.
The researchers examined the feather's ______ isotopes, which include regular hydrogen atoms and ______ with additional neutrons.

And that tells you where they dined.
The analysis showed that the birds that hit the plane were much closer to geese migrating from Canada's Labrador region than the geese who live ______ in New York.
That info could be ______ for strategies to avoid future bird strikes.

2. investigators
3. hydrogen
4. hydrogens
5. year-round
6. important

sense_groups.chinese: 分析显示，撞击飞机的鸟更接近从加拿大拉布拉多地区迁徙来的鹅，而非常年生活在纽约的鹅。

sense_groups.chinese: 这一信息对于制定避免未来鸟击的策略可能很重要。

sense_groups.english: The usual techniques for keeping resident birds away from planes are still working—but we need new ones for strangers just passing through.

sense_groups.english: These tiny molecular flashlights make it possible to study numerous events that take place in cells and whole organisms that were previously invisible—such as the development of nerve cells or the spread of cancer cells.

sense_groups.chinese: 随后，加州大学圣地亚哥分校的Tsien设计了多种颜色的荧光蛋白。

sense_groups.english: The multicolor palette enables researchers to follow multiple biological processes at the same time.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种多色调色板使研究人员能够同时追踪多个生物过程。

questions.name: #281 Coal Mine
questions.en:
A coal mine can degrade its local environment.
But a fungus may inadvertently help clean up the mine—with its own waste products.
Researchers worked with a fungus called Stilbella aciculosa.
As it makes spores, it also ______ superoxide.
That's a highly ______ kind of oxygen.
When the released superoxide bumps into the mineral manganese in the environment, it makes that mineral much more reactive itself.
The pepped-up manganese then grabs and holds a variety of toxic metals and other substances that need to be cleaned up and taken out of coal mine drainage water.
The research, led by Colleen Hansel of Harvard and the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, appears in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
It's been known that various ______ and fungi can help in environmental remediation.
The new ______ shows that production of the vital forms of manganese requires that the fungi and bacteria be actively producing superoxide.
So creating conditions that encourage the organisms to make the superoxide could be the first step in a pathway by which they help manganese to literally do the dirty work.
And make some toxic sites a lot cleaner.

sense_groups.english: A coal mine can degrade its local environment.
sense_groups.chinese: 煤矿会破坏当地环境。

sense_groups.english: But a fungus may inadvertently help clean up the mine—with its own waste products.
sense_groups.chinese: 但一种真菌可能无意中帮助清理煤矿——利用它自己的废物。

sense_groups.english: Researchers worked with a fungus called Stilbella aciculosa.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员研究了一种名为 Stilbella aciculosa 的真菌。

sense_groups.english: As it makes spores, it also produces superoxide.
sense_groups.chinese: 在产生孢子的同时，它也会产生超氧化物。

sense_groups.english: That's a highly reactive kind of oxygen.
sense_groups.chinese: 这是一种高活性的氧。

sense_groups.english: When the released superoxide bumps into the mineral manganese in the environment, it makes that mineral much more reactive itself.
sense_groups.chinese: 当释放出的超氧化物与环境中的锰矿物碰撞时，会使这种矿物本身更具活性。

sense_groups.english: The pepped-up manganese then grabs and holds a variety of toxic metals and other substances that need to be cleaned up and taken out of coal mine drainage water.
sense_groups.chinese: 被激活的锰随后捕获并固定各种有毒金属和其他需要从煤矿排水中清除的物质。

sense_groups.english: The research, led by Colleen Hansel of Harvard and the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, appears in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项由哈佛大学和伍兹霍尔海洋研究所的 Colleen Hansel 领导的研究发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。

sense_groups.english: It's been known that various bacteria and fungi can help in environmental remediation.
sense_groups.chinese: 众所周知，各种细菌和真菌有助于环境修复。

sense_groups.english: The new research shows that production of the vital forms of manganese requires that the fungi and bacteria be actively producing superoxide.
sense_groups.chinese: 新的研究表明，产生关键形态的锰需要真菌和细菌积极产生超氧化物。

sense_groups.english: So creating conditions that encourage the organisms to make the superoxide could be the first step in a pathway by which they help manganese to literally do the dirty work.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，创造鼓励这些微生物产生超氧化物的条件，可能是它们帮助锰真正完成脏活的第一步。

sense_groups.english: And make some toxic sites a lot cleaner.
sense_groups.chinese: 并让一些有毒场所变得更加清洁。

The scientists speculate that other big-billed birds may regulate their body temperatures this way.

sense_groups.english: The toucan's long bill has long perplexed biologists.
sense_groups.chinese: 巨嘴鸟的长喙长期以来一直让生物学家感到困惑。

sense_groups.english: Darwin theorized that it attracted mates.
sense_groups.chinese: 达尔文推测它用于吸引配偶。

sense_groups.english: Other suggested uses ranged from fruit peeling to territorial defense.
sense_groups.chinese: 其他提出的用途包括剥水果和领地防御。

sense_groups.english: But a report in the July 24th issue of the journal Science offers another explanation as to why one-third of the bird is all schnoz.
sense_groups.chinese: 但《科学》杂志7月24日的一篇报告提出了另一种解释，说明为什么这种鸟的三分之一都是喙。

sense_groups.english: The authors of the report say the toucan's bill is so big because it acts like a radiator strapped to its face.
sense_groups.chinese: 报告的作者说，巨嘴鸟的喙之所以这么大，是因为它像一个绑在脸上的散热器。

sense_groups.english: When a toucan needs to cool down, its beak heats up.
sense_groups.chinese: 当巨嘴鸟需要降温时，它的喙会变热。

sense_groups.english: The immense surface area of the beak allows heat to quickly dissipate.
sense_groups.chinese: 喙的巨大表面积使热量迅速散发。

sense_groups.english: In fact, the scientists say, as a toucan lowers its body temperature in preparation for sleep, it can cool 10 degrees Celsius in just minutes.
sense_groups.chinese: 事实上，科学家说，当巨嘴鸟为睡眠降低体温时，它能在几分钟内降温10摄氏度。

sense_groups.english: The scientists used infrared thermography, the same kind of technology used in heat-sensing cameras, to observe toucans at different ambient temperatures.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家使用红外热成像技术——与热感应相机使用的技术相同——来观察不同环境温度下的巨嘴鸟。

sense_groups.english: When outside temperatures rose, the bill also heated up, but the bird's core body temperature did not.
sense_groups.chinese: 当外部温度升高时，喙也会变热，但鸟的核心体温并未升高。

sense_groups.english: The scientists speculate that other big-billed birds may regulate their body temperatures this way.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家推测，其他大喙鸟类可能也以这种方式调节体温。

sense_groups.english: Since birds don't sweat, having a handy heat dissipater undoubtedly keeps their feathers from getting ruffled.
sense_groups.chinese: 由于鸟类不出汗，拥有一个方便的散热器无疑能让它们的羽毛保持平整。

questions.name: #284 Volcano Eruption
questions.en:
2002 was a tough year for the people who live along the shores of Lake Kivu in the ______ Republic of the Congo.
It started off with a bang, when the Nyiragongo volcano erupted in January.
And it tailed off with a shudder, when a magnitude 6.2 earthquake struck the region in October.
Both events devastated local communities—and their close timing struck some scientists as suspicious.
"We were wondering if there could be a link—so, a causality—between those two major geological events."
Christelle Wauthier, a geologist at Pennsylvania State University.
From studying radar images of the ground taken before and after the January eruption, ______ knew that lava didn't just spew out of the volcano.
It also wedged itself into cracks in the crust, forming what ______ call a dike.
"So you can think of it as like a blade-shaped type of magma intrusion, moving from depth toward the surface.
It's very fast, a few hours, a few days, and it can penetrate tens of kilometers of crust."
Dikes are common in rift zones, like east Africa and Iceland, where tectonic forces are slowly ripping Earth's crust apart.
And they're known to cause small ______ right when they happen.
But Wauthier wondered if dikes might also be capable of triggering large earthquakes by pushing the ground apart and affecting nearby faults.
"You will add more stress on a weakness surface, which is a fault.
And so if you add enough stress on it, you can trigger failure on the fault."
Now, Wauthier and her ______ have used a model to show that the stress changes caused by the January dike event made the October earthquake much more likely to occur.
The results are in the journal Geochemistry, Geophysics, Geosystems.
This study marks the first time scientists have linked dike formation to large, damaging earthquakes, and Wauthier is looking back through history for more examples.
She says ______ will never be able to predict exactly when an earthquake might strike after a dike intrusion.
But at least now, researchers and rift zone residents know they're not just in for bangs—they may also be in for shudders.
questions.answer:
1. Democratic
2. Wauthier
3. geologists
4. earthquakes
5. colleagues
6. researchers

questions.name: #285 Hippocampus
questions.en:
You probably remember exactly what you were doing when you first heard the news on 9/11.
That's because the brain has ways to ______ information so that things that happen at the same time are forever linked in our minds.
Now a study published in the journal Neuron; says that newborn cells in a structure called the hippocampus help us remember concurrent events.
The hippocampus is part of the brain that allows us to lay down new memories.
And about ten years ago, scientists were surprised to find that new neurons pop up in this region every day, even in adult animals and people.
But what do these new cells do?
Scientists turned to computer modeling to help them find out.
They put in what they knew about the behavior of these new cells, which start out like puppies that get totally excited over every little thing, and eventually mature into more discerning members of neuronal society.
And they found that the hyperactivity of these excitable young cells, which react with great gusto to everything that goes on, could help stamp memories with a sort of "time code" that indicates which things happened together.
So if you still remember what you were eating when you dumped your loser boyfriend, you can thank your newborn neurons.

questions.name: #286 HIV
questions.en:
Germany's Harald zur Hausen and France's Luc Montagnier and Francoise Barre-Sinoussi share the 2008 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, awarded October 6th.
Barre-Sinoussi and Montagnier discovered HIV.
Shortly after reports in the early 1980s of a new immunodeficiency syndrome, researchers all over the world raced to find the cause.
The two French scientists ______ cells from lymph nodes of patients.
They first detected the enzyme reverse transcriptase, which meant that a retrovirus was active.
Further searching turned up retroviral particles, which could kill white blood cells and which also reacted with antibodies from infected patients.
These discoveries made ______ unprecedented rapid development of blood screening techniques and of new antiviral therapies.
Zur Hausen defied the medical ______ and postulated in the 1970s that cervical cancer was caused by the human ______ virus.
He was able to isolate viral DNA in tumors.
He also determined that there were multiple kinds of papilloma viruses, and that only some caused cancer.
His discovery led to the development of a vaccine against cervical cancer.

questions.name: #287 Seasonal Flu
questions.en:
Seasonal flu ______ hits senior citizens harder than most other age groups.
In fact, some 90 percent of ______ deaths are estimated to occur in adults 65 and older.
But with pandemic influenzas, like bird or swine flu, it's a different story.
Take the 2009 H1N1 flu.
In that outbreak, adults over 65 actually suffered the fewest infections of any age group.
That anomaly ______ they might have some sort of built-in immunity.
Now researchers say the seniors' secret may be in their spit.
Researchers sampled saliva from 180 children, adult and elderly volunteers.
Then they isolated ______ from the saliva, and tested how well the inhibitory proteins stuck to two strains of H9N2 bird flu.
Turns out elderly men and women had ______ more such proteins that interfere with the flu virus—which researchers say could boost the seniors' resistance to bird flu.
Those results appear in the Journal of Proteome Research.
The next step, researchers say, is to develop an oral or nasal spray based on these proteins.
Which might give people of all ages a chance to send the flu a lethal loogie.

questions.name: #288 Testing of Lie
questions.en:
When we lie, our brains work hard to make sure we get the story right and come off as truthful.
Law enforcement officials try to tap into that effort, for example with polygraphs, to find out if a suspect is telling the truth.
But such stress tests are beatable and not admissible in court.
Now comes a report that handwriting tests could be a competitor to the familiar, but unreliable lie detector.
The study appears in the Journal of Applied ______ Psychology.
Researchers at Israel's Haifa University worked with 34 volunteers, who wrote truthful and false paragraphs on paper using a wireless ______ pen and a pressure sensitive tip.
A computerized system measured pressure and stroke duration, both on the paper and in the air.
Spatial measures, such as stroke length, height and width were also tracked.
And the ______ found significant differences in pressure and spatial measures in ______ statements compared with the truth.
The investigators say they need to ______ this initial result and compare the technique with polygraphs and other lie detection tools.
But perhaps in the future even a written claim of innocence could turn out to be a de facto confession.

questions.en:
If you like a glass of wine with your pizza, you might be interested in the news from this week's ______ Chemical Society meeting in Chicago.
First the bad news: it seems that a growing number of winemakers find that their reds, whites and rosés taste a little like ladybugs.
These cute little aphid-eaters are becoming quite a nuisance in vineyards across the country, where they accidentally get harvested with the grapes and stink up the resulting wine.
Chemists at Iowa State University used a gas chromatograph and a panel of human ______ to analyze the odor ______ by ______ of live ladybugs.
They found the stench was made mostly by chemicals that smelled like roasted peanuts and green peppers.
Which maybe nobody wants in a delicate Chablis.
But there's good news about pizza.
Chemists at the University of Maryland have figured out how to boost the antioxidant levels in pizza dough.
Maybe that discovery will ______ a whole new generation of bad foods that are good for you: potato chips that clear your ______ or brownies that deliver insulin.
Until then, at least we've got the antioxidant deep dish, which we can always wash down with a nice glass of ladybug merlot.

Everyone makes mistakes, especially when it comes to entering numbers into a ______ or spreadsheet.
It's not such a big deal if you're ______ how much you spend on pizza.

Now a report in the Journal of the Royal Society Interface shows how devices can be programmed to catch at least some ______ on the spot.
Dosing a patient with 10 times too much medication is disturbingly common.
One study suggests this error occurs in 1 percent of all hospital admissions.
And though the person ______ in the numbers is at fault, most drug-delivery devices don't help.
In one machine, for example, mistakenly entering a number with two decimal points—like 1.2.
3—might be read by the machine as 1.23, or as a 123.
To prevent such wild guessing, scientists tested a system that ______ flags any input that's not a real number.

questions.name: #292 Elephants
questions.en:
Elephants don't need cell phones to hold long distance conversations, their deep calls can travel miles. And inlaw humans can't always hear these vocalizations because of their low frequency, elephants produce them using the same mechanism that lets humans speak and sing. That finding is in the journal Science.
Until now, scientists did not know whether the expressionist made sound the way we speak or differently, such as the way cats purr. A human produces noises because the vocal cords vibrate automatically when air flows past. But a cat must actively squeeze the muscles of its larynx to produce its deep, rhythmic purr.
When a zoo elephant died of natural causes, fieldworkers took the animal's larynx to their lab and ran air through it to find out which method elephants use to make sound. They could reproduce the large mammal's heterogeneity rumble, which means that an elephant doesn't need to actively control its larynx like a cat does. For those who contend that this is irrelevant,
"Irrelevant. There's a whole lot of 'irrelevant's in the circus."

questions.name: #293 Native American Site
questions.en:
There's a Native American site in Ohio that appeared to be a fort.
But recent ______ by archaeologists at the University of Cincinnati show that's not the case.
Instead, it's a two-thousand year old Shawnee water management system.
It stretches out almost six kilometers.
That's much larger than what had been thought to ______ the so-called fort.
It's one of the largest such sites in the country.
What had been thought to be gates for military protection are actually a series of dams and ______ canals.
There are logs and clay bricks for damming; raceways for flowing water ______ in far-off springs.
The water was stored and channeled for irrigation.
Drill cores show water sediments and clay.
The site demonstrates a ______ knowledge of engineering—which archaeologists not realize that Native American communities might have.
The site also reveals an ______ on public works, rather than on war.
So this discovery might rewrite a bit of history.
Another interesting note: Shawnee remains from the time are typically of petite, graceful men—and robust, muscular women.
So it was probably the women who built the water system.
Which means even more history to rewrite.

4. originate
5. sophisticated
6. emphasis
