6. emphasis

sense_groups.english: There's a Native American site in Ohio that appeared to be a fort.
sense_groups.chinese: 俄亥俄州有一个美洲原住民遗址，看起来像一座堡垒。

sense_groups.english: But recent discoveries by archaeologists at the University of Cincinnati show that's not the case.
sense_groups.chinese: 但辛辛那提大学的考古学家最近发现，事实并非如此。

sense_groups.english: Instead, it's a two-thousand year old Shawnee water management system.
sense_groups.chinese: 相反，它是一个有两千年历史的肖尼族水利系统。

sense_groups.english: It stretches out almost six kilometers.
sense_groups.chinese: 它延伸近六公里。

sense_groups.english: That's much larger than what had been thought to comprise the so-called fort.
sense_groups.chinese: 这比人们原先认为构成所谓堡垒的范围要大得多。

sense_groups.english: It's one of the largest such sites in the country.
sense_groups.chinese: 它是该国最大的此类遗址之一。

sense_groups.english: What had been thought to be gates for military protection are actually a series of dams and irrigation canals.
sense_groups.chinese: 原先被认为是军事防御大门的东西，实际上是一系列水坝和灌溉渠。

sense_groups.english: There are logs and clay bricks for damming; raceways for flowing water originate in far-off springs.
sense_groups.chinese: 有用于筑坝的原木和粘土砖；水流通道源自远处的泉水。

sense_groups.english: The water was stored and channeled for irrigation.
sense_groups.chinese: 水被储存并引导用于灌溉。

sense_groups.english: Drill cores show water sediments and clay.
sense_groups.chinese: 钻探岩芯显示出水沉积物和粘土。

sense_groups.english: The site demonstrates a sophisticated knowledge of engineering—which archaeologists not realize that Native American communities might have.
sense_groups.chinese: 该遗址展示了高超的工程知识——考古学家之前没有意识到美洲原住民社区可能拥有这种知识。

sense_groups.english: The site also reveals an emphasis on public works, rather than on war.
sense_groups.chinese: 该遗址还揭示了其对公共工程的重视，而非战争。

sense_groups.english: So this discovery might rewrite a bit of history.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以这一发现可能会改写一些历史。

sense_groups.english: Another interesting note: Shawnee remains from the time are typically of petite, graceful men—and robust, muscular women.
sense_groups.chinese: 另一个有趣的发现：那个时期的肖尼族遗骸通常是身材娇小、优雅的男性和强壮、肌肉发达的女性。

sense_groups.english: So it was probably the women who built the water system.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以很可能是女性建造了水利系统。

sense_groups.english: Which means even more history to rewrite.
sense_groups.chinese: 这意味着有更多的历史需要改写。

questions.name: #294 Flock Warning
questions.en:
When crested pigeons spot a predator, they give a little whistle.
But the sound doesn't come from their beaks.
And ______ to a study published by The Royal Society, that whistle warns the rest of the flock to flee.
There's safety in numbers, and a flock offers ______ in part because it has so many eyes watching for danger.
But it's not clear how an ______ sounds the alarm when it spots a predator.
Maybe anytime one or two birds fly off, they all do.
Just in case.
Of course that kind of knee-jerk ______ could produce a lot of false alarms.
So how can birds tell when their ______ are seriously headed for the hills?
  ______ recorded the sounds made by the wings of crested pigeons during a routine liftoff (wing sound 1).
And the noise their wings make during an emergency takeoff (wing sound 2).
And they found that the sound made by wings flapped in terror includes a distinctive sort of whistle.
That noise alone will scatter a flock of feeding pigeons just as quick as the shadow of a passing hawk.
And gives a whole new meaning to the expression, "on a wing and a prayer."
questions.answer:
1. according
2. protection
3. individual
4. reaction
5. flockmates
6. Scientists
questions.full:
When crested pigeons spot a predator, they give a little whistle.
But the sound doesn't come from their beaks.
And ______ to a study published by The Royal Society, that whistle warns the rest of the flock to flee.
There's safety in numbers, and a flock offers ______ in part because it has so many eyes watching for danger.
But it's not clear how an ______ sounds the alarm when it spots a predator.
Maybe anytime one or two birds fly off, they all do.
Just in case.
Of course that kind of knee-jerk ______ could produce a lot of false alarms.
So how can birds tell when their ______ are seriously headed for the hills?
  ______ recorded the sounds made by the wings of crested pigeons during a routine liftoff (wing sound 1).
And the noise their wings make during an emergency takeoff (wing sound 2).
And they found that the sound made by wings flapped in terror includes a distinctive sort of whistle.
That noise alone will scatter a flock of feeding pigeons just as quick as the shadow of a passing hawk.
And gives a whole new meaning to the expression, "on a wing and a prayer."

答案:
1. according
2. protection
3. individual
4. reaction
5. flockmates
6. Scientists

sense_groups.english: When crested pigeons spot a predator, they give a little whistle.
sense_groups.chinese: 当冠鸽发现捕食者时，它们会发出一点哨声。

sense_groups.english: But the sound doesn't come from their beaks.
sense_groups.chinese: 但声音并非来自它们的喙。

sense_groups.english: And according to a study published by The Royal Society, that whistle warns the rest of the flock to flee.
sense_groups.chinese: 根据皇家学会发表的一项研究，那哨声警告鸽群的其他成员逃离。

sense_groups.english: There's safety in numbers, and a flock offers protection in part because it has so many eyes watching for danger.
sense_groups.chinese: 数量多意味着安全，鸽群提供保护部分是因为有那么多眼睛在监视危险。

sense_groups.english: But it's not clear how an individual sounds the alarm when it spots a predator.
sense_groups.chinese: 但尚不清楚个体发现捕食者时如何发出警报。

sense_groups.english: Maybe anytime one or two birds fly off, they all do.
sense_groups.chinese: 也许每当一两只鸟飞走，它们都会跟着飞。

sense_groups.english: Just in case.
sense_groups.chinese: 以防万一。

sense_groups.english: Of course that kind of knee-jerk reaction could produce a lot of false alarms.
sense_groups.chinese: 当然，那种膝跳反射式的反应可能会产生很多假警报。

sense_groups.english: So how can birds tell when their flockmates are seriously headed for the hills?
sense_groups.chinese: 那么鸟类如何判断它们的同伴是真的要逃之夭夭呢？

sense_groups.english: Scientists recorded the sounds made by the wings of crested pigeons during a routine liftoff (wing sound 1).
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家记录了冠鸽在常规起飞时翅膀发出的声音（翅膀声1）。

sense_groups.english: And the noise their wings make during an emergency takeoff (wing sound 2).
sense_groups.chinese: 以及它们在紧急起飞时翅膀发出的噪音（翅膀声2）。

sense_groups.english: And they found that the sound made by wings flapped in terror includes a distinctive sort of whistle.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现，因恐惧而拍打的翅膀发出的声音包含一种独特的哨声。

sense_groups.english: That noise alone will scatter a flock of feeding pigeons just as quick as the shadow of a passing hawk.
sense_groups.chinese: 仅那种噪音就能像飞过的鹰的影子一样迅速驱散一群正在进食的鸽子。

sense_groups.english: And gives a whole new meaning to the expression, "on a wing and a prayer."
sense_groups.chinese: 并赋予了“靠翅膀和祈祷”这个表达全新的含义。

questions.name: #295 Meat Allergy
questions.en:
You've ______ heard of peanut or shellfish allergies.
But a meat allergy?
Not as common.
Even weirder is what might be causing it—tick bites, according to a study in the Journal of General Internal Medicine.
A few years back, folks started showing up in ______ rooms in the southeast U.S. with hives, swelling or worse—anaphylaxis—after eating red meat.
For this study, researchers looked at three of those cases.
And they found that tick bites, specifically those of the Lone Star tick, seem to be the cause.
The bitten victim's immune system appears to become sensitized to a substance called alpha-gal.
And whereas all the major food allergies are ______ by proteins, the culprit here—alpha-gal—is a carbohydrate.
Alpha-gal is found in the meat and fat of hooved mammals, like cows, sheep or pigs.
So eating a burger can expose you to alpha-gal, which activates antibodies and leads to the release of histamines.
Researchers say something similar to ______ in the tick saliva may set off the immune system—which then goes after the alpha-gal in meat.
And leaves a steak lover ticked off.
questions.full:
You've ______ heard of peanut or shellfish allergies.
But a meat allergy?
Not as common.
Even weirder is what might be causing it—tick bites, according to a study in the Journal of General Internal Medicine.
A few years back, folks started showing up in ______ rooms in the southeast U.S. with hives, swelling or worse—anaphylaxis—after eating red meat.
For this study, researchers looked at three of those cases.
And they found that tick bites, specifically those of the Lone Star tick, seem to be the cause.
The bitten victim's immune system appears to become sensitized to a substance called alpha-gal.
And whereas all the major food allergies are ______ by proteins, the culprit here—alpha-gal—is a carbohydrate.
Alpha-gal is found in the meat and fat of hooved mammals, like cows, sheep or pigs.
So eating a burger can expose you to alpha-gal, which activates antibodies and leads to the release of histamines.
Researchers say something similar to ______ in the tick saliva may set off the immune system—which then goes after the alpha-gal in meat.
And leaves a steak lover ticked off.

答案:
1. probably
2. emergency
3. triggered
4. alpha-gal

sense_groups.english: You've probably heard of peanut or shellfish allergies.
sense_groups.chinese: 你可能听说过花生或贝类过敏。

sense_groups.english: But a meat allergy?
sense_groups.chinese: 但肉类过敏呢？

sense_groups.english: Not as common.
sense_groups.chinese: 不那么常见。

sense_groups.english: Even weirder is what might be causing it—tick bites, according to a study in the Journal of General Internal Medicine.
sense_groups.chinese: 更奇怪的是可能的原因——蜱虫叮咬，根据《普通内科学杂志》的一项研究。

sense_groups.english: A few years back, folks started showing up in emergency rooms in the southeast U.S. with hives, swelling or worse—anaphylaxis—after eating red meat.
sense_groups.chinese: 几年前，人们开始出现在美国东南部的急诊室，出现荨麻疹、肿胀或更严重的过敏性休克，在吃了红肉之后。

sense_groups.english: For this study, researchers looked at three of those cases.
sense_groups.chinese: 在这项研究中，研究人员查看了其中三个病例。

sense_groups.english: And they found that tick bites, specifically those of the Lone Star tick, seem to be the cause.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现蜱虫叮咬，特别是孤星蜱的叮咬，似乎是原因。

sense_groups.english: The bitten victim's immune system appears to become sensitized to a substance called alpha-gal.
sense_groups.chinese: 被叮咬者的免疫系统似乎对一种叫做α-半乳糖的物质变得敏感。

sense_groups.english: And whereas all the major food allergies are triggered by proteins, the culprit here—alpha-gal—is a carbohydrate.
sense_groups.chinese: 而所有主要的食物过敏都是由蛋白质引发的，这里的罪魁祸首——α-半乳糖——是一种碳水化合物。

sense_groups.english: Alpha-gal is found in the meat and fat of hooved mammals, like cows, sheep or pigs.
sense_groups.chinese: α-半乳糖存在于有蹄类哺乳动物的肉和脂肪中，比如牛、羊或猪。

sense_groups.english: So eating a burger can expose you to alpha-gal, which activates antibodies and leads to the release of histamines.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以吃汉堡会让你接触到α-半乳糖，它会激活抗体并导致组胺释放。

sense_groups.english: Researchers say something similar to alpha-gal in the tick saliva may set off the immune system—which then goes after the alpha-gal in meat.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员说，蜱虫唾液中类似α-半乳糖的物质可能会触发免疫系统，然后免疫系统会攻击肉中的α-半乳糖。

sense_groups.english: And leaves a steak lover ticked off.
sense_groups.chinese: 这让牛排爱好者感到恼火。

questions.name: #296 Elephant
questions.en:
Elephants are smart, social animals.
And now we know that they can organize themselves into teams to accomplish tasks.
A research team that ______ renowned primatologist Franz de Waal taught 12 Thai elephants—who already work with human trainers called mahouts—to get a bowl of food by pulling a rope attached to an ______ table.
Then the scientists threaded the rope so that it would take two elephants, pulling both ends at the same time, to move the table.
If one yanked an end without its helpmate doing so, no reward.
The pachyderms were paired up.
Only if they pulled together could they get the food.
The ______ tried the task when they were released ______ or at ______ times.
Even when the release was staggered, an ______ quickly learned that it had to wait for its partner to come and cooperate to get the food.
This finding was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
  ______ are thus on par with apes for fast learning of deliberate cooperation with a partner.
When grouped, individuals also remembered which of the others was their task partner.
Because an elephant never forgets…who helped it rope a meal.
questions.answer:
1. included
2. out-of-reach
3. elephants
4. simultaneously
5. staggered
6. elephant
7. Elephants
questions.full:
Elephants are smart, social animals.
And now we know that they can organize themselves into teams to accomplish tasks.
A research team that ______ renowned primatologist Franz de Waal taught 12 Thai elephants—who already work with human trainers called mahouts—to get a bowl of food by pulling a rope attached to an ______ table.
Then the scientists threaded the rope so that it would take two elephants, pulling both ends at the same time, to move the table.
If one yanked an end without its helpmate doing so, no reward.
The pachyderms were paired up.
Only if they pulled together could they get the food.
The ______ tried the task when they were released ______ or at ______ times.
Even when the release was staggered, an ______ quickly learned that it had to wait for its partner to come and cooperate to get the food.
This finding was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
  ______ are thus on par with apes for fast learning of deliberate cooperation with a partner.
When grouped, individuals also remembered which of the others was their task partner.
Because an elephant never forgets…who helped it rope a meal.

答案:
1. included
2. out-of-reach
3. elephants
4. simultaneously
5. staggered
6. elephant
7. Elephants

sense_groups.english: Elephants are smart, social animals.
sense_groups.chinese: 大象是聪明、群居的动物。

sense_groups.english: And now we know that they can organize themselves into teams to accomplish tasks.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在我们知道，它们能组织成团队来完成任务。

sense_groups.english: A research team that included renowned primatologist Franz de Waal taught 12 Thai elephants—who already work with human trainers called mahouts—to get a bowl of food by pulling a rope attached to an out-of-reach table.
sense_groups.chinese: 一个包括著名灵长类动物学家弗朗斯·德瓦尔的研究团队，教12头泰国大象——它们已经与被称为象夫的驯象师一起工作——通过拉一根系在够不着的桌子上的绳子来获取一碗食物。

sense_groups.english: Then the scientists threaded the rope so that it would take two elephants, pulling both ends at the same time, to move the table.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后科学家们穿好绳子，使得需要两头大象同时拉两端才能移动桌子。

sense_groups.english: If one yanked an end without its helpmate doing so, no reward.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果一头大象独自拉一端而同伴没有拉，就没有奖励。

sense_groups.english: The pachyderms were paired up.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些厚皮动物被配对。

sense_groups.english: Only if they pulled together could they get the food.
sense_groups.chinese: 只有它们一起拉才能得到食物。

sense_groups.english: The elephants tried the task when they were released simultaneously or at staggered times.
sense_groups.chinese: 大象们在同时释放或错时释放时尝试这项任务。

sense_groups.english: Even when the release was staggered, an elephant quickly learned that it had to wait for its partner to come and cooperate to get the food.
sense_groups.chinese: 即使释放时间错开，一头大象也很快学会了必须等待同伴到来并合作才能得到食物。

sense_groups.english: This finding was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
sense_groups.chinese: 这一发现发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。

sense_groups.english: Elephants are thus on par with apes for fast learning of deliberate cooperation with a partner.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，大象在快速学习与同伴有意合作方面与猿类不相上下。

sense_groups.english: When grouped, individuals also remembered which of the others was their task partner.
sense_groups.chinese: 当分组时，个体还能记住其他大象中谁是它们的任务伙伴。

sense_groups.english: Because an elephant never forgets…who helped it rope a meal.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为大象永远不会忘记……是谁帮它拉绳子得到食物。

questions.name: #297 Hearing
questions.en:
Just when you thought you'd heard everything, ______ have found that the reason you can hear everything—including things that are very quiet—is because your ears have tiny tubelike motors that mechanically amplify sounds.
You've probably heard that it's the hair cells in your ears that allow you to hear.
These cells sport tufts of spiky hairs that are like little molecular Mohawks.
When sound waves enter the ear these hairs vibrate, and that motion then gets translated into an ______ message that tells your brain that there's something worth listening to.
But the ______ of those hairs is not passive, like tall grass swaying in the breeze.
The electrical signals they produce feed back on the system, causing the hairs to tilt even more.
It's that ______ "flexo-electric effect" that boosts the audio signal and amplifies the sound, findings ______ in the April 22nd issue of the journal Public Library of Science ONE.
The scientists behind the study also note that the length of the hairs in different species explains why animals like bats can detect such high frequency sounds.
It doesn't, however, explain why your kids can hear their cell phones vibrate two rooms away, yet they never seem to hear a word you say.
questions.full:
Just when you thought you'd heard everything, ______ have found that the reason you can hear everything—including things that are very quiet—is because your ears have tiny tubelike motors that mechanically amplify sounds.
You've probably heard that it's the hair cells in your ears that allow you to hear.
These cells sport tufts of spiky hairs that are like little molecular Mohawks.
When sound waves enter the ear these hairs vibrate, and that motion then gets translated into an ______ message that tells your brain that there's something worth listening to.
But the ______ of those hairs is not passive, like tall grass swaying in the breeze.
The electrical signals they produce feed back on the system, causing the hairs to tilt even more.
It's that ______ "flexo-electric effect" that boosts the audio signal and amplifies the sound, findings ______ in the April 22nd issue of the journal Public Library of Science ONE.
The scientists behind the study also note that the length of the hairs in different species explains why animals like bats can detect such high frequency sounds.
It doesn't, however, explain why your kids can hear their cell phones vibrate two rooms away, yet they never seem to hear a word you say.

答案:
1. scientists
2. electrical
3. movement
4. so-called
5. published

sense_groups.english: Just when you thought you'd heard everything, scientists have found that the reason you can hear everything—including things that are very quiet—is because your ears have tiny tubelike motors that mechanically amplify sounds.
sense_groups.chinese: 就在你以为自己什么都听过的时候，科学家发现你能听到一切——包括非常安静的东西——是因为你的耳朵里有微小的管状马达，它们能机械地放大声音。

sense_groups.english: You've probably heard that it's the hair cells in your ears that allow you to hear.
sense_groups.chinese: 你可能听说过，是耳朵里的毛细胞让你能听到声音。

sense_groups.english: These cells sport tufts of spiky hairs that are like little molecular Mohawks.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些细胞长着一簇簇尖尖的毛发，就像微小的分子莫霍克发型。

sense_groups.english: When sound waves enter the ear these hairs vibrate, and that motion then gets translated into an electrical message that tells your brain that there's something worth listening to.
sense_groups.chinese: 当声波进入耳朵时，这些毛发会振动，然后这种运动被转化为电信号，告诉你的大脑有值得听的东西。

sense_groups.english: But the movement of those hairs is not passive, like tall grass swaying in the breeze.
sense_groups.chinese: 但这些毛发的运动并不是被动的，不像高草在微风中摇摆。

sense_groups.english: The electrical signals they produce feed back on the system, causing the hairs to tilt even more.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们产生的电信号会反馈到系统中，导致毛发更加倾斜。

sense_groups.english: It's that so-called "flexo-electric effect" that boosts the audio signal and amplifies the sound, findings published in the April 22nd issue of the journal Public Library of Science ONE.
sense_groups.chinese: 正是这种所谓的“挠曲电效应”增强了音频信号并放大了声音，这一发现发表在4月22日的《公共科学图书馆·综合》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: The scientists behind the study also note that the length of the hairs in different species explains why animals like bats can detect such high frequency sounds.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究的科学家还指出，不同物种的毛发长度解释了为什么像蝙蝠这样的动物能探测到如此高频的声音。

sense_groups.english: It doesn't, however, explain why your kids can hear their cell phones vibrate two rooms away, yet they never seem to hear a word you say.
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，这并不能解释为什么你的孩子能听到两个房间外手机振动的声音，却似乎从来听不到你说的话。

questions.name: #298 Jalapeno
questions.en:
There are hot peppers, like the jalapeno.
And then there are incendiary peppers like the legendary Habanero.
Now there's a new variety of thermonuclear Habanero, known as the ______ NR Habanero.
The name comes from its appearance—the bright orange pepper resembles a tiger's paw.
And the NR stands for nematode resistant.
The pepper was bred by the US Department of Agriculture's scientists to be ______ to nematodes, round worms that attack the plant's roots.
The pepper was bred conventionally, not genetically engineered.
And it does away with the need to use the soil fumigant methyl bromide, which is being phased out.
So, how hot is the tigerpaw Habanero?
Pepper hotness is measured on something called the Scoville Heat Scale.
A jalapeno comes in at about 5000 on the Scoville scale.
A regular ______ usually scores at least 100,000.
And the TigerPaw Habanero tops the Scoville scale at almost 350,000.
In fact, there's a legend that eating Habanero peppers can have the side effect of ______ making you deaf.
But only so that you cannot hear your own screams.

sense_groups.english: There are hot peppers, like the jalapeno.

sense_groups.english: And then there are incendiary peppers like the legendary Habanero.

sense_groups.english: Now there's a new variety of thermonuclear Habanero, known as the ______ NR Habanero.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在有一种新的热核哈瓦那辣椒，被称为______ NR哈瓦那辣椒。

sense_groups.english: The name comes from its appearance—the bright orange pepper resembles a tiger's paw.
sense_groups.chinese: 这个名字源于它的外观——亮橙色的辣椒像老虎的爪子。

sense_groups.english: And the NR stands for nematode resistant.
sense_groups.chinese: NR代表抗线虫。

sense_groups.english: The pepper was bred by the US Department of Agriculture's scientists to be ______ to nematodes, round worms that attack the plant's roots.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种辣椒是由美国农业部的科学家培育的，以______线虫，这种攻击植物根部的圆虫。

sense_groups.english: The pepper was bred conventionally, not genetically engineered.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种辣椒是传统方式培育的，不是基因工程。

sense_groups.english: And it does away with the need to use the soil fumigant methyl bromide, which is being phased out.
sense_groups.chinese: 它消除了使用土壤熏蒸剂甲基溴的需要，这种熏蒸剂正在被逐步淘汰。

sense_groups.english: So, how hot is the tigerpaw Habanero?
sense_groups.chinese: 那么，虎爪哈瓦那辣椒有多辣？

sense_groups.english: Pepper hotness is measured on something called the Scoville Heat Scale.
sense_groups.chinese: 辣椒的辣度是用一种叫做斯科维尔辣度表来衡量的。

sense_groups.english: A jalapeno comes in at about 5000 on the Scoville scale.
sense_groups.chinese: 墨西哥辣椒在斯科维尔表上大约是5000。

sense_groups.english: A regular ______ usually scores at least 100,000.
sense_groups.chinese: 普通的______通常至少达到10万。

sense_groups.english: And the TigerPaw Habanero tops the Scoville scale at almost 350,000.
sense_groups.chinese: 而虎爪哈瓦那辣椒在斯科维尔表上几乎达到35万。

sense_groups.english: In fact, there's a legend that eating Habanero peppers can have the side effect of ______ making you deaf.
sense_groups.chinese: 事实上，有一个传说，吃哈瓦那辣椒会有副作用，______让你变聋。

sense_groups.english: But only so that you cannot hear your own screams.
sense_groups.chinese: 但只是让你听不到自己的尖叫。

questions.name: #299 Iron
questions.en:
Iron is a great material for making tools.
But the oldest known iron ______ were actually ______ for decoration: nine Egyptian beads that date back to 3200 B.C. And now we know that this ancient jewelry has an even more impressive origin — the iron out of which it was crafted came from space.
The metal cylinders were discovered in Egypt in 1911.
To analyze the structure and chemical composition of the beads, researchers ______ them with neutrons and gamma rays.
The tests revealed that the jewelry contained trace elements not present in Earthly ores — but that are found in ______ meteorites.
The study is in the Journal of ______ Science.
The meteoric metal was hammered flat and rolled into beads more than 5,000 years ago.
This date is some 1,500 years before the ______ of smelting.
That ______ made it possible for terrestrial iron to be shaped into tools, and to supplant copper and bronze as civilization's metal of choice.
The new finding shows that long before smelting revolutionized tool use, some humans were already iron men.
questions.answer:
1. artifacts
2. intended
3. bombarded
4. iron-rich
5. Archaeological
6. invention
7. technique
questions.full:
Iron is a great material for making tools.
But the oldest known iron ______ were actually ______ for decoration: nine Egyptian beads that date back to 3200 B.C. And now we know that this ancient jewelry has an even more impressive origin — the iron out of which it was crafted came from space.
The metal cylinders were discovered in Egypt in 1911.
To analyze the structure and chemical composition of the beads, researchers ______ them with neutrons and gamma rays.
The tests revealed that the jewelry contained trace elements not present in Earthly ores — but that are found in ______ meteorites.
The study is in the Journal of ______ Science.
The meteoric metal was hammered flat and rolled into beads more than 5,000 years ago.
This date is some 1,500 years before the ______ of smelting.
That ______ made it possible for terrestrial iron to be shaped into tools, and to supplant copper and bronze as civilization's metal of choice.
The new finding shows that long before smelting revolutionized tool use, some humans were already iron men.

答案:
1. artifacts
2. intended
3. bombarded
4. iron-rich
5. Archaeological
6. invention
7. technique

sense_groups.english: Iron is a great material for making tools.
sense_groups.chinese: 铁是制造工具的绝佳材料。

sense_groups.english: But the oldest known iron artifacts were actually intended for decoration:
sense_groups.chinese: 但已知最古老的铁制品实际上是被用于装饰的：

sense_groups.english: nine Egyptian beads that date back to 3200 B.C.
sense_groups.chinese: 九颗可追溯到公元前3200年的埃及珠子。

sense_groups.english: And now we know that this ancient jewelry has an even more impressive origin —
sense_groups.chinese: 现在我们知道，这件古代珠宝有着更令人惊叹的来源——

sense_groups.english: the iron out of which it was crafted came from space.
sense_groups.chinese: 制作它的铁来自太空。

sense_groups.english: The metal cylinders were discovered in Egypt in 1911.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些金属圆柱体于1911年在埃及被发现。

sense_groups.english: To analyze the structure and chemical composition of the beads,
sense_groups.chinese: 为了分析这些珠子的结构和化学成分，

sense_groups.english: researchers bombarded them with neutrons and gamma rays.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员用中子和伽马射线轰击它们。

sense_groups.english: The tests revealed that the jewelry contained trace elements not present in Earthly ores —
sense_groups.chinese: 测试显示，这件珠宝含有地球矿石中不存在的微量元素——

sense_groups.english: but that are found in iron-rich meteorites.
sense_groups.chinese: 但存在于富含铁的陨石中。

sense_groups.english: The study is in the Journal of Archaeological Science.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《考古科学杂志》上。

sense_groups.english: The meteoric metal was hammered flat and rolled into beads more than 5,000 years ago.
sense_groups.chinese: 5000多年前，这种陨铁被锤平并卷成珠子。

sense_groups.english: This date is some 1,500 years before the invention of smelting.
sense_groups.chinese: 这个时间比冶炼技术的发明早了大约1500年。

sense_groups.english: That technique made it possible for terrestrial iron to be shaped into tools,
sense_groups.chinese: 这种技术使得地球上的铁可以被塑造成工具，

sense_groups.english: and to supplant copper and bronze as civilization's metal of choice.
sense_groups.chinese: 并取代铜和青铜成为文明的首选金属。

sense_groups.english: The new finding shows that long before smelting revolutionized tool use,
sense_groups.chinese: 这项新发现表明，早在冶炼技术彻底改变工具使用之前，

sense_groups.english: some humans were already iron men.
sense_groups.chinese: 一些人类就已经是铁人了。

questions.name: #300 Pharmaceutical Companies
questions.en:
Pharmaceutical companies sometimes have to pull new drugs off the market because they harm our livers.
The drugs may have been tested on liver cells from rats, or on human cells that are nearly dead.
But these kinds of tests do a poor job of ______ real livers.
Now researchers at MIT have developed a better method.
They've created a colony of human liver cells that act like the real thing.
The ______ was published in the journal Nature Biotechnology.
The cell colonies are only 500 millionths of a meter in diameter.
  ______ arrange the cells on a plate in much the same way as copper wires are placed on computer chips.
These micro livers mimic the actions of real livers—including ______ enzymes necessary to break down drugs and other toxins.
The tiny organs last for six weeks.
So they can ______ the effects of drugs over a longer time period than current tests.
A start-up company has licensed the technology and is ______ it for market.
The little livers could be cheaper and more accurate than drug tests now used.
questions.answer:
1. mimicking
2. research
3. Researchers
4. producing
5. evaluate
6. preparing
questions.full:
Pharmaceutical companies sometimes have to pull new drugs off the market because they harm our livers.
The drugs may have been tested on liver cells from rats, or on human cells that are nearly dead.
But these kinds of tests do a poor job of ______ real livers.
Now researchers at MIT have developed a better method.
They've created a colony of human liver cells that act like the real thing.
The ______ was published in the journal Nature Biotechnology.
The cell colonies are only 500 millionths of a meter in diameter.
  ______ arrange the cells on a plate in much the same way as copper wires are placed on computer chips.
These micro livers mimic the actions of real livers—including ______ enzymes necessary to break down drugs and other toxins.
The tiny organs last for six weeks.
So they can ______ the effects of drugs over a longer time period than current tests.
A start-up company has licensed the technology and is ______ it for market.
The little livers could be cheaper and more accurate than drug tests now used.

答案:
1. mimicking
2. research
3. Researchers
4. producing
5. evaluate
6. preparing

sense_groups.english: Pharmaceutical companies sometimes have to pull new drugs off the market
sense_groups.chinese: 制药公司有时不得不将新药撤出市场

sense_groups.english: because they harm our livers.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为它们会损害我们的肝脏。

sense_groups.english: The drugs may have been tested on liver cells from rats,
sense_groups.chinese: 这些药物可能已经在老鼠的肝细胞上进行了测试，

sense_groups.english: or on human cells that are nearly dead.
sense_groups.chinese: 或者是在几乎死亡的人类细胞上测试的。

sense_groups.english: But these kinds of tests do a poor job of mimicking real livers.
sense_groups.chinese: 但这类测试在模拟真实肝脏方面效果不佳。

sense_groups.english: Now researchers at MIT have developed a better method.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在麻省理工学院的研究人员开发了一种更好的方法。

sense_groups.english: They've created a colony of human liver cells that act like the real thing.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们创建了一个像真实肝脏一样运作的人类肝细胞群落。

sense_groups.english: The research was published in the journal Nature Biotechnology.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《自然生物技术》杂志上。

sense_groups.english: The cell colonies are only 500 millionths of a meter in diameter.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些细胞群落的直径只有500微米。

sense_groups.english: Researchers arrange the cells on a plate in much the same way as copper wires are placed on computer chips.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员将细胞排列在培养皿上，就像将铜线放置在计算机芯片上一样。

sense_groups.english: These micro livers mimic the actions of real livers—including producing enzymes necessary to break down drugs and other toxins.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些微型肝脏模拟真实肝脏的功能——包括产生分解药物和其他毒素所需的酶。

sense_groups.english: The tiny organs last for six weeks.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些微型器官可以维持六周。

sense_groups.english: So they can evaluate the effects of drugs over a longer time period than current tests.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，它们可以比现有测试更长时间地评估药物的效果。

sense_groups.english: A start-up company has licensed the technology and is preparing it for market.
sense_groups.chinese: 一家初创公司已获得该技术的许可，并正在准备将其推向市场。

sense_groups.english: The little livers could be cheaper and more accurate than drug tests now used.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些微型肝脏可能比目前使用的药物测试更便宜、更准确。

questions.name: #301 Climate and Size
questions.en:
Animals that live in cold ______ tend to have stubby limbs—shorter arms and legs—even smaller ears and tails.
Picture a penguin and you'll see what I mean.
  ______ have long assumed that these stumpy appendages are an evolutionary adaptation.
Shorter ______ minimize heat loss, so animals that are more compact are better suited to the cold.
But scientists from Ohio say that temperature may have a more direct effect on the length of an animal's limbs.
Because they find that turning up the heat helps ______ grow—results that were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
The researchers raised mice at several different temperatures, and they ______ that those kept at a balmy 80 degrees were longer limbed than those who lived at a more chill 45.
But how does a little heat make mice more leggy?
The answer, they find, lies in the cartilage.
Long bones grow from the cartilage found at either end.
And the warmer it is, the more that cartilage grows, even when it's just sitting in a test tube.
Which I guess means it's ______ that the dog days of summer lead to ______ dogs.
questions.answer:
1. climates
2. Biologists
3. extremities
4. cartilage
5. confirmed
6. possible
7. longer-legged
questions.full:
Animals that live in cold ______ tend to have stubby limbs—shorter arms and legs—even smaller ears and tails.
Picture a penguin and you'll see what I mean.
  ______ have long assumed that these stumpy appendages are an evolutionary adaptation.
Shorter ______ minimize heat loss, so animals that are more compact are better suited to the cold.
But scientists from Ohio say that temperature may have a more direct effect on the length of an animal's limbs.
Because they find that turning up the heat helps ______ grow—results that were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
The researchers raised mice at several different temperatures, and they ______ that those kept at a balmy 80 degrees were longer limbed than those who lived at a more chill 45.
But how does a little heat make mice more leggy?
The answer, they find, lies in the cartilage.
Long bones grow from the cartilage found at either end.
And the warmer it is, the more that cartilage grows, even when it's just sitting in a test tube.
Which I guess means it's ______ that the dog days of summer lead to ______ dogs.

答案:
1. climates
2. Biologists
3. extremities
4. cartilage
5. confirmed
6. possible
7. longer-legged

sense_groups.english: Animals that live in cold climates tend to have stubby limbs—shorter arms and legs—even smaller ears and tails.
sense_groups.chinese: 生活在寒冷气候中的动物往往有粗短的四肢——更短的手臂和腿——甚至更小的耳朵和尾巴。

sense_groups.english: Picture a penguin and you'll see what I mean.
sense_groups.chinese: 想象一只企鹅，你就会明白我的意思。

sense_groups.english: Biologists have long assumed that these stumpy appendages are an evolutionary adaptation.
sense_groups.chinese: 生物学家长期以来一直认为这些粗短的附属器官是一种进化适应。

sense_groups.english: Shorter extremities minimize heat loss, so animals that are more compact are better suited to the cold.
sense_groups.chinese: 较短的四肢能最大程度地减少热量流失，因此身体更紧凑的动物更适合寒冷环境。

sense_groups.english: But scientists from Ohio say that temperature may have a more direct effect on the length of an animal's limbs.
sense_groups.chinese: 但俄亥俄州的科学家表示，温度可能对动物四肢的长度有更直接的影响。

sense_groups.english: Because they find that turning up the heat helps cartilage grow—results that were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为他们发现，提高温度有助于软骨生长——这一结果发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。

sense_groups.english: The researchers raised mice at several different temperatures, and they confirmed that those kept at a balmy 80 degrees were longer limbed than those who lived at a more chill 45.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员在不同温度下饲养小鼠，并证实那些生活在舒适的80华氏度下的小鼠比生活在更冷的45华氏度下的小鼠四肢更长。

sense_groups.english: But how does a little heat make mice more leggy?
sense_groups.chinese: 但一点点热量是如何让老鼠的腿变长的呢？

sense_groups.english: The answer, they find, lies in the cartilage.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现，答案在于软骨。

sense_groups.english: Long bones grow from the cartilage found at either end.
sense_groups.chinese: 长骨从两端的软骨生长出来。

sense_groups.english: And the warmer it is, the more that cartilage grows, even when it's just sitting in a test tube.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且温度越高，软骨生长得越多，即使它只是放在试管里。

sense_groups.english: Which I guess means it's possible that the dog days of summer lead to longer-legged dogs.
sense_groups.chinese: 我想这意味着夏天的三伏天可能会导致狗腿变长。

They may be our cousins, but orangutans and other primates are nowhere near humans in terms of technological ______ , social organization or culture.

sense_groups.english: They may be our cousins, but orangutans and other primates are nowhere near humans in terms of technological achievement, social organization or culture.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们可能是我们的近亲，但猩猩和其他灵长类动物在技术成就、社会组织或文化方面远不及人类。

sense_groups.english: As humans, capacity for building off one another, an integral part of our so called cumulative culture that has allowed us to build up so much in so little time.
sense_groups.chinese: 作为人类，相互借鉴的能力是我们所谓的累积文化的关键部分，这让我们在短时间内积累了如此多的成就。

sense_groups.english: But how do we develop such advanced methods of learning in the first place?
sense_groups.chinese: 但我们最初是如何发展出如此先进的学习方法的呢？

sense_groups.english: Kevin Leyland of the University of St Andrews spoke with me about his team's quest to pinpoint the social and cognitive process that underlie humans ability to acquire and transmit knowledge.
sense_groups.chinese: 圣安德鲁大学的凯文·莱兰与我谈论了他的团队如何努力确定支撑人类获取和传播知识能力的社会和认知过程。

questions.name: #303 Soil on Mars
questions.en:
The 1976 Mars Viking Landers didn't find any life on the red planet.
But maybe they weren't looking right.
Because at least one ______ thinks that a tenth of a percent of the Martian soil tested by the Vikings could ______ have had a biological origin.
The Dutch researcher, Joop Houtkooper, ______ his ideas on August 24th at the meeting of the European Planetary Science Congress in Potsdam.
One Viking test measured unexplained rises in oxygen and carbon dioxide when it was incubating some soil samples.
Houtkooper ______ that the incredibly dry and cold surface of Mars might be home to living cells.
Such cells, however, would need to be filled with a mixture of water and hydrogen peroxide, which could stay liquid in the harsh conditions.
And if the Viking landers happened to scoop up any of these strange cells, their breakdown ______ would be in line with the oxygen and carbon dioxide measured.
The biomass would then represent a tenth of a percent of the Martian soil by weight—which is, interestingly, comparable to levels found in some Antarctic permafrost.

And if the Viking landers happened to scoop up any of these strange cells, their breakdown ______ would be in line with the oxygen and carbon dioxide measured.
The biomass would then represent a tenth of a percent of the Martian soil by weight—which is, interestingly, comparable to levels found in some Antarctic permafrost.

答案:

2. actually
3. presented
4. conjectures
5. products

sense_groups.english: The 1976 Mars Viking Landers didn't find any life on the red planet.
sense_groups.chinese: 1976年的火星维京着陆器没有在红色星球上发现任何生命。

sense_groups.english: But maybe they weren't looking right.
sense_groups.chinese: 但也许它们找错了方向。

sense_groups.english: Because at least one researcher thinks
sense_groups.chinese: 因为至少有一位研究人员认为

sense_groups.english: that a tenth of a percent of the Martian soil tested by the Vikings
sense_groups.chinese: 维京号测试的火星土壤中，有千分之一

sense_groups.english: could actually have had a biological origin.
sense_groups.chinese: 实际上可能具有生物起源。

sense_groups.english: The Dutch researcher, Joop Houtkooper,
sense_groups.chinese: 荷兰研究员乔普·霍特库珀

sense_groups.english: presented his ideas on August 24th
sense_groups.chinese: 在8月24日提出了他的想法

sense_groups.english: at the meeting of the European Planetary Science Congress in Potsdam.
sense_groups.chinese: 在波茨坦举行的欧洲行星科学大会会议上。

sense_groups.english: One Viking test measured unexplained rises in oxygen and carbon dioxide
sense_groups.chinese: 一次维京测试测量到氧气和二氧化碳的异常升高

sense_groups.english: when it was incubating some soil samples.
sense_groups.chinese: 当它培养一些土壤样本时。

sense_groups.english: Houtkooper conjectures
sense_groups.chinese: 霍特库珀推测

sense_groups.english: that the incredibly dry and cold surface of Mars
sense_groups.chinese: 火星极其干燥寒冷的表面

sense_groups.english: might be home to living cells.
sense_groups.chinese: 可能是活细胞的栖息地。

sense_groups.english: Such cells, however, would need to be filled with
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，这样的细胞需要充满

sense_groups.english: a mixture of water and hydrogen peroxide,
sense_groups.chinese: 水和过氧化氢的混合物，

sense_groups.english: which could stay liquid in the harsh conditions.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种混合物在恶劣条件下能保持液态。

sense_groups.english: And if the Viking landers happened to scoop up any of these strange cells,
sense_groups.chinese: 如果维京着陆器碰巧挖到了这些奇怪的细胞，

sense_groups.english: their breakdown products
sense_groups.chinese: 它们的分解产物

sense_groups.english: would be in line with the oxygen and carbon dioxide measured.
sense_groups.chinese: 就会与测量到的氧气和二氧化碳相符。

sense_groups.english: The biomass would then represent a tenth of a percent of the Martian soil by weight—
sense_groups.chinese: 那么这些生物量按重量计将占火星土壤的千分之一——

sense_groups.english: which is, interestingly, comparable to levels found in some Antarctic permafrost.
sense_groups.chinese: 有趣的是，这与在南极永久冻土中发现的水平相当。

questions.name: #304 Polar Vortex
questions.en:
Fed up with the polar vortex?
If so, consider this: ______ may actually share some of the ______ of exercise—at least in terms of burning fat.
  ______ studied shivering in a group of 10 men and women.
First the volunteers rested under a temperature-controlled blanket, which dropped from 80 degrees Fahrenheit to a chilly 54.
Then they cycled on an ______ bike.
Researchers took blood samples during both activities.
Turns out, shivering and exercise spurred muscles to secrete similar amounts of irisin—a hormone that tells brown fat to turn up the furnace—even though exercise took 10 times as much effort.
The researchers say the metabolic pathway may have evolved to save us energy.
Shivering alone is a costly survival mechanism—it relies on muscle contraction to warm us.
Whereas shivering-activated brown fat can convert ______ energy directly to heat.
The study is in the journal Cell Metabolism.
As for your home thermostat?
Study author Francesco Celi of the NIH likes to keep his at 68—low enough to turn on brown fat.
And it's a win-win—you'll save money on heat, 'cause you're making your own.
questions.full:
Fed up with the polar vortex?
If so, consider this: ______ may actually share some of the ______ of exercise—at least in terms of burning fat.

questions.name: #305 Earthquake in LA
questions.en:
This is gonna surprise anybody who's ever been shaken awake by a quake in ______ California.
But geologists say that the Los Angeles basin is actually in a period of low seismic activity and has been for about the last thousand years.
That's ______ to research published in the September issue of the journal Geology.
The seismic lull is marked by relatively smaller and fewer earthquakes.
That's ______ with other periods with a lot of rumbling and crumbling.
The period of big seismic activity in the LA basin that ended a thousand years ago lasted about four thousand years.
Long-term data on seismic activity indicates that the calm period lasts about 1500 to 2000 years, which gives LA another 500 to 1000 years off.
Now, the researchers are specifically referring to what's called the urban fault network, which is under the LA ______ area.
It does not include the San Andreas fault, which can still throw the occasional big one around.
About 10 major San Andreas biggies have happened during the current LA basin lull.
Nevertheless, if the current lull ends in the next millennium, LA's future could be very shaky.
questions.full:

sense_groups.english: This is gonna surprise anybody who's ever been shaken awake by a quake in southern California.

sense_groups.english: But geologists say that the Los Angeles basin is actually in a period of low seismic activity

sense_groups.chinese: 并且已经持续了大约一千年。

sense_groups.chinese: 这是根据发表在《地质学》期刊九月号上的研究得出的。

sense_groups.english: The seismic lull is marked by relatively smaller and fewer earthquakes.
sense_groups.chinese: 地震平静期的特点是地震相对较小且较少。

sense_groups.english: That's compared with other periods with a lot of rumbling and crumbling.
sense_groups.chinese: 这与那些频繁发生隆隆声和崩塌的时期形成对比。

sense_groups.english: The period of big seismic activity in the LA basin that ended a thousand years ago lasted about four thousand years.

sense_groups.chinese: 它位于洛杉矶大都市区地下。

sense_groups.chinese: 它仍然可能偶尔引发大地震。

sense_groups.chinese: 尽管如此，如果当前的平静期在下个千年结束，

sense_groups.english: LA's future could be very shaky.
sense_groups.chinese: 洛杉矶的未来可能会非常动荡。

questions.name: #306 Teeth
questions.en:
I'm guessing you brush twice a day or aspire to.
Our ancestors were a little less diligent.
But that's a good thing for scientists.
Because ancient, plaque-coated teeth are like time capsules, preserving early evidence of cavities or even plague DNA.
Now researchers have turned to thousand-year-old teeth from a convent ______ outside Frankfurt, Germany.
And they cleaned 'em, much like your dentist does.
"We used the same dental tools, and we collected the calculus from the teeth." That's molecular anthropologist Christina Warinner of the University of Oklahoma.
Inside that calculus—or plaque—she and her colleagues found tiny bits of pork, bread wheat and cabbage, identified by their DNA.
Along with the bugs behind strep throat, ______ meningitis and an oral strain of gonorrhea.
And don't be too quick to judge.
"Nearly all of us still have gonorrhea in our mouth." Their study is in the journal Nature Genetics.
Some of those bugs were ______ resistant too.
Because long before penicillin, some microbes produced natural antibiotics to attack rivals.
"Your mouth is like a ______ of bacteria." So chew on that.
questions.full:
I'm guessing you brush twice a day or aspire to.
Our ancestors were a little less diligent.
But that's a good thing for scientists.
Because ancient, plaque-coated teeth are like time capsules, preserving early evidence of cavities or even plague DNA.
Now researchers have turned to thousand-year-old teeth from a convent ______ outside Frankfurt, Germany.
And they cleaned 'em, much like your dentist does.
"We used the same dental tools, and we collected the calculus from the teeth." That's molecular anthropologist Christina Warinner of the University of Oklahoma.
Inside that calculus—or plaque—she and her colleagues found tiny bits of pork, bread wheat and cabbage, identified by their DNA.
Along with the bugs behind strep throat, ______ meningitis and an oral strain of gonorrhea.
And don't be too quick to judge.
"Nearly all of us still have gonorrhea in our mouth." Their study is in the journal Nature Genetics.
Some of those bugs were ______ resistant too.

"Your mouth is like a ______ of bacteria." So chew on that.

答案:
1. cemetery
2. bacterial
3. antibiotic
4. battlefield

sense_groups.english: I'm guessing you brush twice a day or aspire to.
sense_groups.chinese: 我猜你每天刷两次牙，或者至少想这么做。

sense_groups.english: Our ancestors were a little less diligent.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们的祖先可没那么勤快。

sense_groups.english: But that's a good thing for scientists.
sense_groups.chinese: 但对科学家来说，这是件好事。

sense_groups.english: Because ancient, plaque-coated teeth are like time capsules, preserving early evidence of cavities or even plague DNA.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为古代覆盖着牙菌斑的牙齿就像时间胶囊，保存着蛀牙甚至鼠疫DNA的早期证据。

sense_groups.english: Now researchers have turned to thousand-year-old teeth from a convent cemetery outside Frankfurt, Germany.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，研究人员开始研究德国法兰克福郊外一座修道院墓地里千年历史的牙齿。

sense_groups.english: And they cleaned 'em, much like your dentist does.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们清理了这些牙齿，就像你的牙医做的那样。

sense_groups.english: "We used the same dental tools, and we collected the calculus from the teeth."
sense_groups.chinese: “我们用了同样的牙科工具，从牙齿上收集了牙结石。”

sense_groups.english: That's molecular anthropologist Christina Warinner of the University of Oklahoma.
sense_groups.chinese: 这是俄克拉荷马大学的分子人类学家克里斯蒂娜·沃林纳说的。

sense_groups.english: Inside that calculus—or plaque—she and her colleagues found tiny bits of pork, bread wheat and cabbage, identified by their DNA.
sense_groups.chinese: 在那些牙结石（或牙菌斑）中，她和同事发现了微量的猪肉、面包小麦和卷心菜，通过它们的DNA鉴定出来。

sense_groups.english: Along with the bugs behind strep throat, bacterial meningitis and an oral strain of gonorrhea.
sense_groups.chinese: 还有导致链球菌性咽喉炎、细菌性脑膜炎和一种口腔淋病菌株的细菌。

sense_groups.english: And don't be too quick to judge.
sense_groups.chinese: 别急着下结论。

sense_groups.english: "Nearly all of us still have gonorrhea in our mouth."
sense_groups.chinese: “我们几乎所有人嘴里都还有淋病细菌。”

sense_groups.english: Their study is in the journal Nature Genetics.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们的研究发表在《自然·遗传学》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: Some of those bugs were antibiotic resistant too.
sense_groups.chinese: 其中一些细菌还具有抗生素耐药性。

sense_groups.english: Because long before penicillin, some microbes produced natural antibiotics to attack rivals.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为在青霉素出现很久以前，一些微生物就会产生天然抗生素来攻击对手。

sense_groups.english: "Your mouth is like a battlefield of bacteria."
sense_groups.chinese: “你的嘴就像一个细菌战场。”

sense_groups.english: So chew on that.
sense_groups.chinese: 好好琢磨琢磨吧。

questions.name: #307 Comedy
questions.en:
Everyone from Freud to Tina Fey has tried to understand why some things are funny.
Now, new research concludes that one key to comedy is for a situation to ______ a moral standard, but in a gentle way.
Researchers presented volunteers with a number of different scenarios.
For example, the Jimmy Dean sausage company needs a spokesman for its new line of pork products, so they hire Rabbi Shlomo Rosenfield.
Or, so they hire a farmer.
Participants were more likely to find the rabbi scenario wrong, but they were also more likely to think it was funny.
The researchers found that participants would laugh at situations with moral violations if, for example, they felt that situation was hypothetical, harmless or involved people unconnected to the listener.
The study appears in the journal Psychological Science.
The finding deviates from previously published psychology studies which ______ moral violation solely with disgust.
It also proves that Mel Brooks was onto something when he said, "Tragedy is when I cut my finger.
Comedy is when you fall down an open sewer and die."
questions.full:
Everyone from Freud to Tina Fey has tried to understand why some things are funny.
Now, new research concludes that one key to comedy is for a situation to ______ a moral standard, but in a gentle way.
Researchers presented volunteers with a number of different scenarios.
For example, the Jimmy Dean sausage company needs a spokesman for its new line of pork products, so they hire Rabbi Shlomo Rosenfield.
Or, so they hire a farmer.
Participants were more likely to find the rabbi scenario wrong, but they were also more likely to think it was funny.
The researchers found that participants would laugh at situations with moral violations if, for example, they felt that situation was hypothetical, harmless or involved people unconnected to the listener.
The study appears in the journal Psychological Science.

It also proves that Mel Brooks was onto something when he said, "Tragedy is when I cut my finger.
Comedy is when you fall down an open sewer and die."

答案:
1. violate
2. equate

sense_groups.english: Everyone from Freud to Tina Fey has tried to understand why some things are funny.
sense_groups.chinese: 从弗洛伊德到蒂娜·菲，每个人都试图理解为什么有些东西好笑。

sense_groups.english: Now, new research concludes that one key to comedy is for a situation to violate a moral standard, but in a gentle way.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，新的研究得出结论，喜剧的一个关键是某种情况要违反道德标准，但要以温和的方式。

sense_groups.english: Researchers presented volunteers with a number of different scenarios.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员向志愿者展示了许多不同的场景。

sense_groups.english: For example, the Jimmy Dean sausage company needs a spokesman for its new line of pork products, so they hire Rabbi Shlomo Rosenfield.
sense_groups.chinese: 例如，吉米·迪恩香肠公司为其新猪肉产品线需要一位发言人，于是他们聘请了拉比什洛莫·罗森菲尔德。

sense_groups.english: Or, so they hire a farmer.
sense_groups.chinese: 或者，他们聘请了一位农民。

sense_groups.english: Participants were more likely to find the rabbi scenario wrong, but they were also more likely to think it was funny.
sense_groups.chinese: 参与者更可能认为拉比的情景是错误的，但也更可能觉得它好笑。

sense_groups.english: The researchers found that participants would laugh at situations with moral violations if, for example, they felt that situation was hypothetical, harmless or involved people unconnected to the listener.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员发现，如果参与者觉得某种情况是假设性的、无害的或涉及与听众无关的人，他们就会对违反道德的情景发笑。

sense_groups.english: The study appears in the journal Psychological Science.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《心理科学》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: The finding deviates from previously published psychology studies which equate moral violation solely with disgust.
sense_groups.chinese: 这一发现与先前发表的心理学研究不同，那些研究将道德违反仅仅等同于厌恶。

sense_groups.english: It also proves that Mel Brooks was onto something when he said, 'Tragedy is when I cut my finger. Comedy is when you fall down an open sewer and die.'
sense_groups.chinese: 这也证明了梅尔·布鲁克斯说得有道理，他说：‘悲剧是我割伤了手指，喜剧是你掉进敞开的下水道死了。’

questions.name: #308 Social Dogs
questions.en:
Does your puppy turn his nose up at his own chow—because he wants some of ______ it is that you're having?
A new study finds that, when it comes to food, dogs recognize human social signals about what's good.
The work is in the journal Public Library of Science ONE.
Researchers let pet dogs choose between two plates, one with a single piece of food and the other with six pieces.
Unsurprisingly, the animals generally went for the larger portion.
But when a human being showed a clear liking for the smaller plate, the canines likewise went for the skimpier choice.
The dogs apparently recognized and ______ to the humans' social cues.
And not all cues were equally effective.
When the human ______ but did not touch the smaller portion, dogs ignored the attention-drawing gesture.
For a social signal to influence behavior, it had to demonstrate intention.
And the most ______ cues also involved communication, such as looking from the food to the dog and back while talking encouragingly.
For dogs, choosing a bite may depend on another's bark.

sense_groups.english: Researchers let pet dogs choose between two plates, one with a single piece of food and the other with six pieces.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员让宠物狗在两个盘子之间选择，一个盘子里有一块食物，另一个盘子里有六块。

sense_groups.english: Unsurprisingly, the animals generally went for the larger portion.
sense_groups.chinese: 毫不意外，这些动物通常选择更大的那份。

sense_groups.english: But when a human being showed a clear liking for the smaller plate, the canines likewise went for the skimpier choice.

sense_groups.english: For a social signal to influence behavior, it had to demonstrate intention.
sense_groups.chinese: 要让社交信号影响行为，它必须展示意图。

sense_groups.english: And the most ______ cues also involved communication, such as looking from the food to the dog and back while talking encouragingly.
sense_groups.chinese: 最有效的信号还涉及交流，比如一边鼓励地说话，一边在食物和狗之间来回看。

questions.name: #309 Evolution
questions.en:
If you want to see ______ at work, visit a hospital.
Inside a sick patient, antibiotics wipe out infectious ______ by the millions.
But germs are always mutating.
A few adapt to resist the drug, so they survive—and spread.
Such ______ bacteria infect two million Americans every year; they kill 23,000.
In this arms race between medicine and evolution, evolution is winning.
But could we turn evolution against bacteria?
It turns out that when bacteria mutate to become resistant to one antibiotic, they often become more ______ to a different drug.
So maybe after a jab with the left, a roundhouse to the right will deliver a knockout blow.
To test this idea, ______ in Denmark dosed batches of E. coli with 23 different antibiotics, and waited for resistance to evolve.
In three-quarters of the cases, the mutant germs became more susceptible to a second drug.
The work appears in the journal Science Translational Medicine.
One particular combination of widely used antibiotics—gentamicin, then cefuroxime, then gentamicin again, and so on—looks like it could hold the bugs at bay indefinitely.

sense_groups.english: It turns out that when bacteria mutate to become resistant to one antibiotic, they often become more ______ to a different drug.

sense_groups.english: So maybe after a jab with the left, a roundhouse to the right will deliver a knockout blow.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以也许左勾拳之后，右旋踢就能给予致命一击。

sense_groups.english: To test this idea, ______ in Denmark dosed batches of E. coli with 23 different antibiotics, and waited for resistance to evolve.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了验证这个想法，丹麦的______用23种不同的抗生素处理了一批大肠杆菌，等待耐药性进化。

sense_groups.english: In three-quarters of the cases, the mutant germs became more susceptible to a second drug.
sense_groups.chinese: 在四分之三的案例中，变异细菌对第二种药物变得更加敏感。

sense_groups.english: The work appears in the journal Science Translational Medicine.

sense_groups.english: One particular combination of widely used antibiotics—gentamicin, then cefuroxime, then gentamicin again, and so on—looks like it could hold the bugs at bay indefinitely.
sense_groups.chinese: 一种特定组合的常用抗生素——庆大霉素、头孢呋辛、再庆大霉素，如此循环——似乎能无限期地控制细菌。

questions.name: #310 Female Ticks
questions.en:
We've all heard the old saw about women who let themselves go after getting married.
Well, female ticks take this post honeymoon weight-gain to extremes.
After mating, female ticks in the family Ixodes increase their mass an astonishing 100 times, ballooning from the size of a sand grain to that of a kidney bean.
This ______ growth spurt is actually an ______ part of the tick's whole blood-sucking lifestyle.
Female ticks need to fully engorge before they can lay eggs.
But virgins are better off staying small so that they'll have more time to find a mate.
Not that male ticks have ______ against full-bodied females.
It's just that ticks meet their matches while they're hanging around on their hosts.
And if unwed females become too ______ they're more likely to get knocked off during a good grooming.
As to what spurs the females to really bulk up, Ruben Kaufman of the ______ of Alberta finds that male ticks' semen contains proteins that trigger engorgement.
Vaccines against these proteins could keep ticks from reproducing and transmitting infections such as Lyme disease.
That would be good news for people, but bad news for female ticks who dream of being engorgeous.
questions.full:
We've all heard the old saw about women who let themselves go after getting married.
Well, female ticks take this post honeymoon weight-gain to extremes.
After mating, female ticks in the family Ixodes increase their mass an astonishing 100 times, ballooning from the size of a sand grain to that of a kidney bean.
This ______ growth spurt is actually an ______ part of the tick's whole blood-sucking lifestyle.
Female ticks need to fully engorge before they can lay eggs.
But virgins are better off staying small so that they'll have more time to find a mate.
Not that male ticks have ______ against full-bodied females.
It's just that ticks meet their matches while they're hanging around on their hosts.
And if unwed females become too ______ they're more likely to get knocked off during a good grooming.
As to what spurs the females to really bulk up, Ruben Kaufman of the ______ of Alberta finds that male ticks' semen contains proteins that trigger engorgement.
Vaccines against these proteins could keep ticks from reproducing and transmitting infections such as Lyme disease.
That would be good news for people, but bad news for female ticks who dream of being engorgeous.

答案:
1. post-copulatory
2. important
3. anything
4. unwieldy
5. University

sense_groups.english: We've all heard the old saw about women who let themselves go after getting married.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们都听过那句老话，说女人结婚后就放任自流了。

sense_groups.english: Well, female ticks take this post honeymoon weight-gain to extremes.
sense_groups.chinese: 嗯，雌性蜱虫把这种蜜月后的体重增长发挥到了极致。

sense_groups.english: After mating, female ticks in the family Ixodes increase their mass an astonishing 100 times, ballooning from the size of a sand grain to that of a kidney bean.
sense_groups.chinese: 交配后，硬蜱科的雌性蜱虫体重惊人地增加100倍，从沙粒大小膨胀到肾豆那么大。

sense_groups.english: This post-copulatory growth spurt is actually an important part of the tick's whole blood-sucking lifestyle.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种交配后的生长突增实际上是蜱虫整个吸血生活方式的重要部分。

sense_groups.english: Female ticks need to fully engorge before they can lay eggs.
sense_groups.chinese: 雌性蜱虫需要完全饱食才能产卵。

sense_groups.english: But virgins are better off staying small so that they'll have more time to find a mate.
sense_groups.chinese: 但未交配的蜱虫最好保持小巧，这样它们就有更多时间寻找配偶。

sense_groups.english: Not that male ticks have anything against full-bodied females.
sense_groups.chinese: 并不是雄性蜱虫对丰满的雌性有什么意见。

sense_groups.english: It's just that ticks meet their matches while they're hanging around on their hosts.
sense_groups.chinese: 只是蜱虫在宿主身上活动时才会遇到配偶。

sense_groups.english: And if unwed females become too unwieldy they're more likely to get knocked off during a good grooming.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果未交配的雌性变得过于笨重，它们更可能在宿主梳理时被弄掉。

sense_groups.english: As to what spurs the females to really bulk up, Ruben Kaufman of the University of Alberta finds that male ticks' semen contains proteins that trigger engorgement.
sense_groups.chinese: 至于什么促使雌性真正增肥，阿尔伯塔大学的鲁本·考夫曼发现，雄性蜱虫的精液中含有触发饱食的蛋白质。

sense_groups.english: Vaccines against these proteins could keep ticks from reproducing and transmitting infections such as Lyme disease.
sense_groups.chinese: 针对这些蛋白质的疫苗可以阻止蜱虫繁殖和传播莱姆病等感染。

sense_groups.english: That would be good news for people, but bad news for female ticks who dream of being engorgeous.
sense_groups.chinese: 这对人类来说是好消息，但对梦想变得丰满的雌性蜱虫来说则是坏消息。

questions.name: #311 Animal Sounds
questions.en:
Many animals use sounds to convey information. Humans use vocal labels for objects and for people. We call these words, and names.
A few creatures, such as dolphins and parrots, can learn ontogenetic vocal labels. And wild husbands are known to have particular, drinkable signature whistles. Scientists at Scotland's St. Andrews University wanted to know: can these propositions be used as labels?
The researchers right sounds from dolphins off Scotland's east coast, and extracted these signature whistles. Then they altered the sounds so the calls wouldn't sound exactly like the originating dolphin.
They played those sounds back to the dolphins, along with whistles from dolphins familiar to the animals and whistles from strangers.
When the dolphins heard their own signature whistle they needy responded with that same sound. That reaction only happened twice when they heard sounds from their pals and not at all when they heard the alien dolphin. The research is in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
The researchers think dolphin signature whistles serve as self-identification, and maybe even as a label for addressing each other—just like a name.

They played those sounds back to the dolphins, along with whistles from dolphins familiar to the animals and whistles from strangers. 
When the dolphins heard their own signature whistle they needy responded with that same sound. That reaction only happened twice when they heard sounds from their pals and not at all when they heard the alien dolphin. The research is in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. 
The researchers think dolphin signature whistles serve as self-identification, and maybe even as a label for addressing each other—just like a name.

sense_groups.english: Many animals use sounds to convey information.

sense_groups.english: And wild husbands are known to have particular, drinkable signature whistles.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且野生海豚有独特的、可识别的签名哨声。

sense_groups.english: Scientists at Scotland's St. Andrews University wanted to know: can these propositions be used as labels?
sense_groups.chinese: 苏格兰圣安德鲁大学的科学家想知道：这些声音能否用作标签？

sense_groups.english: The researchers right sounds from dolphins off Scotland's east coast, and extracted these signature whistles.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员录制了苏格兰东海岸海豚的声音，并提取了这些签名哨声。

sense_groups.english: Then they altered the sounds so the calls wouldn't sound exactly like the originating dolphin.

sense_groups.english: They played those sounds back to the dolphins, along with whistles from dolphins familiar to the animals and whistles from strangers.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们向海豚播放这些声音，同时播放海豚熟悉的同伴的哨声和陌生海豚的哨声。

sense_groups.english: When the dolphins heard their own signature whistle they needy responded with that same sound.
sense_groups.chinese: 当海豚听到自己的签名哨声时，它们会回应同样的声音。

sense_groups.english: That reaction only happened twice when they heard sounds from their pals and not at all when they heard the alien dolphin.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种反应在听到同伴声音时只发生了两次，而在听到陌生海豚声音时完全没有。

sense_groups.english: The research is in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。

sense_groups.english: The researchers think dolphin signature whistles serve as self-identification, and maybe even as a label for addressing each other—just like a name.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员认为，海豚的签名哨声用于自我识别，甚至可能像名字一样用作互相称呼的标签。

questions.name: #312 Human and Chimp
questions.en:
When you hear things like: human DNA differs from chimp DNA by only a couple percent, you can't help but wonder, how can that be?
How can so few changes make such a big difference?
  ______ working with fruit bats and mice think they have an answer.
And it lies less in the animals' genes than in the short snippets of DNA that control when and where and how ______ genes are turned on.
If you've ever thought that a bat is basically just a rodent with wings, you're not too far from the mark.
One of the most obvious ______ between bats and mice is their forearms.
Mice have these stubby little legs, and bats have these large leathery wings.
But even those differences are not as major as you might imagine.
Mice and bats both have a gene called Prx1, which regulates limb development.
But the gene is more active in the budding wings of bats.
So the researchers took the piece of DNA that ______ Prx1 activity from a bat and stuck it into a mouse.
The result ______ in the January 15 issue of Genes and Development: mice that have longer front legs.
Ok, they didn't sprout wings, but the study shows that even small changes can have big consequences.

When you hear things like: human DNA differs from chimp DNA by only a couple percent, you can't help but wonder, how can that be?
How can so few changes make such a big difference?
  ______ working with fruit bats and mice think they have an answer.

sense_groups.english: When you hear things like: human DNA differs from chimp DNA by only a couple percent,
sense_groups.chinese: 当你听到类似这样的话：人类DNA与黑猩猩DNA只相差几个百分点，

sense_groups.english: you can't help but wonder, how can that be?
sense_groups.chinese: 你忍不住会想，这怎么可能呢？

sense_groups.english: How can so few changes make such a big difference?
sense_groups.chinese: 这么少的变化怎么能造成如此大的差异？

sense_groups.english: Researchers working with fruit bats and mice think they have an answer.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究果蝠和老鼠的研究人员认为他们找到了答案。

sense_groups.english: And it lies less in the animals' genes than in the short snippets of DNA that control when and where and how those genes are turned on.
sense_groups.chinese: 答案更多在于控制这些基因何时、何地以及如何被开启的短DNA片段，而不是动物基因本身。

sense_groups.english: If you've ever thought that a bat is basically just a rodent with wings, you're not too far from the mark.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你曾认为蝙蝠基本上就是有翅膀的啮齿动物，那你离真相并不远。

sense_groups.english: One of the most obvious differences between bats and mice is their forearms.
sense_groups.chinese: 蝙蝠和老鼠之间最明显的区别之一就是它们的前肢。

sense_groups.english: Mice have these stubby little legs, and bats have these large leathery wings.
sense_groups.chinese: 老鼠有短小的腿，而蝙蝠有巨大的皮革状翅膀。

sense_groups.english: But even those differences are not as major as you might imagine.
sense_groups.chinese: 但即使这些差异也不像你想象的那么大。

sense_groups.english: Mice and bats both have a gene called Prx1, which regulates limb development.
sense_groups.chinese: 老鼠和蝙蝠都有一种名为Prx1的基因，它调节肢体发育。

sense_groups.english: But the gene is more active in the budding wings of bats.
sense_groups.chinese: 但在蝙蝠的翅膀芽中，这种基因更活跃。

sense_groups.english: So the researchers took the piece of DNA that controls Prx1 activity from a bat and stuck it into a mouse.
sense_groups.chinese: 于是研究人员从蝙蝠身上取出了控制Prx1活性的DNA片段，并将其植入老鼠体内。

sense_groups.english: The result pictured in the January 15 issue of Genes and Development: mice that have longer front legs.
sense_groups.chinese: 结果发表在《基因与发育》1月15日刊上：老鼠的前腿变长了。

sense_groups.english: Ok, they didn't sprout wings, but the study shows that even small changes can have big consequences.
sense_groups.chinese: 好吧，它们没有长出翅膀，但这项研究表明，即使是微小的变化也能产生巨大的影响。

questions.name: #313 Solar Wind
questions.en:
If you've ever ______ where the Earth came from, the answer, it seems, is blowin' in the wind—the solar wind.
Or so say ______ who, after examining solar wind samples collected by the Genesis spacecraft, conclude that the inner planets of our solar system formed a little ______ than we'd thought.
The work appears in the journal Science.
Our solar system arose from a large, rotating cloud of interstellar debris called the solar nebula.
The sun came first and the planets ______ not long after.
But the new study shows that the ratio of oxygen and ______ isotopes found in the solar wind is different from the ratio here on earth, or on the moon or Mars.

Now we just have to figure out why.
Scientists say the excess heavy nitrogen could have come from a comet.
And the heavier oxygen from a natural process that left more of the light isotope in the part of the nebula that made the sun.
So we are made of star stuff.

sense_groups.english: The work appears in the journal Science.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《科学》杂志上。
